metadata.section_title: Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.07 Option 7 - Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
text:
Section 2C.07 Option 7 - Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

If the curve has a change in horizontal alignment of 135 degrees or more, the Hairpin Curve (W1-11) sign may be used instead of a Turn or Curve sign.

metadata.section_title: Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.07 Option 8 - Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
text:
Section 2C.07 Option 8 - Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

If the curve has a change of direction of approximately 270 degrees, such as on a cloverleaf interchange ramp, the 270-degree Loop (W1-15) sign may be used instead of a Turn or Curve sign.

metadata.section_title: Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.07 Guidance 9 - Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
text:
Section 2C.07 Guidance 9 - Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

When the Hairpin Curve sign or the 270-degree Loop sign is installed, either a One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign or Chevron Alignment (W1-8) signs should be installed on the outside of the turn or curve.

metadata.section_title: Horizontal Alignment Signs (W1-1 through W1-5, W1-11, and W1-15)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Standard 1 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Standard 1 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

The use of the Chevron Alignment (W1-8) sign (see Figures 2C-1 and 2C-2) to provide additional emphasis and guidance for a change in horizontal alignment shall be in accordance with the information shown in Table 2C-4.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Option 2 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Option 2 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

Chevron Alignment signs may be used instead of or in addition to standard delineators.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Standard 3 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Standard 3 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

The Chevron Alignment sign shall be a vertical rectangle. No border shall be used on the Chevron Alignment sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Standard 4 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Standard 4 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

If used, Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed on the outside of a turn or curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic. Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed at a minimum height of 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Guidance 5 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Guidance 5 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

The approximate spacing of Chevron Alignment signs on the turn or curve measured from the point of curvature (PC) should be as shown in Table 2C-5. Alignment Signs on Horizontal Curves Advisory Speed Curve Radius Sign Spacing

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Guidance 6 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Guidance 6 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

The Chevron Alignment signs should be visible for a sufficient distance to provide the road user with adequate time to react to the change in alignment.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Option 7 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Option 7 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

LEDs may be used to enhance the conspicuity of Chevron Alignment signs (see Section 2A.12).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Standard 8 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Standard 8 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

The LEDs used in the Chevron Alignment sign shall consist of yellow LEDs outlining the chevron symbol.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Standard 9 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Standard 9 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

Chevron Alignment signs shall not be placed on the far side of a T-intersection facing traffic on the stem approach to warn drivers that a through movement is not physically possible, as this is the function of a Two-Direction (or One-Direction) Large Arrow sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Standard 10 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Standard 10 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

Chevron Alignment signs shall not be used to mark obstructions within or adjacent to the roadway, including the beginning of guardrails or barriers, as this is the function of an object marker (see Section 2C.70).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.08 Standard 11 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
text:
Section 2C.08 Standard 11 - Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

Chevron Alignment signs directing traffic to the right shall not be used in the central island of a roundabout or a neighborhood traffic circle.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.09 Option 1 - Combination Horizontal Alignment/Intersection Signs (W1-10 Series)
text:
Section 2C.09 Option 1 - Combination Horizontal Alignment/Intersection Signs (W1-10 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 158

The Turn (W1-1) sign, the Curve (W1-2) sign, and the Reverse Curve (W1-4) sign may be combined with the Cross Road (W2-1) sign or the Side Road (W2-2 or W2-3) sign to create a combination Horizontal Alignment/ Intersection (W1-10 series) sign (see Figure 2C-1) that depicts the condition where an intersection occurs within or immediately adjacent to a turn or curve.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.10 Option 1 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
text:
Section 2C.10 Option 1 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

A One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign may be used to supplement a Turn (W1-1) or Reverse Turn (W1-3) sign (see Figure 2C-2) to emphasize the abrupt curvature.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.10 Option 2 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
text:
Section 2C.10 Option 2 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

A One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign (see Figure 2C-1) may be used either as a supplement or alternative to Chevron Alignment signs or delineators in order to delineate a change in horizontal alignment (see Figure 2C-2) when: Rev. 1 A. Site conditions limit the number of delineators or Chevron Alignment signs that are visible; or B. The number of delineators or Chevron Alignment signs that can be installed within the change in horizontal alignment is less than the number determined by the spacing specified in Sections 2C.08 or 3G.04.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.10 Standard 3 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
text:
Section 2C.10 Standard 3 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

The One-Direction Large Arrow sign shall be a horizontal rectangle with an arrow pointing to the left or right.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.10 Standard 4 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
text:
Section 2C.10 Standard 4 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

If used, the One-Direction Large Arrow sign shall be installed on the outside of a turn or curve in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.10 Standard 5 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
text:
Section 2C.10 Standard 5 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

The One-Direction Large Arrow sign shall not be used where there is no alignment change in the direction of travel, such as at the beginnings and ends of medians or at center piers.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.10 Standard 6 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
text:
Section 2C.10 Standard 6 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

The One-Direction Large Arrow sign directing traffic to the right shall not be used in the central island of a roundabout or a neighborhood traffic circle.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.10 Guidance 7 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
text:
Section 2C.10 Guidance 7 - One-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

The One-Direction Large Arrow sign should be visible for a sufficient distance to provide the road user with adequate time to react to the change in alignment.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.11 Option 1 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
text:
Section 2C.11 Option 1 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

A Truck Rollover (W1-13) sign (see Figure 2C-1) may be used as a supplement to a horizontal alignment warning sign to warn drivers of vehicles with a high center of gravity, such as trucks, tankers, and recreational vehicles, of a curve or turn where there are: A. Past incidents of truck rollovers at the specific location, B. High volumes of trucks, or C. A speed differential (see Section 2C.06) that might pose a greater risk for vehicles with high centers of gravity.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.11 Guidance 2 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
text:
Section 2C.11 Guidance 2 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

Where engineering judgment determines the need for the installation of a Truck Rollover (W1-13) sign, it should be located downstream of the horizontal alignment warning sign in advance of the curve.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.11 Standard 3 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
text:
Section 2C.11 Standard 3 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

If a Truck Rollover (W1-13) sign is used, it shall be accompanied by an Advisory Speed (W13-1P) plaque indicating the recommended speed for vehicles with a higher center of gravity.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.11 Option 4 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
text:
Section 2C.11 Option 4 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 159

The Truck Rollover sign may include conspicuity enhancements, or may be a blank-out sign, activated by the detection of an approaching vehicle with a high center of gravity that is traveling in excess of the recommended speed for the condition.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.11 Support 5 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
text:
Section 2C.11 Support 5 - Truck Rollover Sign (W1-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

The curved arrow on the Truck Rollover sign shows the direction of roadway curvature. The truck tips in the opposite direction. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Standard 1 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Standard 1 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

Where an advisory speed is posted in advance of a freeway or expressway exit, the Advisory Exit Speed (W13-2) sign (see Figure 2C-1) shall be used.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Standard 2 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Standard 2 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

Where an advisory speed is posted in advance of a conventional road ramp or to another roadway or roadside facility, the Advisory Ramp Speed (W13-3) sign (see Figure 2C-1) shall be used.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Standard 3 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Standard 3 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

An Advisory Exit Speed or Advisory Ramp Speed sign shall be used when the difference between the mainline roadway speed limit and the exit or ramp advisory speed in the vicinity of the departure is 20 mph or greater.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Guidance 4 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Guidance 4 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

An Advisory Exit Speed or Advisory Ramp Speed sign should be used when the difference between the mainline roadway speed limit and the exit or ramp advisory speed in the vicinity of the departure is 15 mph.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Option 5 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Option 5 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

An Advisory Exit Speed or Advisory Ramp Speed sign may be used based on engineering judgment when the difference between the mainline roadway speed limit and the exit or ramp advisory speed in the vicinity of the departure is 10 mph or less.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Option 6 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Option 6 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

The Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit Speed (W13-6, W13-8, and W13-10) signs (see Figure 2C-1) may be used in lieu of the Advisory Exit Speed (W13-2) sign, and the combination Horizontal Alignment/ Advisory Ramp Speed (W13-7, W13-9, and W13-11) signs (see Figure 2C-1) may be used in lieu of the Advisory Ramp Speed (W13-3) sign.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Option 7 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Option 7 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

The Combination Truck Rollover/Advisory Exit Speed and Truck Rollover/Advisory Ramp Speed (W13-12 and W13-13) signs (see Figure 2C-1) may be used in lieu of the W13-2 and W13-3 signs, respectively, if the tip over condition is in the vicinity of the gore.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Standard 8 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Standard 8 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

Roadway geometrics represented on the Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Ramp Speed signs (see Figure 2C-1) shall be limited to the standard signs shown in this Manual.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Guidance 9 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Guidance 9 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

If used, the Advisory Exit Speed sign or the Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit Speed sign should be installed along the deceleration lane. The Advisory Exit Speed or the Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit signs should be visible in time for the road user to decelerate and make an exiting maneuver. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.12 Guidance 10 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
text:
Section 2C.12 Guidance 10 - Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 160

Regulatory Speed Limit signs (see Section 2B.21) should not be located in the vicinity of exit ramps or deceleration lanes, particularly where they will conflict with the advisory speed displayed on the Advisory Exit or Ramp Speed signs.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-2 and W13-3) and Combination Horizontal Alignment/Advisory Exit and Ramp Speed Signs (W13-6 through W13-13)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.13 Support 1 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
text:
Section 2C.13 Support 1 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 166

Vehicle Speed Feedback (W13-20) signs or (W13-20aP) plaques (see Figure 2C-4) that display the speed of an approaching vehicle to the vehicle operator are sometimes used to provide warning to drivers of their speed in relation to either a speed limit (R2-1) sign or a horizontal alignment warning sign assembly with a posted advisory speed.

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.13 Standard 2 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
text:
Section 2C.13 Standard 2 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 166

The Vehicle Speed Feedback (W13- 20aP) plaque shall only be mounted below a Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (see Section 2B.21) to display the speed of an approaching vehicle in relation to the posted speed limit.

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.13 Standard 3 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
text:
Section 2C.13 Standard 3 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 166

The Vehicle Speed Feedback (W13-20) sign shall only be an independent installation near the point of curvature of a horizontal curve (see Section 2C.06) to supplement the advisory speed that is displayed with the horizontal alignment warning sign.

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.13 Standard 4 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
text:
Section 2C.13 Standard 4 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 166

The legend YOUR SPEED shall be a black legend on a yellow retroreflective background, except as provided in Sections 6H.01 and 7B.01. The changeable legend displaying the speed of the approaching vehicle shall be a yellow luminous legend on a black opaque background. The vehicle speed displayed on the changeable portion of the sign shall be displayed as an integer. The Vehicle Speed Feedback sign and plaque shall not flash, strobe, change color, or use other animated elements integrated into the changeable legend display. When no vehicles are approaching, the changeable display shall not display a legend.

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.13 Guidance 5 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
text:
Section 2C.13 Guidance 5 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 166

The changeable portion of the Vehicle Speed Feedback legend should be approximately the same height, width, and stroke of those on the Speed Limit sign it supplements or is mounted below.

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.13 Guidance 6 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
text:
Section 2C.13 Guidance 6 - Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 167

When a W13-20aP plaque is used with a Speed Limit sign it should be approximately the same width as the Speed Limit sign it is mounted below. December 2025 VERTICAL GRADE WARNING SIGNS AND PLAQUES

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Speed Feedback Sign and Plaque (W13-20 and W13-20aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.14 Guidance 1 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
text:
Section 2C.14 Guidance 1 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 167

The Hill (W7-1) sign (see Figure 2C-5) should be used in advance of a downgrade where the length, percent of grade, horizontal curvature, and/or other physical features require special precautions on the part of road users.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.14 Guidance 2 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
text:
Section 2C.14 Guidance 2 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 167

The Hill sign and supplemental grade (W7-3P) plaque (see Figure 2C-5 and Section 2C.64) used in combination, or the W7-1a sign used alone, should be installed in advance of downgrades for the following conditions: A. 5% grade that is more than 3,000 feet in length, B. 6% grade that is more than 2,000 feet in length, C. 7% grade that is more than 1,000 feet in length, D. 8% grade that is more than 750 feet in length, or E. 9% grade that is more than 500 feet in length.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.14 Guidance 3 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
text:
Section 2C.14 Guidance 3 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 167

These signs should also be installed for steeper grades or where crash experience and field observations indicate a need.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.14 Guidance 4 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
text:
Section 2C.14 Guidance 4 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 167

Supplemental plaques (see Sections 2C.57 and 2C.64) and larger signs should be used for emphasis or where special hill characteristics exist. On longer grades, the use of the Hill sign with a distance (W7-3aP) plaque or the combination distance/grade (W7-3bP) plaque (see Figure 2C-5) at periodic intervals of approximately 1-mile spacing should be considered.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.14 Option 5 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
text:
Section 2C.14 Option 5 - Hill Signs (W7-1 and W7-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 168

A USE LOW GEAR (W7-2P) or TRUCKS USE LOWER GEAR (W7-2bP) supplemental plaque (see Figure 2C-5) may be used to indicate a situation where downshifting as well as braking might be advisable. Figure 2C-5. Vertical Grade Signs and Plaques

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.15 Guidance 1 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
text:
Section 2C.15 Guidance 1 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 168

Where applicable, truck escape (or runaway truck) ramp advance warning signs (see Figure 2C-5) should be located approximately 1 mile and approximately ½ mile in advance of the grade, and of the escape ramp. An additional W7-4b or W7-4c sign should be placed at the gore.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.15 Guidance 2 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
text:
Section 2C.15 Guidance 2 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 168

A RUNAWAY VEHICLES ONLY (R4-10) sign (see Section 2B.41) should be installed near the escape ramp entrance to discourage other road users from entering the ramp. No Parking (R8-3) signs should be placed near the ramp entrance.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.15 Standard 3 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
text:
Section 2C.15 Standard 3 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 168

When truck escape ramps are installed, at least one of the W7-4 series signs shall be used.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.15 Option 4 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
text:
Section 2C.15 Option 4 - Truck Escape Ramp Signs (W7-4 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 168

A SAND (W7-4dP), GRAVEL (W7-4eP), or PAVED (W7-4fP) supplemental plaque (see Figure 2C-5) may be used to describe the ramp surface. State and local highway agencies may develop appropriate word message signs for the specific situation.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.16 Option 1 - HILL BLOCKS VIEW Sign (W7-6)
text:
Section 2C.16 Option 1 - HILL BLOCKS VIEW Sign (W7-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 168

A HILL BLOCKS VIEW (W7-6) sign (see Figure 2C-5) may be used on the approach to a crest vertical curve where the vertical curvature provides inadequate stopping sight distance at the posted speed limit.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.16 Guidance 2 - HILL BLOCKS VIEW Sign (W7-6)
text:
Section 2C.16 Guidance 2 - HILL BLOCKS VIEW Sign (W7-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 168

When a vertical curve results in a sight distance obstruction to a specific condition beyond the crest of the vertical curve, the warning sign for the specific condition beyond the vertical crest should be used rather than the HILL BLOCKS VIEW sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.16 Guidance 3 - HILL BLOCKS VIEW Sign (W7-6)
text:
Section 2C.16 Guidance 3 - HILL BLOCKS VIEW Sign (W7-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 169

When a HILL BLOCKS VIEW sign is used, it should be supplemented by an Advisory Speed (W13-1P) plaque (see Figure 2C-1) indicating the recommended speed for traveling over the hillcrest based on available stopping sight distance. ROADWAY GEOMETRY WARNING SIGNS

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.17 Guidance 1 - ROAD NARROWS Sign (W5-1)
text:
Section 2C.17 Guidance 1 - ROAD NARROWS Sign (W5-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

Except as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section, a ROAD NARROWS (W5-1) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used in advance of a transition on two-lane roads where the pavement width is reduced abruptly to a width such that vehicles traveling in opposite directions cannot simultaneously travel through the narrow portion of the roadway without reducing speed. Figure 2C-6. Miscellaneous Warning Signs

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.17 Option 2 - ROAD NARROWS Sign (W5-1)
text:
Section 2C.17 Option 2 - ROAD NARROWS Sign (W5-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

The ROAD NARROWS (W5-1) sign may be omitted on low-volume local streets that have speed limits of 30 mph or less.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.17 Option 3 - ROAD NARROWS Sign (W5-1)
text:
Section 2C.17 Option 3 - ROAD NARROWS Sign (W5-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

Additional emphasis may be provided by the use of object markers and delineators (see Sections 2C.70 through 2C.73 and Chapter 3G). The Advisory Speed (W13-1P) plaque (see Figure 2C-1 and Section 2C.59) may be used to indicate the recommended speed.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.18 Guidance 1 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
text:
Section 2C.18 Guidance 1 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

A NARROW BRIDGE (W5-2) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used in advance of any bridge or culvert having a two-way roadway horizontal clearance of 16 to 18 feet, or any bridge or culvert having a roadway horizontal clearance less than the width of the approach travel lanes. Where these conditions exist for an underpass, a NARROW UNDERPASS (W5-2a) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used.

metadata.section_title: NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.18 Guidance 2 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
text:
Section 2C.18 Guidance 2 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

Additional emphasis should be provided by the use of object markers, delineators, and/or pavement markings.

metadata.section_title: NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.18 Option 3 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
text:
Section 2C.18 Option 3 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

A NARROW BRIDGE sign may be used in advance of a bridge or culvert on which the approach shoulders are narrowed or eliminated. Where these conditions exist for an underpass, a NARROW UNDERPASS sign may be used.

metadata.section_title: NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.18 Option 4 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
text:
Section 2C.18 Option 4 - NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

The NARROW BRIDGE or NARROW UNDERPASS sign may be omitted on low-volume rural roads where there is adequate sight distance to the bridge, culvert, or underpass on both approaches.

metadata.section_title: NARROW BRIDGE and NARROW UNDERPASS Signs (W5-2 and W5-2a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.19 Guidance 1 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
text:
Section 2C.19 Guidance 1 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

A ONE LANE BRIDGE (W5-3) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used on two-way roadways in advance of any bridge or culvert: A. Having a roadway horizontal clearance of less than 16 feet, or B. Having a roadway horizontal clearance of less than 18 feet when commercial vehicles constitute a high proportion of the traffic, or C. Having a roadway horizontal clearance of 18 feet or less where the sight distance on the approach is less than that shown in Condition A of Table 2C-3.

metadata.section_title: ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.19 Guidance 2 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
text:
Section 2C.19 Guidance 2 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

Where these conditions exist for an underpass, a ONE LANE UNDERPASS (W5-3a) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used.

metadata.section_title: ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.19 Guidance 3 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
text:
Section 2C.19 Guidance 3 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

Additional emphasis should be provided by the use of object markers, delineators, and/or pavement markings.

metadata.section_title: ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.19 Option 4 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
text:
Section 2C.19 Option 4 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

The ONE LANE BRIDGE or ONE LANE UNDERPASS sign may be omitted on low-volume rural roads where there is adequate sight distance to the bridge, culvert, or underpass on both approaches.

metadata.section_title: ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.19 Option 5 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
text:
Section 2C.19 Option 5 - ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

STOP (R1-1) or YIELD (R1-2) signs (see Sections 2B.04 and 2B.05) and related pavement markings (see Sections 3B.21 and 3B.22) may be used when conditions A, B, or C in Paragraph 1 of this Section apply.

metadata.section_title: ONE LANE BRIDGE and ONE LANE UNDERPASS Signs (W5-3 and W5-3a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.20 Guidance 1 - Divided Highway Sign (W6-1)
text:
Section 2C.20 Guidance 1 - Divided Highway Sign (W6-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

A Divided Highway (W6-1) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used on the approaches to a section of highway (not an intersection or junction) where the opposing flows of traffic are separated by a median or other physical barrier.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.20 Standard 2 - Divided Highway Sign (W6-1)
text:
Section 2C.20 Standard 2 - Divided Highway Sign (W6-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

The Divided Highway (W6-1) sign shall not be used instead of a Keep Right (R4-7 series) sign on the approach end of a median island.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.21 Guidance 1 - Divided Highway Ends Sign (W6-2)
text:
Section 2C.21 Guidance 1 - Divided Highway Ends Sign (W6-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 170

A Divided Highway Ends (W6-2) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used in advance of the end of a section of physically divided highway (not an intersection or junction) as a warning of two-way traffic ahead.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.21 Guidance 2 - Divided Highway Ends Sign (W6-2)
text:
Section 2C.21 Guidance 2 - Divided Highway Ends Sign (W6-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

The Two-Way Traffic (W6-3) sign (see Section 2C.51) should be used to give warning and notice of the transition to a two-lane, two-way section.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.22 Option 1 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
text:
Section 2C.22 Option 1 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

A FREEWAY ENDS XX MILES (W19-1) sign or a FREEWAY ENDS (W19-3) sign (see Figure 2C-6) may be used in advance of the end of a freeway.

metadata.section_title: Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.22 Option 2 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
text:
Section 2C.22 Option 2 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

An EXPRESSWAY ENDS XX MILES (W19-2) sign or an EXPRESSWAY ENDS (W19-4) sign (see Figure 2C-6) may be used in advance of the end of an expressway.

metadata.section_title: Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.22 Option 3 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
text:
Section 2C.22 Option 3 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

The rectangular W19-1 and W19-2 signs may be post-mounted or may be mounted overhead for increased emphasis.

metadata.section_title: Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.22 Guidance 4 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
text:
Section 2C.22 Guidance 4 - Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

If the reason that the freeway is ending is that the next portion of the freeway is not yet constructed and as a result all traffic must use an exit ramp to leave the freeway, an ALL TRAFFIC MUST EXIT (W19-5) sign (see Figure 2C-6) should be used in addition to the Freeway Ends signs in advance of the downstream end of the freeway.

metadata.section_title: Freeway or Expressway Ends Signs (W19 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.23 Option 1 - Double Arrow Sign (W12-1)
text:
Section 2C.23 Option 1 - Double Arrow Sign (W12-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

The Double Arrow (W12-1) sign (see Figure 2C-6) may be used to advise road users that traffic is permitted to pass on either side of an island, obstruction, or gore in the roadway. Traffic separated by this sign may either rejoin or change directions.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.23 Guidance 2 - Double Arrow Sign (W12-1)
text:
Section 2C.23 Guidance 2 - Double Arrow Sign (W12-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

If used on an island, the Double Arrow sign should be mounted near the approach end.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.23 Guidance 3 - Double Arrow Sign (W12-1)
text:
Section 2C.23 Guidance 3 - Double Arrow Sign (W12-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

If used in front of a pier or obstruction, the Double Arrow sign should be mounted on the face of, or just in front of, the pier or obstruction. Where stripe markings are used on the pier or obstruction, they should be discontinued to leave a 3-inch space around the outside of the Double Arrow sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.24 Option 1 - DEAD END, NO OUTLET, and ROAD ENDS Signs (W14-1, W14-1a, W14-2, W14-2a, W8-26, and W8-26a)
text:
Section 2C.24 Option 1 - DEAD END, NO OUTLET, and ROAD ENDS Signs (W14-1, W14-1a, W14-2, W14-2a, W8-26, and W8-26a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 171

The DEAD END (W14-1) sign (see Figure 2C-6) may be used at the entrance to a single road or street that terminates without intersecting another street. The NO OUTLET (W14-2) sign (see Figure 2C-6) may be used at the entrance to a road or road network from which there is no other exit.

metadata.section_title: DEAD END, NO OUTLET, and ROAD ENDS Signs (W14-1, W14-1a, W14-2, W14-2a, W8-26, and W8-26a)

title: Section 2C.24 Option 2 - DEAD END, NO OUTLET, and ROAD ENDS Signs (W14-1, W14-1a, W14-2, W14-2a, W8-26, and W8-26a)

title: Section 2C.25 Standard 1 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Standard 1 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

The Low Clearance Advance (W12-2) sign (see Figure 2C-6) shall be used to warn road users of vertical clearances less than 14 feet 6 inches, or vertical clearances less than 12 inches above the statutory maximum vehicle height, whichever is greater.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Guidance 2 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Guidance 2 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

The actual clearance should be displayed on the Low Clearance (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b) sign to the nearest 1 inch not exceeding the actual clearance. However, in areas that experience changes in temperature causing frost action, a reduction, not exceeding 3 inches, should be used for this condition.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Guidance 3 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Guidance 3 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

Clearances should be evaluated periodically to determine if additional low clearance signing is necessary, particularly when resurfacing operations have occurred, on routes onto which over-height vehicles are normally directed under the permit process, and structures that are susceptible to catastrophic failure when struck by over- height vehicles.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Guidance 4 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Guidance 4 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

The W12-2 sign with a supplemental distance plaque should also be placed at the nearest intersecting road or wide point in the road at which a vehicle can detour or turn around.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Guidance 5 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Guidance 5 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

Where there is a need to warn of a low clearance on an intersecting road or off a freeway or expressway exit, a rectangular warning sign with an appropriate word legend should be used rather than a W12-2 sign.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Option 6 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Option 6 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

The Low Clearance Overhead (W12-2a or W12-2b) sign (see Figure 2C-6) may be installed on the structure to supplement the advance warning sign.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Option 7 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Option 7 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

In cases where physical conditions on a structure limit the width such that the W12-2a or W12-2b signs are physically unable to fit, a W12-2 sign may be installed overhead on the structure or post-mounted in front of the structure, in addition to the required W12-2 sign at the advance location.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Guidance 8 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Guidance 8 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

In the case of an arch, or other structure under which the clearance varies greatly, two or more Low Clearance Overhead (W12-2a or 12-2b) signs should be installed on the structure itself to give information as to the clearances over the low clearance portions of the roadway.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Standard 9 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Standard 9 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 172

If used, the Low Clearance Overhead (W12-2b) sign shall be placed over a lane or shoulder to indicate the portion of the structure with low clearance if the posted clearance does not apply to the entire structure.

metadata.section_title: Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.25 Guidance 10 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
text:
Section 2C.25 Guidance 10 - Low Clearance Signs (W12-2, W12-2a, and W12-2b)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

The clearance shown on the Low Clearance Advance sign should match the clearance on the W12-2a or W12-2b sign or, if there are multiple W12-2b signs, should match the lowest clearance. ROADWAY AND WEATHER-CONDITION WARNING SIGNS AND PLAQUES

Section 2C.26 Guidance 3 - BUMP and DIP Signs (W8-1 and W8-2)

metadata.section_title: BUMP and DIP Signs (W8-1 and W8-2)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.26 Guidance 4 - BUMP and DIP Signs (W8-1 and W8-2)
text:
Section 2C.26 Guidance 4 - BUMP and DIP Signs (W8-1 and W8-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

A short stretch of depressed alignment that might momentarily hide a vehicle should be treated as a no-passing zone when center line striping is provided on a two-lane or three-lane road (see Section 3B.03).

metadata.section_title: BUMP and DIP Signs (W8-1 and W8-2)

title: Section 2C.27 Guidance 1 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
text:
Section 2C.27 Guidance 1 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

The SPEED HUMP (W17-1) sign (see Figure 2C-7) should be used in advance of a vertical deflection in the roadway that is designed to limit the speed of traffic.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.27 Guidance 2 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
text:
Section 2C.27 Guidance 2 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

If used, the SPEED HUMP sign should be supplemented by an Advisory Speed plaque (see Figure 2C-1 and Section 2C.59).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.27 Option 3 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
text:
Section 2C.27 Option 3 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

If a series of speed humps exists in close proximity, an Advisory Speed plaque may be eliminated on all but the first SPEED HUMP sign in the series.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.27 Option 4 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
text:
Section 2C.27 Option 4 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

The legend SPEED BUMP may be used instead of the legend SPEED HUMP on the W17-1 sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.27 Support 5 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
text:
Section 2C.27 Support 5 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

Speed humps generally provide more gradual vertical deflection than speed bumps. Speed bumps limit the speed of traffic more severely than speed humps. Other forms of speed humps include speed tables and raised crosswalks or intersections. However, these differences in engineering terminology are not well known by the public, so for signing purposes these terms are interchangeable.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.27 Support 6 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
text:
Section 2C.27 Support 6 - SPEED HUMP Sign (W17-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 173

Sections 3B.29 and 3B.30 contain information about the use of markings at and in advance of speed humps.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.31 Support 1 - Warning Signs and Plaque for Motorcyclists (W8-15, W8-15aP, and W8-16)
text:
Section 2C.31 Support 1 - Warning Signs and Plaque for Motorcyclists (W8-15, W8-15aP, and W8-16)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 175

The signs and plaques described in this Section are intended to give motorcyclists advance notice of surface conditions that might adversely affect their ability to maintain control of their motorcycle under wet or dry conditions. The use of some of the advance surface condition warning signs described in Section 2C.30, such as Slippery When Wet, LOOSE GRAVEL, or ROUGH ROAD, can also be helpful to motorcyclists if those conditions exist.

If a portion of a street or highway features a roadway pavement surface that is grooved or textured instead of smooth, such as a grooved skid resistance treatment for a horizontal curve or a brick pavement surface, a GROOVED PAVEMENT (W8-15) sign (see Figure 2C-7) may be used to provide advance warning of this condition to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and other road users. Alternate legends such as TEXTURED PAVEMENT or BRICK PAVEMENT may also be used on the W8-15 sign.

Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 180

The TRAFFIC APPROACHING WHEN FLASHING (W2-11) sign (see Figure 2C-10) may be used on the side road stop-controlled approach to warn of traffic approaching on the uncontrolled through road.

metadata.section_title: Actuated Advance Intersection Signs (W2-10 and W2-11)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.42 Standard 4 - Actuated Advance Intersection Signs (W2-10 and W2-11)
text:
Section 2C.42 Standard 4 - Actuated Advance Intersection Signs (W2-10 and W2-11)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 180

When used, the TRAFFIC ENTERING WHEN FLASHING sign and the TRAFFIC APPROACHING WHEN FLASHING sign shall be supplemented with a Warning Beacon (see Section 4S.03) that activates when a vehicle on a conflicting approach is detected.

metadata.section_title: Actuated Advance Intersection Signs (W2-10 and W2-11)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.43 Standard 1 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
text:
Section 2C.43 Standard 1 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 180

The Two-Direction Large Arrow (W1-7) sign (see Figure 2C-10) shall be a horizontal rectangle.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.43 Standard 2 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
text:
Section 2C.43 Standard 2 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 180

If used, the Two-Direction Large Arrow sign shall be installed on the far side of a T-intersection in line with, and at approximately a right angle to, traffic approaching from the stem of the T-intersection.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.43 Standard 3 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
text:
Section 2C.43 Standard 3 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 181

The Two-Direction Large Arrow sign shall not be used where there is no change in the direction of travel such as at the beginnings and ends of medians or at center piers.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.43 Guidance 4 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
text:
Section 2C.43 Guidance 4 - Two-Direction Large Arrow Sign (W1-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 181

The Two-Direction Large Arrow sign should be visible for a sufficient distance to provide the road user with adequate time to react to the intersection configuration.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.44 Standard 1 - Traffic Signal Oncoming Extended Green Signs (W25-1 and W25-2)
text:
Section 2C.44 Standard 1 - Traffic Signal Oncoming Extended Green Signs (W25-1 and W25-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 182

At locations where either a W25-1 or a W25-2 sign is required based on the provisions in Section 4F.01, the W25-1 or W25-2 sign (see Figure 2C-10) shall be installed near the left-most signal face for the approach. MERGING, TWO-WAY TRAFFIC, AND NO PASSING WARNING SIGNS AND PLAQUES

metadata.section_title: Traffic Signal Oncoming Extended Green Signs (W25-1 and W25-2)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Option 1 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Option 1 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 182

A Merge (W4-1) sign (see Figure 2C-11) may be used to warn road users on the major roadway that merging movements might be encountered in advance of a point where lanes from two separate roadways converge as a single traffic lane and no turning conflict occurs.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Option 2 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Option 2 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 182

A Merge sign may also be installed on the side of the entering roadway to warn road users on the entering roadway of the merge condition.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Guidance 3 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Guidance 3 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

The Merge sign should be installed on the side of the major roadway where merging traffic will be encountered and in such a position as to not obstruct the road user’s view of entering traffic. Figure 2C-11. Merging and Passing Signs and Plaques

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Guidance 4 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Guidance 4 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

When a Merge sign is installed on a major roadway, the symbol should be oriented right or left as appropriate to depict the side from which the merge occurs, with the arrow representing the major roadway and the curved stem representing the entering roadway (see Figure 2C-11)

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Guidance 5 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Guidance 5 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

When a Merge sign is installed on an entering roadway that curves before merging with the major roadway, such as a ramp with a curving horizontal alignment as it approaches the major roadway, the Entering Roadway Merge (W4-5) sign (see Figure 2C-11) should be used to better portray the actual geometric conditions to road users on the entering roadway.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Guidance 6 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Guidance 6 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

Where two roadways of approximately equal importance converge and merging movements are required, a Merge sign should be placed on each roadway.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Guidance 7 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Guidance 7 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

The Merge sign should not be used where two roadways converge and merging movements are not required.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Standard 8 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Standard 8 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

The Merge sign shall not be used in place of a Lane Ends (W4-2) sign (see Section 2C.47) where lanes of traffic moving on a single roadway must merge because of a reduction in the actual or usable pavement width.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Option 9 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Option 9 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

An Entering Roadway Merge (W4-5) sign with a NO MERGE AREA (W4-5aP) supplemental plaque (see Figure 2C-11) mounted below it may be used to warn road users on an entering roadway that they will encounter an abrupt merging situation without an acceleration lane at the downstream end of the ramp.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Option 10 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Option 10 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

A Merge (W4-1) sign with a NO MERGE AREA (W4-5aP) supplemental plaque mounted below it may be used to warn road users on the major roadway that traffic on an entering roadway will encounter an abrupt merging situation without an acceleration lane at the downstream end of the ramp.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Option 11 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Option 11 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

For a yield-controlled channelized right-turn movement onto a roadway without an acceleration lane, a NO MERGE AREA (W4-5aP) supplemental plaque may be mounted below a Yield Ahead (W3-2) sign and/or below a YIELD (R1-2) sign when engineering judgment indicates that road users would expect an acceleration lane to be present.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.45 Support 12 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
text:
Section 2C.45 Support 12 - Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

Examples of the use of Merge (W4-1) signs are shown in Drawing A in Figure 2C-12.

metadata.section_title: Merge Signs and Plaque (W4-1, W4-5, and W4-5aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.46 Guidance 1 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
text:
Section 2C.46 Guidance 1 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

The Added Lane (W4-3) sign (see Figure 2C-11) should be installed in advance of a point where two roadways converge and merging movements are not required. When possible, the Added Lane sign should be placed such that it is visible from both roadways; if this is not possible, an Added Lane sign should be placed on the side of each roadway.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.46 Guidance 2 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
text:
Section 2C.46 Guidance 2 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

When an Added Lane (W4-3) sign is installed on a major roadway, the symbol should be oriented right or left as appropriate to depict the side from which the entering roadway converges, with the straight arrow representing the major roadway and the curved arrow representing the entering roadway. The sign should be located on the side of the major roadway from which the entering roadway converges.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.46 Guidance 3 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
text:
Section 2C.46 Guidance 3 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

When an Added Lane sign is to be installed on a roadway that curves before converging with another roadway that has a tangent alignment at the point of convergence, the Entering Roadway Added Lane (W4-6) sign (see Figure 2C-11) should be used to better portray the actual geometric conditions to road users on the curving roadway.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.46 Support 4 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
text:
Section 2C.46 Support 4 - Added Lane Signs (W4-3 and W4-6)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

Examples of the use of Added Lane (W4-3) and Entering Roadway Added Lane (W4-6) signs are shown in Drawing B in Figure 2C-12.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Support 1 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Support 1 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

The Lane Ends (W4-2) and RIGHT (LEFT) LANE ENDS (W9-1) signs (see Figure 2C-11) are used to warn of the reduction in the number of traffic lanes in the direction of travel.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Support 2 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Support 2 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 183

The sequence of the W4-2 and W9-1 signs is illustrated in Figure 2C-13.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Guidance 3 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Guidance 3 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 186

The Lane Ends (W4-2) sign should be installed at the advance placement distance in accordance with Table 2C-3. Figure 2C-12. Examples of Merge and Added Lane Sign Placement for Entering and Converging Roadways A - Example for converging and entering roadways B - Examples for an added lane MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2C-13. Example Sequences for Lane Ends and Lane Merge Signs (Sheet 1 of 5) A - Freeway or expressway - lane ends Note: See Section 3B.12 for lane-reduction pavement markings Rev. 1 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2C-13. Example Sequences for Lane Ends and Lane Merge Signs (Sheet 2 of 5) B - Right lane on conventional road - lane ends Note: See Section 3B.12 for lane-reduction pavement markings Rev. 1

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Option 4 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Option 4 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 186

A RIGHT (LEFT) LANE ENDS (W9-1) sign may be installed in advance of the Lane Ends sign to provide additional warning that a lane is ending and that a merging maneuver will be required.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Guidance 5 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Guidance 5 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 186

If a W9-1 sign is installed, a Distance (W16-2P series or W16-3P series) plaque (see Figure 2C-16) should be installed below the W9-1 sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Guidance 6 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Guidance 6 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 186

On one-way streets or on divided highways where the left-hand lane is ending and the width of the median will permit, the W9-1 and W4-2 signs should be placed facing approaching traffic on the left-hand side or median.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Option 7 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Option 7 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 186

Where a lane ends a distance beyond the intersection that is less than the advance placement distance indicated in Table 2C-3, the W4-2 sign may be located at the far side of the intersection (see Sheet 4 of Figure 2C-13).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.47 Guidance 8 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
text:
Section 2C.47 Guidance 8 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 186

When the W4-2 sign is located at the far side of the intersection in accordance with Paragraph 7 of this Section, the W9-1 sign should be placed upstream of the intersection with the appropriate distance plaque.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.48 Support 1 - Lanes Merge Signs (W9-4 and W4-8)
text:
Section 2C.48 Support 1 - Lanes Merge Signs (W9-4 and W4-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 187

The LANES MERGE (W9-4) and Single-Lane Transition (W4-8) signs (see Figure 2C-11) are used to warn of a merge of two lanes to one in the same direction of travel with a merging maneuver required for each lane (see Sheet 5 of Figure 2C-13). This type of merge is for a geometric condition where both approach lanes merge into a single lane, not where one lane merges into the other. Section 6H.08 contains information about the use of the late merge sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.48 Guidance 2 - Lanes Merge Signs (W9-4 and W4-8)
text:
Section 2C.48 Guidance 2 - Lanes Merge Signs (W9-4 and W4-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 187

The Single-Lane Transition (W4-8) sign should be located at the advance placement distance in accordance with Table 2C-3.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.48 Option 3 - Lanes Merge Signs (W9-4 and W4-8)
text:
Section 2C.48 Option 3 - Lanes Merge Signs (W9-4 and W4-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 188

The Lanes Merge (W9-4) sign may be used in advance of the W4-8 sign to provide additional warning that both lanes form a single lane and that a merging maneuver is needed for the traffic in each lane. December 2025 Figure 2C-13. Example Sequences for Lane Ends and Lane Merge Signs (Sheet 4 of 5) E - Lane ends beyond major intersection or side road Note: See Section 3B.12 for lane-reduction pavement markings

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.49 Option 1 - HEAVY MERGE FROM LEFT (RIGHT) Sign (W4-7)
text:
Section 2C.49 Option 1 - HEAVY MERGE FROM LEFT (RIGHT) Sign (W4-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 188

The HEAVY MERGE FROM LEFT (RIGHT) (W4-7) sign (see Figure 2C-11) may be used to supplement a W4-1 sign at multilane approaches to congested areas to inform road users that it is desirable for through traffic to move out of a lane that will be occupied by a high volume of entering traffic. If used, the W4-7 sign may be supplemented with a W16-2P series or W16-3P series plaque (see Section 2C.61).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.49 Standard 2 - HEAVY MERGE FROM LEFT (RIGHT) Sign (W4-7)
text:
Section 2C.49 Standard 2 - HEAVY MERGE FROM LEFT (RIGHT) Sign (W4-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 188

If used, the W4-7 sign shall be installed at a location upstream from the location of the W4-1 sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.50 Option 1 - RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
text:
Section 2C.50 Option 1 - RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 188

The RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY (W9-7) sign (see Figure 2C-11) may be used to provide advance warning to road users that traffic in the right-hand (left-hand) lane of a roadway will be required to depart the roadway at the next exit.

metadata.section_title: RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.50 Guidance 2 - RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
text:
Section 2C.50 Guidance 2 - RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 188

If used, the W9-7 sign should be installed upstream from the first overhead guide sign that contains an EXIT ONLY sign panel or upstream from the first RIGHT (LEFT) LANE MUST EXIT (R3-33) regulatory sign, if used, whichever is farther upstream from the exit.

metadata.section_title: RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.50 Option 3 - RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
text:
Section 2C.50 Option 3 - RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 189

A legend or plaque displaying the distance may be added to the W9-7 sign where the distance along the dropped lane between the sign and the exit ramp is greater than 1 mile. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2C-13.
