See Section 3B.12 for lane-reduction pavement markings 2. See Section 2C.48 for information about this type of merge

metadata.section_title: RIGHT (LEFT) LANE FOR EXIT ONLY Sign (W9-7)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.51 Guidance 1 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
text:
Section 2C.51 Guidance 1 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 189

A Two-Way Traffic (W6-3) sign (see Figure 2C-11) should be used to warn road users of a transition from a multi-lane divided section of roadway to a two-lane, two-way section of roadway.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.51 Guidance 2 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
text:
Section 2C.51 Guidance 2 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 189

A Two-Way Traffic (W6-3) sign with an AHEAD (W16-9P) plaque (see Figure 2C-16) should be used to warn road users of a transition from a one-way street to a two-lane, two-way section of roadway (see Figure 2B-18).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.51 Option 3 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
text:
Section 2C.51 Option 3 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 190

The Two-Way Traffic sign may be used at intervals along a two-lane, two-way roadway and may be used to supplement the Divided Highway (Road) Ends (W6-2) sign discussed in Section 2C.21. December 2025

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.52 Option 1 - Two-Way Traffic on a Three-Lane Roadway Signs (W6-5 and W6-5a)
text:
Section 2C.52 Option 1 - Two-Way Traffic on a Three-Lane Roadway Signs (W6-5 and W6-5a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 190

The Two-Way Traffic on a Three-Lane Roadway (W6-5 and W6-5a) signs (see Figure 2C-11) may be installed along three-lane roadways with two lanes in one direction and one in the opposing direction.

metadata.section_title: Two-Way Traffic on a Three-Lane Roadway Signs (W6-5 and W6-5a)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.53 Standard 1 - NO PASSING ZONE Sign (W14-3)
text:
Section 2C.53 Standard 1 - NO PASSING ZONE Sign (W14-3)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 191

The NO PASSING ZONE (W14-3) sign (see Figure 2C-11) shall be a pennant-shaped isosceles triangle with its longer axis horizontal and pointing to the right. When used, the NO PASSING ZONE sign shall be installed on the left-hand side of the roadway at the beginning of no-passing zones identified by pavement markings or DO NOT PASS signs or both (see Sections 2B.36 and 3B.03). The TRAIL CROSSING (W11-15a) sign may be used to warn of shared-use path crossings where pedestrians, bicyclists, and other user groups might be crossing the roadway.

If a W11-2 sign has been post-mounted at the crosswalk location where a Yield Here To (Stop Here For) Pedestrians sign is used on the approach, the Yield Here To (Stop Here For) Pedestrians sign shall not be placed on the same post as the W11-2 sign.

text:
Section 2C.55 Option 10 - Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

An advance Pedestrian Crossing (W11-2) sign with an AHEAD or a distance supplemental plaque may be used in conjunction with a Yield Here To (Stop Here For) Pedestrians sign on the approach to the same crosswalk.

Section 2C.55 Option 11 - Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)

The crossing location identified by a W11-2, W11-6, W11-7, or W11-9 sign may be defined with crosswalk markings (see Chapter 3C).

Section 2C.55 Option 12 - Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

The W11-2 and W11-9 signs and their related supplemental plaques may have a fluorescent yellow-green background with a black legend and border.

text:
Section 2C.55 Guidance 13 - Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 193

When a fluorescent yellow-green background is used, a systematic approach featuring one background color within a zone or area should be used. The mixing of standard yellow and fluorescent yellow-green backgrounds within a selected site area should be avoided.

metadata.section_title: Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

text:
Section 2C.55 Option 14 - Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

A Warning Beacon (see Section 4S.03) may be used with any Non-Vehicular Warning sign to indicate specific periods when the condition or activity is present or is likely to be present, or to provide enhanced sign conspicuity.

text:
Section 2C.55 Option 15 - Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 194

A supplemental WHEN FLASHING (W16-13P) plaque (see Figure 2C-16) may be used with any Non- Vehicular Warning sign that is supplemented with a Warning Beacon to indicate specific periods when the condition or activity is present or is likely to be present.

metadata.section_title: Non-Vehicular Warning Signs (W11-2, W11-3, W11-4, W11-6, W11-7, W11-9, and W11-16 through W11-22)

title: Section 2C.56 Option 1 - Playground Sign (W15-1)
text:
Section 2C.56 Option 1 - Playground Sign (W15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 194

The Playground (W15-1) sign (see Figure 2C-15) may be used to give advance warning of a designated children’s playground that is located adjacent to the road.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.56 Option 2 - Playground Sign (W15-1)
text:
Section 2C.56 Option 2 - Playground Sign (W15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 194

The Playground sign may have a fluorescent yellow-green background with a black legend and border.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.56 Guidance 3 - Playground Sign (W15-1)
text:
Section 2C.56 Guidance 3 - Playground Sign (W15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 195

If the access to the playground area requires a roadway crossing, the application of crosswalk pavement markings (see Chapter 3C) and a Non-Vehicular Warning sign (see Section 2C.55) should be considered. SUPPLEMENTAL WARNING PLAQUES

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.57 Option 1 - Use of Supplemental Warning Plaques
text:
Section 2C.57 Option 1 - Use of Supplemental Warning Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 195

A supplemental warning plaque (see Figure 2C-16) may be displayed with a warning or regulatory sign when engineering judgment indicates that road users require additional warning information beyond that contained in the main message of the warning or regulatory sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.57 Standard 2 - Use of Supplemental Warning Plaques
text:
Section 2C.57 Standard 2 - Use of Supplemental Warning Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 195

Supplemental warning plaques shall be used only in combination with and installed on the same post(s) as warning or regulatory signs. They shall not be mounted alone or displayed alone.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.57 Standard 3 - Use of Supplemental Warning Plaques
text:
Section 2C.57 Standard 3 - Use of Supplemental Warning Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 195

Unless otherwise provided in this Manual for a particular plaque, supplemental warning plaques shall be mounted below the sign they supplement.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.58 Standard 1 - Design of Supplemental Warning Plaques
text:
Section 2C.58 Standard 1 - Design of Supplemental Warning Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 195

A supplemental warning plaque used with a warning sign shall have the same legend, border, and background color as the warning sign with which it is displayed. A supplemental warning plaque used with a regulatory sign shall have a black legend and border on a yellow background.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.58 Standard 2 - Design of Supplemental Warning Plaques
text:
Section 2C.58 Standard 2 - Design of Supplemental Warning Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

Supplemental warning plaques shall be square or rectangular. Figure 2C-16. Supplemental Warning Plaques Note: The background color (yellow or fluorescent yellow-green) shall match the color of the warning sign that it supplements. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Option 1 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Option 1 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The Advisory Speed (W13-1P) plaque (see Figure 2C-1) may be used to supplement an advance warning sign to indicate the advisory speed for a condition.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Option 2 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Option 2 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The Confirmation Advisory Speed (W13-1aP) plaque (see Figure 2C-1) may be used to supplement a One- Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign on the outside of a turn or curve in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Standard 3 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Standard 3 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The use of the Advisory Speed and Confirmation Advisory Speed plaques for horizontal curves shall be in accordance with Section 2C.06 and Table 2C-6. The speed differential in Table 2C-6 shall be the difference between the advisory speed for the horizontal curve and the posted speed limit, statutory speed limit, or the 85th percentile speed on the approach to the curve. The Advisory Speed plaque shall also be used where an engineering study indicates a need to advise road users of the advisory speed for other roadway conditions. Table 2C-6. Use of Advisory Speed Plaque for Horizontal Alignment Changes Speed Differential Use of Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)1 5 mph Optional 10 mph Recommended 15 mph or more Required 1 See Section 2C.59

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Standard 4 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Standard 4 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The speed displayed on the Advisory Speed and Confirmation Advisory Speed plaques shall be a multiple of 5 mph.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Standard 5 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Standard 5 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

Except in emergencies or when the condition is temporary, an Advisory Speed or Confirmation Advisory Speed plaque shall not be installed until the advisory speed has been determined by an engineering study.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Standard 6 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Standard 6 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The Advisory Speed plaque shall only be used to supplement an advance warning sign. The Advisory Speed plaque or the Confirmation Advisory Speed plaque shall not be installed as a separate sign installation.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Guidance 7 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Guidance 7 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The Advisory Speed plaque, if used with a sign that is also supplemented with another plaque, such as an Advance Street Name plaque (see Section 2C.65), should be mounted immediately below the primary warning sign with any other plaque mounted below the Advisory Speed plaque.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Standard 8 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Standard 8 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The Confirmation Advisory Speed plaque shall only be used to supplement a One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign (see Section 2C.10) or an Exit Gore (E5-1 series) (see Section 2E.26) sign and shall not be installed as a separate sign installation.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Standard 9 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Standard 9 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The advisory speed shall be determined by an engineering study that follows established engineering practices.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Guidance 10 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Guidance 10 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The advisory speed should be determined based on free-flowing traffic conditions.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Guidance 11 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Guidance 11 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

Because changes in conditions, such as roadway geometrics, surface characteristics, or sight distance, might affect the advisory speed, each location should be evaluated periodically or when conditions change.

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Support 12 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Support 12 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 196

The 2nd Edition of the “Traffic Control Devices Handbook,” 2013, Institute of Transportation Engineers contains engineering practices for the determination of the recommended advisory speed for a horizontal curve including following: Rev. 1 A. Compass method B. Safety-based method C. Accelerometer method D. Design equation method E. Ball-bank method using the following criteria: 1. 16 degrees of ball-bank for speeds of 20 mph or less 2. 14 degrees of ball-bank for speeds of 25 to 30 mph 3. 12 degrees of ball-bank for speeds of 35 mph and higher

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.59 Support 13 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.59 Support 13 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

The 16, 14, and 12 degrees of ball-bank criteria are comparable to the current AASHTO horizontal curve design guidance. Research has shown that drivers often exceed existing posted advisory curve speeds by 7 to 10 mph. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P) and Confirmation Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.60 Option 1 - NEW Plaque (W16-15P)
text:
Section 2C.60 Option 1 - NEW Plaque (W16-15P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

A NEW (W16-15P) plaque (see Figure 2C-16) may be mounted above a regulatory sign when a new regulation takes effect in order to alert road users to the new traffic regulation. A NEW plaque may also be mounted above an advance warning sign (such as a Signal Ahead sign for a newly-installed traffic control signal) for a warning of a new traffic condition.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.60 Guidance 2 - NEW Plaque (W16-15P)
text:
Section 2C.60 Guidance 2 - NEW Plaque (W16-15P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

The NEW plaque should be removed no later than 12 months after it was installed. Rev. 1

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.61 Option 1 - Distance Plaques (W16-2 Series, W16-3 Series, W16-4P, and W7-3aP)
text:
Section 2C.61 Option 1 - Distance Plaques (W16-2 Series, W16-3 Series, W16-4P, and W7-3aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

The Distance Ahead (W16-2 series and W16-3 series) plaques (see Figure 2C-16) may be used to inform the road user of the distance to the condition indicated by the warning sign.

metadata.section_title: Distance Plaques (W16-2 Series, W16-3 Series, W16-4P, and W7-3aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.61 Option 2 - Distance Plaques (W16-2 Series, W16-3 Series, W16-4P, and W7-3aP)
text:
Section 2C.61 Option 2 - Distance Plaques (W16-2 Series, W16-3 Series, W16-4P, and W7-3aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

The Next Distance (W7-3aP and W16-4P) plaques (see Figures 2C-5 and 2C-16) may be used to inform road users of the length of roadway over which the condition indicated by the warning sign exists.

metadata.section_title: Distance Plaques (W16-2 Series, W16-3 Series, W16-4P, and W7-3aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.62 Guidance 1 - Supplemental Arrow Plaques (W16-5P and W16-6P)
text:
Section 2C.62 Guidance 1 - Supplemental Arrow Plaques (W16-5P and W16-6P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

If the condition indicated by a warning sign is located on an intersecting road and the distance between the intersection and condition is not sufficient to provide adequate advance placement of the warning sign, a Supplemental Arrow (W16-5P or W16-6P) plaque (see Figure 2C-16) should be used below the warning sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.62 Standard 2 - Supplemental Arrow Plaques (W16-5P and W16-6P)
text:
Section 2C.62 Standard 2 - Supplemental Arrow Plaques (W16-5P and W16-6P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

Supplemental Arrow plaques shall have the same legend design as the Advance Turn Arrow and Directional Arrow auxiliary signs (see Sections 2D.26 and 2D.28) except that they shall have a black legend and border on a yellow or fluorescent yellow-green background, as appropriate.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.63 Support 1 - Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
text:
Section 2C.63 Support 1 - Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

Diagonal downward-pointing arrow (W16-7P and W16-7aP) plaques (see Figure 2C-16) are used with certain Vehicular Traffic Warning signs (see Section 2C.54) and certain Non-Vehicular Warning signs (see Section 2C.55), and School Crossing signs (see Section 7B.03) to indicate the specific location of a crossing point.

metadata.section_title: Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.63 Support 2 - Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
text:
Section 2C.63 Support 2 - Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

The W16-7P plaque contains a single arrow pointing diagonally down to the right or left, toward the roadway, depending on which side of the roadway it is located.

metadata.section_title: Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.63 Option 3 - Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
text:
Section 2C.63 Option 3 - Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

A W16-7aP plaque may be used with a single crossing sign located on a narrow median separating two roadways with traffic in the same direction where the crossing traverses both roadways.

metadata.section_title: Diagonal Downward-Pointing Arrow Plaques (W16-7P and W16-7aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.64 Guidance 1 - Hill-Related Plaques (W7-2 Series and W7-3 Series)
text:
Section 2C.64 Guidance 1 - Hill-Related Plaques (W7-2 Series and W7-3 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

Hill-Related (W7-2 series and W7-3 series) plaques (see Figure 2C-5) or other appropriate legends and larger signs should be used for emphasis or where special hill characteristics exist.

metadata.section_title: Hill-Related Plaques (W7-2 Series and W7-3 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.64 Guidance 2 - Hill-Related Plaques (W7-2 Series and W7-3 Series)
text:
Section 2C.64 Guidance 2 - Hill-Related Plaques (W7-2 Series and W7-3 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

On longer grades, the use of a distance (W7-3aP or W7-3bP) plaque (see Figure 2C-5) at periodic intervals of approximately 1-mile spacing should be considered.

metadata.section_title: Hill-Related Plaques (W7-2 Series and W7-3 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.65 Option 1 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
text:
Section 2C.65 Option 1 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

An Advance Street Name (W16-8P or W16-8aP) plaque (see Figure 2C-16) may be used with any Intersection (W1-10 series, W2 series, W10-2, W10-3, or W10-4) or Advance Traffic Control (W3 series) sign to identify the name of the intersecting street.

metadata.section_title: Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.65 Standard 2 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
text:
Section 2C.65 Standard 2 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 197

The lettering on Advance Street Name plaques shall be composed of a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters.

metadata.section_title: Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.65 Standard 3 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
text:
Section 2C.65 Standard 3 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

If two street names are used on the Advance Street Name plaque, a directional arrow pointing in the direction of the street shall be placed next to each street name. Arrows pointing to the left shall be placed to the left of the street name, and arrows pointing to the right shall be placed to the right of the street name. December 2025

metadata.section_title: Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.65 Guidance 4 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
text:
Section 2C.65 Guidance 4 - Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

If two street names are used on the Advance Street Name plaque, the street names and associated arrows should be displayed in the following order: A. For a single intersection, the name of the street to the left should be displayed above the name of the street to the right; or B. For two sequential intersections, such as where the plaque is used with an Offset Side Roads (W2-7) or a Double Side Road (W2-8) sign, the name of the first street encountered should be displayed above the name of the second street encountered, and the arrow associated with the second street encountered should be an advance arrow, such as the arrow shown on the W16-6P arrow plaque (see Figure 2C-16).

metadata.section_title: Advance Street Name Plaques (W16-8P and W16-8aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.66 Option 1 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
text:
Section 2C.66 Option 1 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

The CROSS TRAFFIC DOES NOT STOP (W4-4P) plaque (see Figure 2C-10) may be used in combination with a STOP sign when engineering judgment indicates that conditions are present that are causing or could cause road users to misinterpret the intersection as an all-way stop.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.66 Option 2 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
text:
Section 2C.66 Option 2 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

The TRAFFIC FROM LEFT (RIGHT) DOES NOT STOP (W4-4aP) or ONCOMING TRAFFIC DOES NOT STOP (W4-4bP) plaque may be used when such messages more accurately describe the traffic controls established at the intersection.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.66 Guidance 3 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
text:
Section 2C.66 Guidance 3 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

The W4-4aP and W4-4bP plaques should be used at intersections where STOP signs control all but one approach to the intersection, unless the only non-stopped approach is from a one-way street.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.66 Standard 4 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
text:
Section 2C.66 Standard 4 - Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

If a W4-4P series plaque is used, it shall be mounted below the STOP sign.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Does Not Stop Plaques (W4-4P Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.67 Option 1 - IN ROAD and IN STREET Plaques (W16-1P and W16-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.67 Option 1 - IN ROAD and IN STREET Plaques (W16-1P and W16-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

In situations where there is a need to warn drivers to watch for other slower forms of transportation traveling along the highway, such as bicycles, pedestrians, golf carts, horse-drawn vehicles, or farm machinery, an IN ROAD (W16-1P) plaque or IN STREET (W16-1aP) plaque (see Figure 2C-16) may be used.

metadata.section_title: IN ROAD and IN STREET Plaques (W16-1P and W16-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.67 Standard 2 - IN ROAD and IN STREET Plaques (W16-1P and W16-1aP)
text:
Section 2C.67 Standard 2 - IN ROAD and IN STREET Plaques (W16-1P and W16-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

The background color of the W16-1P or W16-1aP plaque shall match the background color of the warning sign with which it is displayed. If a W16-1P or W16-1aP plaque is used, it shall be mounted below either a Vehicular Traffic Warning sign (see Section 2C.54) or a Non-Vehicular Warning sign (see Section 2C.55), and shall not be mounted alone.

metadata.section_title: IN ROAD and IN STREET Plaques (W16-1P and W16-1aP)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.68 Option 1 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Plaque (W16-20P)
text:
Section 2C.68 Option 1 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Plaque (W16-20P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

Where it is desired to notify bicyclists that the conditions depicted by a warning sign are not applicable to bicycles, the EXCEPT BICYCLES (W16-20P) supplemental warning plaque (see Figure 2C-16) may be mounted below the warning sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.68 Support 2 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Plaque (W16-20P)
text:
Section 2C.68 Support 2 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Plaque (W16-20P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 198

Examples of warning signs with which an EXCEPT BICYCLES (W16-20P) plaque can be mounted include DEAD END (W14-1) or NO OUTLET (W14-2) signs.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.69 Option 1 - Photo Enforced Plaques (W16-10P and W16-10aP)
text:
Section 2C.69 Option 1 - Photo Enforced Plaques (W16-10P and W16-10aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 199

A Photo Enforced (W16-10P) plaque or a PHOTO ENFORCED (W16-10aP) word message plaque (see Figure 2C-16) may be mounted below a warning sign to advise road users that the regulations associated with the condition being warned about (such as a traffic control signal or a toll plaza) are being enforced by photographic equipment. OBJECT MARKERS

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.70 Support 1 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
text:
Section 2C.70 Support 1 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 199

Types 1, 2, and 3 object markers are used to mark obstructions within or adjacent to the roadway. Type 4 object markers are used to mark the end of a roadway.

metadata.section_title: Object Marker Design and Placement Height
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.70 Standard 2 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
text:
Section 2C.70 Standard 2 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 199

When used, object markers (see Figure 2C-17) shall not have a border and shall consist of an arrangement of one or more of the following types: Type 1 Object Markers (obstructions within the roadway) Type 1-a diamond-shaped sign, at least 18 inches on a side, consisting of either a yellow (OM1-1) or black (OM1-2) sign with nine yellow retroreflective devices, each with a minimum diameter of 3 inches, mounted symmetrically on the sign, or an all-yellow retroreflective sign (OM1-3). Type 2-either a marker (OM2-1V or OM2- 1H) consisting of three yellow retroreflective devices, each with a minimum diameter of 3 inches, arranged either horizontally or vertically on a white sign measuring at least 6 x 12 inches; or an all-yellow horizontal or vertical retroreflective sign (OM2-2V or OM2-2H), measuring at least 6 x 12 inches. Type 2 Object Markers (obstructions adjacent to the roadway) Type 3-a striped marker, 12 x 36 inches, consisting of a vertical rectangle with alternating black and retroreflective yellow stripes sloping downward at an angle of 45 degrees toward the side of the obstruction on which traffic is to pass. The minimum width of the yellow and black stripes shall be 3 inches. Type 3 Object Markers (obstructions adjacent to or within the roadway) Type 4-a diamond-shaped sign, at least 18 inches on a side, consisting of either a red (OM4-1) or black (OM4-2) sign with nine red retroreflective devices, each with a minimum diameter of 3 inches, mounted symmetrically on the sign, or an all-red retroreflective sign (OM4-3).

metadata.section_title: Object Marker Design and Placement Height
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.70 Support 3 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
text:
Section 2C.70 Support 3 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 199

Type 3 object markers with stripes that begin at the upper right side and slope downward to the lower left side are designated as right object markers (OM3-R). Object markers with stripes that begin at the upper left side and slope downward to the lower right side are designated as left object markers (OM3-L). Object markers with chevron stripes that slope downward to both the lower left and lower right sides are designated as center object markers (OM3-C).

metadata.section_title: Object Marker Design and Placement Height
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.70 Guidance 4 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
text:
Section 2C.70 Guidance 4 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 199

When used for marking obstructions within the roadway or obstructions that are 8 feet or less from the shoulder or curb, the minimum mounting height, measured from the bottom of the object marker to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way, should be 4 feet.

metadata.section_title: Object Marker Design and Placement Height
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.70 Guidance 5 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
text:
Section 2C.70 Guidance 5 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 199

When used to mark obstructions more than 8 feet from the shoulder or curb, the clearance from the ground to the bottom of the object marker should be at least 4 feet.

metadata.section_title: Object Marker Design and Placement Height
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.70 Guidance 6 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
text:
Section 2C.70 Guidance 6 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

Object markers should not present a vertical or horizontal clearance obstacle for pedestrians. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Object Marker Design and Placement Height
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.70 Option 7 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
text:
Section 2C.70 Option 7 - Object Marker Design and Placement Height
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

When object markers or markings are applied to an obstruction that by its nature requires a lower or higher mounting, the vertical mounting height may vary according to need.

metadata.section_title: Object Marker Design and Placement Height
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.71 Standard 1 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.71 Standard 1 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

Obstructions within the roadway shall be marked with a Type 1 or Type 3 object marker. In addition to markers on the face of the obstruction, warning of approach to the obstruction shall be given by appropriate pavement markings (see Section 3B.13).

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.71 Option 2 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.71 Option 2 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

To provide additional emphasis, a Type 1 or Type 3 object marker may be installed at or near the approach end of a median island.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.71 Option 3 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.71 Option 3 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

To provide additional emphasis, large surfaces such as bridge piers may be painted with diagonal stripes, 12 inches or greater in width, similar in design to the Type 3 object marker.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.71 Standard 4 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.71 Standard 4 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

The alternating black and retroreflective yellow stripes (OM3-L, OM3-R) shall be sloped down at an angle of 45 degrees toward the side on which traffic is to pass the obstruction. If traffic can pass to either side of the obstruction, the alternating black and retroreflective yellow stripes (OM3-C) shall form chevrons that point upwards.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.71 Option 5 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.71 Option 5 - Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

Appropriate signs (see Sections 2B.39 and 2C.23) directing traffic to one or both sides of the obstruction may be used instead of the object marker. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions within the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.72 Support 1 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.72 Support 1 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

Obstructions not actually within the roadway are sometimes so close to the edge of the road that they need a marker. These include underpass piers, bridge abutments, handrails, ends of traffic barriers, utility poles, and culvert headwalls. In other cases there might not be a physical object involved, but other roadside conditions exist, such as narrow shoulders, drop-offs, gores, small islands, and abrupt changes in the roadway alignment, that might make it undesirable for a road user to leave the roadway, and therefore would create a need for a marker.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.72 Option 2 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.72 Option 2 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

Type 2 or Type 3 object markers may be used to mark an obstruction adjacent to the roadway.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.72 Guidance 3 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.72 Guidance 3 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

If a Type 2 or Type 3 object marker is used to mark an obstruction adjacent to the roadway, the edge of the object marker that is closest to the road user should be installed in line with the closest edge of the obstruction.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.72 Guidance 4 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.72 Guidance 4 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

When a marker is applied to the approach ends of guardrail or crash cushion terminals it should have the appearance of a Type 3 object marker and should be directly affixed, without a substrate, to the approach end of the guardrail or crash cushion and generally conform to the size and shape of the approach end of the guardrail or crash cushion.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.72 Standard 5 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.72 Standard 5 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

Type 1 and Type 4 object markers shall not be used to mark obstructions adjacent to the roadway.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.72 Guidance 6 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
text:
Section 2C.72 Guidance 6 - Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

Standard warning signs in this Chapter should also be used where applicable.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Obstructions Adjacent to the Roadway
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.73 Support 1 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
text:
Section 2C.73 Support 1 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

The Type 4 object marker is used to warn and alert road users of the end of a roadway in other than construction or maintenance areas.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.73 Standard 2 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
text:
Section 2C.73 Standard 2 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 200

If an object marker is used to mark the end of a roadway, a Type 4 object marker shall be used.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.73 Option 3 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
text:
Section 2C.73 Option 3 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 201

The Type 4 object marker may be used in instances where there are no alternate vehicular paths. December 2025

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.73 Option 4 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
text:
Section 2C.73 Option 4 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 201

Where conditions warrant, more than one marker, or a larger marker with or without a Type 3 Barricade (see Section 2B.75), may be used at the end of the roadway.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.73 Standard 5 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
text:
Section 2C.73 Standard 5 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 201

The minimum mounting height, measured vertically from the bottom of a Type 4 object marker to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way, shall be 4 feet.

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2C.73 Guidance 6 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
text:
Section 2C.73 Guidance 6 - Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 203

Appropriate advance warning signs in this Chapter should be used. (This page intentionally left blank)

metadata.section_title: Object Markers for Ends of Roadways
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 2D.01 Standard 1 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Standard 1 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to any road or street other than expressways and freeways, except as otherwise provided in this Manual.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Support 2 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Support 2 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Guide signs direct road users along streets and highways; inform them of intersecting routes; direct them to cities, towns, villages, or other important destinations; identify nearby rivers and streams, parks, forests, and historical sites; and provide information that will help them along their way in the most simple and direct manner possible.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Guidance 3 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Guidance 3 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

The selection of primary or control destinations (those displayed consistently over longer distances along a route) displayed on guide signs should be meaningful to road users in navigation and orientation. The destinations selected should be identifiable on official maps.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Guidance 4 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Guidance 4 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

The familiarity of the road users with the road should be considered in determining the need for guide signs on low-volume roads.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Support 5 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Support 5 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Low-volume roads generally do not require guide signs to the extent that they are needed on higher classes of roads. Because guide signs are typically only beneficial as a navigational aid for road users who are unfamiliar with a low-volume road, guide signs might not be needed on low-volume roads that serve only local traffic.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Support 6 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Support 6 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Guide signs, other than Street Name signs, generally are not used on low-volume rural roads except as needed to guide road users back to the major roadways.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Guidance 7 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Guidance 7 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

If used on low-volume roads, destination names should be as specific and descriptive as possible. Destinations such as campgrounds, ranger stations, recreational areas, and the like should be clearly indicated so that they are not interpreted to be communities or locations with road user services.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Option 8 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Option 8 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Guide signs may be used on low-volume roads at intersections to provide information for road users returning to a higher class of roads.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.01 Support 9 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
text:
Section 2D.01 Support 9 - Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Chapter 2A addresses placement, location, and other general criteria for signs.

metadata.section_title: Scope of Conventional Road Guide Sign Standards and Application

title: Section 2D.02 Support 1 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
text:
Section 2D.02 Support 1 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Requirements for illumination, retroreflection, and color are stated under the specific headings for individual guide signs or groups of signs. General provisions are given in 2A.06, 2A.21, and 2A.22.

title: Section 2D.02 Standard 2 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
text:
Section 2D.02 Standard 2 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Except as otherwise provided in this Manual for individual signs or groups of signs, guide signs on streets and highways shall have a white message and border on a green background. All messages, borders, and legends shall be retroreflective and all backgrounds shall be retroreflective or illuminated.

title: Section 2D.02 Support 3 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
text:
Section 2D.02 Support 3 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Color coding is sometimes used to help road users distinguish between multiple potentially confusing destinations. Examples of valuable uses of color coding include guide signs for roadways approaching or inside an airport property with multiple terminals serving multiple airlines, and community wayfinding guide signs for various traffic generator destinations within a community or area.

title: Section 2D.02 Standard 4 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
text:
Section 2D.02 Standard 4 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, different color sign backgrounds shall not be used to provide color coding of destinations. The color coding shall be accomplished by the use of different colored square or rectangular sign panels on the face of the guide signs (see Figure 2D-1).

title: Section 2D.02 Option 5 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
text:
Section 2D.02 Option 5 - Color, Retroreflection, and Illumination
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 205

title: Section 2D.04 Standard 2 - Lettering Style
text:
Section 2D.04 Standard 2 - Lettering Style
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 206

The lettering for names of places, streets, and highways on conventional road guide signs shall be a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters (see Section 2A.08). The nominal loop height of the lower-case letters shall be ¾ the height of the initial upper-case letter. When a mixed-case legend letter height is specified referring only to the initial upper-case letter, the height of the lower-case letters that follow shall be determined by this proportion. When the height of a lower-case letter is referenced, the reference is made to the nominal loop height. The height of the initial upper-case letter shall also be determined by this proportion.

title: Section 2D.05 Support 1 - Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2D.05 Support 1 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 208

Sign legibility is a direct function of letter size and spacing. Legibility distance has to be sufficient to give road users enough time to read and comprehend the sign. Under optimum conditions, a guide sign message can be read and understood in a brief glance. The legibility distance takes into account factors such as inattention, blocking of view by other vehicles, unfavorable weather, inferior eyesight, or other causes for delayed or slow reading. Where conditions permit, repetition of guide information on successive signs gives the road user more than one opportunity to obtain the information needed.

title: Section 2D.05 Standard 2 - Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2D.05 Standard 2 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

Design layouts for conventional road guide signs showing interline spacing, edge spacing, and other specification details shall be as shown in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05). Month 2023

title: Section 2D.05 Standard 3 - Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2D.05 Standard 3 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, the principal legend on post-mounted guide signs shall be in letters and numerals at least 6 inches in height for all upper-case letters, or a combination of 6 inches in height for upper-case letters and 4.5 inches in nominal loop height (see Section 2D.04) for lower-case letters. On low-volume roads with speeds of 25 mph or less, and on urban streets with speeds of 25 mph or less, the principal legend on post-mounted guide signs shall be in letters at least 4 inches in height for all upper-case letters, or a combination of 4 inches in height for upper-case letters and 3 inches in nominal loop height for lower-case letters.

title: Section 2D.05 Standard 4 - Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2D.05 Standard 4 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, the principal legend on overhead guide signs shall be in letters and numerals at least 6 inches in height for all upper-case letters, or a combination of 6 inches in height for upper-case letters and 4.5 inches in nominal loop height (see Section 2D.04) for lower- case letters.

text:
Section 2D.05 Guidance 5 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads

text:
Section 2D.05 Guidance 6 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

The minimum lettering and numeral sizes provided in this Manual (see Table 2D-2) should be exceeded where conditions indicate a need for greater legibility.

title: Section 2D.06 Support 1 - Amount of Legend
text:
Section 2D.06 Support 1 - Amount of Legend
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

The longer the legend on a guide sign, the longer it will take road users to recognize and comprehend it, regardless of letter size.

title: Section 2D.06 Guidance 2 - Amount of Legend
text:
Section 2D.06 Guidance 2 - Amount of Legend
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

Except where otherwise provided in this Manual, guide signs should be limited to no more than three lines of destinations, which include place names, route numbers, street names, and cardinal directions. Where two or more signs are included in the same overhead display, the amount of legend should be further minimized. Where appropriate, a distance message or action information, such as an exit number, NEXT RIGHT, or directional arrows, should be provided on guide signs in addition to the destinations.

title: Section 2D.07 Support 1 - Abbreviations
text:
Section 2D.07 Support 1 - Abbreviations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

The use of commonly recognized abbreviations for certain words can be useful in reducing the reading time and improve quicker comprehension of a sign message. Descriptors and directional or quadrant orientations for street names and destinations, such as Boulevard (Blvd), North (N), and Southwest (SW), are some examples of commonly recognized abbreviations. Examples of the use of some guide sign abbreviations are shown in Figure 2D-2.

title: Section 2D.07 Standard 2 - Abbreviations
text:
Section 2D.07 Standard 2 - Abbreviations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

The words NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, and WEST shall not be abbreviated when used to indicate cardinal directions of numbered or named highways on guide signs.

title: Section 2D.07 Guidance 3 - Abbreviations
text:
Section 2D.07 Guidance 3 - Abbreviations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 209

Abbreviations should be kept to a minimum; however, they are useful when complete destination messages produce excessively long signs. If used, abbreviations should be unmistakably recognized by road users (see Section 1D.08). Longer commonly used words that are not part of a proper name and are readily recognizable, such as street name descriptors (such as Street, Boulevard, or Avenue), should be abbreviated as provided in Table 2D-3 to expedite recognition of the sign legend by reducing the amount and complexity of the legend. Shorter street name descriptors, such as those shown in Table 2D-4, should not be abbreviated.

Page: 209

text:
Section 2D.08 Support 1 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 213

Arrows are used for lane assignment and to indicate the direction toward designated routes or destinations. Figure 2D-3 shows the various standard arrow designs that have been approved for use on guide signs. Detailed drawings are shown for these arrows in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05).

title: Section 2D.08 Standard 2 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Standard 2 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 213

Except for Overhead Arrow-per- Lane signs (see Section 2D.37), on overhead signs where it is desirable to indicate a lane to be followed, a down arrow shall be positioned over the approximate center of the lane and shall point vertically downward toward the approximate center of that lane. Down arrows shall be used only on overhead guide signs that restrict the use of specific lanes to traffic bound for the destination(s) and/or route(s) indicated by these arrows. Down arrows shall not be used unless an arrow can be located over and pointed to the approximate center of each lane that can be used to reach the destination displayed on the sign. Part: Part 2 Signs

Page: 213

text:
Section 2D.08 Guidance 7 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs

Page: 213

When a directional arrow in a vertical, upward- pointing orientation is placed to the side of a group of destinations to indicate a through movement, the Type A directional arrow should be used. When a directional arrow in a vertical, upward-pointing orientation is placed to the side of a single destination or under a destination or group of destinations, the Type B directional arrow should be used.

Page: 213

Part: Part 2 Signs

Page: 214

title: Section 2D.08 Option 14 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Option 14 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 214

On conventional roads on the approach to an intersection where the Combination Lane-Use/Destination overhead guide sign (see Section 2D.38) is not used, the Type C advance turn directional arrow may be used beneath the legend of an overhead guide sign to indicate the fact that a turn must be made from a mandatory movement lane over which the sign is placed to reach the destination or destinations displayed on the sign.

title: Section 2D.08 Option 15 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Option 15 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 214

The Type D directional arrow may be used on post-mounted guide signs on conventional roads with lower operating speeds if the height of the text on the sign is 8 inches or less. Type D arrows may be used on a Street Name (D3-1 only) sign displaying two street names to indicate the different direction of travel for each street.

title: Section 2D.08 Option 16 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Option 16 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 214

title: Section 2D.08 Option 17 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Option 17 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 214
