title: Section 2D.08 Guidance 18 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Guidance 18 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 214

Arrows used on guide signs to indicate the directions toward designated routes or destinations should be pointed at the appropriate angle to clearly convey the direction to be taken. A horizontally-oriented directional arrow design should be used at right-angle intersections.

title: Section 2D.08 Guidance 19 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Guidance 19 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 214

On a post-mounted guide sign, a directional arrow for a straight-through movement should point upward. Except as provided in Section 2D.50, for a turn, the arrow on a guide sign should point horizontally or at an upward angle that approximates the sharpness of the turn.

title: Section 2D.08 Guidance 20 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Guidance 20 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 215

At an exit, an arrow should be placed at the side of the sign that will reinforce the movement of exiting traffic. The directional arrow design should be used. Month 2023 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 2D.08 Standard 21 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Standard 21 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 215

If used, the Type C advance turn directional arrow shall display a right or left arrow, the shaft of which is bent at a 90-degree or oblique angle.

title: Section 2D.08 Option 22 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Option 22 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 215

Arrows may be placed below the principal sign legend or on the appropriate side of the legend that is consistent with the direction of the movement.

title: Section 2D.08 Option 23 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Option 23 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 215

On a post-mounted sign at an exit where placement of the arrow to the side of the legend farthest from the roadway would create an unusually wide sign that limits the road user’s view of the arrow, the directional arrow may be placed at the bottom portion of the sign, centered under the legend.

title: Section 2D.08 Guidance 24 - Arrows
text:
Section 2D.08 Guidance 24 - Arrows
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 215

The width across the arrowhead for the Types A, B, and C directional arrows should be between 1.5 and 1.75 times the height of the upper-case letters of the principal legend on the sign. The width across the arrowhead for the Type D directional arrow should be at least equal to the height of the upper-case letters of the principal legend on the sign. For down arrows used on overhead signs, the width across the arrowhead should be approximately 2 times the height of the upper-case letters of the principal legend on the sign.

title: Section 2D.09 Support 1 - Numbered Highway Systems
text:
Section 2D.09 Support 1 - Numbered Highway Systems
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

The purpose of numbering and signing highway systems is to identify routes and facilitate travel.

title: Section 2D.09 Support 2 - Numbered Highway Systems
text:
Section 2D.09 Support 2 - Numbered Highway Systems
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

The Interstate and United States (U.S.) highway systems are numbered by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) upon recommendations of the State highway organizations because the respective States own these systems. State and county road systems are numbered by the appropriate authorities.

title: Section 2D.09 Support 3 - Numbered Highway Systems
text:
Section 2D.09 Support 3 - Numbered Highway Systems
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

The basic policy for numbering the Interstate and U.S. highway systems is contained in the following Purpose and Policy statements published by AASHTO: A. “Establishment and Development of United States Numbered Highways,” and B. “Establishment of a Marking System of the Routes Comprising the National System of Interstate and Defense Highways.”

title: Section 2D.09 Guidance 4 - Numbered Highway Systems
text:
Section 2D.09 Guidance 4 - Numbered Highway Systems
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

The principles of these policies should be followed in establishing the highway systems described in Paragraph 3 of this Section and any other systems, with effective coordination between adjacent jurisdictions. Care should be taken to avoid the use of numbers or other designations that have been assigned to Interstate, U.S., or State routes in the same geographic area. Overlapping numbered routes should be kept to a minimum.

title: Section 2D.09 Standard 5 - Numbered Highway Systems
text:
Section 2D.09 Standard 5 - Numbered Highway Systems
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

Route systems shall be given preference in this order: Interstate, United States, State, and county. The preference shall be given by installing the highest-priority route number on the top or the left of the sign, except as provided in Paragraph 7 of this Section. Rev. 1

title: Section 2D.09 Standard 6 - Numbered Highway Systems
text:
Section 2D.09 Standard 6 - Numbered Highway Systems
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

Interstate route numbering shall be approved by the FHWA.

title: Section 2D.09 Option 7 - Numbered Highway Systems
text:
Section 2D.09 Option 7 - Numbered Highway Systems
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

The prioritization of route systems may be modified when a different prioritization would better accommodate the expectancy of the road user and provide more effective direction, such as for separate decision points for routes that are encountered in a particular order.

title: Section 2D.10 Standard 1 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.10 Standard 1 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

Except as provided in Paragraph 9 of Section 2D.29, all numbered highway routes shall be identified by route signs and auxiliary plaques.

title: Section 2D.10 Standard 2 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.10 Standard 2 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

The signs for each system of numbered highways, which are distinctive in shape and color, shall be used only on that system and the approaches thereto.

title: Section 2D.10 Option 3 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.10 Option 3 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

Route signs and auxiliary plaques may be proportionally enlarged where greater conspicuity or legibility is needed.

title: Section 2D.10 Support 4 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.10 Support 4 - Route Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

Route signs are typically mounted in assemblies with auxiliary plaques.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 1 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 1 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 216

The design of standard route signs shall conform to the designs provided in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05). The design of other route signs shall be established by the authority having jurisdiction and shall be in general conformance with the designs provided in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 2 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 2 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 217

Interstate Route (M1-1 and M1-1a) signs (see Figure 2D-4) shall be used on all Interstate routes and in connection with Route Sign assemblies on intersecting highways. Month 2023 December 2025 Figure 2D-4. Route Signs

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 3 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 3 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 217

Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, a 24 x 24-inch minimum sign size shall be used for Interstate route numbers with one or two digits, and a 30 x 24-inch minimum sign size shall be used for Interstate route numbers having three digits.

title: Section 2D.11 Option 4 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Option 4 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 217

When the Interstate Route sign is used in a Route Sign assembly (see Section 2D.29), the M1-1a sign, containing the State name in white upper-case letters on a blue background as detailed in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05), may be used in place of the M1-1 sign.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 5 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 5 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 217

Use of the M1-1a sign shall be limited to Route Sign assemblies.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 6 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 6 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 217

Off-Interstate Business Route (M1-2 and M1-3) signs (see Figure 2D-4) shall consist of a cutout shield displaying the number of the connecting Interstate route and the words BUSINESS and either LOOP (when the route rejoins the same Interstate route) or SPUR (when the route leaves the corresponding Interstate route and does not rejoin) in upper-case letters. The legend and border shall be white on a green background, and the shield shall be the same shape and dimensions as the Interstate Route sign. In no instance shall the word INTERSTATE appear on the Off-Interstate Business Route sign.

title: Section 2D.11 Option 7 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Option 7 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

The Off-Interstate Business Route sign may be used on a major highway that is not a part of the Interstate system, but one that serves the business area of a city from an interchange on the system. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 8 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 8 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

U.S. Route signs (see Figure 2D-4) shall consist of black numerals on a white shield surrounded by a rectangular black background without a border. This sign shall be used on all U.S. routes and in connection with Route Sign assemblies on intersecting highways.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 9 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 9 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

A 24 x 24-inch minimum sign size shall be used for U.S. route numbers with one or two digits, and a 30 x 24-inch minimum sign size shall be used for U.S. route numbers having three digits.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 10 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 10 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

State Route signs shall be designed by the individual State highway agencies.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 11 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 11 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

The legend on State Route signs shall conform to the Standard Alphabets contained in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05).

title: Section 2D.11 Guidance 12 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Guidance 12 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

State Route signs (see Figure 2D-4) should be rectangular and should be approximately the same size as the U.S. Route sign. State Route signs should also be similar to the U.S. Route sign by containing approximately the same size black numerals on a white area surrounded by a rectangular black background without a border, and should be devoid of complex graphics. The shape of the white area should be circular in the absence of any determination to the contrary by the individual State concerned.

title: Section 2D.11 Guidance 13 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Guidance 13 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

Where U.S. or State Route signs are used as components of guide signs, only the distinctive shape of the shield itself and the route numerals within should be used. The rectangular background upon which the distinctive shape of the shield is mounted, such as the black area around the outside of the shields on the M1-4 and standard M1-5 signs, should not be included on the guide sign. Where U.S. or State Route signs are used as components of other signs of non-contrasting background colors, the rectangular background should be used so that recognition of the distinctive shape of the shield can be maintained.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 14 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 14 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

If county road authorities elect to establish and identify a special system of important county roads, a statewide policy for such signing shall be established that includes a uniform numbering system to uniquely identify each route. The County Route (M1-6) sign (see Figure 2D-4) shall consist of a pentagon shape with a yellow county name and route number and border on a blue background. County Route signs shall be a minimum size of 24 x 24 inches.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 15 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 15 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

If a jurisdiction uses letters instead of numbers to identify routes, all references to numbered routes in this Chapter shall be interpreted to also include lettered routes.

title: Section 2D.11 Guidance 16 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Guidance 16 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

If used with other route signs in common assemblies, the County Route sign should be of a size compatible with that of the other route signs.

title: Section 2D.11 Option 17 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Option 17 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

When the County Route (M1-6) sign is used as a component of a guide sign, the county name and the legend COUNTY may be omitted from the County Route sign.

title: Section 2D.11 Standard 18 - Design of Route Signs
text:
Section 2D.11 Standard 18 - Design of Route Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

The design of the National Forest Route (M1-7) sign (see Figure 2D-4) shall be as detailed in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05). Route signs for other park and forest roads shall be designed with an appropriate level of distinctiveness and adequate legibility, but in general compliance with the design principles for route signs and of a size compatible with other route signs used in common assemblies. Rev. 1

title: Section 2D.12 Standard 1 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.12 Standard 1 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

Route sign auxiliary plaques displaying word legends, except the Junction (M2-1P) auxiliary plaque, shall have a minimum standard size of 24 x 12 inches. The Junction auxiliary plaque and those auxiliary plaques displaying arrows shall have a minimum standard size of 21 x 15 inches. All route sign auxiliary plaques shall match the color combination of the route sign that they supplement.

metadata.section_title: Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques

title: Section 2D.12 Guidance 2 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.12 Guidance 2 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 218

The background, legend, and border of a route sign auxiliary plaque should have the same colors as those of the route sign with which the auxiliary plaque is mounted in a Route Sign assembly (see Section 2D.29). For a route sign design that uses multiple background colors, such as the Interstate Route sign, the background color of the corresponding auxiliary plaque should be that of the background area on which the route number is placed on the route sign.

metadata.section_title: Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques

title: Section 2D.12 Option 3 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.12 Option 3 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

A route sign and any auxiliary plaques used with it may be combined on a single sign as a guide sign. Month 2023 December 2025

metadata.section_title: Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques

title: Section 2D.12 Standard 4 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.12 Standard 4 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

If a route sign and its auxiliary plaques are combined to form a single guide sign, the background color of the sign shall be green and the design shall comply with the basic principles for the design of guide signs. The auxiliary messages shall be white legends placed directly on the green background. Auxiliary plaques shall not be mounted directly to a guide sign or other type of sign.

metadata.section_title: Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques

title: Section 2D.12 Support 5 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.12 Support 5 - Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

Chapter 2F contains information regarding auxiliary plaques for toll highways.

metadata.section_title: Design of Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques

title: Section 2D.13 Standard 1 - Junction Auxiliary Plaque (M2-1P)
text:
Section 2D.13 Standard 1 - Junction Auxiliary Plaque (M2-1P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

The Junction (M2-1P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) shall display the abbreviated legend JCT and shall be mounted at the top of an assembly (see Section 2D.30) directly above the route sign, the sign for an alternative route (see Section 2D.17) that is part of the route designation, or the Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque where access is available only to one direction of the intersected route. The minimum size of the Junction auxiliary plaque shall be 21 x 15 inches for compatibility with auxiliary plaques displaying arrow symbols.

title: Section 2D.14 Option 1 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
text:
Section 2D.14 Option 1 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

As an alternative to the standard Junction assembly where more than one route is to be intersected or joined, a rectangular guide sign may be used displaying the word JUNCTION above the route numbers.

title: Section 2D.14 Standard 2 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
text:
Section 2D.14 Standard 2 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

The Combination Junction (M2-2) sign (see Figure 2D-5) shall have a green background with white border and lettering for the word JUNCTION.

title: Section 2D.14 Guidance 3 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
text:
Section 2D.14 Guidance 3 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

The Combination Junction sign should comply with the specific provisions of Section 2D.11 regarding the incorporation of the route signs as components of guide signs.

title: Section 2D.14 Guidance 4 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
text:
Section 2D.14 Guidance 4 - Combination Junction Sign (M2-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

Although the size of the Combination Junction sign will depend on the number of routes involved, the numerals should be large enough for clear legibility and should be of a size comparable with those in the individual route signs.

title: Section 2D.15 Guidance 1 - Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)
text:
Section 2D.15 Guidance 1 - Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaques (see Figure 2D-5) displaying the legend NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, or WEST should be used to indicate the general direction of the entire route.

metadata.section_title: Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)

title: Section 2D.15 Standard 2 - Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)
text:
Section 2D.15 Standard 2 - Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 219

To improve the readability and recognition of the cardinal directions, the first letter of the cardinal direction words shall be ten percent larger, rounded up to the nearest whole number size.

metadata.section_title: Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)

title: Section 2D.15 Standard 3 - Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)
text:
Section 2D.15 Standard 3 - Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

If used, the Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above a route sign or, if used, an auxiliary plaque for an alternative route. Figure 2D-5. Route Sign Auxiliary Plaques and Combination Junction Sign Month 2023

metadata.section_title: Cardinal Direction Auxiliary Plaques (M3-1P through M3-4P)

title: Section 2D.16 Option 1 - Alternative Route Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P through M4-4P)
text:
Section 2D.16 Option 1 - Alternative Route Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P through M4-4P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

Alternative Route auxiliary plaques (see Figure 2D-5) displaying legends such as ALTERNATE, BY-PASS, BUSINESS, or TRUCK, may be used to indicate an alternate route of the same number between two points on that route.

metadata.section_title: Alternative Route Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P through M4-4P)

title: Section 2D.16 Standard 2 - Alternative Route Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P through M4-4P)
text:
Section 2D.16 Standard 2 - Alternative Route Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P through M4-4P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

If used, the Alternative Route auxiliary plaques shall be mounted directly above a route sign.

metadata.section_title: Alternative Route Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P through M4-4P)

title: Section 2D.17 Option 1 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.17 Option 1 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

The ALTERNATE (M4-1P) or the ALT (M4-1aP) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) may be used to indicate an officially designated alternate routing of a numbered route between two points on that route.

title: Section 2D.17 Standard 2 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.17 Standard 2 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

If used, the ALTERNATE or ALT auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above a route sign.

title: Section 2D.17 Standard 3 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.17 Standard 3 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

The M4-1P series plaques shall not be used to sign an alternative routing that is not officially designated and incorporated into the numbered highway system, such as alternative routings for incident management or emergency detours.

title: Section 2D.17 Guidance 4 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.17 Guidance 4 - ALTERNATE Auxiliary Plaques (M4-1P and M4-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

The shorter (time or distance) or better-constructed route should retain the regular route number, and the longer or worse-constructed route should be designated as the alternate route.

title: Section 2D.18 Option 1 - BY-PASS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-2P)
text:
Section 2D.18 Option 1 - BY-PASS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-2P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

The BY-PASS (M4-2P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) may be used to designate a route that branches from the numbered route through a city, bypasses a part of the city or congested area, and rejoins the numbered route beyond the city.

title: Section 2D.18 Standard 2 - BY-PASS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-2P)
text:
Section 2D.18 Standard 2 - BY-PASS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-2P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

If used, the BY-PASS auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above a route sign.

title: Section 2D.19 Option 1 - BUSINESS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-3P)
text:
Section 2D.19 Option 1 - BUSINESS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-3P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

The BUSINESS (M4-3P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) may be used to designate an alternate route that branches from a numbered route, passes through the business portion of a city, and rejoins the numbered route beyond that area.

title: Section 2D.19 Standard 2 - BUSINESS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-3P)
text:
Section 2D.19 Standard 2 - BUSINESS Auxiliary Plaque (M4-3P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

If used, the BUSINESS auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above a route sign.

title: Section 2D.20 Option 1 - TRUCK Auxiliary Plaque (M4-4P)
text:
Section 2D.20 Option 1 - TRUCK Auxiliary Plaque (M4-4P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

The TRUCK (M4-4P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) may be used to designate an alternate route that branches from a numbered route, when it is desirable to encourage or require commercial vehicles to use the alternate route.

title: Section 2D.20 Standard 2 - TRUCK Auxiliary Plaque (M4-4P)
text:
Section 2D.20 Standard 2 - TRUCK Auxiliary Plaque (M4-4P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

If used, the TRUCK auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above a route sign.

title: Section 2D.21 Option 1 - TO Auxiliary Plaque (M4-5P)
text:
Section 2D.21 Option 1 - TO Auxiliary Plaque (M4-5P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 220

The TO (M4-5P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) may be used to provide directional guidance to a particular road facility from other highways in the vicinity (see Section 2D.34).

title: Section 2D.21 Standard 2 - TO Auxiliary Plaque (M4-5P)
text:
Section 2D.21 Standard 2 - TO Auxiliary Plaque (M4-5P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If used, the TO auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above a route sign or an auxiliary plaque for an alternative route. If a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque is also included in the assembly, the TO auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above the Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 2D.22 Guidance 1 - END Auxiliary Plaque (M4-6P)
text:
Section 2D.22 Guidance 1 - END Auxiliary Plaque (M4-6P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

The END (M4-6P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) should be used where the route being traveled ends, usually at a junction with another route.

title: Section 2D.22 Standard 2 - END Auxiliary Plaque (M4-6P)
text:
Section 2D.22 Standard 2 - END Auxiliary Plaque (M4-6P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If used, the END auxiliary plaque shall be mounted either directly above a route sign or above a sign for an alternative route that is part of the designation of the route being terminated.

title: Section 2D.23 Option 1 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
text:
Section 2D.23 Option 1 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

The BEGIN (M4-14P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) may be used where a route begins, usually at a junction with another route.

title: Section 2D.23 Standard 2 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
text:
Section 2D.23 Standard 2 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If used, the BEGIN auxiliary plaque shall be mounted at the top of the first Confirming assembly (see Section 2D.33) for the route that is beginning.

title: Section 2D.23 Guidance 3 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
text:
Section 2D.23 Guidance 3 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If a BEGIN auxiliary plaque is included in the first Confirming assembly, a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque should also be included in the assembly.

title: Section 2D.23 Standard 4 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
text:
Section 2D.23 Standard 4 - BEGIN Auxiliary Plaque (M4-14P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque is also included in the assembly, the BEGIN auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above the Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque.

title: Section 2D.24 Option 1 - TEMPORARY Auxiliary Plaques (M4-7P and M4-7aP)
text:
Section 2D.24 Option 1 - TEMPORARY Auxiliary Plaques (M4-7P and M4-7aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

The TEMPORARY (M4-7P) or the TEMP (M4-7aP) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-5) may be used for an interim period to designate a section of highway that is not planned as a permanent part of a numbered route, but that connects completed portions of that route.

title: Section 2D.24 Standard 2 - TEMPORARY Auxiliary Plaques (M4-7P and M4-7aP)
text:
Section 2D.24 Standard 2 - TEMPORARY Auxiliary Plaques (M4-7P and M4-7aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If used, the TEMPORARY or TEMP auxiliary plaque shall be mounted directly above the route sign, above a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque, or above an auxiliary plaque for an alternate route that is a part of the route designation.

title: Section 2D.24 Standard 3 - TEMPORARY Auxiliary Plaques (M4-7P and M4-7aP)
text:
Section 2D.24 Standard 3 - TEMPORARY Auxiliary Plaques (M4-7P and M4-7aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

TEMPORARY or TEMP auxiliary plaques shall be promptly removed when the temporary route is abandoned.

title: Section 2D.25 Support 1 - Temporary Detour Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
text:
Section 2D.25 Support 1 - Temporary Detour Signs and Auxiliary Plaques
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

Chapter 6I contains information regarding Temporary Detour signs and auxiliary plaques. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Temporary Detour Signs and Auxiliary Plaques

title: Section 2D.26 Standard 1 - Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)
text:
Section 2D.26 Standard 1 - Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If used, the Advance Turn Arrow auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-6) shall be mounted directly below the route sign in Advance Route Turn assemblies, and shall display a right or left arrow, the shaft of which is bent at a 90-degree angle (M5-1P) or at an oblique angle (M5-2P).

metadata.section_title: Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)

title: Section 2D.26 Standard 2 - Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)
text:
Section 2D.26 Standard 2 - Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 221

If used, the Circular Intersection Advance Turn Arrow (M5-3P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-6) shall be used only on the approach to a circular intersection to depict a movement along the circulatory roadway around the central island and to the left, relative to the approach roadway and entry into the intersection.

metadata.section_title: Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)

title: Section 2D.26 Guidance 3 - Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)
text:
Section 2D.26 Guidance 3 - Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 222

If the M5-3P plaque is used, then this arrow type should also be used consistently on any regulatory lane- use signs (see Chapter 2B), Destination signs (see Section 2D.36), and pavement markings (see Part 3) for a particular destination or movement. Month 2023 December 2025 Figure 2D-6. Advance Turn and Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques

metadata.section_title: Advance Turn Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M5-1P, M5-2P, and M5-3P)

title: Section 2D.27 Option 1 - Lane Designation Auxiliary Plaques (M5-4P, M5-5P, and M5-6P)
text:
Section 2D.27 Option 1 - Lane Designation Auxiliary Plaques (M5-4P, M5-5P, and M5-6P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 222

A Lane Designation (M5-4P, M5-5P, or M5-6P) auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-6) may be mounted directly below the route sign in an Advance Route Turn assembly on multi-lane roadways to allow road users to move into the appropriate lane prior to reaching the intersection or interchange.

metadata.section_title: Lane Designation Auxiliary Plaques (M5-4P, M5-5P, and M5-6P)

title: Section 2D.27 Standard 2 - Lane Designation Auxiliary Plaques (M5-4P, M5-5P, and M5-6P)
text:
Section 2D.27 Standard 2 - Lane Designation Auxiliary Plaques (M5-4P, M5-5P, and M5-6P)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 222

If used, the Lane Designation auxiliary plaques shall be used only where the designated lane is a mandatory movement lane and shall be located adjacent to the full-width portion of the mandatory movement lane. The Lane Designation auxiliary plaques shall not be installed adjacent to a through lane in advance of a lane that is being added or along the taper for a lane that is being added.

metadata.section_title: Lane Designation Auxiliary Plaques (M5-4P, M5-5P, and M5-6P)

title: Section 2D.28 Standard 1 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
text:
Section 2D.28 Standard 1 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 222

If used, the Directional Arrow auxiliary plaque (see Figure 2D-6) shall be mounted below the route sign and any other auxiliary plaques in Directional assemblies (see Section 2D.32), and shall display a single-headed or double-headed arrow pointing in the general direction that the route follows.

title: Section 2D.28 Standard 2 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
text:
Section 2D.28 Standard 2 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 222

A Directional Arrow auxiliary plaque that displays a double-headed arrow shall not be mounted in any Directional assembly in advance of or at a circular intersection.

title: Section 2D.28 Option 3 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
text:
Section 2D.28 Option 3 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 222

The diagonal downward-pointing arrow auxiliary (M6-2aP) plaque may be used in a Directional assembly at the far corner of an intersection to indicate the immediate entry point to a freeway or expressway entrance ramp (see Section 2D.50).

title: Section 2D.28 Standard 4 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
text:
Section 2D.28 Standard 4 - Directional Arrow Auxiliary Plaques (M6 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

The M6-2aP plaque shall not be used on the approach to or on the near side of an intersection, such as to designate an approach lane. Month 2023 SIGN ASSEMBLIES

title: Section 2D.29 Standard 1 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Standard 1 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

A Route Sign assembly shall consist of a route sign and auxiliary plaques that further identify the route and indicate the direction. Except as provided in Paragraph 9 of this Section, Route Sign assemblies shall be installed on all approaches to numbered routes that intersect with other numbered routes.

title: Section 2D.29 Standard 2 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Standard 2 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Where two or more routes follow the same section of highway, the route signs for Interstate, U.S., State, and county routes shall be mounted in that order from the left in horizontal arrangements and from the top in vertical arrangements. Subject to this order of precedence, route signs for lower-numbered routes shall be placed at the left or top.

title: Section 2D.29 Standard 3 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Standard 3 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Within groups of assemblies, information for routes intersecting from the left shall be mounted at the left in horizontal arrangements and at the top or center of vertical arrangements. Similarly, information for routes intersecting from the right shall be at the right or bottom, and for straight-through routes at the center in horizontal arrangements or top in vertical arrangements.

title: Section 2D.29 Standard 4 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Standard 4 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Route Sign assemblies shall be mounted in accordance with the general specifications for signs (Chapter 2A), with the lowest sign in the assembly at the height prescribed for single signs.

title: Section 2D.29 Guidance 5 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Guidance 5 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Assemblies for two or more routes, or for different directions on the same route, should be mounted in groups on a common support.

title: Section 2D.29 Guidance 6 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Guidance 6 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Where more than four route signs would be needed in a single Advance Route Turn or Directional assembly, the route signs should instead be mounted in a guide sign to minimize the need for repetition of the same information on multiple Cardinal Direction and Directional Arrow auxiliary plaques (see Figure 2D-7).

title: Section 2D.29 Option 7 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Option 7 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Route Sign assemblies may be installed on the approaches to numbered routes on unnumbered roads and streets that carry an appreciable amount of traffic destined for the numbered route.

title: Section 2D.29 Option 8 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Option 8 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

If engineering judgment indicates that groups of assemblies that include overlapping routes or multiple turns might be confusing, route signs or auxiliary signs may be omitted or combined, provided that clear directions are given to road users.

title: Section 2D.29 Option 9 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Option 9 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Route Sign assemblies may be omitted for routes that are part of an agency’s internal numbering system, such as for maintenance or other purposes, and are not publicly mapped or intended to be used for navigational purposes by the general public. Similarly, numbered routes that are not maintained during certain times of year, such as not being plowed during winter months, may be omitted from Route Sign assemblies.

title: Section 2D.29 Support 10 - Route Sign Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.29 Support 10 - Route Sign Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Figure 2D-8 shows typical placements of route signs.

title: Section 2D.30 Standard 1 - Junction Assembly
text:
Section 2D.30 Standard 1 - Junction Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

A Junction assembly shall consist of a Junction auxiliary plaque (see Section 2D.13) and a route sign. The route sign shall display the number of the intersected or joined route.

title: Section 2D.30 Standard 2 - Junction Assembly
text:
Section 2D.30 Standard 2 - Junction Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

The Junction assembly shall be installed in advance of every intersection where a numbered route is intersected or joined by another numbered route.

title: Section 2D.30 Guidance 3 - Junction Assembly
text:
Section 2D.30 Guidance 3 - Junction Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

In urban areas, the Junction assembly should be installed in the block preceding the intersection. In urban areas where speeds are low, the Junction assembly should not be installed more than 300 feet in advance of the intersection.

title: Section 2D.30 Guidance 4 - Junction Assembly
text:
Section 2D.30 Guidance 4 - Junction Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

In rural areas, the Junction assembly should be installed at least 400 feet in advance of the intersection. In rural areas, the minimum distance between a Junction assembly and either a Destination sign or an Advance Route Turn assembly should be 200 feet.

title: Section 2D.30 Guidance 5 - Junction Assembly
text:
Section 2D.30 Guidance 5 - Junction Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 223

Where speeds are high, greater spacings should be used.

title: Section 2D.30 Option 6 - Junction Assembly
text:
Section 2D.30 Option 6 - Junction Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

Where two or more routes are to be indicated, a single Junction auxiliary plaque may be used for the assembly and all route signs grouped in a single mounting, or a Combination Junction (M2-2) sign (see Section 2D.14) may be used.
