title: Section 2D.31 Standard 1 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
text:
Section 2D.31 Standard 1 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

An Advance Route Turn assembly shall consist of a route sign, an Advance Turn Arrow or word message auxiliary plaque, and a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque, if needed. It shall be installed in advance of an intersection where a turn must be made to remain on the indicated route.

title: Section 2D.31 Option 2 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
text:
Section 2D.31 Option 2 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

The Advance Route Turn assembly may be used to supplement the required Junction assembly in advance of intersecting routes.

title: Section 2D.31 Guidance 3 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
text:
Section 2D.31 Guidance 3 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

Where a multi-lane highway approaches an interchange or intersection with a numbered route, the Advance Route Turn assembly should be used to provide advance notice so that road users know the correct lane(s) from which to make their turn.

title: Section 2D.31 Option 4 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
text:
Section 2D.31 Option 4 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

Lane Designation auxiliary plaques (see Section 2D.27) may be used in Advance Route Turn Assemblies in place of the Advance Turn Arrow auxiliary plaques where engineering judgment indicates that specific lane information associated with each route is needed and overhead signing is impracticable and the designated lane is a mandatory movement lane. An assembly with the Lane Designation auxiliary plaques may supplement or substitute for an assembly with Advance Turn Arrow auxiliary plaques.

title: Section 2D.31 Guidance 5 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
text:
Section 2D.31 Guidance 5 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

In low-speed areas, the Advance Route Turn assembly should be installed not less than 200 feet in advance of the turn. In high-speed areas, the Advance Route Turn assembly should be installed not less than 300 feet in advance of the turn. In rural areas, the minimum distance between an Advance Route Turn assembly and either a Destination sign or a Junction assembly should be 200 feet.

title: Section 2D.31 Standard 6 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
text:
Section 2D.31 Standard 6 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

An assembly that includes an Advance Turn Arrow auxiliary plaque shall not be placed where there is an intersection between it and the designated turn.

title: Section 2D.31 Guidance 7 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
text:
Section 2D.31 Guidance 7 - Advance Route Turn Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

Sufficient distance should be allowed between the assembly and any preceding intersection that could be mistaken for the indicated turn.

title: Section 2D.32 Standard 1 - Directional Assembly
text:
Section 2D.32 Standard 1 - Directional Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 230

A Directional assembly shall consist of a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque, if needed; a route sign; and a Directional Arrow auxiliary plaque. The uses of Directional assemblies shall comply with the following: A. Turn movements (indicated in advance by an Advance Route Turn assembly) shall be marked by a Directional assembly with a route sign displaying the number of the turning route and a single- headed arrow pointing in the direction of the turn. B. The beginning of a route (indicated in advance by a Junction assembly) shall be marked by a Directional assembly with a route sign displaying the number of that route and a single-headed arrow pointing in the direction of the route. C. An intersected route (indicated in advance by a Junction assembly) on a crossroad where the route is designated on both legs shall be designated by: 1. Two Directional assemblies, each with a route sign displaying the number of the intersected route, a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque, and a single-headed arrow pointing in the direction of movement on that route; or 2. A Directional assembly with a route sign displaying the number of the intersected route and a double-headed arrow, pointing at appropriate angles to the left, right, or ahead. D. An intersected route (indicated in advance by a Junction assembly) on a side road or on a crossroad where the route is designated only on one of the legs shall be designated by a Directional assembly with a route sign displaying the number of the intersected route, a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque, and a single-headed arrow pointing in the direction of movement on that route.

title: Section 2D.32 Guidance 2 - Directional Assembly
text:
Section 2D.32 Guidance 2 - Directional Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

Straight-through movements should be indicated by a Directional assembly with a route sign displaying the number of the continuing route and a vertical arrow. A Directional assembly should not be used for a straight- through movement in the absence of other assemblies indicating right or left turns, as the Confirming assembly sign beyond the intersection normally provides adequate guidance. Month 2023

title: Section 2D.32 Guidance 3 - Directional Assembly
text:
Section 2D.32 Guidance 3 - Directional Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

Directional assemblies should be located on the near right corner of the intersection. At major intersections and at Y or offset intersections, additional Directional assemblies should be installed on the far right or left corner to confirm the near-side assemblies. When the near-corner position is impractical for Directional assemblies, the far right corner should be the preferred alternative, with oversized signs, if necessary, for legibility. Where unusual conditions exist, the location of a Directional assembly should be determined by engineering judgment with the goal being to provide the best possible combination of view and safety.

title: Section 2D.32 Support 4 - Directional Assembly
text:
Section 2D.32 Support 4 - Directional Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

It is more important that guide signs be readable, and that the information and direction displayed thereon be readily understood, at the appropriate time and place than to be located with absolute uniformity.

title: Section 2D.32 Support 5 - Directional Assembly
text:
Section 2D.32 Support 5 - Directional Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

Figure 2D-8 shows typical placements of Directional assemblies.

title: Section 2D.33 Standard 1 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.33 Standard 1 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

If used, Confirming or Reassurance assemblies shall consist of a Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque and a route sign. Where the Confirming or Reassurance assembly is for an alternative route, the appropriate auxiliary plaque for an alternative route (see Section 2D.16) shall also be included in the assembly.

title: Section 2D.33 Guidance 2 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.33 Guidance 2 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

A Confirming assembly should be installed just beyond intersections of numbered routes. It should be placed 25 to 200 feet beyond the far shoulder or curb line of the intersected highway.

title: Section 2D.33 Guidance 3 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.33 Guidance 3 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

If used, Reassurance assemblies should be installed between intersections in urban areas as needed, and beyond the built-up area of any incorporated city or town.

title: Section 2D.33 Guidance 4 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
text:
Section 2D.33 Guidance 4 - Confirming or Reassurance Assemblies
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

Route signs for either confirming or reassurance purposes should be spaced at such intervals as necessary to keep road users informed of their routes.

title: Section 2D.34 Support 1 - Trailblazer Assembly
text:
Section 2D.34 Support 1 - Trailblazer Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

Trailblazer assemblies provide directional guidance to a particular road facility from other highways in the vicinity. This guidance is accomplished by installing Trailblazer assemblies at strategic locations to indicate the direction to the nearest or most convenient point of access. The use of the word TO indicates that the road or street where the sign is posted is not a part of the indicated route, and that a road user is merely being directed progressively to the route.

title: Section 2D.34 Standard 2 - Trailblazer Assembly
text:
Section 2D.34 Standard 2 - Trailblazer Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

A Trailblazer assembly shall consist of a TO auxiliary plaque (see Section 2D.21), a route sign for a numbered or named highway (see Section 2D.56) or an identification sign for a byway, historic trail, or auto tour route sign (see Sections 2D.57 and 2D.58), and a single-headed Directional Arrow auxiliary plaque pointing in the direction leading to the route. Where the Trailblazer assembly is for an alternative route, the appropriate auxiliary plaque for an alternative route (see Section 2D.16) shall also be included in the assembly.

title: Section 2D.34 Option 3 - Trailblazer Assembly
text:
Section 2D.34 Option 3 - Trailblazer Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

A Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque (see Section 2D.15) may be used in a Trailblazer assembly where the direction leading to the route provides access only to one direction of travel for that route.

title: Section 2D.34 Guidance 4 - Trailblazer Assembly
text:
Section 2D.34 Guidance 4 - Trailblazer Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 231

The TO auxiliary plaque, Cardinal Direction auxiliary plaque, and Directional Arrow auxiliary plaque should be of the standard size provided for auxiliary plaques of their respective type. The route sign should be the size provided in Section 2D.11.

title: Section 2D.34 Option 5 - Trailblazer Assembly
text:
Section 2D.34 Option 5 - Trailblazer Assembly
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

Trailblazer assemblies may be installed with other Route Sign assemblies, or alone, in the immediate vicinity of the designated facilities. Month 2023 DESTINATION AND DISTANCE SIGNS

title: Section 2D.35 Support 1 - Destination and Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.35 Support 1 - Destination and Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

In addition to guidance by route numbers, it is desirable to supply the road user information concerning the destinations that can be reached by way of numbered or unnumbered routes. This is done by means of Destination signs and Distance signs.

title: Section 2D.35 Option 2 - Destination and Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.35 Option 2 - Destination and Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

Route shields and cardinal directions may be included on the Destination sign with the destinations and arrows.

title: Section 2D.35 Guidance 3 - Destination and Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.35 Guidance 3 - Destination and Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

If Route shields and cardinal directions are included on a Destination sign, the height of the route shields should be at least two times the height of the upper-case letters of the principal legend and not less than 18 inches, and the letter height of cardinal directions should be at least the minimum letter height specified for these signs.

title: Section 2D.35 Guidance 4 - Destination and Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.35 Guidance 4 - Destination and Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

If used, destination names on low-volume rural roads should be as specific and descriptive as possible. Destinations such as campgrounds, ranger stations, and recreational areas should be clearly indicated so that they are not interpreted to be communities or locations with road user services.

title: Section 2D.36 Standard 1 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Standard 1 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

Except on approaches to interchanges (see Section 2D.49), the Destination (D1-1 through D1-3) signs (see Figure 2D-9), if used, shall be a horizontal rectangle displaying the name of a city, town, village, or other traffic generator, and a directional arrow.

title: Section 2D.36 Option 2 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Option 2 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

The distance (see Section 2D.43) to the place named may also be displayed on the Destination (D1-1a through D1-3a) signs (see Figure 2D-9). If several destinations are to be displayed at a single point, the several names may be placed on a single sign with an arrow (and the distance, if desired) for each name. If more than one destination lies in the same direction, a single arrow may be used for such a group of destinations.

title: Section 2D.36 Guidance 3 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Guidance 3 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

Adequate separation should be made between any destinations or group of destinations in one direction and those in other directions by suitable design of the arrow, spacing of lines of legend, heavy lines entirely across the sign, or separate signs.

title: Section 2D.36 Support 4 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Support 4 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

Separation of destinations by direction by the use of a horizontal separator line can enhance the readability of a Destination sign by relating an arrow and its corresponding destination(s) and by eliminating the need for multiple arrows that point in the same direction and excessive space between lines of legend.

title: Section 2D.36 Standard 5 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Standard 5 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, an arrow pointing to the right shall be at the extreme right of the sign, and an arrow pointing left or up shall be at the extreme left. The distance numerals, if used, shall be placed to the right of the destination names.

title: Section 2D.36 Option 6 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Option 6 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

An arrow pointing up may be placed at the extreme right of the sign when the sign is mounted to the left of the traffic to which it applies.

title: Section 2D.36 Guidance 7 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Guidance 7 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

Unless a sloping arrow will convey a clearer indication of the direction to be followed, the directional arrows should be horizontal or vertical.

title: Section 2D.36 Guidance 8 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Guidance 8 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 232

If several individual name signs are assembled into a group, all signs in the assembly should be of the same horizontal width.

title: Section 2D.36 Guidance 9 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Guidance 9 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 233

Destination signs should be used: A. At the intersections of U.S. or State numbered routes with Interstate, U.S., or State numbered routes; and B. At points where they serve to direct traffic from U.S. or State numbered routes to the business section of towns, or to other destinations reached by unnumbered routes. Month 2023 Figure 2D-9. Destination and Distance Signs

title: Section 2D.36 Standard 10 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Standard 10 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 233

Where a total of three or fewer destinations are displayed on the Advance guide (see Section 2E.23) and Supplemental guide (see Section 2E.51) signs, no more than three destination names shall be displayed on a Destination sign. Where four destinations are displayed on the Advance guide and Supplemental guide signs, no more than four destination names shall be displayed on a Destination sign.

title: Section 2D.36 Guidance 11 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Guidance 11 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 233

If space permits, four destinations should be displayed on two separate signs at two separate locations.

title: Section 2D.36 Option 12 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Option 12 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 233

Where space does not permit, or where all four destinations are in one direction, a single sign may be used. Where a single sign is used and all destinations are in the same direction, the arrow may be placed below the destinations for the purpose of enhancing the conspicuity of the arrow.

title: Section 2D.36 Standard 13 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Standard 13 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Where a single four-name sign assembly is used, a heavy line approximating the width of the sign border entirely across the sign or separate signs shall be used to separate destinations by direction. Month 2023

title: Section 2D.36 Guidance 14 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Guidance 14 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

The closest destination lying straight ahead should be at the top of the sign or assembly, and below it the closest destinations to the left and to the right, in that order. The destination displayed for each direction should ordinarily be the next county seat or the next principal city, rather than a more distant destination. In the case of overlapping routes, only one destination should be displayed in each direction for each route.

title: Section 2D.36 Standard 15 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Standard 15 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

If more than one destination is displayed in the same direction, the name of a nearer destination shall be displayed above the name of a destination that is farther away.

title: Section 2D.36 Support 16 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Support 16 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Overhead destination guide signs are sometimes helpful on multi-lane conventional roadways with complex or unusual roadway alignments or geometrics at intersecting highways to provide positive direction to destinations and to assign lanes to be used for destinations.

title: Section 2D.36 Option 17 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Option 17 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Overhead Destination signs may be used to provide lane assignment and destination information for some or all of the lanes on the approach to a multi-lane intersection. Destination information may include cardinal directions, route numbers, street names, and/or place names.

title: Section 2D.36 Option 18 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
text:
Section 2D.36 Option 18 - Destination Signs (D1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Overhead signs using the Arrow-per-Lane sign design configuration (see Figure 2D-10) may be used to provide lane assignments for some or all lane destinations at the approach to a multi-lane intersection (see Section 2D.37).

title: Section 2D.37 Support 1 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Support 1 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Overhead Arrow-per-Lane destination guide signs are sometimes used on multi-lane conventional roadways to provide positive direction to destinations and to indicate lanes to be used for those destinations. These locations typically include complex or unusual roadway alignments or geometrics. Overhead Arrow-per-Lane signs on conventional roads do not always have arrows for every lane. Sheet 2 of Figure 2A-4 and Sheet 1 of Figure 2D-10 show examples of the use of an Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Guide sign on a conventional road. Unlike the Combined Lane-Use/Destination (D15-1) sign (see Section 2D.38), Overhead Arrow-per-Lane signs can be used to provide lane assignments where the designated lane is not a mandatory movement lane.

title: Section 2D.37 Option 2 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Option 2 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

At complex intersection approaches involving multiple lanes and destinations, an Overhead Arrow-per- Lane destination guide sign may be used to provide destination information for some or all lanes. Destination information may include cardinal direction, route numbers, street names, and/or place names.

title: Section 2D.37 Standard 3 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Standard 3 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Overhead Arrow-per-Lane signs for conventional roads shall only be used for multi-lane approaches to intersections that have an option lane.

title: Section 2D.37 Standard 4 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Standard 4 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Overhead Arrow-per-Lane guide signs used on conventional roads shall include as a minimum one arrow above each mandatory turn lane and a bifurcated arrow for the option lane from which both the through and turning movements are allowed.

title: Section 2D.37 Guidance 5 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Guidance 5 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 234

Displaying an arrow over each through movement lane that does not allow turning should be considered for providing additional positive guidance.

title: Section 2D.37 Standard 6 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Standard 6 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 235

Overhead Arrow-per-Lane signs for conventional roads shall be designed in accordance with the following criteria: A. The shaft of each arrow shall be located over the approximate center of the lane to which it applies. B. Arrows for continuing through lanes shall be vertically upward-pointing (see Figure 2D-10). C. The arrow for a lane that must turn shall be curved in the direction of the turn and shall be accompanied by a black-on-yellow ONLY (E11-1b) sign panel (see Figure 2E-17) adjacent to the lower end of the arrow shaft. D. The arrow for an optional exit lane that also carries the through route shall have a single shaft that bifurcates into a vertically upward-pointing arrow and a curving arrow corresponding to the configuration of the through and turn lanes. E. A vertical white line shall be used to separate the route shields and destinations for the two diverging movements from each other. F. The number of lanes displayed on a sign shall correspond to the number of lanes being signed for at the location of that sign. An advance sign shall not depict lanes that are added downstream of a sign location. Month 2023 Figure 2D-10. Examples of Overhead Signs at an Intersection (Sheet 1 of 3) A - Combination of mandatory and optional movement lanes * Overhead Arrow-per Lane guide sign only for destinations that include an optional movement lane ** Conventional guide sign for destinations with one or more mandatory movement lanes

title: Section 2D.37 Guidance 7 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Guidance 7 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 235

Overhead Arrow-per-Lane guide signs used on conventional roads should be designed in accordance with the following additional criteria: A. No more than one destination should be displayed for each movement, and no more than three destinations should be displayed per sign. B. The arrowhead(s) for the diverging movement should be positioned lower on the sign than the arrowhead(s) for the movement that continues straight ahead. C. Route shields, cardinal directions, and destinations should be positioned on the sign such that they are clearly related to the arrowhead(s) for the movement to which they apply. D. The vertical white line that is used to separate the route shields and destinations for the two diverging movements from each other should not descend below the top of the arrowheads for the through lanes, and should be positioned approximately halfway between the diverging arrowheads for the optional movement lane.

title: Section 2D.37 Guidance 8 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Guidance 8 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 236

Destination information should be kept to a minimum necessary to provide positive guidance without overloading the road user. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2D-10. Examples of Overhead Signs at an Intersection (Sheet 2 of 3) B - Mandatory movement lanes

title: Section 2D.37 Standard 9 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Standard 9 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 236

The minimum height of arrows on an Overhead Arrow-per-Lane sign used on a conventional road shall be as shown in Table 2D-5.

title: Section 2D.37 Guidance 10 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Guidance 10 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 236

When letter heights and other sign legend elements are enlarged there should be a corresponding increase in the arrow size used.

title: Section 2D.37 Option 32 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Option 32 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 236

25.333

title: Section 2D.37 Option 11 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Option 11 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 236

Curved-stem arrows may be substituted on Overhead Arrow-per- Lane signs on multi-lane approaches to a circular intersection with an option lane (see Section 2D.39). Rev. 1 10.67 25.5 20.188

title: Section 2D.37 Option 21 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
text:
Section 2D.37 Option 21 - Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination Guide Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 237

16.625 Note: Letter and arrow heights are shown in inches. Month 2023 December 2025 Figure 2D-10. Examples of Overhead Signs at an Intersection (Sheet 3 of 3) C - Mandatory movement lanes with dual turn lanes

title: Section 2D.38 Option 1 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
text:
Section 2D.38 Option 1 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 237

At intersection approaches involving multiple turn lanes and destinations, a Combination Lane-Use/ Destination (D15-1) overhead guide sign (see Figure 2D-9) that combines a lane-use regulatory sign with destination information such as a cardinal direction, a route number, a street name, and/or a place name may be used.

title: Section 2D.38 Support 2 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
text:
Section 2D.38 Support 2 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 237

At such locations, the combined information on the D15-1 signs can be even more effective than separate lane- use and guide signs for conveying to unfamiliar drivers which lane or lanes to use for a particular destination.

title: Section 2D.38 Support 3 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
text:
Section 2D.38 Support 3 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Figure 2D-9 shows an example of a D15-1 sign that combines lane-use and street name information and an example of a D15-1 sign that combines lane-use, cardinal direction, and route number information. Month 2023

title: Section 2D.38 Standard 4 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
text:
Section 2D.38 Standard 4 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

The Combination Lane-Use/Destination (D15-1) overhead guide sign shall be used only where the designated lane is a mandatory movement lane. The D15-1 sign shall not be used for lanes with optional movements.

title: Section 2D.38 Standard 5 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
text:
Section 2D.38 Standard 5 - Combination Lane-Use/Destination Overhead Guide Sign (D15-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

The D15-1 sign shall have a green background with a white border. As shown in Figure 2D-9, the lane- use sign (see Chapter 2B) shall be placed near the bottom of the sign and the destination information shall be placed near the top of the sign. The D15-1 sign shall be located over the approximate center of the lane to which it applies.

title: Section 2D.39 Standard 1 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Standard 1 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Destination signs that are used at circular intersections shall comply with the provisions of Section 2D.36, except as provided in this Section.

title: Section 2D.39 Option 2 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Option 2 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Exit Destination (D1-1d and D1-1e) signs (see Figure 2D-11) with diagonal upward-pointing arrows or Directional assemblies (see Section 2D.32) may be used to designate a particular exit from a circular intersection.

title: Section 2D.39 Option 3 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Option 3 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Destination (D1-2d and D1-3d) signs (see Figure 2D-11) with curved-stem arrows may be used on approaches to circular intersections to represent the left-turn movements.

title: Section 2D.39 Option 4 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Option 4 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Curved-stem arrows on circular intersection destination signs may point in diagonal directions to depict the location of an exit relative to the approach roadway and entry into the intersection.

title: Section 2D.39 Option 5 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Option 5 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

An Overhead Arrow-per-Lane Destination sign (see Section 2D.37) with curved-stem arrows may be used on multi-lane approaches to circular intersections that have an option lane.

title: Section 2D.39 Option 6 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Option 6 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

A Destination (D1-5 or D1-5a) sign (see Figure 2D-11) with a diagram of the circular intersection may be used on approaches to circular intersections.

title: Section 2D.39 Guidance 7 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Guidance 7 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

If curved-stem arrows are used on destination signs, then this arrow type should also be used consistently on any regulatory lane-use signs (see Chapter 2B), Directional assemblies (see Section 2D.32), and pavement markings (see Part 3) for a particular destination or movement.

title: Section 2D.39 Support 8 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Support 8 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Figure 2D-12 shows examples of guide signing for circular intersections.

title: Section 2D.39 Support 9 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Support 9 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Circular Intersection Diagrammatic (D1-5 or D1-5a) signs might be preferable where space is available and where the geometry of the circular intersection is non-typical, such as where more than four legs are present or where the legs are not at approximately 90-degree angles to each other. In such cases, minimizing the amount of legend for each destination and designing the sign so that the arrows for each destination clearly align with the roadway geometry will aid road user understanding of the sign and navigation through the area.

title: Section 2D.39 Standard 10 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Standard 10 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

If used, the Circular Intersection Diagrammatic signs shall not depict the number of lanes within the circulatory roadway of the intersection, or on its approaches or exits, through the use of lane lines, multiple arrow shafts for the same movement, or other methods.

title: Section 2D.39 Support 11 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
text:
Section 2D.39 Support 11 - Destination Signs at Circular Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Chapter 2B contains information regarding regulatory signs at circular intersections, Chapter 2C contains information regarding warning signs at circular intersections, and Chapter 3D contains information regarding pavement markings at circular intersections.

title: Section 2D.40 Standard 1 - Destination Signs at Jughandles
text:
Section 2D.40 Standard 1 - Destination Signs at Jughandles
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

Destination signs that are used at jughandles shall comply with the provisions of Section 2D.36.

title: Section 2D.41 Guidance 1 - Destination Signs at Intersections with Indirect Turning Movements
text:
Section 2D.41 Guidance 1 - Destination Signs at Intersections with Indirect Turning Movements
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 238

A system of guide signs along with associated lane markings should be used to direct traffic through intersections with indirect turning movements.

text:
Section 2D.41 Support 2 - Destination Signs at Intersections with Indirect Turning Movements
Part: Part 2 Signs

title: Section 2D.42 Guidance 1 - Location of Destination Signs
text:
Section 2D.42 Guidance 1 - Location of Destination Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

When used in high-speed areas, Destination signs should be located 200 feet or more in advance of the intersection, and following any Junction or Advance Route Turn assemblies that might be required. In rural areas, the minimum distance between a Destination sign and either an Advance Route Turn assembly or a Junction assembly should be 200 feet.

title: Section 2D.42 Option 2 - Location of Destination Signs
text:
Section 2D.42 Option 2 - Location of Destination Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

In urban areas, advance distances shorter than those specified in Paragraph 1 of this Section may be used.

title: Section 2D.42 Option 3 - Location of Destination Signs
text:
Section 2D.42 Option 3 - Location of Destination Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

Because the Destination sign is of lesser importance than the Junction, Advance Route Turn, or Directional assemblies, the Destination sign may be eliminated where the distance in which to provide adequate sign spacing is limited.

title: Section 2D.42 Support 4 - Location of Destination Signs
text:
Section 2D.42 Support 4 - Location of Destination Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

Figure 2D-8 shows typical placements of Destination signs.

title: Section 2D.43 Standard 1 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Standard 1 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

If used, the Distance (D2-1 through D2-3) signs (see Figure 2D-9) shall be a horizontal rectangle of a size appropriate for the required legend, displaying the names of no more than three cities, towns, junctions, or other traffic generators, and the distance (to the nearest mile) to those places.

title: Section 2D.43 Standard 2 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Standard 2 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

The distance numerals shall be placed to the right of the destination names as shown in Figure 2D-9.

title: Section 2D.43 Guidance 3 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Guidance 3 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

The distance displayed should be selected on a case-by-case basis by the jurisdiction that owns the road or by statewide policy. A well-defined central area or central business district should be used where one exists. In other cases, the layout of the community should be considered in relation to the highway being signed and the decision based on where it appears that most drivers would feel that they are in the center of the community in question.

title: Section 2D.43 Guidance 4 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Guidance 4 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 239

The top name on the Distance sign should be that of the next place on the route having a post office or a railroad station, a route number or name of an intersected highway, or any other significant geographical identity. The bottom name on the sign should be that of the next major destination or control city. If three destinations are displayed, the middle line should be used to indicate communities of general interest along the route or important route junctions.

title: Section 2D.43 Option 5 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Option 5 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 243

The choice of names for the middle line may be varied on successive Distance signs to give road users additional information concerning communities served by the route. Month 2023 Figure 2D-12. Examples of Guide Signs for Circular Intersections (Sheet 1 of 4) Notes: 1. The spacings shown on this figure are for rural intersections. See Sections 2D.29, 2D.30, 2D.31, 2D.32, 2D.33, 2D.42, and 2D.44 for low-speed and/or urban conditions. 2. Signs shown for only one direction. See Chapter 2B for regulatory signs and Chapter 2C for warning signs at circular intersections. See Chapter 3D for details on markings. Month 2023 Figure 2D-12. Examples of Guide Signs for Circular Intersections (Sheet 2 of 4) Notes: 1. The spacings shown on this figure are for rural intersections. See Sections 2D.29, 2D.30, 2D.31, 2D.32, 2D.33, 2D.42, and 2D.44 for low-speed and/or urban conditions. 2. Signs shown for only one direction. See Chapter 2B for regulatory signs and Chapter 2C for warning signs at circular intersections. See Chapter 3D for details on markings. Month 2023 Figure 2D-12. Examples of Guide Signs for Circular Intersections (Sheet 3 of 4) Notes: 1. The spacings shown on this figure are for rural intersections. See Sections 2D.29, 2D.30, 2D.31, 2D.32, 2D.33, 2D.42, and 2D.44 for low-speed and/or urban conditions. 2. Signs shown for only one direction. See Chapter 2B for regulatory signs and Chapter 2C for warning signs at circular intersections. See Chapter 3D for details on markings. Month 2023 Figure 2D-12. Examples of Guide Signs for Circular Intersections (Sheet 4 of 4) Note: Signs shown for only one direction. See Chapter 2B for regulatory signs and Chapter 2C for warning signs at circular intersections. See Chapter 3D for details on markings.

title: Section 2D.43 Guidance 6 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Guidance 6 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 243

The control city should remain the same on all successive Distance signs throughout the length of the route until that city is reached.

title: Section 2D.43 Option 7 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Option 7 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 243

If more than one distant point may properly be designated, such as where the route divides at some distance ahead to serve two destinations of similar importance, and if these two destinations cannot appear on the same sign, the two names may be alternated on successive signs.

title: Section 2D.43 Option 8 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.43 Option 8 - Distance Signs (D2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 243

On a route continuing into another State, destinations in the adjacent State may be displayed.

title: Section 2D.44 Guidance 1 - Location of Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.44 Guidance 1 - Location of Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 243

If used, Distance signs should be installed on important routes leaving municipalities and just beyond intersections of numbered routes in rural areas. If used, they should be placed just outside the municipal limits or at the edge of the built-up area if it extends beyond the limits.

title: Section 2D.44 Guidance 2 - Location of Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.44 Guidance 2 - Location of Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 243

Where overlapping routes separate a short distance from the municipal limits, the Distance sign at the municipal limits should be omitted. The Distance sign should be installed approximately 300 feet beyond the separation of the two routes.

title: Section 2D.44 Guidance 3 - Location of Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.44 Guidance 3 - Location of Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 243

Where, just outside of an incorporated municipality, two routes are concurrent and continue concurrently to the next incorporated municipality, the top name on the Distance sign should be that of the place where the routes separate; the bottom name should be that of the city to which the greater part of the through traffic is destined.

title: Section 2D.44 Support 4 - Location of Distance Signs
text:
Section 2D.44 Support 4 - Location of Distance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 247

Figures 2D-7 and 2D-8 show typical placements of Distance signs. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2D-13. Examples of Signing for Intersections with Indirect Left Turns (Sheet 1 of 3) A - Intercepted crossroad with left turns prohibited Rev. 1 Rev. 1 Month 2023 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2D-13. Examples of Signing for Intersections with Indirect Left Turns (Sheet 2 of 3) B - Intercepted crossroad with left turns prohibited Rev. 1 Month 2023 December 2025 Figure 2D-13. Examples of Signing for Intersections with Indirect Left Turns (Sheet 3 of 3) C - Continuous flow intersection Month 2023 STREET NAME AND PARKING SIGNS

title: Section 2D.45 Support 1 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Support 1 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 247

Street Name signs at intersections and along roadways provide road users with important navigation information. Section 2H.10 contains information about signs used to identify the names of grade-separated streets, railways, bikeways, or other transportation facilities.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 2 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 2 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 247

Street Name (D3-1 or D3-1a) signs (see Figure 2D-14) should be installed in urban areas at all street intersections regardless of other route signs that might be present and should be installed in rural areas to identify important roads that are not otherwise signed.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 3 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 3 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 247

To minimize wrong-way movements onto freeway or expressway exit ramps, Street Name signs should not be used at the intersection of a freeway or expressway exit ramp with the crossroad to display the name of the freeway or expressway to traffic on the crossroad.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 4 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 4 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 247

For streets that are part of a U.S., State, or county numbered route, a D3-1a Street Name sign (see Figure 2D-14) that incorporates a route shield may be used to assist road users who might not otherwise be able to associate the name of the street with the route number.

title: Section 2D.45 Standard 5 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Standard 5 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 247

The lettering for names of streets and highways on Street Name signs shall be composed of a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters (see Section 2A.08).

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 6 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 6 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 247

The determination of letter heights to be used on Street Name signs should be based on, but not limited to, the following considerations: A. Use of Advance Street Name signs (see Section 2D.46); B. Number of lanes on the intersection approach; C. Length of turn lanes; D. Distance the Street Name sign is located across the intersection (if a sign is not provided on the near side of the intersection).

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 7 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 7 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

Letter heights on street name signs should be as shown in Table 2D-6. Figure 2D-14. Street Name and Parking Signs Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Table 2D-6. Minimum Letter Heights on Street Name Signs Recommended Minimum Type of Mounting Type of Street or Letter Height * Highway Speed Limit Initial Upper-Case Lower-Case Overhead All types All speed limits 12 inches 9 inches Post-mounted Multi-lane More than 40 mph 8 inches 6 inches Post-mounted Multi-lane 40 mph or less 6 inches 4.5 inches Post-mounted 2-lane All speed limits 6 inches** 4.5 inches** * Letter heights shown are for the street name. Descriptors or other supplementary legend may be displayed in smaller lettering of at least 3 inches. ** On two-lane local streets with speed limits of 25 mph or less, 4-inch initial upper-case letters with 3-inch lower-case letters may be used.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 8 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 8 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

For two-lane local roadways with speed limits of 25 mph or less, the lettering on post-mounted Street Name signs may be composed of initial upper-case letters at least 4 inches in height and lower-case letters at least 3 inches in nominal loop height.

title: Section 2D.45 Support 9 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Support 9 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

The recommended minimum letter heights for Street Name signs are summarized in Table 2D-6. The speed limits specified and the recommended minimum letter heights provided in this Section apply to the roadway that each Street Name sign faces rather than to the street that has its name displayed on the Street Name sign. The letter heights specified in Table 2D-6 are the combination of lower-case letters with the initial upper-case letter of a mixed-case legend. Rev. 1

title: Section 2D.45 Support 10 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Support 10 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

A minimum upper-case letter height of 12 inches with a lower-case nominal loop height of 9 inches is recommended for all overhead Street Name signs regardless of posted speed limit as Street Name signs generally require greater legibility distances for road users to properly react.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 11 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 11 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

Each Street Name sign in a sign assembly may use different letter heights determined by the speed limit of the street that each sign faces.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 12 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 12 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

The letter height of the street name descriptor (such as St, Ave, or Rd), the directional legend (such as NW), or any other supplemental legend (such as block or house numbers) on the D3-1 and D3-1a signs may be smaller than that of the street name itself.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 13 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 13 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

The letter height of the street name descriptor, the directional legend, or any other supplemental legend on the D3-1 and D3-1a signs should be at least two-thirds of the letter height of the street name itself, but not less than 3 inches for the initial upper-case letters and not less than 2.25 inches for the nominal loop height of the lower-case letters.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 14 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 14 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

Conventional abbreviations (see Section 1D.08) should be used except for the street name itself. Acceptable abbreviations for street name descriptors such as “Ave” for Avenue and “Blvd” for Boulevard should be as provided in Table 2D-3 (see Section 2D.07). The street name descriptors that are provided in Table 2D-4 should not be abbreviated (see Section 2D.07).

title: Section 2D.45 Option 15 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 15 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

Block or house numbers may be displayed as a supplemental legend on a Street Name sign to aid emergency responders and road users in locating addresses.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 16 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 16 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

If block or house numbers are displayed on a Street Name sign where only a single Street Name sign is provided for the crossroad, the block or house numbers for the left and right blocks should be positioned at the left and right sides of the sign, respectively.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 17 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 17 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 248

If block or house numbers are displayed on a Street Name sign where two Street Name signs are provided for the crossroad, such as on diagonally opposite corners of an intersection, each Street Name sign should display only the block or house numbers associated with that block of the crossroad.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 18 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 18 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

A pictograph (see definition in Section 1C.02) representing the municipality, in accordance with the provisions of Section 2A.04, may be used on a D3-1 sign. For street networks under the primary jurisdiction of another governmental-approved entity, such as within a college or university campus, within a military base, or within a transportation facility (such as an airport or port), a pictograph representing that entity, in accordance with the provisions of Section 2A.04, may be used on a D3-1 sign within the jurisdictional boundaries of that entity. Month 2023 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 2D.45 Standard 19 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Standard 19 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

Pictographs shall not be displayed on D3-1a or Advance Street Name (D3-2) signs (see Section 2D.46).

title: Section 2D.45 Standard 20 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Standard 20 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

If a pictograph is used on a D3-1 sign, the height and width of the pictograph shall not exceed the upper- case letter height of the principal legend of the sign.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 21 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 21 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

The pictograph should be positioned to the left of the street name.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 22 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 22 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

Pictographs should not be used on a D3-1 sign that contains directional arrows.

title: Section 2D.45 Standard 23 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Standard 23 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

The Street Name sign shall be retroreflective or illuminated in accordance with the provisions of Section 2A.21.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 24 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 24 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

The border may be omitted from a post-mounted Street Name sign.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 25 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 25 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

The decision to omit the border from a post-mounted Street Name sign should be based on such factors as the visual complexity of the environment and the degree of conspicuity needed to provide for adequate recognition of the sign by the road user.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 26 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 26 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

An alternative background color (see Paragraph 28 of this Section) other than the standard guide sign color of green may be used for Street Name (D3-1 or D3-1a) signs where the highway agency determines this is necessary to assist road users in determining jurisdictional authority for roads.

title: Section 2D.45 Standard 27 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Standard 27 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

Alternative background colors shall not be used for Advance Street Name (D3-2) signs (see Section 2D.46).

title: Section 2D.45 Standard 28 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Standard 28 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

The only acceptable alternative background colors for Street Name (D3-1 or D3-1a) signs shall be blue, brown, or white. Regardless of whether green, blue, or brown is used as the background color for Street Name (D3-1 or D3-1a) signs, the legend (and border, if used) shall be white. For Street Name signs that use a white background, the legend (and border, if used) shall be black.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 29 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 29 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

An alternative background color for Street Name signs, if used, should be applied to the Street Name (D3-1 or D3-1a) signs on all roadways under the jurisdiction of a particular highway agency.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 30 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 30 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

In business or commercial areas and on principal arterials, Street Name signs should be placed at least on diagonally opposite corners. In residential areas, at least one Street Name sign should be mounted at each intersection. Signs naming both streets should be installed at each intersection. They should be mounted with their faces parallel to the streets they name.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 31 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 31 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

Where used, Street Name signs should display their legends on both the front and back sides of the sign to facilitate navigation for pedestrians.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 32 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 32 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

To optimize visibility, Street Name signs may be mounted overhead. Street Name signs may also be placed above a regulatory or STOP or YIELD sign with no required vertical separation.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 33 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 33 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

In urban or suburban areas, especially where Advance Street Name signs for signalized and other major intersections are not used, the use of overhead Street Name signs should be strongly considered.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 34 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 34 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

At intersection crossroads where the same road has two different street names for each direction of travel, both street names may be displayed on the same Street Name (D3-1) sign along with Type D directional arrows, except where one arrow would point in a direction opposing the flow of traffic on a one-way street or where a turn in the direction of the arrow is not allowed.

title: Section 2D.45 Option 35 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Option 35 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 249

On lower-speed roadways, historic street name signs within locally identified historic districts that are consistent with the criteria contained in 36 CFR 60.4 for such structures and districts may remain in service without complying with the provisions of Paragraphs 5, 7, 8, 13, 14, 20, 21, 23, and 28 through 30 of this Section.

title: Section 2D.45 Guidance 36 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Guidance 36 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Streets or segments of a street that have been memorialized or dedicated should not use a second Street Name sign to display the memorial or dedication name (see Section 2D.56). When signed, the Memorial or Dedication sign should be located to minimize its conspicuity and potential for confusion. Rev. 1 Month 2023 December 2025

title: Section 2D.45 Support 37 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Support 37 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Information regarding the use of street names on supplemental plaques for use with intersection-related warning signs is contained in Section 2C.65.

title: Section 2D.45 Support 38 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
text:
Section 2D.45 Support 38 - Street Name Signs (D3-1 and D3-1a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Information regarding the identification of overcrossing and undercrossing roadways at grade separations is contained in Section 2H.10.

title: Section 2D.46 Support 1 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Support 1 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Advance Street Name (D3-2) signs (see Figure 2D-14) identify a downstream intersection. Although this is often the next intersection, it could also be several intersections away in cases where the next signalized intersection is referenced.

title: Section 2D.46 Standard 2 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Standard 2 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Advance Street Name (D3-2) signs, if used, shall supplement rather than be used instead of the Street Name (D3-1 or D3-1a) signs at the intersection.

title: Section 2D.46 Option 3 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Option 3 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Advance Street Name (D3-2) signs may be installed in advance of signalized or unsignalized intersections to provide road users with advance information to identify the name(s) of the next intersecting street to prepare for crossing traffic and to facilitate timely deceleration and/or lane changing in preparation for a turn.

title: Section 2D.46 Guidance 4 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Guidance 4 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

On arterial highways in rural areas, Advance Street Name signs should be used in advance of all signalized intersections and in advance of all intersections with mandatory turn lanes.

title: Section 2D.46 Guidance 5 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Guidance 5 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

In urban areas, Advance Street Name signs should be used in advance of all signalized intersections on major arterial streets, except where signalized intersections are so closely spaced that advance placement of the signs is impracticable.

title: Section 2D.46 Guidance 6 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Guidance 6 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

The heights of the letters on Advance Street Name signs should comply with the provisions of Section 2D.05.

title: Section 2D.46 Standard 7 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Standard 7 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

If used, Advance Street Name signs shall have a white legend and border on a green background. Alternative background colors shall not be used on Advance Street Name signs.

title: Section 2D.46 Standard 8 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Standard 8 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

If used, Advance Street Name signs shall provide the name(s) of the intersecting street(s) on the top line(s) of the legend and the distance to the intersecting streets or messages such as NEXT SIGNAL, NEXT INTERSECTION, NEXT CIRCLE, or directional arrow(s) on the bottom line of the legend.

title: Section 2D.46 Standard 9 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Standard 9 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Pictographs shall not be displayed on Advance Street Name signs.

title: Section 2D.46 Option 10 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Option 10 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

Directional arrow(s) may be placed to the right or left of the street name or message such as NEXT SIGNAL, as appropriate, rather than on the bottom line of the legend. Curved-stem arrows may be used on Advance Street Name signs on approaches to circular intersections.

title: Section 2D.46 Option 11 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Option 11 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

For intersecting crossroads where the same road has a different street name for each direction of travel, the different street names may be displayed on the same Advance Street Name sign along with directional arrows.

title: Section 2D.46 Option 12 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Option 12 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

In advance of two closely-spaced intersections where it is impracticable to install separate Advance Street Name signs, the Advance Street Name sign may include the street names for both intersections along with appropriate supplemental legends for both street names, such as NEXT INTERSECTION, 2ND INTERSECTION, or NEXT LEFT and NEXT RIGHT, or directional arrows.

title: Section 2D.46 Guidance 13 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Guidance 13 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 250

If two street names are used on the Advance Street Name sign, the street names should be displayed in the following order: A. For a single intersection where the same road has a different street name for each direction of travel, the name of the street to the left should be displayed above the name of the street to the right; or B. For two closely-spaced intersections, the name of the first street encountered should be displayed above the name of the second street encountered, and the arrow associated with the second street encountered should be an advance arrow, such as the arrow shown on the W16-6P arrow plaque (see Figure 2C-16).

title: Section 2D.46 Option 14 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
text:
Section 2D.46 Option 14 - Advance Street Name Signs (D3-2 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

An Advance Street Name (W16-8P or W16-8aP) plaque (see Section 2C.65) with black legend on a yellow background, installed to supplement an Intersection (W2 series) or Advance Traffic Control (W3 series) warning sign may be used instead of an Advance Street Name guide sign. Month 2023

title: Section 2D.47 Option 1 - Parking Area Guide Sign (D4-1)
text:
Section 2D.47 Option 1 - Parking Area Guide Sign (D4-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

The Parking Area (D4-1) guide sign (see Figure 2D-14) may be used to show the direction to a nearby public parking area or parking facility.

title: Section 2D.47 Standard 2 - Parking Area Guide Sign (D4-1)
text:
Section 2D.47 Standard 2 - Parking Area Guide Sign (D4-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

The smaller size of 18 x 15 inches for the Parking Area guide sign shall be limited to minor, low- speed streets.

title: Section 2D.47 Guidance 3 - Parking Area Guide Sign (D4-1)
text:
Section 2D.47 Guidance 3 - Parking Area Guide Sign (D4-1)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

If used, the Parking Area guide sign should be installed on major thoroughfares at the nearest point of access to the parking facility and where it can advise drivers of a place to park. The sign should not be used more than four blocks from the parking area.

title: Section 2D.48 Option 1 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
text:
Section 2D.48 Option 1 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

A PARK - RIDE (D4-2) sign (see Figure 2D-14) may be used to direct road users to park-and-ride facilities.

title: Section 2D.48 Standard 2 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
text:
Section 2D.48 Standard 2 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

The signs shall display the word message PARK - RIDE and direction information (arrow or word message).

title: Section 2D.48 Option 3 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
text:
Section 2D.48 Option 3 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

PARK - RIDE signs may display the local transit pictograph and/or carpool symbol.

title: Section 2D.48 Standard 4 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
text:
Section 2D.48 Standard 4 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

If used, the local transit pictograph and/or carpool symbol shall be located in the top part of the sign above the message PARK - RIDE. In no case shall the vertical dimension of the local transit pictograph and/or carpool symbol exceed 18 inches.

title: Section 2D.48 Guidance 5 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
text:
Section 2D.48 Guidance 5 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

If the function of the parking facility is to provide parking for persons using public transportation, the local transit pictograph should be used on the guide sign. If the function of the parking facility is to serve carpool riders, the carpool symbol should be used on the guide sign. If the parking facility serves both functions, both the pictograph and carpool symbol should be used.

title: Section 2D.48 Standard 6 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
text:
Section 2D.48 Standard 6 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 251

These signs shall have a white legend and border on a rectangular green background. The carpool symbol shall be as shown for the D4-2 sign. The color of the local transit pictograph shall be selected by the local transit authority.

title: Section 2D.48 Option 7 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
text:
Section 2D.48 Option 7 - PARK - RIDE Sign (D4-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

To increase the target value and contrast of the local transit pictograph, and to allow the local transit pictograph to retain its distinctive color and shape, the pictograph may be included within a white border or placed on a white background. Month 2023 FREEWAY INTERCHANGE APPROACH SIGNS

title: Section 2D.49 Support 1 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Support 1 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

Because there are a number of different ramp configurations that are commonly used at interchanges with conventional roads, drivers on the conventional road cannot reliably predict whether they will be required to turn left or right in order to enter the correct ramp to access the freeway or expressway in the desired direction of travel. Consistently applied signing for conventional road approaches to freeway or expressway interchanges is highly desirable.

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Standard 2 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Standard 2 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

On multi-lane conventional roads approaching an interchange, guide signs shall be provided to identify which direction of turn is to be made and/or which specific lane to use for ramp access to each direction of the freeway or expressway.

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Guidance 3 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Guidance 3 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

The signing of conventional roads with one lane of traffic approaching an interchange should consist of a sequence containing the following signs (see Figure 2D-15): A. Junction Assembly B. Destination sign C. Directional Assembly or Entrance Direction sign for the first ramp D. Advance Route Turn Assembly or Advance Entrance Direction sign with an advance turn arrow E. Directional Assembly or Entrance Direction sign for the second ramp

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Standard 4 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Standard 4 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

If used, the Entrance Direction sign shall consist of a white legend and border on a green background. It shall contain the freeway or expressway route shield(s), cardinal direction, and directional arrow(s).

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Option 5 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Option 5 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

The Entrance Direction sign may contain a destination(s) and/or an action message such as NEXT RIGHT.

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
