title: Section 2D.49 Option 6 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Option 6 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

At minor interchanges (see Section 2E.30), the following sequence of signs may be used (see Figure 2D-16): A. Junction Assembly B. Directional Assembly for the first ramp C. Directional Assembly for the second ramp

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Guidance 7 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Guidance 7 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

On multi-lane conventional roads approaching an interchange, the sign sequence should contain the following signs (see Figures 2D-17 through 2D-19): A. Junction Assembly B. Advance Entrance Direction sign(s) for both directions (if applicable) of travel on the freeway or expressway C. Entrance Direction sign for first ramp D. Advance Turn Assembly E. Entrance Direction sign for the second ramp

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Support 8 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Support 8 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

Advance Entrance Direction signs are used to direct road users to the appropriate lane(s).

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Standard 9 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Standard 9 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

The Advance Entrance Direction sign shall consist of a white legend and border on a green background. It shall contain the freeway or expressway route shield(s) and cardinal direction(s).

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Option 10 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Option 10 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 252

The Advance Entrance Direction sign may have destinations, directional arrows, and/or an action message such as KEEP LEFT, NEXT LEFT, or SECOND RIGHT. Signs in this sequence may be mounted overhead to improve visibility as shown in Figures 2D-17 through 2D-19.

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Support 11 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Support 11 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 254

A post-mounted Advance Entrance Direction diagrammatic sign (see Figure 2D-20), within the sequence of approach guide signing described in Paragraphs 3, 6, and 7 of this Section, might be helpful in depicting the location of a freeway or expressway entrance ramp that is in close proximity to an intervening intersection on the same side of the approach roadway and where signing for only the ramp might cause confusion to road users. Month 2023 Figure 2D-15. Example of Interchange Crossroad Guide Signing for a One-Lane Approach Notes: 1. Signs shown for only one direction of travel. 2. See Chapter 2B for regulatory signs and Chapter 2C for warning signs. Month 2023 Figure 2D-16. Example of Minor Interchange Crossroad Guide Signing Notes: 1. Signs shown for only one direction of travel. 2. See Chapter 2B for regulatory signs and Chapter 2C for warning signs.

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Standard 12 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Standard 12 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 254

If used, the post-mounted Advance Entrance Direction diagrammatic sign shall display only the two successive turns from the same side of the roadway, one of which shall be the entrance ramp. The post- mounted Advance Entrance Direction sign shall depict only the successive turns and shall not depict lane use with lane lines, multiple arrow shafts for the approach roadway, action messages, or other representations.

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.49 Support 13 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
text:
Section 2D.49 Support 13 - Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 254

Example guide signing for a transposed-alignment crossroad at a diamond interchange is shown in Figure 2D-21. Example guide signing for a single-point urban intersection at a diamond interchange is shown in Figure 2D-22.

metadata.section_title: Signing on Conventional Roads on Approaches to Interchanges

title: Section 2D.50 Option 1 - Freeway Entrance Signs (D13-3 and D13-3a)
text:
Section 2D.50 Option 1 - Freeway Entrance Signs (D13-3 and D13-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 254

FREEWAY ENTRANCE (D13-3) signs or FREEWAY ENTRANCE with diagonal downward-pointing arrow (D13-3a) signs (see Figure 2D-18) may be used on entrance ramps near the crossroad to inform road users of the freeway or expressway entrance, as appropriate.

title: Section 2D.50 Option 2 - Freeway Entrance Signs (D13-3 and D13-3a)
text:
Section 2D.50 Option 2 - Freeway Entrance Signs (D13-3 and D13-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 254

The D13-3 and D13-3a signs may display an alternate legend in place of FREEWAY, such as EXPRESSWAY or PARKWAY, as appropriate, or may display the name of an unnumbered highway.

title: Section 2D.50 Option 3 - Freeway Entrance Signs (D13-3 and D13-3a)
text:
Section 2D.50 Option 3 - Freeway Entrance Signs (D13-3 and D13-3a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 254

A Directional assembly (see Section 2D.32) with a diagonal downward-pointing arrow (M6-2aP) auxiliary plaque (see Section 2D.28) may be used at the far left-hand corner of an intersection with a freeway or expressway entrance ramp as an alternative to the D13-3a sign, facing left-turning traffic on the conventional road approach to indicate the immediate point of entry to the freeway or expressway and distinguish the entrance ramp from an adjoining exit ramp terminal at the same intersection with the conventional road (see Figure 2D-18). A similar Directional assembly may be used at the far right-hand corner of an intersection with a freeway or expressway entrance ramp where the entrance ramp and a crossroad or side road follow one another in close succession on the conventional road approach and the point of entry to the freeway or expressway might be difficult for the road user to distinguish from the crossroad or side road on the conventional road approach (see Figure 2D-20).

title: Section 2D.51 Support 1 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Support 1 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

Independent facilities or areas have been added along many highways where certain commercial vehicles are directed to stop to be weighed and/or inspected. These areas are sometimes permanent, such as in a roadside area, or temporary mobile facilities deployed along the roadway.

title: Section 2D.51 Support 2 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Support 2 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

The general concept for signing permanent Weigh Stations is similar to signing Rest Areas (see Section 2I.05) because in both cases traffic using either area remains within the right-of-way.

title: Section 2D.51 Standard 3 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Standard 3 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

The standard sequence of signs for a Weigh Station on a conventional highway shall include three basic signs (see Figure 2D-23): A. Weigh Station Ahead (D8-1a) or Advance Weigh Station Distance (D8-1) sign, B. Weigh Station Advance Direction (D8-2) or Advance Weigh Station Distance (D8-1) sign, and C. Weigh Station Entrance Direction (D8-3) sign.

title: Section 2D.51 Guidance 4 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Guidance 4 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

A Gore sign with the same basic legend as the Weigh Station Entrance Direction (D8-3) sign should also be used to emphasize the entrance to the weigh station.

title: Section 2D.51 Option 5 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Option 5 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

Where State law requires trucks of a certain weight to enter the Weigh Station, a Weigh Station (R13-1) regulatory sign (see Section 2B.65) may be located following the Weigh Station Ahead sign (see Figure 2D-23). Rev. 1

title: Section 2D.51 Option 6 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Option 6 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

Where only commercial vehicle inspections are conducted in the inspection area, the WEIGH STATION legend of the D8 series signs may be replaced with the alternate legend, COMMERCIAL VEHICLE INSPECTION.

title: Section 2D.51 Guidance 7 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Guidance 7 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

The Weigh Station Advance Direction (D8-2) sign, the Weigh Station Ahead (D8-1a) sign, or the Advance Weigh Station Distance (D8-1) sign should display, either on the sign or on a supplemental plaque or sign panel, the changeable legend OPEN or CLOSED.

title: Section 2D.51 Standard 8 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
text:
Section 2D.51 Standard 8 - WEIGH STATION Signing (D8 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

When the WEIGH STATION legend of the D8 series signs is replaced with the COMMERCIAL VEHICLE INSPECTION legend, as provided in Paragraph 6 of this Section, the WEIGH STATION legend of the R13-1 sign shall likewise be replaced with the alternate legend.

title: Section 2D.52 Option 1 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
text:
Section 2D.52 Option 1 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

Crossover signs may be installed on divided highways to identify median openings not otherwise identified by warning or other guide signs.

title: Section 2D.52 Standard 2 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
text:
Section 2D.52 Standard 2 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

A Crossover (D13-1) sign (see Figure 2D-24) shall not be used to identify a median opening that is permitted to be used only by official or authorized vehicles.

title: Section 2D.52 Guidance 3 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
text:
Section 2D.52 Guidance 3 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

If used, the Crossover sign should be installed immediately beyond the median opening, either on the right- hand side of the roadway or in the median.

title: Section 2D.52 Option 4 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
text:
Section 2D.52 Option 4 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 261

The Advance Crossover (D13-2) sign (see Figure 2D-24) may be installed in advance of the Crossover sign to provide advance notice of the crossover.

title: Section 2D.52 Guidance 5 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
text:
Section 2D.52 Guidance 5 - Crossover Signs (D13-1 and D13-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 263

The distance displayed on the Advance Crossover sign should be 1 MILE, ½ MILE, or ¼ MILE, unless unusual conditions require some other distance. If used, the sign should be installed either on the right-hand side of the roadway or in the median at approximately the distance displayed on the sign. Month 2023 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2D-23. Example of Weigh Station Signing - Conventional Road The D8-1a, D8-1, or the D8-2 sign should display, either on the sign or on a supplemental plaque or sign panel, the changeable message OPEN or CLOSED. Rev. 1 An R13-1 sign (see Section 2B.65) should be used only where State law requires trucks of a certain weight to enter the weigh station. Rev. 1 Month 2023 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2D-24. Crossover Signs

title: Section 2D.53 Guidance 1 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
text:
Section 2D.53 Guidance 1 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 263

If an extra lane has been provided to the right-hand side of the travel lane for use by trucks and other slow- moving traffic, an Advance Truck Lane (D17-2) sign (see Figure 2D-25) should be installed in advance of the lane.

metadata.section_title: Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)

title: Section 2D.53 Guidance 2 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
text:
Section 2D.53 Guidance 2 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 263

If a series of truck lanes is provided along a highway, a Next Truck Lane (D17-1) sign (see Figure 2D-25) should be installed after each truck lane segment.

metadata.section_title: Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)

title: Section 2D.53 Guidance 3 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
text:
Section 2D.53 Guidance 3 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 263

If an extra lane has been provided to the left-hand side of the travel lane for passing slower moving vehicles in the travel lane, an Advance Passing Lane (D17-4) sign (see Figure 2D-25) should be installed in advance of the lane. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)

title: Section 2D.53 Guidance 4 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
text:
Section 2D.53 Guidance 4 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 263

If a series of passing lanes are provided along a highway, a Next Passing Lane (D17-3) sign (see Figure 2D-25) should be installed after each passing lane segment.

metadata.section_title: Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)

title: Section 2D.53 Support 5 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
text:
Section 2D.53 Support 5 - Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 263

An example of signing for a truck lane is shown in Figure 2D-26. An example of signing for an intermittent passing lane is shown in Figure 2D-27.

metadata.section_title: Truck and Passing Lane Signs (D17-1 through D17-4)

title: Section 2D.54 Guidance 1 - Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)
text:
Section 2D.54 Guidance 1 - Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 266

If an emergency turn-out area has been provided where a shoulder is not available for emergency stopping or where there is part-time shoulder use by traffic (see Section 2G.23), Emergency Turn-Out signs should be installed. The Advance Emergency Turn-Out (D17-5) sign (see Figure 2D-28) should be installed between ¼ mile and 500 feet in advance of the turn-out area. The Emergency Turn-Out Directional (D17-6) sign (see Figure 2D-28) should be installed near the beginning of the turn-out area. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)

title: Section 2D.54 Guidance 2 - Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)
text:
Section 2D.54 Guidance 2 - Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 266

If a slow vehicle turn-out area has been provided for slow-moving traffic, an Advance Slow Vehicle Turn-Out (D17-7) sign (see Figure 2D-28) should be installed in advance of the turn-out area.

metadata.section_title: Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)

title: Section 2D.54 Support 3 - Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)
text:
Section 2D.54 Support 3 - Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 266

An example of signing for an emergency turn-out is shown in Figure 2D-29.

metadata.section_title: Emergency and Slow Vehicle Turn-Out Signs (D17-5 through D17-7)

title: Section 2D.55 Support 1 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Support 1 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

Community wayfinding guide signs are part of a coordinated and continuous system of signs that direct tourists and other road users to key civic, cultural, visitor, and recreational attractions and other similar secondary destinations within a city or a local urbanized or downtown area.

title: Section 2D.55 Support 2 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Support 2 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

Community wayfinding guide signs are a type of destination guide sign for conventional roads with a common color and/or identification marker for destinations within an overall wayfinding guide sign plan for an area.

title: Section 2D.55 Support 3 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Support 3 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

Figures 2D-30 through 2D-32 illustrate various examples of the design and application of community wayfinding guide signs.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 4 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 4 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

The use of community wayfinding guide signs shall be limited to conventional roads. Community wayfinding guide signs shall not be installed on freeway or expressway mainlines or ramps. Direction to community wayfinding destinations from a freeway or expressway shall be limited to the use of a Supplemental guide sign (see Section 2E.51) on the mainline and a Destination sign (see Section 2D.36) on the ramp to direct road users to the area or areas within which community wayfinding guide signs are used. The individual wayfinding destinations shall not be displayed on the Supplemental guide and Destination signs except where the destinations are in accordance with the State or agency policy on Supplemental guide signs.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 5 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 5 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

Community wayfinding guide signs shall not be used to provide direction to primary destinations or highway routes or streets. Destination or other guide signs shall be used for this purpose as described elsewhere in this Chapter and shall have priority over any community wayfinding sign in placement, prominence, and conspicuity.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 6 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 6 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

Because regulatory, warning, and other guide signs have a higher priority, community wayfinding guide signs shall not be installed where adequate spacing cannot be provided between the community wayfinding guide sign and other higher-priority signs. Community wayfinding guide signs shall not be installed in a position where they would obscure the road users’ view of other traffic control devices.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 7 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 7 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

Community wayfinding guide signs shall not be mounted overhead.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 8 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 8 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 268

If used, a community wayfinding guide sign system should be established on a local municipal or equivalent jurisdictional level or for an urbanized area of adjoining municipalities or equivalent that form an identifiable geographic entity that is conducive to a cohesive and continuous system of signs. Community wayfinding guide signs should not be used on a regional or statewide basis where infrequent or sparse placement does not contribute to a continuous or coordinated system of signing that is readily identifiable as such to the road user. In such cases, Destination or other guide signs detailed in this Chapter should be used to direct road users to an identifiable area in which the type of eligible destination described in Paragraph 1 of this Section is located.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 9 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 9 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 269

When a system of community wayfinding guide signs is being considered, the system of existing guide signs should be evaluated for applicability and general compliance with the provisions of this Manual to ensure road user directional guidance is adequately being addressed. Figure 2D-30. Examples of Community Wayfinding Guide Signs Month 2023 Figure 2D-31. Example of a Community Wayfinding Guide Sign System Showing Direction from a Freeway or Expressway

title: Section 2D.55 Support 10 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Support 10 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 269

The specific provisions of this Section regarding the design of community wayfinding sign legends apply to vehicular community wayfinding signs and do not apply to those signs that are intended only to provide information or direction to pedestrians or other users of a sidewalk or roadside area.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 11 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 11 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 270

Because pedestrian wayfinding signs typically use smaller legends that are inadequately sized for viewing by vehicular traffic and because they can provide direction to pedestrians that might conflict with that appropriate for vehicular traffic, wayfinding signs designed for and intended to provide direction to pedestrians or other users of a sidewalk or other roadside area should be located to minimize their conspicuity to vehicular traffic. Such signs should be located as far as practicable from the street, such as at the far edge of the sidewalk. Where locating such signs farther from the roadway is impracticable, the pedestrian wayfinding signs should have their conspicuity to vehicular traffic minimized by employing one or a combination of the following methods: A. Locating signs away from intersections where high-priority traffic control devices are present. B. Facing the pedestrian message toward the sidewalk and away from the street. C. Cantilevering the sign over the sidewalk if the pedestrian wayfinding sign is mounted at a height consistent with vehicular traffic signs, removing the pedestrian wayfinding signs from the line of sight in a sequence of vehicular signs. Month 2023 Figure 2D-32. Example of a Color-Coded Community Wayfinding Guide Sign System

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 12 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 12 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 270

To further minimize their conspicuity to vehicular traffic during nighttime conditions, pedestrian wayfinding signs should not be retroreflective.

title: Section 2D.55 Support 13 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Support 13 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 270

Color coding is sometimes used on community wayfinding guide signs to help road users distinguish between multiple potentially confusing traffic generator destinations located in different neighborhoods or subareas within a community or area.

title: Section 2D.55 Option 14 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Option 14 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 270

At the boundaries of the geographical area within which community wayfinding guide signing is used, an informational guide sign may be posted to inform road users about the presence of wayfinding signing and to identify the meanings of the various color codes or pictographs that are being used.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 15 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 15 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 270

These informational guide signs shall have a white legend and border on a green background and shall have a design similar to that illustrated in Figure 2D-1 and shall be consistent with the basic design principles for guide signs. These informational guide signs shall not be installed on freeway or expressway mainlines or ramps.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 16 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 16 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

The color coding or a pictograph of the identification markers of the community wayfinding guide signing system shall be included on the informational guide sign posted at the boundary of the community wayfinding guide signing area. The color coding or pictographs shall apply to a specific, identifiable neighborhood or geographical subarea within the overall area covered by the community wayfinding guide signing. Color coding or pictographs shall not be used to distinguish between different types of destinations that are within the same designated neighborhood or subarea. The color coding shall be accomplished by the use of different colored square or rectangular panels on the face of the informational guide sign, each positioned to the left of the neighborhood or named geographic area to which the color-coding panel applies. The height of the colored square or rectangular panels shall not exceed 2 times the height of the upper-case letters of the principal legend on the sign. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 2D.55 Option 17 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Option 17 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

The different colored square or rectangular panels may include either a black or a white (whichever provides the better contrast with the color of the panel) letter, numeral, or other appropriate designation to identify the destination.

title: Section 2D.55 Option 18 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Option 18 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Except for the informational guide sign posted at the boundary of the wayfinding guide sign area, community wayfinding guide signs may use background colors other than green in order to provide a color identification for the wayfinding destinations by geographical area within the overall wayfinding guide signing system. Color-coded community wayfinding guide signs may be used with or without the boundary informational guide sign displaying corresponding color-coding panels described in Paragraphs 13 through 16 of this Section. Except as provided in Paragraph 19 of this Section, in addition to the colors that are approved in this Manual for use on official traffic control signs (see Section 2A.06), other background colors may also be used for the color coding of community wayfinding guide signs.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 19 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 19 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

The standard colors of red, orange, yellow, purple, or the fluorescent versions thereof, fluorescent yellow-green, and fluorescent pink shall not be used as background colors for community wayfinding guide signs, in order to minimize possible confusion with critical, higher-priority regulatory and warning sign color meanings readily understood by road users.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 20 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 20 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

The minimum contrast value of legend color to background color for community wayfinding guide signs shall be at least 0.70 (or 70%).

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 21 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 21 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

All messages, borders, legends, and backgrounds of community wayfinding guide signs and any identification markers shall be retroreflective (see Sections 2A.21 and 2A.22).

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 22 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 22 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Community wayfinding guide signs, exclusive of any identification marker used, shall be rectangular in shape.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 23 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 23 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Simplicity and uniformity in design, position, and application as described in Section 2A.04 are important and should be incorporated into the community wayfinding guide sign design and location plans for the area.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 24 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 24 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Community wayfinding guide signs should be limited to three destinations per sign (see Section 2D.06).

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 25 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 25 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Abbreviations (see Section 1D.08) should be kept to a minimum, and should include only those that are commonly recognized and understood.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 26 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 26 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Horizontal lines of a color that contrasts with the sign background color should be used to separate groups of destinations by direction from each other.

title: Section 2D.55 Support 27 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Support 27 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

The basic requirement for all highway signs, including community wayfinding signs, is that they be legible to those for whom they are intended and that they be understandable in time to permit a proper response. Section 2A.04 contains additional information on the design of signs, including desirable attributes of effective designs.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 28 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 28 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Word messages should be as brief as practical and the lettering should be large enough to provide the necessary legibility distance.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 29 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 29 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

The minimum specific ratio of letter height to legibility distance shall comply with the provisions of Section 2A.08. The size of lettering used for destination and directional legends on community wayfinding signs shall comply with the provisions of minimum letter heights as provided in Section 2D.05.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 30 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 30 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Interline and edge spacing shall comply with the provisions of Section 2D.05.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 31 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 31 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Except as provided in Paragraph 34 of this Section, the lettering style used for destination and directional legends on community wayfinding guide signs shall comply with the provisions of Section 2D.04.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 32 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 32 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

The lettering for destinations on community wayfinding guide signs shall be a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters (see Section 2D.04). All other word messages on community wayfinding guide signs shall be in all upper-case letters.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 33 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 33 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 271

Except as provided in Paragraphs 34 and 35 of this Section, letters, numerals, and other characters should be composed of the Standard Alphabets as detailed in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05).

title: Section 2D.55 Option 34 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Option 34 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

A lettering style other than the Standard Alphabets provided in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05) may be used on community wayfinding guide signs if an engineering study determines that the legibility and recognition values for the chosen lettering style meet or exceed the values for the Standard Alphabets for the same legend height and stroke width. Rev. 1 Month 2023 December 2025

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 35 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 35 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

If a lettering style other than the Standard Alphabets is used, the alternative lettering style shall be conventional in form. The letters, numerals, and other characters shall not be italic, oblique, script, highly decorative, or of other unusual forms.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 36 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 36 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

In accordance with Section 2A.04, except for signs that are designed and located with the intent to be viewed only by pedestrians, bicyclists stopped out of the flow of traffic, or occupants of parked vehicles, Internet and e-mail addresses, including domain names and uniform resource locators (URL), and scanning graphics for the purpose of obtaining information (see Section 2A.04), shall not be displayed on any community wayfinding guide sign or sign assembly.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 37 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 37 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

The arrow location and priority order of destinations shall follow the provisions described in Sections 2D.08 and 2D.36. Arrows shall be of the designs provided in Section 2D.08.

title: Section 2D.55 Option 38 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Option 38 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

Pictographs (see definition in Section 1C.02) may be used on community wayfinding guide signs.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 39 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 39 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

If a pictograph is used, its height shall not exceed 2 times the height of the upper-case letters of the principal legend on the sign.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 40 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 40 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

Except for pictographs, symbols that are not approved in this Manual for use on guide signs shall not be used on community wayfinding guide signs.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 41 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 41 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

Business logos, commercial graphics, or other forms of advertising (see Section 1D.07) shall not be used on community wayfinding guide signs or sign assemblies.

title: Section 2D.55 Option 42 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Option 42 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

Other graphics that specifically identify the wayfinding system, including identification markers, may be used on the overall sign assembly and sign supports.

title: Section 2D.55 Support 43 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Support 43 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

An identification marker consists of a shape, color, and/or pictograph that is used as a visual identifier for the community wayfinding guide signing system for an area. Figure 2D-30 shows examples of identification marker designs that can be used with community wayfinding guide signs.

title: Section 2D.55 Option 44 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Option 44 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

An identification marker may be used in a community wayfinding guide sign assembly, or may be incorporated into the overall design of a community wayfinding guide sign, as a means of visually identifying the sign as part of an overall system of community wayfinding signs and destinations.

title: Section 2D.55 Standard 45 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Standard 45 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

The sizes and shapes of identification markers shall be smaller than the community wayfinding guide signs themselves. Identification markers shall not be designed to have an appearance that could be mistaken by road users as being a traffic control device.

title: Section 2D.55 Guidance 46 - Community Wayfinding Signs
text:
Section 2D.55 Guidance 46 - Community Wayfinding Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

The area of the identification marker should not exceed ¹⁄5 of the area of the community wayfinding guide sign with which it is mounted in the same sign assembly.

title: Section 2D.56 Support 1 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
text:
Section 2D.56 Support 1 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

A highway name is the officially designated name of a freeway, expressway, or conventional road for navigational, official mapping, and address purposes. Some highways are named in addition to or in lieu of being assigned a highway route number. Memorial, honorary, ceremonial, or other secondary names, such as touring route and byway names, are not considered to be highway names.

metadata.section_title: Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes

title: Section 2D.56 Option 2 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
text:
Section 2D.56 Option 2 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

Guide signs may contain street or highway names if the purpose is to enhance driver communication and guidance; however, they are to be considered as supplemental information to route numbers.

metadata.section_title: Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes

title: Section 2D.56 Standard 3 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
text:
Section 2D.56 Standard 3 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

Highway names shall not replace official numeral designations.

metadata.section_title: Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes

title: Section 2D.56 Standard 4 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
text:
Section 2D.56 Standard 4 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 272

Memorial, honorary, or other secondary names (see Section 2M.10) shall not appear on supplemental signs or on any other information sign on or along the highway or its intersecting routes.

metadata.section_title: Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes

title: Section 2D.56 Standard 5 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
text:
Section 2D.56 Standard 5 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 273

The use of route signs shall be restricted to signs officially used for guidance of traffic in accordance with this Manual and the “Purpose and Policy” statement of the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials that applies to Interstate and U.S. numbered routes. Month 2023

metadata.section_title: Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes

title: Section 2D.56 Option 6 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
text:
Section 2D.56 Option 6 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 273

Unnumbered routes having major importance to proper guidance of traffic may be signed if carried out in accordance with the aforementioned policies. For unnumbered highways, a name to enhance route guidance may be used where the name is applied consistently throughout its length.

metadata.section_title: Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes

title: Section 2D.56 Guidance 7 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
text:
Section 2D.56 Guidance 7 - Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 273

Only one name should be used to identify any highway, whether numbered or unnumbered.

metadata.section_title: Signing of Named Highways for Mapping and Address Purposes

title: Section 2D.57 Support 1 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.57 Support 1 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 273

Certain roads have been designated by the U.S. Secretary of Transportation as National Scenic Byways or All-American Roads based on their archeological, cultural, historic, natural, recreational, or scenic qualities.

metadata.section_title: National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)

title: Section 2D.57 Option 2 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.57 Option 2 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 273

State and local highway agencies may install the National Scenic Byways (M10-1) sign or (M10-1aP) plaque (see Figure 2D-33) at entrance points to a route that has been recognized by the U.S. Secretary of Transportation as a National Scenic Byway or an All-American Road. The M10-1 sign may be installed as independent Directional (see Section 2D.32) or Confirming (see Section 2D.33) assemblies at periodic intervals along the designated route and near intersections where the designated route turns or follows a different numbered highway. The M10-1aP plaque may be installed below a route sign in a Confirming assembly. At locations where roadside features have been developed to enhance the traveler’s experience such as rest areas, historic sites, interpretive facilities, or scenic overlooks, the National Scenic Byways sign or plaque may be placed on the associated sign assembly to inform travelers that the site contributes to the byway travel experience.

metadata.section_title: National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)

title: Section 2D.57 Guidance 3 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.57 Guidance 3 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 274

Where the byway is identified only by the National Scenic Byways sign, the Directional assembly should consist of the M10-1 sign and an M5 series or M6 series auxiliary plaque when indication of a turn is necessary to remain on the byway route. Figure 2D-33. National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque, and Examples of Use A - National Scenic Byways sign and plaque B - Examples of use of the National Scenic Byways sign and plaque Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)

title: Section 2D.57 Guidance 4 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
text:
Section 2D.57 Guidance 4 - National Scenic Byways Sign and Plaque (M10-1 and M10-1aP)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 274

Where the name of the byway is to be displayed on identification signs or plaques along the byway route, the name should be displayed in a Directional or Confirming assembly as follows (see Figure 2D-34): A. On a Byway Identification (M10-2aP) plaque (see Section 2D.58) mounted below the M10-1 sign; or B. On a Byway Identification (M10-2) sign (see Section 2D.58) with the M10-1aP plaque mounted below the sign.

title: Section 2D.59 Support 1 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
text:
Section 2D.59 Support 1 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 279

As part of an agency’s transportation incident management plan it is sometimes desirable to permanently sign routes that provide rerouting of traffic around highway segments susceptible to traffic incidents. Permanently- installed Emergency Routing signs and plaques (see Figure 2D-37) provide direction on conventional roads from an exit located upstream of an area that can be susceptible to traffic incidents back to the original route at a point downstream of the incident-susceptible area.

metadata.section_title: Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)

title: Section 2D.59 Option 2 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
text:
Section 2D.59 Option 2 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 279

EMERGENCY ROUTE (M4-11 and M4-11a) signs and EMERGENCY ROUTE TO (M4-11bP and M4-11cP) plaques mounted on a directional assembly may be permanently installed on conventional roadways to provide trailblazing along a designated diversionary route to bypass a traffic incident.

metadata.section_title: Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)

title: Section 2D.59 Support 3 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
text:
Section 2D.59 Support 3 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 279

The purpose of Emergency Routing signs and plaques is for corridor management along routes that have recurring incidents and have reasonable rerouting paths available. These signs are intended to be permanently installed to provide instant rerouting guidance to road users when traffic congestion or backups first begin even before emergency responders could provide temporary traffic control for rerouting traffic. These signs can be used as a stand-alone system or be a part of a larger system which might also incorporate other devices such as changeable message signs. These signs provide road users assurance that a diversionary route will lead them back to their original route of travel.

metadata.section_title: Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)

title: Section 2D.59 Standard 4 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
text:
Section 2D.59 Standard 4 - Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 279

Emergency Routing signs and plaques shall only be installed at departure points and along diversion routes for directing road users around highway segments in areas that are more susceptible to traffic incidents (see Figure 2D-38). EMERGENCY ROUTE and EMERGENCY ROUTE TO signs shall be placed at each turning decision point along the designated route until it rejoins the original route or until other directional signs leading back to the original route are provided.

metadata.section_title: Emergency Routing Signs and Plaques (M4-11 and M4-12 Series)

Orange or pink shall not be used as alternate colors on permanently-installed signs or plaques for rerouting traffic during an incident or other event. If a route shield is displayed as part of the message, the wording of the sign or plaque shall be EMERGENCY ROUTE TO as shown in Figure 2D-37.

An EMERGENCY ROUTE TO plaque with either a white legend and border on a green background (M4-11bP) or black legend and border on a yellow background (M4-11cP) may be added to the top of a conventional Route assembly on a diversion route to provide direction back to the original route downstream of the incident (see Figures 2D-37 and 2D-38).

title: Section 2D.60 Support 1 - Signing at Airports
text:
Section 2D.60 Support 1 - Signing at Airports
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 282

Many roadways within airport facilities (including terminal curbside roadways) are considered to be conventional roads because they typically have frequent driveways and at-grade intersections and might have pedestrian activity along and/or across them.

title: Section 2D.60 Support 2 - Signing at Airports
text:
Section 2D.60 Support 2 - Signing at Airports
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 282

Some airport roadways have full or partial control of access and operating speeds higher than 45 mph and thus would be classified as freeways or expressways for signing purposes (see Chapter 2E). Freeway or expressway conditions typically exist on the approaches to the airport from other highways; on the approaches to access points to terminals, parking, and other patron facilities; and on roadways that provide exits from the airport facility to connect with the local or regional highway network.

title: Section 2D.60 Support 3 - Signing at Airports
text:
Section 2D.60 Support 3 - Signing at Airports
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 282

Roadways within airports and other similarly-contained roadway networks with multiple closely-spaced access points to multiple destinations (such as terminals, parking facilities, rental car facilities, and other airport services) often present challenges for the application of guide signing. Closely-spaced signs, excessive sign messaging either co-located or in succession, and the resulting excessive informational load imposed on the road user are of particular concern for such roadways. The Transportation Research Board’s Airport Cooperative Research Program Report 52, “Wayfinding and Signing Guidelines for Airport Terminal and Landside,” contains additional information on the application of traffic control devices to the unique geometrics and roadway environment that are typical of airports.

title: Section 2D.60 Support 4 - Signing at Airports
text:
Section 2D.60 Support 4 - Signing at Airports
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 282

An example of major guide signing on the approaches to and within an airport facility roadway network is shown in Figure 2D-39.

title: Section 2D.60 Guidance 5 - Signing at Airports
text:
Section 2D.60 Guidance 5 - Signing at Airports
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 282

If adequate sign spacing cannot be provided due to the site and roadway characteristics of an airport or similar facility, then measures should be taken to reduce the speeds of vehicles on the roadway to provide road users with adequate time to comprehend and respond to the sign messages. Consideration should also be given to increasing the sign letter heights to provide greater viewing distances and decision times. Where a single terminal serves a large number of airlines, the airline information should be displayed on separate signs that appear in sequence to limit the number of airlines displayed on a single sign or at a single location. Changeable message signs (see Chapter 2L) should not be used to rotate the display of airlines to an approaching road user.

title: Section 2D.60 Support 6 - Signing at Airports
text:
Section 2D.60 Support 6 - Signing at Airports
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2D. Guide Signs—Conventional Roads
Page: 283

There are various methods that can be used to help reduce vehicle speeds, including roadway geometric changes, implementing traffic calming measures, and increased enforcement. Provisions on setting speed limits are found in Section 2B.21. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2D-39.
