text:
Section 2F.18 Standard 2 - Guide Signs for ETC-Only Entrance Ramps to Non-Toll Highways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2F. Toll Road Signs
Page: 404

Guide signs for ETC-Only Entrance Ramps to non-toll highways shall comply with the provisions of Section 2F.17.

metadata.section_title: Guide Signs for ETC-Only Entrance Ramps to Non-Toll Highways

title: Section 2F.18 Option 3 - Guide Signs for ETC-Only Entrance Ramps to Non-Toll Highways
text:
Section 2F.18 Option 3 - Guide Signs for ETC-Only Entrance Ramps to Non-Toll Highways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2F. Toll Road Signs
Page: 404

A NO TOLL panel with a black legend and a yellow background may be included on the top section of the Exit Gore sign for an exit that provides access to the facility without charging a toll. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Guide Signs for ETC-Only Entrance Ramps to Non-Toll Highways

title: Section 2F.19 Standard 1 - ETC Account Program Information Signs
text:
Section 2F.19 Standard 1 - ETC Account Program Information Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2F. Toll Road Signs
Page: 404

Except as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section, signs that inform road users of telephone numbers, Internet addresses, including domain names and uniform resource locators (URLs), or e-mail addresses for enrolling in an ETC account program of a toll facility or managed lane, obtaining an ETC transponder, and/or obtaining ETC account program information shall only be installed in rest areas, parking areas, or similar roadside facilities where the signs are viewed only by pedestrians or occupants of parked vehicles.

title: Section 2F.19 Option 2 - ETC Account Program Information Signs
text:
Section 2F.19 Option 2 - ETC Account Program Information Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2F. Toll Road Signs
Page: 405

ETC account program information signs displaying telephone numbers that have no more than four characters may be installed on roadways in locations where they will not obscure the road user’s view of higher priority traffic control devices and that are removed from key decision points where the road user’s view is more appropriately focused on other traffic control devices, roadway geometry, or traffic conditions, including exit and entrance ramps, intersections, toll plazas, temporary traffic control zones, and areas of limited sight distance. December 2025

title: Section 2G.01 Support 1 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 1 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Preferential lanes are lanes designated for special traffic uses such as high-occupancy vehicles (HOVs), light rail, buses, or taxis. Preferential lane treatments might be as simple as restricting a turning lane to a certain class of vehicles during peak periods, or as sophisticated as providing a separate roadway system within a highway corridor for certain vehicles.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.01 Support 2 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 2 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Preferential lanes might be barrier-separated (on a separate alignment or physically separated from the other travel lanes by a barrier or median), buffer-separated (separated from the adjacent general-purpose lanes only by a narrow buffer area created with longitudinal pavement markings), or contiguous (separated from the adjacent general-purpose lanes only by a lane line). Preferential lanes might allow continuous access with the adjacent general-purpose lanes or restrict access only to designated locations. Preferential lanes might be operated in a constant direction or operated as reversible lanes. Some reversible preferential lanes on a divided highway might be operated counter-flow to the direction of traffic on the immediately adjacent general-purpose lanes.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.01 Support 3 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 3 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Preferential lanes might be operated on a 24-hour basis, for extended periods of the day, during peak travel periods only, during special events, or during other activities.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.01 Support 4 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 4 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Open-road tolling lanes and toll plaza lanes that segregate traffic based on payment method are not considered preferential lanes. Chapter 2F contains information regarding signing of open-road tolling lanes and toll plaza lanes.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.01 Support 5 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 5 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Managed lanes typically restrict access with the adjacent general-purpose lanes to designated locations only.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.01 Support 6 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 6 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Under certain operational strategies, such as the occupancy requirement of an HOV lane changing in response to actual congestion levels, a managed lane is a special type of preferential lane (see Sections 2G.03 through 2G.07).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.01 Support 7 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 7 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

A managed lane operated on a real-time basis in response to changing conditions might be operated as an HOV lane for a period of time as needed to manage congestion levels.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.01 Support 8 - Scope
text:
Section 2G.01 Support 8 - Scope
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Sections 2G.17 through 2G.19 contain additional information regarding signs for managed lanes that use tolling or pricing as a management strategy.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.02 Standard 1 - Sizes of Preferential and Managed Lane Signs
text:
Section 2G.02 Standard 1 - Sizes of Preferential and Managed Lane Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 406

Except as provided in Section 2A.07, the minimum sizes of preferential and managed lane signs that have standardized designs shall be as shown in Table 2G-1.

metadata.section_title: Sizes of Preferential and Managed Lane Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 1 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 1 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

When a preferential lane is established, the Preferential Lane regulatory signs (see Figure 2G-1) and pavement markings (see Chapter 3E) for these lanes shall be used to advise road users.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Support 2 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Support 2 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

Preferential Lane (R3-10 series through R3-15 series) regulatory signs (see Figure 2G-1) consist of several different general types of regulatory signs as follows: A. Vehicle Occupancy Definition signs define the vehicle occupancy requirements applicable to an HOV lane (such as “2 OR MORE PERSONS PER VEHICLE”) or types of vehicles not meeting the minimum occupancy requirement (such as motorcycles or Inherently Low Emission Vehicles (ILEVs)) that are allowed to use an HOV lane (see Section 2G.04). B. Preferential Lane Operation signs notify road users of the days and hours during which the preferential restrictions are in effect (see Section 2G.05). C. Preferential Lane Advance signs notify road users that a preferential lane restriction begins ahead (see Section 2G.06). D. Preferential Lane Ends signs notify users of the termination point of the preferential lane restrictions (see Section 2G.07).

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 3 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 3 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

Regulatory signs applicable only to a preferential lane shall be distinguished from regulatory signs applicable to general-purpose lanes by the inclusion of the applicable symbol(s) and/or word(s) (see Figure 2G-1).

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Support 4 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Support 4 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

The symbol and word message displayed on a particular Preferential Lane regulatory sign will vary based on the specific type of allowed traffic and on other related operational constraints that have been established for a particular lane, such as an HOV lane, a bus lane, or a taxi lane.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Option 5 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Option 5 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

Changeable message signs may supplement, substitute for, or be incorporated into static Preferential Lane regulatory signs where travel conditions change or where multiple types of operational strategies (such as variable occupancy requirements or vehicle types) are used and varied throughout the day or week, or on a real-time basis, to manage the use of, control of, or access to preferential lanes.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Support 6 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Support 6 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

Figure 2G-1 illustrates examples of changeable messages incorporated into static Preferential Lane regulatory signs displaying open and closed status using lane-use control signal indications (see Chapter 4T).

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 7 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 7 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

When changeable message signs (see Chapter 2L) are used as regulatory signs for preferential lanes, they shall be the required sign size and shall display the required letter height and legend format that corresponds to the type of roadway facility and design speed.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Guidance 8 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Guidance 8 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

When Preferential Lane regulatory signs are used on conventional roads, the decision regarding whether to use a post-mounted or overhead version of a particular type of sign should be based on an engineering study that considers the available space, the existing signs for the adjacent general-purpose traffic lanes, roadway and traffic characteristics, the proximity to existing overhead signs, the ability to install overhead signs, and any other unique local factors.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Guidance 9 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Guidance 9 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

If overhead regulatory signs applicable only to a preferential lane are located in approximately the same longitudinal position along the highway as overhead signs applicable only to the general-purpose lanes, the signs for the preferential lane should be separated laterally from the signs for the general-purpose lanes to the maximum extent practicable to minimize conflicting information, while maintaining their visual relationship to the lanes below necessitated by specific legend or arrows indicating lane assignment.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 10 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 10 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 409

If used, overhead Preferential Lane (R3-13 series, R3-14 series, and R3-15 series) regulatory signs shall be installed on the side of the roadway where the entrance to the preferential lane is located and any appropriate adjustments shall be made to the sign message.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Option 11 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Option 11 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 410

Where a median of sufficient width is available, the R3-13 series and R3-15 series signs may be post-mounted. Figure 2G-1. Preferential Lane Regulatory Signs and Plaque (Sheet 1 of 2) A - Post-mounted Preferential Lane regulatory signs and plaque Notes: 1. The minimum vehicle occupancy requirement may vary for each facility (such as 2+, 3+, 4+). 2. The occupancy requirement may be added to the first line of the R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, and R3-12d signs. 3. Some of the legends shown on these signs are for example purposes only. The specific legend for a particular application should be based upon local conditions, ordinances, and State statutes.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Support 12 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Support 12 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 410

The sizes for Preferential Lane regulatory signs will differ to reflect the design speeds for each type of roadway facility. Table 2G-1 provides sizes for each type of roadway facility.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Guidance 13 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Guidance 13 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 410

The edges of Preferential Lane regulatory signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier should not project beyond the outer edges of the barrier, including in areas where lateral clearance is limited.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Option 14 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Option 14 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 411

Where lateral clearance is limited, Preferential Lane regulatory signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier and that are 72 inches or less in width may be skewed up to 45 degrees in order to fit within the barrier width or may be mounted higher, such that the vertical clearance to the bottom of the sign, light fixture, or structural support, whichever is lowest, is not less than 17 feet above any portion of the pavement and shoulders. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2G-1. Preferential Lane Regulatory Signs and Plaque (Sheet 2 of 2) B - Overhead Preferential Lane regulatory signs A lane-use control signal may be incorporated into an overhead preferential lane regulatory sign to indicate the status of a reversible operation as shown in the following example: Notes: 1. The minimum vehicle occupancy requirement may vary for each facility (such as 2+, 3+, 4+). 2. The occupancy requirement may be added to the first line of the R3-15b and R3-15c signs. 3. Some of the legends shown on these signs are for example purposes only. The specific legend for a particular application should be based upon local conditions, ordinances, and State statutes. 4. Where sufficient median width is available, the R3-13 series and R3-15 series signs may be post-mounted.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 15 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 15 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 411

Where lateral clearance is limited, Preferential Lane regulatory signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier and that are wider than 72 inches shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with the provisions of Section 2A.15 for overhead mounting if any portion of the sign extends over the roadway or shoulder.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Guidance 16 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Guidance 16 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

On conventional roadways, Preferential Lane regulatory sign spacing should be determined by engineering judgment based on speed, block length, distances from adjacent intersections, and other site-specific considerations. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Support 17 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Support 17 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

Sections 2G.04 and 2G.05 contain provisions regarding the placement of Preferential Lane regulatory signs on freeways and expressways.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 18 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 18 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

The signs illustrated in Figure 2G-1 that incorporate the diamond symbol shall be used exclusively with preferential lanes for high-occupancy vehicles to indicate the particular occupancy requirement and time restrictions applying to that lane. The signs illustrated in Figure 2G-1 that do not have a diamond symbol shall be used with preferential lanes that are not HOV lanes, but are designated for use by other types of vehicles (such as bus and/or taxi use).

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 19 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 19 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

The diamond symbol shall not be used on the bus, taxi, or bicycle Preferential Lane signs.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Standard 20 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Standard 20 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

Vehicle Occupancy Definition, Preferential Lane Operation, and Preferential Lane Advance regulatory signs for HOV lanes shall display the minimum allowable vehicle occupancy requirement established for each HOV lane, displayed immediately after the word message HOV.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Support 21 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Support 21 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

The agencies that own and operate HOV lanes have the authority and responsibility to determine how they are operated and the minimum occupancy requirements. Information about federal requirements for certain types of vehicles not meeting the minimum occupancy requirement to be eligible to use HOV lanes that receive Federal- aid program funding and about requirements associated with proposed significant changes to the operation of an existing HOV lane and certain vehicles are contained in the “Federal-Aid Highway Program Guidance on High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lanes.”

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.03 Support 22 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
text:
Section 2G.03 Support 22 - Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

Figures 2G-2 and 2G-3 illustrate the use of regulatory signs for the beginning, along the length, and at the end of contiguous or buffer-separated preferential lanes that provide continuous access with the adjacent general- purpose lanes.

metadata.section_title: Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes – General
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.04 Standard 1 - Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
text:
Section 2G.04 Standard 1 - Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

The R3-10, R3-13, and R3-13a Vehicle Occupancy Definition signs (see Figure 2G-1) shall be used where agencies determine that it is appropriate to provide a sign that defines the minimum occupancy of vehicles that are allowed to use an HOV lane.

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.04 Guidance 2 - Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
text:
Section 2G.04 Guidance 2 - Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

The Inherently Low Emission Vehicle (ILEV) (R3-10a) sign (see Figure 2G-1) should be used when it is permissible for a properly labeled and certified ILEV, regardless of the number of occupants, to use an HOV lane. When used, the ILEV signs should be post-mounted in advance of and at intervals along the HOV lane based upon engineering judgment and the placement of other Preferential Lane regulatory signs. The R3-10a sign is only applicable to HOV lanes and should not be used with other preferential lane applications.

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.04 Support 3 - Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
text:
Section 2G.04 Support 3 - Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 412

ILEVs are defined by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) as vehicles having no fuel vapor (hydrocarbon) emissions and are certified by the EPA as meeting the emissions standards and requirements specified in 40 CFR §88.311-93 and 40 CFR §88.312-93(c).

metadata.section_title: Vehicle Occupancy Definition Signs (R3-10 Series and R3-13 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Support 1 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Support 1 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 415

The standardized sizes of post-mounted Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11 series) signs are consistent to accommodate any future addition or removal of a single line of legend for each sign. Each size accommodates two lines of legend for the times of day and days of week that the regulation is in effect. Consistent sign sizes are beneficial for agencies when ordering sign materials, as well as when making legend changes to existing signs if changes occur to operating times or occupancy restrictions in the future.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Guidance 2 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Guidance 2 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 415

Where the regulation is in effect during more than one time period of the day, such as during the morning and afternoon peak periods, the height of the R3-11 and R3-14 series signs should be suitably increased to accommodate the additional line(s) of legend.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 3 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 3 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 415

When used, the post-mounted Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11 series) signs shall be located adjacent to the preferential lane, and the overhead Preferential Lane Operation (R3-14 series) signs shall be mounted directly over the lane.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 4 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 4 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 415

The legend format of the post-mounted Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11 series) signs shall have the following sequence: A. Top Lines: Lanes applicable, such as “RIGHT LANE” or “2 RIGHT LANES” B. Middle Lines: Eligible uses, such as “HOV 2+ ONLY” (or 3+ or 4+, if appropriate) or “BUSES ONLY” or other applicable uses or eligible turning movements C. Bottom Lines: Applicable times and days, such as “7 AM - 9 AM” or “6:30 AM - 9:30 AM, MON-FRI”

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 5 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 5 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 415

The legend format of the overhead Preferential Lane Operation (R3-14 series) signs shall have the following sequence: A. Top Lines: Eligible uses, such as “HOV 2+ ONLY” (or 3+ or 4+, if appropriate) or “BUSES ONLY” or other applicable uses or eligible turning movements B. Bottom Lines: Applicable times and days, with the time and day placed above the down arrow, such as “7 AM - 9 AM” or “6:30 AM - 9:30 AM, MON-FRI.” When the operating periods exceed the available line width, the hours and days of the week shall be stacked as shown for the R3-14a sign in Figure 2G-1.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 6 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 6 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

For preferential lane restrictions that are in effect on a full-time (24 hours per day, seven days per week) basis, the Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11b, R3-11c, R3-11e, and R3-14b) signs that include a period of operation legend shall be modified to display no legend relative to the period of operation except as provided in Paragraph 7 of this Section. Rev. 1 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Option 7 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Option 7 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

In lieu of removing the period of operation text from the Preferential Lane Operation signs for full-time operation, the legend 24 HOURS may be substituted for the times and days of the week on the Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11, R3-11a, R3-11d, R3-11f, R3-11g, R3-14, R3-14a, and R3-14c) signs for preferential lane restrictions that are in effect on a full-time basis.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Support 8 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Support 8 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

The 24 HOURS legend displayed on the Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11 and R3-14 series) signs reinforces the full-time operation where several facilities in the same area have different hours of operation-some part time, others full time, or where the same lane changes from part-time to full-time operation somewhere along its length.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 9 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 9 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

The full-time Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11b, R3-11c, R3-11e, and R3-14b) signs that do not display a period of operation legend, as described in Paragraph 6 of this Section, shall not be used where the preferential lane restriction is in effect only on a part-time basis.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Option 10 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Option 10 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

Where additional movements are allowed from a preferential lane on an approach to an intersection by vehicles not meeting the preferential lane regulation, the format and words used in the legend in the middle lines on the post-mounted Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11 series) signs and on the top line of the overhead Preferential Lane Operation (R3-14 series) signs may be modified to accommodate the allowable movements (such as “HOV 2+ AND RIGHT TURNS ONLY”).

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Option 11 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Option 11 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

The MOTORCYCLES ALLOWED (R3-11hP) plaque (see Figure 2G-1) may be used where motorcycles, regardless of the number of occupants, are allowed to use an HOV lane.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 12 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 12 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

If used, the MOTORCYCLES ALLOWED plaque shall be mounted below a post-mounted Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11, R3-11a, or R3-11b) sign.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 13 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 13 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

For all barrier-separated or buffer-separated or contiguous preferential lanes where access is restricted to designated locations, an overhead Preferential Lane Operation (R3-14 series) sign shall be used at the beginning or initial entry point on freeways, expressways, and at locations on conventional roadways where the preferential lane is not the outermost (far right or far left) lane of the roadway, and at any intermediate entry points or gaps in the barrier or buffer where vehicles are allowed to legally enter the access-restricted preferential lanes. For all barrier-separated and buffer-separated preferential lanes, post-mounted Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11 series) signs shall be used only as a supplement to the overhead signs on freeways, expressways, and at locations on conventional roadways where the preferential lane is not the outermost lane of the roadway at the beginning or initial entry point, or at any intermediate entry points or gaps in the barrier or buffer.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 14 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 14 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

For buffer-separated or contiguous preferential lanes where continuous access with the adjacent general-purpose lanes is provided, including those where a preferential lane is added to the roadway (see Figure 2G-2 for HOV lanes) and those where a general-purpose lane transitions into a preferential lane (see Figure 2G-3 for HOV lanes), an overhead Preferential Lane Operation (R3-14 series) sign shall be used at the beginning or initial entry point of the preferential lane on freeways and expressways.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Option 15 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Option 15 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

On conventional roads where preferential lane operations exist, R3-11 series post-mounted signs may be used in lieu of or in addition to overhead R3-14 series signs, except where overhead signs are required as provided in Paragraph 13 of this Section. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Option 16 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Option 16 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

Additional overhead (R3-14 series) or post-mounted (R3-11 series) Preferential Lane Operation signs may be provided along the length of any type of preferential lane.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Standard 17 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Standard 17 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

For all types of direct access ramps that provide access to or lead to preferential lanes, a post-mounted Preferential Lane Operation (R3-11 series) sign shall be used at the beginning or initial entry point of the direct access ramp.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Option 18 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Option 18 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 416

For direct access ramps to preferential lanes, an overhead Preferential Lane Operation (R3-14 series) sign may be used at the beginning or initial entry point to supplement the required post-mounted signs.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.05 Option 19 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
text:
Section 2G.05 Option 19 - Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

Lane-use control signals (see Chapter 4T) may be used at access points to preferential lanes to indicate that a ramp or access roadway leading to the preferential lane or facility, or one or more specific lanes of the facility, are open or closed (see Figure 2G-1). December 2025

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Operation Signs (R3-11 Series and R3-14 Series)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.06 Guidance 1 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
text:
Section 2G.06 Guidance 1 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

The Preferential Lane Advance (R3-12, R3-12f, R3-15, and R3-15d) signs (see Figure 2G-1) should be used for advance notification of a barrier-separated, buffer-separated, or contiguous preferential lane that is added to the general-purpose lanes (see Figure 2G-2).

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.06 Guidance 2 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
text:
Section 2G.06 Guidance 2 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

The Preferential Lane Advance (R3-12e and R3-15a) signs (see Figure 2G-1) should be used for advance notification of a general-purpose lane that becomes a preferential lane (see Figure 2G-3).

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.06 Option 3 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
text:
Section 2G.06 Option 3 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

The legends on the R3-12f and R3-15d signs may be modified to suit the type of preferential lane.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)

title: Section 2G.06 Guidance 4 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
text:
Section 2G.06 Guidance 4 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

On conventional roads, for general-purpose lanes that become preferential lanes, a post-mounted (R3-12e) or overhead (R3-15a) Preferential Lane Advance sign should be installed in advance of the beginning of or initial entry point to the preferential lane at a distance determined by engineering judgment based on speed, traffic characteristics, and other site-specific considerations. The distance selected should provide adequate opportunity for ineligible vehicles to vacate the lane prior to the beginning of the restriction.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
metadata.chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs

title: Section 2G.06 Guidance 5 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
text:
Section 2G.06 Guidance 5 - Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

On freeways and expressways, for general-purpose lanes that become preferential lanes, an overhead Preferential Lane Advance (R3-15a) sign should be installed at least 1 mile in advance of the beginning of the preferential lane restriction.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Advance Signs (R3-12, R3-12e, R3-12f, R3-15, R3-15a, and R3-15d)

Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

Additional post-mounted or overhead Preferential Lane Advance signs may be placed farther in advance of or closer to the beginning or initial entry points to a preferential lane.

text:
Section 2G.07 Standard 1 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

A post-mounted Preferential Lane Ends (R3-12b or R3-12h) sign (see Figure 2G-1) shall be installed at least ½ mile in advance of the termination of a preferential lane on freeways and expressways.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)

text:
Section 2G.07 Standard 2 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

Except as provided in Paragraph 7 of this Section, a post-mounted Preferential Lane Ends (R3-12a or R3-12g) sign shall be installed at the point where a preferential lane and restriction end and traffic must merge into the general-purpose lanes.

text:
Section 2G.07 Standard 3 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

A post-mounted Preferential Lane Ends (R3-12d) sign (see Figure 2G-1) shall be installed at least ½ mile in advance of the point where a preferential lane restriction ends and the lane becomes a general- purpose lane on freeways and expressways.

metadata.section_title: Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)

text:
Section 2G.07 Standard 4 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs

Except as provided in Paragraph 8 of this Section, a post-mounted Preferential Lane Ends (R3-12c) sign shall be installed at the point where a preferential lane restriction ends and the lane becomes a general- purpose lane.

text:
Section 2G.07 Guidance 5 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

On conventional roads, the distance at which Preferential Lane Ends signs are installed in advance of the termination of a preferential lane and/or restriction should be determined by engineering judgment.

Section 2G.07 Option 6 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

The legends on the R3-12g and R3-15e signs may be modified to suit the type of preferential lane.

text:
Section 2G.07 Option 7 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
Page: 417

An overhead Preferential Lane Ends (R3-15b or R3-15e) sign may be installed instead of or in addition to a post-mounted R3-12a or R3-12g sign at the point where a preferential lane and restriction ends and traffic must merge into the general-purpose lanes.

Section 2G.07 Option 8 - Preferential Lane Ends Signs (R3-12a, R3-12b, R3-12c, R3-12d, R3-12g, R3-12h, R3-15b, R3-15c, and R3-15e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2G. Preferential And Managed Lane Signs
