metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 12 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 12 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

If the distance to the next point where services are available is greater than 10 miles, a Next Services Advance (D9-17P) plaque (see Figure 2I-2) may be installed below the Exit Direction sign.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Standard 13 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Standard 13 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

Signs for services shall comply with the format for General Service signs (see Section 2I.02) and as provided in this Manual. No more than six general road user services shall be displayed on one sign, which includes any appended supplemental signs or plaques. General Service signs shall display the legends for one or more of the following services: Food, Gas, EV Charging, Lodging, Camping, Phone, Hospital, 24- Hour Pharmacy, or Tourist Information.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Standard 14 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Standard 14 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

The qualified services available shall be displayed at specific locations on the sign.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Guidance 15 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Guidance 15 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

To provide for future services that might become available, the sign space normally reserved for a given service symbol or word should be left blank when that service is not present.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Guidance 16 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Guidance 16 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

The standard display of word messages should be FOOD and PHONE in that order on the top line, and GAS and LODGING on the second line. If used, HOSPITAL, 24-HOUR PHARMACY, and CAMPING should be on separate lines (see Figure 2I-3).

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 17 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 17 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

Signing for EV Charging, DIESEL, LP-GAS, or other alternative fuel services may be substituted for any of the general services or appended to such signs. The International Symbol of Accessibility (D9-6) sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be used for facilities that qualify.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Guidance 18 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Guidance 18 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

When symbols are used for the road user services, they should be displayed as follows: A. Six services: 1. Top row-GAS, FOOD, and LODGING 2. Bottom row-PHONE, HOSPITAL, and CAMPING B. Four services: 1. Top row-GAS and FOOD 2. Bottom row-LODGING and PHONE C. Three services: 1. Top row-GAS, FOOD, and LODGING

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 19 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 19 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

Substitutions of other services for any of the services described in Paragraph 18 of this Section may be made by placing the substitution in the lower right (four or six services) or extreme right (three services) portion of the sign. An action message or an interchange exit number may be used for symbol signs in the same manner as they are used for word message signs. The Diesel Fuel (D9-11) symbol or the LP-GAS (D9-11e) symbol may be substituted for the symbol representing fuel or appended to such assemblies. The Tourist Information (D9-10) or the 24-Hour Pharmacy (D9-20 and D9-20aP) symbol may be substituted on any of the configurations provided in Paragraph 18 of this Section. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 20 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 20 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

At rural interchange areas where limited road user services are available and where it is unlikely that additional services will be provided within the near future, a Rural Interchange General Services (D9-18dP, D9-18eP, or D9-18fP) plaque displaying one to three services (words or symbols) may be mounted below a post-mounted Interchange Advance guide sign.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Standard 21 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Standard 21 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

If more than three services become available at rural interchange areas where limited road user services were anticipated, the appended supplemental plaque described in Paragraph 20 of this Section shall be removed and replaced with an independently-mounted General Service sign as described in this Section.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 22 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 22 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

A separate Telephone Service (D9-1) sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be installed if telephone facilities are located adjacent to the route at places where public telephones would not normally be expected.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 23 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 23 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

The Recreational Vehicle Sanitary Station (D9-12) sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be used as needed to indicate the availability of facilities designed for dumping wastes from recreational vehicle holding tanks.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 24 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 24 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

In some locations, signs may be used to indicate that services are not available.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 25 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 25 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 482

A separate Truck Parking (D9-16) sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be mounted below the other general road user services to direct truck drivers to designated parking areas.

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.03 Option 26 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 2I.03 Option 26 - General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 483

A TRUCK EXTERNAL POWER (D9-16aP) plaque (see Figure 2I-1) may be mounted below the Truck Parking (D9-16) sign to indicate the availability of receptacles providing power for electrical devices within the truck. Rev. 1 December 2025

metadata.section_title: General Service Signs for Freeways and Expressways

title: Section 2I.04 Support 1 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
text:
Section 2I.04 Support 1 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 483

An Interstate Oasis is a facility near an Interstate highway that provides products and services to the public, 24-hour access to public restrooms, and parking for automobiles and heavy trucks. Interstate Oasis guide signs inform road users on Interstate highways as to the presence of an Interstate Oasis at an interchange and which businesses have been designated by the State within which they are traveling as having met the eligibility criteria of the Federal Highway Administration’s Interstate Oasis policy. The FHWA’s policy, which is dated October 18, 2006, and which can be viewed on the MUTCD Web site at http://mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov/res-policy.htm, provides a more detailed definition of an Interstate Oasis and specifies the eligibility criteria for an Interstate Oasis designation in compliance with the requirements of laws enacted by Congress.

title: Section 2I.04 Guidance 2 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
text:
Section 2I.04 Guidance 2 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 483

If a State elects to provide or allow Interstate Oasis signing (see Figure 2I-4), there should be a statewide policy, program, procedures, and criteria for the designation and signing of a facility as an Interstate Oasis that complies with the FHWA’s policy and with the provisions of this Section.

title: Section 2I.04 Guidance 3 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
text:
Section 2I.04 Guidance 3 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 483

States electing to provide or allow Interstate Oasis signing should use the following signing practices on the freeway for any given exit to identify the availability of a designated Interstate Oasis: A. If adequate sign spacing allows, a separate Interstate Oasis (D5-12) sign should be installed in an effective location with spacing of at least 800 feet from other adjacent guide signs, including any Specific Service signs. This Interstate Oasis sign should be located upstream from the Advance Guide sign or between the Advance Guide sign and the Exit Direction sign for the exit leading to the Interstate Oasis. The Interstate Oasis sign should display the words INTERSTATE OASIS and the exit number or, for an unnumbered interchange, an action message such as NEXT RIGHT. B. If the spacing of the other guide signs precludes the use of a separate sign as described in Item A of this Paragraph, an INTERSTATE OASIS (D5-12aP) supplemental plaque should be mounted below an existing D9-18 series General Service sign for the interchange.

title: Section 2I.04 Option 4 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
text:
Section 2I.04 Option 4 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 483

If Specific Service signing is provided at the interchange, a business designated as an Interstate Oasis and having a business identification sign panel on the Food and/or Gas Specific Service signs may use the bottom portion of the business identification sign panel to display the word OASIS.

title: Section 2I.04 Option 5 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
text:
Section 2I.04 Option 5 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If Specific Service signing is not provided at the interchange, the name of the business designated as an Interstate Oasis may be displayed on a business identification sign panel, in compliance with the provisions of Sections 2J.03 through 2J.05, below the INTERSTATE OASIS legend on the D5-12 sign. Figure 2I-4. Examples of Interstate Oasis Signs and Plaques

title: Section 2I.04 Standard 6 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
text:
Section 2I.04 Standard 6 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If Specific Service signs containing the OASIS legend as a part of the business identification sign panel(s) are not used on the ramp and if the Interstate Oasis is not clearly visible and identifiable from the exit ramp, an Interstate Oasis Directional (D5-12b) sign shall be provided on the exit ramp to indicate the direction and distance to the Interstate Oasis.

title: Section 2I.04 Standard 7 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
text:
Section 2I.04 Standard 7 - Interstate Oasis Signing (D5-12 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If needed, additional trailblazer guide signs shall be used along the crossroad to guide road users to an Interstate Oasis.

title: Section 2I.05 Standard 1 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Standard 1 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

Rest Area signs (see Figure 2I-5) shall have a retroreflective white legend and border on a blue background.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Standard 2 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Standard 2 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

Signs that include the legend REST AREA shall be used only where parking and restroom facilities are available.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Guidance 3 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Guidance 3 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

A roadside area that does not contain restroom facilities should be signed to indicate the major road user service that is provided. For example, the sign legends for an area with only parking should use the words PARKING AREA (D5-9 series) instead of REST AREA. The sign legends for an area with only picnic tables and parking should use words such as PICNIC AREA, ROADSIDE TABLE, or ROADSIDE PARK (D5-10 series) instead of REST AREA.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Guidance 4 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Guidance 4 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

Rest areas that have tourist information and welcome centers should be signed as provided in Section 2I.08.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Guidance 5 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Guidance 5 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

Scenic area signing should be consistent with that provided for rest areas, except that the legends should use words such as SCENIC AREA, SCENIC VIEW, or SCENIC OVERLOOK (D5-11 series) instead of REST AREA.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Guidance 6 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Guidance 6 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If a rest area or other roadside area is provided on a conventional road, a D5-1 and/or D5-1a sign should be installed in advance of the rest area or other roadside area to permit the driver to reduce speed in preparation for leaving the highway. A D5-5 sign (or a D5-2 sign if an exit ramp is provided) should be installed at the turn-off point where the driver needs to leave the highway to access the rest area or other roadside area.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Guidance 7 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Guidance 7 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If a rest area or other roadside area is provided on a freeway or expressway, a D5-1 sign should be placed 1 mile and/or 2 miles in advance of the rest area.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Standard 8 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Standard 8 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

A D5-2a sign shall be placed at the rest area or other roadside area exit gore.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Option 9 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Option 9 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

A D5-1a sign may be placed between the D5-1 sign and the exit gore on a freeway or expressway. A second D5-1 sign may be used in place of the D5-1a sign with a distance to the nearest ½ or ¼ mile displayed as a fraction rather than a decimal for distances of less than 1 mile.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Option 10 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Option 10 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

To provide the road user with information on the location of succeeding rest areas, a Next Rest Area (D5-6) sign (see Figure 2I-5) may be installed independently or as a supplemental sign mounted below one of the REST AREA advance guide signs.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Standard 11 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Standard 11 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

All signs on freeways and expressways for rest and other roadside areas shall have letter and numeral sizes that comply with the minimum requirements of Tables 2E-2 through 2E-5. The sizes for General Service signs that have standardized designs shall be as shown in Table 2I-1.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Option 12 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Option 12 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If the rest area has facilities for persons with disabilities (see Section 2I.02), the International Symbol of Accessibility (D9-6) sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be placed with or beneath an advance guide sign for the rest area.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Option 13 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Option 13 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If telecommunication devices for the deaf (TDD) are available at the rest area, the TDD (D9-21) symbol sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be used to supplement the advance guide signs for the rest area.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.05 Option 14 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
text:
Section 2I.05 Option 14 - Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 484

If wireless Internet services are available at the rest area, the Wireless Internet (D9-22) symbol sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be used to supplement the advance guide signs for the rest area.

metadata.section_title: Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs (D5-1 through D5-11 Series)

title: Section 2I.06 Guidance 1 - Brake Check Area Signs (D5-13 and D5-14)
text:
Section 2I.06 Guidance 1 - Brake Check Area Signs (D5-13 and D5-14)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 486

If an area has been provided for drivers to pull off of the roadway to check the brakes on their vehicle, a Brake Check Area Advance (D5-13) sign (see Figure 2I-6) should be installed in advance of the brake check area, and a D5-14 sign (see Figure 2I-6) should be placed at the entrance to the brake check area. Figure 2I-5. Rest Area and Other Roadside Area Signs Note: Alternate legends may be substituted for the PICNIC AREA legend, such as ROADSIDE TABLE and ROADSIDE PARK, and for the SCENIC AREA legend, such as SCENIC VIEW and SCENIC OVERLOOK. Figure 2I-6. Brake Check Area and Chain-Up Area Signs

metadata.section_title: Brake Check Area Signs (D5-13 and D5-14)

title: Section 2I.07 Guidance 1 - Chain-Up Area Signs (D5-15 and D5-16)
text:
Section 2I.07 Guidance 1 - Chain-Up Area Signs (D5-15 and D5-16)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 486

If an area has been provided for drivers to pull off of the roadway to install chains on their tires, a Chain-Up Area Advance (D5-15) sign (see Figure 2I-6) should be installed in advance of the chain-up area, and a D5-16 sign (see Figure 2I-6) should be placed at the entrance to the chain-up area.

title: Section 2I.08 Support 1 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Support 1 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 486

Tourist information and welcome centers have been constructed within rest areas on freeways and expressways and are operated by either a State or a private organization. Others have been located within close proximity to these facilities and operated by civic clubs, chambers of commerce, or private enterprise.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Guidance 2 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Guidance 2 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 486

The number of supplemental sign panels installed with Tourist Information or Welcome Center signs should be limited to three so as not to impose an undue informational load on the road user.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Standard 3 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Standard 3 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 486

Tourist Information or Welcome Center signs (see Figure 2I-7) shall have a white legend and border on a blue background. Continuously staffed or unstaffed operation at least 8 hours per day, 7 days per week, shall be required.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Standard 4 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Standard 4 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 486

If operated only on a seasonal basis, the Tourist Information or Welcome Center signs shall be removed or covered during the off seasons.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Guidance 5 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Guidance 5 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 486

For freeway or expressway rest area locations that also serve as tourist information or welcome centers, the following signing criteria should be used: A. The locations for tourist information and welcome center Advance Guide, Exit Direction, and Exit Gore signs should meet the General Service signing requirements described in Section 2I.03. B. If the signing for the tourist information or welcome center is to be accomplished in conjunction with the initial signing for the rest areas, the message on the Rest Area Tourist Info Center Advance (D5-7) sign should be REST AREA, TOURIST INFO CENTER, XX MILES or REST AREA, STATE NAME (optional), WELCOME CENTER XX MILES. On the Rest Area Tourist Info Center Entrance Direction (D5-8) sign the message should be REST AREA, TOURIST INFO CENTER with a diagonally upward-pointing directional arrow (or NEXT RIGHT), or REST AREA, STATE NAME (optional), WELCOME CENTER with a diagonally upward-pointing directional arrow (or NEXT RIGHT). C. If the initial rest area Advance Guide and Exit Direction signing is in place, these signs should include, on supplemental signs, the legend TOURIST INFO CENTER or STATE NAME (optional), WELCOME CENTER. D. The Exit Gore sign should contain only the legend REST AREA with the arrow and should not be supplemented with any legend pertaining to the tourist information center or welcome center.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Option 6 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Option 6 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

As an alternative to the supplemental TOURIST INFO CENTER legend, the Tourist Information (D9-10) sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be appended beneath the REST AREA advance guide sign. Figure 2I-7. Examples of Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs Note: Alternate legends may be substituted for the TOURIST INFO CENTER legend, such as WELCOME CENTER and (State Name) WELCOME CENTER.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Option 7 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Option 7 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

The name of the State or local jurisdiction may appear on the Advance Guide and Exit Direction tourist information/welcome center signs if the jurisdiction controls the operation of the tourist information or welcome center and the center meets the operating criteria set forth in this Manual and is consistent with State policies.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Guidance 8 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Guidance 8 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

For tourist information centers that are located off the freeway or expressway facility, additional signing criteria should be as follows: A. Each State should adopt a policy establishing the maximum distance that a tourist information center can be located from the interchange in order to be included on official signs. B. The location of signing should be in accordance with requirements pertaining to General Service signing (see Section 2I.03). C. Signing along the crossroad should be installed to guide the road user from the interchange to the tourist information center and back to the interchange.

metadata.section_title: Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)

title: Section 2I.08 Option 9 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
text:
Section 2I.08 Option 9 - Tourist Information and Welcome Center Signs (D5-7 Series and D5-8)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

As an alternative, the Tourist Information (D9-10) sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be appended to the guide signs for the exit that provides access to the tourist information center. As a second alternative, the Tourist Information sign may be combined with General Service signing.

title: Section 2I.09 Option 1 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
text:
Section 2I.09 Option 1 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

A Radio-Weather Information (D12-1) sign (see Figure 2I-8) may be used in areas where difficult driving conditions commonly result from weather systems. Radio-Traffic Information (D12-1a) signs may be used in conjunction with traffic management systems.

title: Section 2I.09 Standard 2 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
text:
Section 2I.09 Standard 2 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

Radio-Weather and Radio-Traffic Information signs shall have a white legend and border on a blue background. Only the numerical indication of the radio frequency shall be used to identify a station broadcasting travel-related weather or traffic information. No more than three frequencies shall be displayed on each sign. Only radio stations whose signal will be of value to the road user and who agree to broadcast either of the following two items shall be identified on Radio-Weather and Radio-Traffic Information signs: A. Periodic weather warnings at a rate of at least once every 15 minutes during periods of adverse weather; or B. Driving condition information (affecting the roadway being traveled) at a rate of at least once every 15 minutes, or when required, during periods of adverse traffic conditions, and when supplied by an official agency having jurisdiction.

title: Section 2I.09 Standard 3 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
text:
Section 2I.09 Standard 3 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

If a station to be considered operates only on a seasonal basis, its signs shall be removed or covered during the off season.

title: Section 2I.09 Guidance 4 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
text:
Section 2I.09 Guidance 4 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

The radio station should have a signal strength to adequately broadcast at least 70 miles along the route. Signs should be spaced as needed for each direction of travel at distances determined by an engineering study. The stations to be included on the signs should be selected in cooperation with the association(s) representing major broadcasting stations in the area to provide: (1) maximum coverage to all road users on both AM and FM frequencies; and (2) consideration of 24 hours per day, 7 days per week broadcast capability.

title: Section 2I.09 Option 5 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
text:
Section 2I.09 Option 5 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

The URGENT MESSAGE WHEN FLASHING (D12-1bP) plaque may be mounted below the D12-1 or D12-1a sign if supplemented by Warning Beacons (see Section 4S.03) that flash only when a message related to adverse travel conditions is being broadcast.

title: Section 2I.09 Option 6 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
text:
Section 2I.09 Option 6 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 487

In roadway rest area locations, a smaller sign using a greater number of radio frequencies, but of the same general design, may be used.

title: Section 2I.09 Standard 7 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
text:
Section 2I.09 Standard 7 - Radio Information Signing (D12-1 Series)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 488

Radio-Weather and Radio-Traffic Information signs installed in rest areas shall be positioned such that they are not visible from the main roadway. Figure 2I-8. Radio, Telephone, and Carpool Information Signs * The pictograph of the transportation agency or the travel information service or program may be used in place of the 511 pictograph (see Section 2I.12)

text:
Section 2I.10 Option 1 - Channel 9 Monitored Sign (D12-3)

Page: 488

A Channel 9 Monitored (D12-3) sign (see Figure 2I-8) may be installed as needed. Official public agencies or their designees may be displayed as the monitoring agency on the sign.

title: Section 2I.10 Standard 2 - Channel 9 Monitored Sign (D12-3)
text:
Section 2I.10 Standard 2 - Channel 9 Monitored Sign (D12-3)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 488

Only official public agencies or their designee shall be displayed as the monitoring agency on the Channel 9 Monitored sign.

text:
Section 2I.11 Option 1 - EMERGENCY CALL 911 Sign (D12-4)
Part: Part 2 Signs

Page: 489

An Emergency CALL 911 (D12-4) sign (see Figure 2I-8) may be used for cellular telephone communications.

title: Section 2I.12 Option 1 - TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 Signs (D12-5 and D12-5a)
text:
Section 2I.12 Option 1 - TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 Signs (D12-5 and D12-5a)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 489

A TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 (D12-5 or D12-5a) sign (see Figure 2I-8) may be installed if a 511 travel information services telephone number is available to road users for obtaining traffic, public transportation, weather, construction, or road condition information.

metadata.section_title: TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 Signs (D12-5 and D12-5a)

title: Section 2I.12 Option 2 - TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 Signs (D12-5 and D12-5a)
text:
Section 2I.12 Option 2 - TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 Signs (D12-5 and D12-5a)
Part: Part 2 Signs

Page: 489

The pictograph of the transportation agency or the travel information service or program that is providing the travel information may be displayed in place of the 511 pictograph on the D12-5 sign above the TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 legend.

Section 2I.12 Standard 3 - TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 Signs (D12-5 and D12-5a)

The logo of a commercial entity shall not be incorporated within the TRAVEL INFO CALL 511 signs.

A Roadside Assistance (D12-6) sign (see Figure 2I-8) displaying the Highway Assistance cellular telephone code designated for that roadway or jurisdiction may be used along a highway that is served by an authorized roadside assistance program with authorized service vehicles and personnel that provide roadside vehicle repair assistance to road users free of charge.

text:
Section 2I.14 Option 1 - Carpool and Ridesharing Signing (D12-2)

Page: 489

In areas having carpool matching services, a Carpool Information (D12-2) sign (see Figure 2I-8) may be provided adjacent to highways with preferential lanes or along any other highway.

text:
Section 2I.14 Option 2 - Carpool and Ridesharing Signing (D12-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs

Carpool Information signs may include an Internet domain name or telephone number of more than four characters within the legend.

title: Section 2I.14 Standard 3 - Carpool and Ridesharing Signing (D12-2)
text:
Section 2I.14 Standard 3 - Carpool and Ridesharing Signing (D12-2)
Part: Part 2 Signs

Page: 489

If a local transit pictograph or carpool symbol is incorporated into the Carpool Information sign, the maximum vertical dimension of the pictograph or symbol shall not exceed 18 inches and the maximum horizontal dimension shall not exceed 30 inches.

title: Section 2I.15 Option 1 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)
text:
Section 2I.15 Option 1 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 489

General Service signs may be used to display the number of available truck parking spaces at roadside areas such as rest areas, welcome centers, and weigh stations, and at facilities off a highway that are open to the public and provide parking for commercial vehicles 24 hours per day, 7 days per week.

metadata.section_title: Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)

title: Section 2I.15 Standard 2 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)
text:
Section 2I.15 Standard 2 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 489

The Truck Parking Availability General Service (D9-16b through D9-16e) signs (see Figure 2I-9) shall include a changeable message element with a white changeable legend on a black opaque background that displays only the number of parking spaces currently available at each location or the legend FULL. The upper section of the sign shall display the Truck Parking (D9-16) symbol sign and the legend SPACES OPEN. The sign shall display the number of available truck parking spaces for no more than three parking facilities. Where two lines of legend, such as the location and a distance, are displayed for a parking facility, not more than two parking facilities shall be displayed on the sign.

metadata.section_title: Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)

title: Section 2I.15 Standard 3 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)
text:
Section 2I.15 Standard 3 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 489

Where the truck parking facility is located off the main highway and is accessed from the crossroad, directional assemblies with the Truck Parking (D9-16) sign shall be installed along the ramp and along crossroads where the route to the facility requires a turn, where it is unclear as to which roadway to follow, or where additional guidance is needed.

metadata.section_title: Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)

text:
Section 2I.15 Support 4 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2I. General Service Signs
Page: 490

Displaying the number of parking spaces available at a facility when the number is low could result in truckers choosing to continue to a distant facility that no longer has available spaces by the time they arrive. Section 2I.15 Option 5 - Signing for Truck Parking Availability (D9-16b through D9-16e)

The word FULL in a white legend may be displayed on changeable message elements of a Truck Parking Availability General Service sign when the number of truck parking spaces available at the associated facility reaches a predetermined lower threshold.
