title: Section 2J.01 Standard 1 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Standard 1 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

Specific Service signs shall be defined as guide signs that provide road users with business identification and directional information for eligible services. Eligible service categories shall be limited to gas, food, lodging, camping, attractions, and electric vehicle (EV) charging.

title: Section 2J.01 Guidance 2 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Guidance 2 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

The use of Specific Service signs should be limited to areas primarily rural in character with adequate space for all signs to be properly accommodated.

title: Section 2J.01 Support 3 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Support 3 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

When services at an interchange are abundant, this is an indication that the character of the area is no longer primarily rural and General Service signs would be more appropriate.

title: Section 2J.01 Option 4 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Option 4 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

Where an engineering study determines a need, Specific Service signs may be used on any class of highway, including freeways, expressways, and conventional roads.

title: Section 2J.01 Guidance 5 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Guidance 5 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

Specific Service signs should not be installed at an interchange where the road user cannot conveniently reenter the freeway or expressway and continue in the same direction of travel.

title: Section 2J.01 Standard 6 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Standard 6 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

Eligible service facilities shall comply with laws concerning the provisions of public accommodations without regard to race, religion, color, age, sex, or national origin, and laws concerning the licensing and approval of service facilities.

title: Section 2J.01 Standard 7 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Standard 7 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

The attraction services shall include only facilities that have the primary purpose of providing amusement, historical, cultural, or leisure activities to the public.

title: Section 2J.01 Guidance 8 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Guidance 8 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

Except as provided in Paragraph 9 of this Section, distances to eligible services should not exceed 3 miles in any direction.

title: Section 2J.01 Option 9 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Option 9 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

If, within the 3-mile limit, facilities for the services being considered are not available or choose not to participate in the program, the limit of eligibility may be extended in 3-mile increments until one or more facilities for the services being considered chooses to participate, or until 15 miles is reached, whichever comes first.

title: Section 2J.01 Standard 10 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Standard 10 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 492

If State or local agencies elect to provide Specific Service signing, there shall be a statewide policy for such signing and criteria for the eligibility and availability of the various types of services.

title: Section 2J.01 Guidance 11 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Guidance 11 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

The criteria for the statewide policy should consider the following: A. To qualify for a GAS business identification sign panel, a business should have: 1. Vehicle services including gasoline, oil, and water; 2. Continuous operation at least 16 hours per day, 7 days per week for freeways and expressways, and continuous operation at least 12 hours per day, 7 days per week for conventional roads; and 3. Modern sanitary facilities and drinking water. B. To qualify for a FOOD business identification sign panel, a business should have: 1. Licensing or approval, where required; 2. Continuous operations to serve at least 2 meals per day, at least 6 days per week; and 3. Modern sanitary facilities. C. To qualify for a LODGING business identification sign panel, a business should have: 1. Licensing or approval, where required; 2. Adequate sleeping accommodations; and 3. Modern sanitary facilities. D. To qualify for a CAMPING business identification sign panel, a business should have: 1. Licensing or approval, where required; 2. Adequate parking accommodations; and 3. Modern sanitary facilities and drinking water. E. To qualify for an ATTRACTION business identification sign panel, a facility should have: 1. Regional significance, in compliance with the provisions of Paragraph 7 of this Section; and 2. Adequate parking accommodations.

title: Section 2J.01 Standard 12 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Standard 12 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

To be eligible for an Electric Vehicle (EV) CHARGING business identification sign panel, the EV chargers provided shall meet the criteria for Direct Current Fast Chargers provided in 23 CFR 680.106 and be in continuous operation at least 16 hours per day, 7 days per week.

title: Section 2J.01 Option 13 - Eligibility
text:
Section 2J.01 Option 13 - Eligibility
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

Business identification sign panels for a proprietary electric vehicle charging service may be included on an EV Charging Specific Service sign if it meets the eligibility criteria in Paragraph 12 of this Section.

title: Section 2J.02 Support 1 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Support 1 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

Examples of Specific Service signs are shown in Figure 2J-1.

title: Section 2J.02 Support 2 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Support 2 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

Examples of sign locations are shown in Figure 2J-2.

title: Section 2J.02 Standard 3 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Standard 3 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

The number of Specific Service signs along an approach to an interchange or intersection, regardless of the number of service types displayed, shall be limited to a maximum of four. Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, in the direction of traffic flow, successive Specific Service signs shall be for attraction, camping, lodging, food, EV charging, and gas services, in that order.

title: Section 2J.02 Option 4 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Option 4 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

When spacing does not allow EV Charging Specific Service signs to be located as described in Paragraph 3 of this Section, then the EV Charging Specific Service signs may be located anywhere within the successive Specific Service sign order where adequate spacing between signs allows.

title: Section 2J.02 Guidance 5 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Guidance 5 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

The Specific Service signs should be located to take advantage of natural terrain, to have the least impact on the scenic environment, and to avoid visual conflict with other signs within the highway right-of-way.

title: Section 2J.02 Guidance 6 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Guidance 6 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

Where a service type is displayed on two signs, the signs for that service should follow one another in succession.

title: Section 2J.02 Standard 7 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Standard 7 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

A Specific Service sign shall display the word message GAS, EV CHARGING, FOOD, LODGING, CAMPING, or ATTRACTION, an appropriate directional legend such as the word message EXIT XX, NEXT RIGHT, SECOND RIGHT, or directional arrows, and the related business identification sign panels. Distances to eligible facilities shall not be displayed on the Specific Service signs on the approach to an interchange.

title: Section 2J.02 Standard 8 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Standard 8 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

A business that does not offer gasoline, but offers alternative fuels, shall not be signed using GAS Specific Service signs.

title: Section 2J.02 Option 9 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Option 9 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

A business that does not offer gasoline but offers alternative fuels may be signed using General Service signs for the alternative fuel provided.

title: Section 2J.02 Support 10 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Support 10 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

General Service signs for facilities providing alternative fuels, including EV charging, compressed natural gas, liquefied natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, and hydrogen, are provided in Chapter 2I.

title: Section 2J.02 Guidance 11 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Guidance 11 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 493

Due to the unique and widely varying characteristics of the services that qualify as attractions, and lesser recognition of their business identification sign panels (see Paragraph 12 of this Section), ATTRACTION Specific Service signs should have no more than four business identification sign panels.

title: Section 2J.02 Support 12 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Support 12 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

The types of services that meet the definition of attraction, such as those providing amusement, historical, cultural, or leisure activities to the public, vary considerably. In most cases, attractions do not include well-known services or easily recognizable logos, making it more difficult and requiring more time to distinguish between types of attractions shown on an ATTRACTION sign than for other categories of Specific Service signs. Figure 2J-1. Examples of Business Identification Panel Arrangements on Specific Service Signs MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2J-2. Examples of Specific Service Sign Locations *Specific service ramp signs (as needed) Spacing should be at least 100 feet from the exit gore sign, from each other, and from the ramp terminal. Rev. 1 December 2025

title: Section 2J.02 Standard 13 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Standard 13 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

No more than three types of services shall be represented on any sign or sign assembly and no more than six business identification sign panels shall be displayed on any one sign. If three types of services are displayed on one sign, then the business identification sign panels shall be limited to two for each service type (for a total of six business identification sign panels). If two types of services are displayed on one sign, then the business identification sign panels shall be limited to either three for each service type, or four for one service type and two for the other service type (for a total of six business identification sign panels in either case). The legend and business identification sign panels applicable to a service type shall be displayed such that the road user will not associate them with another service type on the same sign. Other configurations or arrangements of business identification sign panels shall not be allowed.

title: Section 2J.02 Standard 14 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Standard 14 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

No service type shall appear on more than two signs (see Paragraph 6 of this Section).

title: Section 2J.02 Standard 15 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Standard 15 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

The Specific Service signs shall have a blue background, a white border, and white legends of upper- case letters, numerals, and arrows.

title: Section 2J.02 Guidance 16 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Guidance 16 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

If a service type is no longer available from an interchange or intersection, the Specific Service sign should be removed when the business identification sign panels are removed. If a sign is to remain, but the service type is no longer available, then the service type legend should be covered so that road users do not misinterpret the sign as a General Service sign implying that the service is available.

title: Section 2J.02 Guidance 17 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Guidance 17 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

A Specific Service sign should not be installed unless a service type is currently available from an interchange or intersection.

title: Section 2J.02 Option 18 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Option 18 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

If there is indication that a service type will again be available in the near future, the sign may be covered, in accordance with Paragraph 16 of this Section, rather than removed.

title: Section 2J.02 Option 19 - Application
text:
Section 2J.02 Option 19 - Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

Separate installations of General Service signs (see Figure 2J-3 and Sections 2I.02 and 2I.03) may be used in conjunction with Specific Service signs for eligible types of services that are not represented by a Specific Service sign.

title: Section 2J.03 Standard 1 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.03 Standard 1 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

A business identification sign panel legend shall be either an identification trademark or a word message of the business’s name. Each logo or word message shall be placed on a separate business identification sign panel that shall be attached to the Specific Service sign. Logos or trademarks used alone for a business identification sign panel shall be reproduced in the colors and general shape consistent with customary use, and any integral legend shall be in proportionate size. A logo that resembles an official traffic control device shall not be used.

metadata.section_title: Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.03 Standard 2 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.03 Standard 2 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

Scanning graphics that are visible to the road user from the roadway for the purpose of obtaining information shall not be displayed on business identification sign panels, including on any logo displayed thereupon.

metadata.section_title: Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.03 Guidance 3 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.03 Guidance 3 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

The logo or trademark used on a business identification sign panel should be consistent with the on-premise business identification signs at the location of the business that are visible from the roadway.

metadata.section_title: Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.03 Guidance 4 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.03 Guidance 4 - Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 496

A word message business identification sign panel that does not use a logo or trademark should have a blue background with a white legend and border.

metadata.section_title: Logos and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.04 Guidance 1 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.04 Guidance 1 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 498

Sign sizes should be determined by the amount and height of legend and the number and size of business identification sign panels attached to the sign. All business identification sign panels on a sign should be the same size.

metadata.section_title: Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.04 Standard 2 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.04 Standard 2 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 499

Each Specific Service sign or sign assembly shall be limited to no more than six business identification sign panels. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.04 Option 3 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.04 Option 3 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 499

Where more than six businesses of a specific service type are eligible for business identification sign panels at the same interchange, additional business identification sign panels of that same specific service type may also be displayed in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 4 of this Section. The additional business identification sign panels may be displayed either by placing more than one specific service type on the same sign (see Paragraph 13 of Section 2J.02) or by using a second Specific Service sign of that specific service type if the additional sign can be added without exceeding the limit of four Specific Service signs at an interchange or intersection approach (see Paragraph 3 of Section 2J.02).

metadata.section_title: Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.04 Standard 4 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
text:
Section 2J.04 Standard 4 - Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 499

Where business identification sign panels for more than six businesses of a specific service type are displayed at the same interchange or intersection approach, the following provisions shall apply: A. No more than 12 business identification sign panels of a specific service type shall be displayed on no more than two Specific Service signs or sign assemblies; B. No more than six business identification sign panels shall be displayed on a single Specific Service sign; and C. No more than four Specific Service signs shall be displayed on the approach.

metadata.section_title: Number and Size of Signs and Business Identification Sign Panels

title: Section 2J.05 Standard 1 - Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2J.05 Standard 1 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 499

All Specific Service signs and business identification sign panels shall have letter and numeral sizes that comply with the minimum requirements of Table 2J-1.

title: Section 2J.05 Guidance 2 - Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2J.05 Guidance 2 - Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 499

All lettering on the business identification sign panels should be composed of a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters, except within the design of a logo. Any legend on a business identification graphic/trademark should be proportional to the size of the graphic trademark. Rev. 1

title: Section 2J.06 Standard 1 - Signs at Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.06 Standard 1 - Signs at Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 499

The Specific Service signs shall be installed between the preceding interchange and at least 800 feet in advance of the Exit Direction sign at the interchange from which the services are available (see Figure 2J-2).

title: Section 2J.06 Standard 2 - Signs at Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.06 Standard 2 - Signs at Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 499

Specific Service signs shall not be used at freeway-to-freeway interchanges (see Section 2E.37), except where the exit ramp also provides direct access to a conventional road within that interchange (see Figure 2J-5).

title: Section 2J.06 Guidance 3 - Signs at Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.06 Guidance 3 - Signs at Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 500

There should be at least an 800-foot spacing between the Specific Service signs, except for Specific Service ramp signs. Excessive spacing should not be used between Specific Service signs, as this is not desirable either. December 2025 Figure 2J-5. Example of Specific Services Signing for a Conventional Road Accessed within a Freeway-to-Freeway Interchange

title: Section 2J.06 Guidance 4 - Signs at Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.06 Guidance 4 - Signs at Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 500

Specific Service ramp signs should be spaced at least 100 feet longitudinally beyond the Exit Gore sign, from each other, and from the ramp terminal. Specific Service ramp signs should be spaced at least 200 feet longitudinally from any Destination guide signs along the ramp. Longer longitudinal spacing should be provided between Specific Service ramp signs and any warning or regulatory signs along the ramp, and any intersection traffic control devices at the ramp terminal.

title: Section 2J.06 Guidance 5 - Signs at Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.06 Guidance 5 - Signs at Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 500

When the distance to the next exit providing access to EV charging service is 50 miles or greater, the Next EV Charging (D9-17a) sign should be used (see Figure 2H-9). When used, the Next EV Charging sign should be located directly after the General Service sign for the fuel type displayed in the signing sequence for the exit (see Figure 2H-10).

title: Section 2J.07 Standard 1 - Single-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.07 Standard 1 - Single-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 500

At numbered single-exit interchanges, the name of the service type followed by the exit number shall be displayed on one line above the business identification sign panels. At unnumbered interchanges, the directional legend NEXT RIGHT (LEFT) shall be used in place of the exit number.

title: Section 2J.07 Standard 2 - Single-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.07 Standard 2 - Single-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

At single-exit interchanges where traffic is allowed to turn onto the crossroad in either direction from the ramp, Specific Service ramp signs shall be installed along the ramp or opposite the ramp terminal for facilities that have business identification sign panels displayed along the main roadway if the facilities are not readily visible from the ramp terminal. Directions to the service facilities shall be indicated by arrows on the ramp signs. Business identification sign panels on Specific Service ramp signs shall be duplicates of those displayed on the Specific Service signs located in advance of the interchange, but shall be reduced in size (see Paragraph 7 of Section 2J.04).

title: Section 2J.07 Option 3 - Single-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.07 Option 3 - Single-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

Specific Service ramp signs may display distances (see Paragraphs 14 and 15 of Section 2A.08) to a service facility when the facility is not visible from ramp intersection with the crossroad.

title: Section 2J.07 Guidance 4 - Single-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.07 Guidance 4 - Single-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

Distances of less than ¼ mile, when displayed, should be displayed to the nearest ¹⁄10 mile.

title: Section 2J.08 Guidance 1 - Double-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.08 Guidance 1 - Double-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

At double-exit interchanges, the Specific Service signs should consist of two sections, one for each exit (see Figure 2J-1).

title: Section 2J.08 Standard 2 - Double-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.08 Standard 2 - Double-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

At a double-exit interchange, the top section shall display the business identification sign panels for the first exit and the bottom section shall display the business identification sign panels for the second exit. At numbered interchanges, the name of the service type and the exit number shall be displayed above the business identification sign panels in each section. At unnumbered interchanges, the word message NEXT RIGHT (LEFT) and SECOND RIGHT (LEFT) shall be used in place of the exit number. The number of business identification sign panels on the sign (total of both sections) or the sign assembly shall be limited to six.

title: Section 2J.08 Guidance 3 - Double-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.08 Guidance 3 - Double-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

At a double-exit interchange, where a service type is displayed on two Specific Service signs in accordance with the provisions of Section 2J.04, one of the signs should display the business identification sign panels for that service type for the businesses that are accessible from one of the two exits and the other sign should display the business identification sign panels for that service type for the businesses that are accessible from the other exit.

title: Section 2J.08 Option 4 - Double-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.08 Option 4 - Double-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

At a double-exit interchange where there are four business identification sign panels to be displayed for one of the exits and one or two business identification sign panels to be displayed for the other exit, the business identification sign panels may be arranged in three rows with two business identification sign panels per row.

title: Section 2J.08 Option 5 - Double-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.08 Option 5 - Double-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

At a double-exit interchange, where a service is to be signed for only one exit, one section of the Specific Service sign may be omitted, or a single exit interchange sign may be used.

title: Section 2J.08 Option 6 - Double-Exit Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.08 Option 6 - Double-Exit Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

Signs on ramps and crossroads as described in Section 2J.07 may be used at a double-exit interchange.

title: Section 2J.09 Support 1 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.09 Support 1 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

Examples of Specific Service signs used in advance of interchanges for collector-distributor roadways that provide access to multiple interchanges are shown in Figure 2J-6.

title: Section 2J.09 Option 2 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.09 Option 2 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

If services are available from more than one of the interchanges along the collector-distributor roadway and those services are signed with Specific Service signs as described in Paragraph 4 of this Section, then Specific Service signs may be used on the mainline in conformance with the provisions of this Chapter.

title: Section 2J.09 Standard 3 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.09 Standard 3 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

No more than four Specific Service signs shall be displayed on a highway mainline approach to a collector-distributor roadway.

title: Section 2J.09 Standard 4 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.09 Standard 4 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 501

If Specific Service signs are located on the highway mainline for services accessed from the collector- distributor roadway, then the business identification sign panels displayed on the collector-distributor roadway shall be only duplicates of those displayed on the highway mainline.

title: Section 2J.09 Standard 5 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
text:
Section 2J.09 Standard 5 - Collector-Distributor Roadways for Successive Interchanges
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

If more than four Specific Services signs would be required on the mainline in advance of the collector-distributor roadway in order to display all the business identification sign panels used on Specific Service signs in advance of the collector-distributor roadway exits, then General Service signs shall be used on the mainline to identify the types of services displayed on Specific Service signs on the collector- distributor roadway. Figure 2J-6. Example of Signing for Services Accessed from a Collector-Distributor Road Adjacent to a Freeway

title: Section 2J.10 Support 1 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Support 1 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

Specific Service trailblazer signs (see Figure 2J-7) are guide signs with one to four business identification sign panels that display business identification and directional information for services and eligible attractions. Specific Service trailblazer signs are installed along crossroads for facilities that have business identification sign panels displayed along the main roadway and ramp, and that require additional vehicle maneuvers or are a long distance from the ramp along the crossroad.

title: Section 2J.10 Standard 2 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Standard 2 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

Specific Service trailblazer signs shall be installed along crossroads where the route to the business requires a direction change, where it is questionable as to which roadway to follow, or where additional guidance is needed. Where it is not feasible or practical to install Specific Service trailblazer signs to such businesses, those businesses shall not be considered eligible for signing from the ramp and main roadway. A Specific Service trailblazer sign shall not be required at the point where the business is visible from the roadway and its access is readily apparent.

title: Section 2J.10 Guidance 3 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Guidance 3 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

If used, a Specific Service trailblazer sign should be located a maximum of 500 feet in advance of any required turn.

title: Section 2J.10 Standard 4 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Standard 4 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

The location of other traffic control devices shall take precedence over the location of a Specific Service trailblazer sign.

title: Section 2J.10 Standard 5 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Standard 5 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

When used, each Specific Service trailblazer sign or sign assembly shall be limited to no more than four business identification sign panels. The business identification sign panels on Specific Service trailblazer signs shall be duplicates of those displayed on the Specific Service ramp signs.

title: Section 2J.10 Standard 6 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Standard 6 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

Appropriate legends, such as directional arrows or the action message NEXT RIGHT or SECOND RIGHT, shall be displayed with the business identification sign panel to provide proper guidance. The directional legend and border shall be white and shall be displayed on a blue background.

title: Section 2J.10 Option 7 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Option 7 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

Specific Service trailblazer signs may contain various types of services on a single sign or on a sign assembly.

title: Section 2J.10 Option 8 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
text:
Section 2J.10 Option 8 - Specific Service Trailblazer Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

Specific Service trailblazer signs may be placed farther from the edge of the road than other traffic control signs.

title: Section 2J.11 Guidance 1 - Signs at Intersections
text:
Section 2J.11 Guidance 1 - Signs at Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 503

If both tourist-oriented information (see Chapter 2K) and specific service information are proposed to be used at the same intersection, the tourist-oriented directional and Specific Service signs should be spaced sufficiently apart from one another, as well as apart from other guide, warning, and regulatory signs, to avoid confusion and allow sufficient time for road users to read and react to the information.

title: Section 2J.11 Standard 2 - Signs at Intersections
text:
Section 2J.11 Standard 2 - Signs at Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 504

If sufficient space to provide appropriate reading and reaction to all proposed signs is not available, higher priority shall be given to guide, warning, and regulatory signs and either the tourist-oriented directional signs or the Specific Service signs, or both, shall not be used.

title: Section 2J.11 Guidance 3 - Signs at Intersections
text:
Section 2J.11 Guidance 3 - Signs at Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 504

If Specific Service signs are used on conventional roads or at intersections on expressways, they should be installed between the previous interchange or intersection and at least 300 feet in advance of the intersection from which the services are available.

title: Section 2J.11 Guidance 4 - Signs at Intersections
text:
Section 2J.11 Guidance 4 - Signs at Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 504

Business identification sign panels should not be displayed for a type of service for which a qualified facility is readily visible.

title: Section 2J.11 Standard 5 - Signs at Intersections
text:
Section 2J.11 Standard 5 - Signs at Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 504

If Specific Service signs are used on conventional roads or at intersections on expressways, the name of each type of service shall be displayed above its business identification sign panel(s), together with an appropriate legend, such as NEXT RIGHT (LEFT) or a directional arrow, either displayed on the same line as the name of the type of service or displayed below the business identification sign panel(s).

title: Section 2J.11 Option 6 - Signs at Intersections
text:
Section 2J.11 Option 6 - Signs at Intersections
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 504

Signs similar to Specific Service ramp signs as described in Section 2J.07 may be provided on the crossroad.

title: Section 2J.12 Standard 1 - Signing Policy
text:
Section 2J.12 Standard 1 - Signing Policy
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 504

In addition to a statewide policy for eligibility of service providers (see Section 2J.01), each highway agency that elects to use Specific Service signs shall establish a signing policy.

title: Section 2J.12 Guidance 2 - Signing Policy
text:
Section 2J.12 Guidance 2 - Signing Policy
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2J. Specific Service Signs
Page: 505

The signing policy should include, at a minimum, the provisions of Section 2J.01 and at least the following criteria: A. Selection of eligible businesses; B. Distances to eligible services; C. The use of business identification sign panels, legends, and signs complying with the provisions of this Manual and State design requirements; D. Removal or covering of business identification sign panels during off seasons for businesses that operate on a seasonal basis; E. The circumstances, if any, under which Specific Service signs are permitted to be used in non-rural areas; and F. Determination of the costs to businesses for initial permits, installations, annual maintenance, and removal of business identification sign panels. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 2K.01 Support 1 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 2K.01 Support 1 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

Tourist-oriented directional signs are post-mounted guide sign assemblies with one or more signs that display the business identification of and directional information for eligible business, service, and activity facilities.

title: Section 2K.01 Standard 2 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 2K.01 Standard 2 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

A facility shall be eligible for tourist-oriented directional signs only if it derives its major portion of income or visitors during the normal business season from road users not residing in the area of the facility.

title: Section 2K.01 Option 3 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 2K.01 Option 3 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

Tourist-oriented directional signs may include businesses involved with seasonal agricultural products.

title: Section 2K.01 Standard 4 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 2K.01 Standard 4 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

The use of tourist-oriented directional signs shall be limited to rural highways (see definition in Section 1C.02). Tourist-oriented directional signs shall not be installed on conventional roads in urban or urbanized areas or on freeway or expressway main roadways or ramps.

title: Section 2K.01 Option 5 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 2K.01 Option 5 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

Tourist-oriented directional signs may be used in conjunction with General Service signs (see Section 2I.02).

title: Section 2K.02 Standard 1 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Standard 1 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

Tourist-oriented directional sign assemblies shall have one or more signs (see Figure 2K-1) for the purpose of displaying the business identification of and directional information for eligible facilities. Except as provided in Paragraph 7 of this Section, each sign shall be rectangular in shape and shall have a white legend and border on a blue background.

title: Section 2K.02 Standard 2 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Standard 2 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

The content of the legend on each sign shall be limited to the identification and directional information for no more than one eligible business, service, or activity facility. The legends shall not include promotional advertising.

title: Section 2K.02 Guidance 3 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Guidance 3 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

Each sign should have a maximum of two lines of legend including no more than one symbol (see Paragraph 4 of this Section), a separate directional arrow, and the distance to the facility displayed beneath the arrow. Arrows pointing to the left or up should be at the extreme left of the sign panel. Arrows pointing to the right should be at the extreme right of the sign panel. Symbols, when used, should be to the left of the word legend or business identification sign panel (see Paragraphs 6 and 9 of this Section).

title: Section 2K.02 Option 4 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Option 4 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

The General Service sign symbols (see Section 2I.02) and the symbols for recreational and cultural interest area signs (see Chapter 2M) may be used on tourist-oriented directional signs.

title: Section 2K.02 Option 5 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Option 5 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

Based on engineering judgment, the hours of operation may be displayed on the sign.

title: Section 2K.02 Option 6 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Option 6 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

Business identification sign panels (see Section 2J.03) for specific businesses, services, and activities may display a logo in place of a word legend on a tourist-oriented directional sign.

title: Section 2K.02 Standard 7 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Standard 7 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

When used, recreational and cultural interest area symbols shall be white on a brown background.

title: Section 2K.02 Standard 8 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Standard 8 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

When used, symbols shall be an appropriate size (see Section 2K.04).

title: Section 2K.02 Standard 9 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Standard 9 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

When used, business identification sign panels shall not exceed 24 inches in width and 15 inches in height. Logos resembling official traffic control devices shall not be permitted.

title: Section 2K.02 Option 10 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Option 10 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

The word message TOURIST ACTIVITIES may be displayed at the top of the tourist-oriented directional sign assembly.

title: Section 2K.02 Standard 11 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Standard 11 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 505

The TOURIST ACTIVITIES word message shall have a white legend in all upper-case letters and a white border on a blue background. If used, it shall be placed above and in addition to the directional signs.

title: Section 2K.02 Support 12 - Design
text:
Section 2K.02 Support 12 - Design
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 506

Examples of tourist-oriented directional signs are shown in Figures 2K-1 and 2K-2. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 2K-1. Examples of Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs

title: Section 2K.03 Guidance 1 - Style and Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2K.03 Guidance 1 - Style and Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 506

All letters and numbers on tourist-oriented directional signs, except on the business identification sign panels, should be upper-case and at least 6 inches in height. All lettering on the business identification sign panels should be composed of a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters, except within the design of a logo. Any legend on a business identification sign panel should be proportional to the size of the business identification sign panel.

title: Section 2K.03 Standard 2 - Style and Size of Lettering
text:
Section 2K.03 Standard 2 - Style and Size of Lettering
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

Design standards for letters, numerals, and spacing shall be as provided in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05). December 2025 Figure 2K-2. Examples of Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs on an Intersection Approach (1) Optional sign panel and legend (2) Optional legend (3) Use if there is an intervening intersection

title: Section 2K.04 Standard 1 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
text:
Section 2K.04 Standard 1 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The total height of the tourist-oriented directional signs in a sign assembly shall be limited to a maximum of 6 feet. Additional height shall be allowed to accommodate the addition of the optional TOURIST ACTIVITIES message provided in Section 2K.02 and the action messages provided in Section 2K.05.

title: Section 2K.04 Guidance 2 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
text:
Section 2K.04 Guidance 2 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The number of intersection approach sign assemblies (one sign assembly for tourist-oriented destinations to the left, one for destinations to the right, and one for destinations straight ahead) installed in advance of an intersection should not exceed three. The number of signs installed in each assembly should not exceed three. The signs for right-turn, left-turn, and straight-through destinations should be on separate sign assemblies. Signs for facilities in the straight-through direction should be considered only when there are signs for destinations in either the left or right direction.

title: Section 2K.04 Guidance 3 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
text:
Section 2K.04 Guidance 3 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

If it has been determined to be appropriate to combine the left-turn and right-turn destination signs on a single sign assembly, the left-turn destination signs should be above the right-turn destination signs (see Figure 2K-1). When there are multiple destinations in the same direction, they should be in order based on their distance from the intersection. Except as provided in Paragraph 5 of this Section, a straight-through sign should not be combined in a sign assembly displaying left-turn and/or right-turn destinations.

title: Section 2K.04 Guidance 4 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
text:
Section 2K.04 Guidance 4 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The signs should not exceed the size necessary to accommodate two lines of legend without crowding. Symbols on a directional sign should not exceed the height of two lines of a word legend. All directional signs and other parts of the sign assembly should be the same width, which should not exceed 6 feet.

title: Section 2K.04 Option 5 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
text:
Section 2K.04 Option 5 - Arrangement and Size of Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

At intersection approaches where three or fewer facilities are displayed, the left-turn, right-turn, and straight- through destination sign panels may be combined on the same sign.

title: Section 2K.05 Guidance 1 - Advance Signs
text:
Section 2K.05 Guidance 1 - Advance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

Advance signs should be limited to those situations where sight distance, intersection vehicle maneuvers, or other vehicle operating characteristics require advance notification of the destinations and their directions.

title: Section 2K.05 Guidance 2 - Advance Signs
text:
Section 2K.05 Guidance 2 - Advance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The design of the advance sign should be identical to the design of the intersection approach sign. However, the directional arrows and distances to the destinations should be omitted and the action messages NEXT RIGHT, NEXT LEFT, or AHEAD should be placed on the sign above the business identification signs. The action messages should have the same letter height as the other word messages on the directional signs (see Figures 2K-1 and 2K-2).

title: Section 2K.05 Standard 3 - Advance Signs
text:
Section 2K.05 Standard 3 - Advance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The action message signs shall have a white legend in all upper-case letters and a white border on a blue background.

title: Section 2K.05 Option 4 - Advance Signs
text:
Section 2K.05 Option 4 - Advance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The legend RIGHT ½ MILE or LEFT ½ MILE may be used on advance sign assemblies when there are intervening minor roads.

title: Section 2K.05 Option 5 - Advance Signs
text:
Section 2K.05 Option 5 - Advance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The height required to add the directional word messages recommended for the advance sign assembly may be added to the maximum sign height of 6 feet.

title: Section 2K.05 Guidance 6 - Advance Signs
text:
Section 2K.05 Guidance 6 - Advance Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

The optional TOURIST ACTIVITIES message, when used on an advance sign assembly, and the action message should be combined on a single sign with TOURIST ACTIVITIES as the top line and the action message as the bottom line (see Figure 2K-2).

title: Section 2K.06 Guidance 1 - Sign Locations
text:
Section 2K.06 Guidance 1 - Sign Locations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 508

If used, the intersection approach signs should be located at least 200 feet in advance of the intersection. Sign assemblies should be spaced at least 200 feet apart and at least 200 feet from other traffic control devices.

title: Section 2K.06 Guidance 2 - Sign Locations
text:
Section 2K.06 Guidance 2 - Sign Locations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 509

If used, advance signs should be located approximately ½ mile from the intersection with 500 feet between these sign assemblies. In the direction of travel, the order of advance sign placement should be to show the destinations to the left first, then destinations to the right, and last, the destinations straight ahead (see Figure 2K-2).

title: Section 2K.06 Guidance 3 - Sign Locations
text:
Section 2K.06 Guidance 3 - Sign Locations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 509

Position, height, and lateral offset of sign assemblies should be governed by Chapter 2A except as permitted in this Section.

title: Section 2K.06 Option 4 - Sign Locations
text:
Section 2K.06 Option 4 - Sign Locations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 509

Tourist-oriented directional signs may be placed farther from the edge of the road than other traffic control signs.

title: Section 2K.06 Standard 5 - Sign Locations
text:
Section 2K.06 Standard 5 - Sign Locations
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 509

The location of other traffic control devices shall take precedence over the location of tourist-oriented directional signs.

title: Section 2K.07 Standard 1 - State Policy
text:
Section 2K.07 Standard 1 - State Policy
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 509

To be eligible for tourist-oriented directional signing, facilities shall comply with applicable State and Federal laws concerning the provisions of public accommodations without regard to race, religion, color, age, sex, or national origin, and with laws concerning the licensing and approval of service facilities. Each State that elects to use tourist-oriented directional signs shall adopt a policy that complies with these provisions.

title: Section 2K.07 Guidance 2 - State Policy
text:
Section 2K.07 Guidance 2 - State Policy
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2K. Tourist-Oriented Directional Signs
Page: 510

The State policy should include: A. A definition of tourist-oriented business, service, and activity facilities. B. Eligibility criteria for signs for facilities. C. Provision for covering signs during off seasons for facilities operated on a seasonal basis. D. Provisions for signs to facilities that are not located on the crossroad when such facilities are eligible for signs. E. A definition of the immediate area in compliance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Section 2K.01. F. Maximum distances to eligible facilities. The maximum distance should be 5 miles. G. Provision for information centers (plazas) when the number of eligible sign applicants exceeds the maximum permissible number of sign panel installations. H. Provision for limiting the number of signs when there are more applicants than the maximum number of signs permitted. I. Criteria for use at intersections on expressways. J. Provisions for controlling or excluding those businesses which have illegal signs as defined by the Highway Beautification Act of 1965 (23 U.S.C. 131). K. Provisions for States to charge fees to cover the cost of signs through a permit system. L. A definition of the conditions under which the time of operation is displayed. M. Provisions for determining if advance signs will be permitted, and the circumstances under which they will be installed.

title: Section 2L.01 Support 1 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Support 1 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

A changeable message sign (CMS) is a traffic control device that is capable of displaying one or more alternative messages. Some CMS have a blank mode when no message is displayed, while others display multiple messages with only one of the messages displayed at a time (such as OPEN/CLOSED signs at weigh stations).

title: Section 2L.01 Support 2 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Support 2 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

The provisions in this Chapter apply to both permanent and portable changeable message signs with electronic displays or the electronic display portion of an otherwise conventional static sign. Additional provisions that only apply to portable changeable message signs (PCMS) can be found in Section 6L.05. The provisions in this Chapter generally do not apply to CMS with non-electronic displays that are changed either manually or electromechanically, such as a hinged-panel, rotating-drum, or back-lit curtain or scroll CMS.

title: Section 2L.01 Support 3 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Support 3 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

The CMS is a traffic control device at all times regardless of the type of message being displayed. Accordingly, the limitations on design, format, and manner of display of a message conveyed on a conventional sign apply to CMS regardless of the type of message being displayed at any given time. Some of the general provisions regarding traffic control devices are reiterated in this Chapter. However, this Chapter is not an independent or stand-alone reference for CMS. Users of CMS are expected to consult the other chapters in this Manual for criteria on how to develop effective messages that comply with this Manual and that meet the expectancy and limitations of the road user. In this regard, the engineering processes applied to decisions about whether to use a particular sign, for example, are no different for the decisions about the type and content of the message under consideration for display on a CMS. The other limited-use messages allowed on CMS as provided for in this Chapter likewise fall under the same MUTCD provisions as the primary-use traffic operation regulatory, warning, and guidance messages except as stated otherwise in this Chapter.

title: Section 2L.01 Support 4 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Support 4 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

CMS messaging can be subject to habituation, a phenomenon by which repeated exposure to a stimulus results in diminished response. CMS habituation can occur through repeated exposure to messages, especially those messages that might not be perceived as having relevance to the road user, resulting in diminished responsiveness of the road user to that message. Because messages can be changed or extinguished, the effectiveness of CMS is tied more to the messages displayed thereon, the frequency of displayed messages, and the relevance to the road user, rather than to the installation of the signs themselves.

title: Section 2L.01 Guidance 5 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Guidance 5 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

Changeable message signs should be used judiciously to avoid habituation and preserve their effectiveness during the display of real-time messages about traffic conditions or traffic advisories.

title: Section 2L.01 Standard 6 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Standard 6 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

The design of legends for non-electronic display CMS shall comply with the provisions of Chapters 2A through 2K, 2M, and 2N of this Manual. Other CMS shall comply with the design and application principles established in this Chapter, Chapter 2A, and provisions elsewhere in this Manual for specific signs.

title: Section 2L.01 Standard 7 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Standard 7 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

No items other than inventory or maintenance-related information (see Section 2A.04) shall be displayed on the front or back of a CMS or portable CMS. Names or logos of the manufacturer, brand, or model shall not be displayed on a CMS or portable CMS, either in the message display itself or on the exterior housing.

title: Section 2L.01 Guidance 8 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.01 Guidance 8 - Description of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 510

Blank-out signs that display only single-phase, predetermined electronic-display legends that are limited by their composition and arrangement of pixels or other illuminated forms in a fixed arrangement (such as a blank-out sign indicating a part-time turn prohibition, a blank-out or changeable lane-use sign, or a changeable OPEN/CLOSED sign for a weigh station) should comply with the provisions of the applicable Section for the specific type of sign, provided that the letter forms, symbols, and other legend elements are duplicates of the conventional messages as detailed in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05). Because such a sign is effectively an illuminated version of a conventional sign, the size of its legend elements, the overall size of the sign, and the placement of the sign should comply with the applicable provisions for the conventional version of the sign.

title: Section 2L.02 Standard 1 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Standard 1 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

CMS shall display only traffic operational, regulatory, warning, and guidance information except as otherwise provided in this Chapter. Advertising or other messages not related to traffic control shall not be displayed on a CMS or on its supports or other equipment.

title: Section 2L.02 Option 2 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Option 2 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

CMS may display traffic safety campaign messages (see Section 2L.07), transportation-related messages, emergency homeland security messages, and America’s Missing: Broadcast Emergency Response (AMBER) alert messages, all as provided for in this Chapter.

title: Section 2L.02 Option 3 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Option 3 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

Transportation-related messages for the purpose of improving traffic conditions, such as those providing information on alternative means of transportation, electronic toll collection, or carpooling may be displayed to remind or inform drivers of relevant options or opportunities for transportation.

title: Section 2L.02 Support 4 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Support 4 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

Messages regarding broader transportation items not related to improving traffic conditions, such as reminders of driver’s license or vehicle registration renewal, vehicle recall information, and vehicle maintenance, do not meet the purpose of a transportation-related message.

title: Section 2L.02 Support 5 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Support 5 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

Examples of transportation-related messages include “STADIUM EVENT SUNDAY, DELAYS NOON TO 4 PM” and “OZONE ALERT-USE TRANSIT.”

title: Section 2L.02 Guidance 6 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Guidance 6 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

A CMS should not be used to display a transportation-related message if doing so could adversely affect respect for the sign. “CONGESTION AHEAD” or other overly simplistic or vague messages should not be displayed alone. These messages should be supplemented with a message on the location or distance to the congestion or incident, delay and travel time, alternative route, or other similar messages.

title: Section 2L.02 Guidance 7 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Guidance 7 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

CMS should not be used in place of conventional signs for conditions that do not change, except for blank- out type signs used to display regulatory, warning, and guidance information that routinely reoccurs, but only on a part-time basis. Similarly, when only certain elements of a message on a non-changeable sign are subject to change, only those elements of the sign should be in an electronic display, for example the prices shown on the R3-48 and R3-48a signs (see Figure 2G-18).

title: Section 2L.02 Support 8 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Support 8 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

The purpose of CMS is to provide real-time traffic regulatory, warning, or guidance messages as follows: A. Incident management and route diversion; B. Warning of adverse roadway travel conditions due to weather; C. Special event applications associated with traffic control or conditions; D. Lane, ramp, and roadway control; E. Priced or other types of managed lanes; F. Travel times; G. Warning situations; H. Traffic regulations; I. Speed control or warning; J. Variable destination guidance; K. Supporting temporary traffic control; or L. Active Traffic Management.

title: Section 2L.02 Support 9 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Support 9 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

CMS provide significant flexibility and capability in communicating many types of real-time traffic control messages to road users. While their intended purpose is the display of traffic regulatory, warning, or guidance information, other limited uses are also allowed under certain conditions, as provided in this Chapter. Their integrity as an official traffic control device rests significantly on their judicious use and proper messaging format and content, regardless of the message type being displayed.

title: Section 2L.02 Standard 10 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Standard 10 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

State and local highway agencies that have permanently-installed or positioned CMS shall issue and maintain a policy regarding the use and display of all types of messages to be used on their CMS. The policy shall define the types of messages that will be allowed, the priority of messages, the proper syntax of messages, the timing of messages, and other important messaging elements to ensure messages displayed meet the basic principles that govern the design and use of traffic control devices in general (see Section 1D.01) and traffic signs in particular as provided for in this Manual.

title: Section 2L.02 Guidance 11 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Guidance 11 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 511

State and local agencies that use CMS, but do not have permanently-installed or positioned signs, should develop and establish a policy as discussed in Paragraph 10 of this Section.

title: Section 2L.02 Guidance 12 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Guidance 12 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

When CMS are used at multiple locations to address a specific situation, the message displays should be consistent along the roadway corridor and adjacent corridors, which might necessitate coordination among different operating agencies.

title: Section 2L.02 Guidance 13 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Guidance 13 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

AMBER alerts (see Paragraph 2 of this Section), when displayed, should not preempt messages related to traffic or travel conditions. AMBER alert messages should be kept as brief as possible and, when possible, direct road users to another source, such as broadcast or highway advisory radio, for detailed information about the alert.

title: Section 2L.02 Standard 14 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Standard 14 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

Types of “alert” messages other than AMBER alerts that are unrelated to traffic or travel conditions shall not be displayed on CMS.

title: Section 2L.02 Standard 15 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Standard 15 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

The format of CMS displays shall not be of a type that could be considered similar to advertising or promotional displays.

title: Section 2L.02 Support 16 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Support 16 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

In times of a declared state of emergency, it might be appropriate to display messages related to evacuation, homeland security, or emergency information. Traffic patterns, movement, or other situations might be atypical due to the emergency, necessitating unique messaging not specifically related to traffic conditions.

title: Section 2L.02 Standard 17 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Standard 17 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

Homeland security and emergency messages shall only be displayed in declared states of emergency when there is an imminent threat to the general population. Generic security or personal safety messages shall not be displayed when there is no context of a declared state of emergency or known imminent national security threat. Homeland security and emergency messages shall not be promotional or advisory in nature, including the message design, layout, or manner of display.

title: Section 2L.02 Guidance 18 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.02 Guidance 18 - Applications of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

Homeland Security and emergency messages should undergo significant levels of scrutiny prior to being approved for broadcast to ensure accuracy and consistency with emergency conditions. These messages should be designed to convey a clear and simple meaning in a similar format to traffic control messages.

title: Section 2L.03 Support 1 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.03 Support 1 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

The maximum distance at which a driver can first correctly identify letters and words on a sign is called the legibility distance of the sign. Legibility distance is affected by the characteristics of the sign design and the visual capabilities of drivers. Visual capabilities, and thus legibility distances, vary among drivers.

metadata.section_title: Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs

title: Section 2L.03 Support 2 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.03 Support 2 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

For the more common types of CMS, the longest measured legibility distances on sunny days occur during mid-day when the sun is overhead. Legibility distances are much shorter when the sun is behind the sign face, when the sun is on the horizon and shining on the sign face, or at night.

metadata.section_title: Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs

title: Section 2L.03 Support 3 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.03 Support 3 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

Visibility is the characteristic that enables a CMS to be seen. Visibility is associated with the point where the CMS is first detected, whereas legibility is the point where the message on the CMS can be read. Environmental conditions such as rain, fog, and snow impact the visibility of CMS and can reduce the available legibility distances. During these conditions, there might not be enough viewing time for drivers to read the message.

metadata.section_title: Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs

title: Section 2L.03 Guidance 4 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.03 Guidance 4 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 512

CMS used on roadways with speed limits of 55 mph or higher should be visible from ½ mile under both day and night conditions. The message should be designed to be legible from a minimum distance of 600 feet for nighttime conditions and 800 feet for normal daylight conditions. When environmental conditions that reduce visibility and legibility are present, or when the legibility distances stated in the previous sentences in this paragraph cannot be practically achieved, messages composed of fewer units of information should be used and consideration should be given to limiting the message to a single phase (see Section 2L.05 for information regarding the lengths of messages displayed on CMS).

metadata.section_title: Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs

title: Section 2L.03 Guidance 5 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 2L.03 Guidance 5 - Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

The electronic display of standardized regulatory and warning signs used individually or as part of the legend for a larger sign should meet the size and legend requirements for those specific signs in Chapters 2B and 2C.

metadata.section_title: Legibility and Visibility of Changeable Message Signs

title: Section 2L.04 Standard 1 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Standard 1 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

Except as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section, messages shall not include animation, flashing, dissolving, exploding, scrolling, or other dynamic display elements.

title: Section 2L.04 Standard 2 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Standard 2 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

When a portable CMS is used as an arrow board that uses a flashing or sequential display for a lane or shoulder closure, the display and operation shall be considered that of an arrow board and shall comply with the provisions of Sections 6L.05 and 6L.06.

title: Section 2L.04 Guidance 3 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Guidance 3 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

In developing messages for display on CMS, the provisions of Section 1D.01 should be consulted for the principles of an effective traffic control device.

title: Section 2L.04 Standard 4 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Standard 4 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

All message displays on CMS, whether for traffic operational, regulatory, warning, or guidance information, or for the other allowable message types as defined in this Chapter, shall follow the same design and display principles found in this Manual used for other traffic control signs, except as provided elsewhere in this Chapter.

title: Section 2L.04 Guidance 5 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Guidance 5 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

Except in the case of a limited-legend CMS (such as a blank-out or a part-time regulatory sign display) that is used in place of a conventional regulatory sign or an activated blank-out warning sign that supplements a conventional warning sign at a separate location, the signs should be used as a supplement to and not as a substitute for conventional signs and markings unless otherwise provided for in this Manual.

title: Section 2L.04 Support 6 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Support 6 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

When CMS are overused for messages not directly associated with real-time driving conditions, road users might pay less attention to the sign, thereby limiting their effectiveness as traffic control devices.

title: Section 2L.04 Guidance 7 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Guidance 7 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

Warning Beacons (see Section 4S.03) should not be installed on CMS, rather CMS should be used predominately to display messages that are critical to real-time travel conditions. CMS word messages should be limited to no more than three lines, with no more than 20 characters per line.

title: Section 2L.04 Guidance 8 - Design Characteristics of Messages
text:
Section 2L.04 Guidance 8 - Design Characteristics of Messages
Part: Part 2 Signs
Chapter: Chapter 2L. Changeable Message Signs
Page: 513

The spacing between characters in a word should be between 25 and 40 percent of the letter height. The spacing between words in a message should be between 75 and 100 percent of the letter height. Spacing between the message lines should be between 50 and 75 percent of the letter height. Table 2L-1 contains information for spacing between characters, words, and lines of text. Table 2L-1. The width-to-height ratio of the sign characters should be between 0.7 and 1.0. The stroke width-to-height ratio should be 0.2.
