Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

The primary purposes of the Bicycle Signal (R10-40, R10-40a, R10-41, R10-41a, R10-41b) sign (see Section 9B.22) are to inform road users that the signal indications in the bicycle signal face are intended only for bicyclists, and to inform bicyclists which specific bicyclist movements are controlled by the bicycle signal face. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 4H.03 Standard 2 - Bicycle Signal Signs
text:
Section 4H.03 Standard 2 - Bicycle Signal Signs
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

Except as provided in Paragraph 3 of this Section, a Bicycle Signal (R10-40, R10-40a, R10-41, R10-41a, R10-41b, or R10-41c) sign shall be installed immediately adjacent to (including above or below) every bicycle signal face. The Bicycle Signal sign shall have a minimum size of 24 inches x 36 inches if it is placed next to an overhead-mounted bicycle signal face and shall have a minimum size of 12 inches x 21 inches if it is placed next to a post-mounted bicycle signal face.

title: Section 4H.03 Option 3 - Bicycle Signal Signs
text:
Section 4H.03 Option 3 - Bicycle Signal Signs
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

The Bicycle Signal sign may be omitted adjacent to a supplemental near-side bicycle signal face containing 4-inch indications.

title: Section 4H.04 Standard 1 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Steady (Stop-and-Go) Operation
text:
Section 4H.04 Standard 1 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Steady (Stop-and-Go) Operation
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

Steady bicycle symbol signal indications shall be applied as follows: A. A steady RED BICYCLE signal indication shall be displayed when it is intended to prohibit bicyclists in a designated bicycle lane or from a separate facility such as a shared-use path from entering the intersection or other controlled area. Turning after stopping shall be permitted as stated in Item C in Paragraph 1 of Section 4A.05. B. A steady YELLOW BICYCLE signal indication shall be displayed following a GREEN BICYCLE signal indication in the same bicycle signal face. A YELLOW BICYCLE signal indication shall not be displayed in conjunction with the change from the RED BICYCLE signal indication to a GREEN BICYCLE signal indication. The YELLOW BICYCLE signal indication shall be followed by a RED BICYCLE signal indication. C. A steady GREEN BICYCLE signal indication shall be displayed only when it is intended to permit bicyclists in a designated bicycle lane or from a separate facility such as a shared-use path to enter the intersection as discussed in Section 4A.05.

metadata.section_title: Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Steady (Stop-and-Go) Operation

title: Section 4H.05 Standard 1 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation
text:
Section 4H.05 Standard 1 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

The mode of operation of the bicycle signal faces at a traffic control signal shall be the same as the mode of operation of the other traffic signal faces at the same signalized location. Bicycle signal faces shall operate in the steady (stop-and-go) mode when the other traffic signal faces are operating in the steady (stop-and-go) mode. Bicycle signal faces shall operate in the flashing mode when the other signal faces are operating in the flashing mode. Bicycle signal faces shall not be placed in a dark mode when other vehicular traffic signal faces are operating in the flashing mode.

metadata.section_title: Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation

title: Section 4H.05 Guidance 2 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation
text:
Section 4H.05 Guidance 2 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

When a traffic control signal is operated in the flashing mode, bicycle signal faces should display a flashing RED BICYCLE signal indication if the other vehicular signal faces on the same approach are displaying flashing red signal indications or if there are no other vehicular signal faces on the same approach.

metadata.section_title: Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation

title: Section 4H.05 Guidance 3 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation
text:
Section 4H.05 Guidance 3 - Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

When a traffic control signal is operated in the flashing mode, bicycle signal faces should display a flashing YELLOW BICYCLE signal indication if the other vehicular signal faces for the through lanes on the same approach are displaying flashing yellow signal indications unless it is determined by engineering judgment that a flashing RED BICYCLE signal indication would provide a safer operation.

metadata.section_title: Application of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications during Flashing Operation

title: Section 4H.06 Standard 1 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.06 Standard 1 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 715

Bicycle signal faces shall consist of all bicycle symbol signal indications (see Figure 4H-1). Circular or arrow signal indications shall not be used in a bicycle signal face.

title: Section 4H.06 Option 2 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.06 Option 2 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

Bicycle signal faces may be oriented vertically or horizontally. December 2025

title: Section 4H.06 Standard 3 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.06 Standard 3 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

The layouts and arrangements of the bicycle signal face shall be in accordance with the following provisions: A. Only the bicycle symbol shown on Page 6-7 in the 2004 Standard Highway Signs publication (see Section 1A.05) shall be used for bicycle symbol signal indications and shall be proportioned to fit within the signal lens. The bicycle symbol shall only be positioned horizontally and shall face to the left. B. The RED BICYCLE, YELLOW BICYCLE, and GREEN BICYCLE signal indications shall be in the same relative position to each other as specified for the CIRCULAR RED, CIRCULAR YELLOW, and CIRCULAR GREEN signal indications, respectively, in Sections 4E.04 and 4E.05. C. As a specific exception to Paragraph 5 of Section 4E.04, two YELLOW BICYCLE signal indications or two GREEN BICYCLE signal indications shall not be arranged horizontally adjacent to each other at right angles to the basic straight line arrangement to form a clustered signal face.

title: Section 4H.06 Option 4 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.06 Option 4 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

Backplates (see Paragraphs 18 and 19 in Section 4D.06) may be used with bicycle signal faces.

title: Section 4H.06 Option 5 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.06 Option 5 - Layout of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

If a bicycle signal face having 4-inch signal indications is used, the accompanying visors may be omitted.

title: Section 4H.07 Standard 1 - Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications
text:
Section 4H.07 Standard 1 - Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

There shall be three nominal diameter sizes for bicycle signal indications: 4 inches, 8 inches, and 12 inches.

metadata.section_title: Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications

title: Section 4H.07 Standard 2 - Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications
text:
Section 4H.07 Standard 2 - Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

All signal indications in a bicycle signal face shall be of the same size.

metadata.section_title: Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications

title: Section 4H.07 Standard 3 - Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications
text:
Section 4H.07 Standard 3 - Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

Four-inch signal indications shall not be used for any bicycle signal face other than a supplemental, post-mounted, near-side bicycle signal face.

metadata.section_title: Size of Bicycle Symbol Signal Indications

title: Section 4H.08 Standard 1 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.08 Standard 1 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

The provisions of Sections 4D.05 through 4D.08 shall apply to the placement of the bicycle signal faces except as follows: A. As a specific exception to Item A in Paragraph 1 of Section 4D.05, a minimum of one primary bicycle signal face shall be provided to control traffic for the bicyclist movement, even if a bicyclist through movement exists. B. The primary bicycle signal face shall have either 8-inch or 12-inch signal indications, even if it is located at the near side of the signal-controlled location. C. When the primary bicycle signal face is located more than 120 feet beyond the stop line, a supplemental near-side bicycle signal face shall be provided.

title: Section 4H.08 Guidance 2 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.08 Guidance 2 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

When the primary bicycle signal face is located more than 80 feet and up to 120 feet beyond the stop line, a supplemental near-side bicycle signal face should be provided.

title: Section 4H.08 Guidance 3 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.08 Guidance 3 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 716

A bicycle signal face should be separated horizontally or vertically from the nearest vehicular traffic signal face for the same approach by at least 3 feet measured either horizontally perpendicular to the approach between the centers of the signal faces or vertically from the center of the lowest signal indication of the top signal face to the center of the highest signal indication of the bottom signal face. If horizontally-arranged or clustered signal faces are used, the minimum 3-foot horizontal separation between the two signal faces should be measured from the center of the right-most signal indication in the signal face on the left to the center of the left-most signal indication in the signal face on the right.

title: Section 4H.08 Guidance 4 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.08 Guidance 4 - Placement of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

Bicycle signal faces should be placed such that visibility is maximized for bicyclists and minimized for adjacent or conflicting vehicle movements not controlled by the bicycle signal face. Consideration should be given to using visibility-limited bicycle signal faces in situations where drivers not controlled by the bicycle signal face might be confused by viewing the bicycle signal indications, such as when the bicyclist movement controlled by the bicycle signal face is sometimes allowed to proceed or sometimes required to stop at times when motor vehicle traffic, making the same movement and controlled by other vehicular signal faces, is required to stop or allowed to proceed, respectively.

title: Section 4H.09 Standard 1 - Mounting Height of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.09 Standard 1 - Mounting Height of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

The provisions of Section 4D.09 shall apply to the mounting height of bicycle signal faces except as follows: A. The bottom of the signal housing (including brackets) of a bicycle signal face that is not located over a roadway or shoulder shall be a minimum of 7 feet above the sidewalk or ground, and B. If 4-inch signal indications are used in a supplemental, post-mounted, near-side bicycle signal face, the bottom of the signal housing (including brackets) shall be a minimum of 4 feet and a maximum of 8 feet above the sidewalk or ground. Bicycle signal faces with 4-inch signal indications installed above a pedestrian sidewalk or pathway shall not project more than 4 inches into the pedestrian facility.

metadata.section_title: Mounting Height of Bicycle Signal Faces

title: Section 4H.10 Guidance 1 - Intensity and Light Distribution of Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.10 Guidance 1 - Intensity and Light Distribution of Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

Except for the 4-inch nominal size of the lens diameter, the intensity and distribution of light from each illuminated bicycle signal face should be similar to that recommended for vehicular traffic signal faces in accordance with Paragraph 11 of Section 4E.01 to the extent practical.

metadata.section_title: Intensity and Light Distribution of Bicycle Signal Faces

title: Section 4H.11 Standard 1 - Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.11 Standard 1 - Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

The provisions of Section 4F.17 shall apply to the duration of the yellow change and the red clearance intervals of a bicycle signal phase.

metadata.section_title: Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces

title: Section 4H.11 Guidance 2 - Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.11 Guidance 2 - Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

The minimum duration of the yellow change interval of a bicycle signal phase should be 3 seconds.

metadata.section_title: Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces

title: Section 4H.11 Support 3 - Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces
text:
Section 4H.11 Support 3 - Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

The function of the yellow change interval is to warn bicyclists approaching a signalized location that their permission to proceed is being terminated after which they will be directed to stop. Providing clearance time for a bicyclist to travel through the intersection or conflict area is the purpose of the red clearance interval rather than the yellow change interval.

metadata.section_title: Yellow Change and Red Clearance Intervals for Bicycle Signal Faces

title: Section 4H.12 Option 1 - Bicycle Push Buttons
text:
Section 4H.12 Option 1 - Bicycle Push Buttons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

Bicycle push buttons may be used for bicycle detection.

title: Section 4H.12 Support 2 - Bicycle Push Buttons
text:
Section 4H.12 Support 2 - Bicycle Push Buttons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

The location of bicycle push buttons intended only for use by bicyclists and not pedestrians are determined by engineering judgment considering a reasonable reach without requiring most bicyclists to dismount.

title: Section 4H.12 Standard 3 - Bicycle Push Buttons
text:
Section 4H.12 Standard 3 - Bicycle Push Buttons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 717

Where used, push buttons intended to be used by both pedestrians and bicyclists shall be located and operated to meet all accessibility requirements (see Section 4I.05).

title: Section 4H.12 Standard 4 - Bicycle Push Buttons
text:
Section 4H.12 Standard 4 - Bicycle Push Buttons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4H. Bicycle Signals
Page: 718

Bicycle push buttons shall be accompanied by an appropriate regulatory sign (R10-4, R10-24, or R10-26) explaining the purpose and operation of the push button (see Sections 2B.58 and 9B.20).

title: Section 4I.01 Support 1 - Pedestrian Signal Heads
text:
Section 4I.01 Support 1 - Pedestrian Signal Heads
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 718

Pedestrian signal heads provide special types of traffic signal indications exclusively intended for controlling pedestrians. These signal indications consist of the illuminated symbols of a WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) and an UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK).

title: Section 4I.02 Standard 1 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Standard 1 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 718

All new pedestrian signal head indications shall be displayed within a rectangular background and shall consist of symbolized messages (see Figure 4I-1), except that existing pedestrian signal head indications with lettered or outline style symbol messages shall be permitted to be retained for the remainder of their useful service life. The symbol designs that are set forth in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05) shall be used. Each pedestrian signal head indication shall be independently displayed and emit a single color. Figure 4I-1. Typical Pedestrian Signal Indications A - With countdown display

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Standard 2 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Standard 2 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 718

If a two-section pedestrian signal head is used, the UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal section shall be mounted directly above the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal section. If a one-section pedestrian signal head is used, the symbols shall be either overlaid upon each other or arranged side-by- side with the UPRAISED HAND symbol to the left of the WALKING PERSON symbol, and a light source that can display each symbol independently shall be used. B - Without countdown display

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Standard 3 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Standard 3 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

The WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication shall be white, with all except the symbol obscured by an opaque material for signal optical units that use incandescent lamps within optical assemblies that include lenses. The UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be Portland orange, with all except the symbol obscured by an opaque material for signal optical units that use incandescent lamps within optical assemblies that include lenses.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Standard 4 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Standard 4 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

Except as provided in Paragraph 5 of this Section, the requirements of Chapter 3 of the publication entitled “Equipment and Materials Standards of the Institute of Transportation Engineers,” 2008, ITE, that pertain to the aspects of the pedestrian signal head design that affect the display of the signal indications shall be met for signal optical units that use incandescent lamps within optical assemblies that include lenses. Except as provided in Paragraph 5 of this Section, the requirements of the publication entitled “Pedestrian Traffic Control Signal Indicators - Light Emitting Diode (LED) Signal Modules,” 2011, ITE, that pertain to the aspects of the signal head design that affect the display of the signal indications shall be met for light-emitting diode (LED) pedestrian signal head modules.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Guidance 5 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Guidance 5 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

The intensity and distribution of light from each illuminated pedestrian signal lens or LED pedestrian signal head module should comply with the publications specified in Paragraph 4 of this Section, as appropriate.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Guidance 6 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Guidance 6 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

When not illuminated, the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) and UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) symbols should not be visible to pedestrians at the far end of the crosswalk that the pedestrian signal head indications control.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Standard 7 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Standard 7 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

For pedestrian signal head indications, the symbols shall be at least 6 inches high.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Standard 8 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Standard 8 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

The light source of a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be flashed continuously at a rate of not less than 50 or more than 60 times per minute. The displayed period of each flash shall be a minimum of ½ and a maximum of ²⁄³ of the total flash cycle.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Guidance 9 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Guidance 9 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

Pedestrian signal head indications should be conspicuous and recognizable to pedestrians at all distances from the beginning of the controlled crosswalk to a point 10 feet from the end of the controlled crosswalk during both day and night.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Guidance 10 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Guidance 10 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

For crosswalks where the pedestrian enters the crosswalk more than 100 feet from the pedestrian signal head indications, the symbols should be at least 9 inches high.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Guidance 11 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Guidance 11 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

If the pedestrian signal indication is so bright that it causes excessive glare in nighttime conditions, some form of automatic dimming should be used to reduce the brilliance of the signal indication.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Option 12 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Option 12 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

An animated eyes symbol may be added to a pedestrian signal head in order to prompt pedestrians to look for vehicles in the intersection during the time that the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication is displayed.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.02 Standard 13 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
text:
Section 4I.02 Standard 13 - Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

If used, the animated eyes symbol shall consist of an outline of a pair of white steadily illuminated eyes with white eyeballs that scan from side to side at a rate of approximately once per second. The animated eyes symbol shall be at least 12 inches wide with each eye having a width of at least 5 inches and a height of at least 2.5 inches. The animated eyes symbol shall be illuminated at the start of the walk interval and shall terminate at the end of the walk interval.

metadata.section_title: Size, Design, and Illumination of Pedestrian Signal Head Indications

title: Section 4I.03 Standard 1 - Location and Height of Pedestrian Signal Heads
text:
Section 4I.03 Standard 1 - Location and Height of Pedestrian Signal Heads
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

Pedestrian signal heads shall be mounted with the bottom of the signal housing including brackets not less than 7 feet or more than 10 feet above sidewalk level, and shall be positioned and adjusted to provide maximum visibility at the beginning of the controlled sidewalk.

metadata.section_title: Location and Height of Pedestrian Signal Heads

title: Section 4I.03 Guidance 2 - Location and Height of Pedestrian Signal Heads
text:
Section 4I.03 Guidance 2 - Location and Height of Pedestrian Signal Heads
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 719

If pedestrian signal heads are mounted on the same support as vehicular signal heads, there should be a physical separation between them.

metadata.section_title: Location and Height of Pedestrian Signal Heads

title: Section 4I.04 Standard 1 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Standard 1 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

All pedestrian signal heads used at crosswalks where the pedestrian change interval is more than 7 seconds shall include a pedestrian change interval countdown display in order to inform pedestrians of the number of seconds remaining in the pedestrian change interval.

title: Section 4I.04 Option 2 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Option 2 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

Pedestrian signal heads used at crosswalks where the pedestrian change interval is 7 seconds or less may include a pedestrian change interval countdown display in order to inform pedestrians of the number of seconds remaining in the pedestrian change interval.

title: Section 4I.04 Standard 3 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Standard 3 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

Where countdown pedestrian signals are used, the countdown shall always be displayed simultaneously with the flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication displayed for that crosswalk.

title: Section 4I.04 Standard 4 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Standard 4 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

Countdown pedestrian signals shall consist of Portland orange numbers that are at least 6 inches in height on a black opaque background. The countdown pedestrian signal shall be located immediately adjacent to the associated UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) pedestrian signal head indication (see Figure 4I-1).

title: Section 4I.04 Standard 5 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Standard 5 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

The display of the number of remaining seconds shall begin only at the beginning of the pedestrian change interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND). After the countdown displays zero, the display shall remain dark until the beginning of the next countdown.

title: Section 4I.04 Standard 6 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Standard 6 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

The countdown pedestrian signal shall display the number of seconds remaining until the termination of the pedestrian change interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND). Countdown displays shall not be used during the walk interval. Countdown displays shall not be used during the red clearance interval of a concurrent vehicular phase that is ending simultaneously with or after the end of the pedestrian phase.

title: Section 4I.04 Guidance 7 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Guidance 7 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

If used with a pedestrian signal head that does not have a concurrent vehicular phase, the pedestrian change interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND) should be set to be approximately 4 seconds less than the required pedestrian clearance time (see Section 4I.06) and an additional clearance interval (during which a steady UPRAISED HAND is displayed) should be provided prior to the start of the conflicting vehicular phase.

title: Section 4I.04 Guidance 8 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Guidance 8 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

For crosswalks where the pedestrian enters the crosswalk more than 100 feet from the countdown pedestrian signal display, the numbers should be at least 9 inches in height.

title: Section 4I.04 Guidance 9 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Guidance 9 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

Because some technology includes the countdown pedestrian signal logic in a separate timing device that is independent of the timing in the traffic signal controller, care should be exercised by the engineer when timing changes are made to pedestrian change intervals.

title: Section 4I.04 Guidance 10 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
text:
Section 4I.04 Guidance 10 - Countdown Pedestrian Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

If the pedestrian change interval is interrupted or shortened as a part of a transition into a preemption sequence (see Section 4F.19), the countdown pedestrian signal display should be discontinued and go dark immediately upon activation of the preemption transition.

title: Section 4I.05 Option 1 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Option 1 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

Pedestrian detectors may be push buttons or passive detection devices.

title: Section 4I.05 Support 2 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Support 2 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

Passive detection devices register the presence of a pedestrian in a position indicative of a desire to cross, without requiring the pedestrian to push a button. Some passive detection devices are capable of tracking the progress of a pedestrian as the pedestrian crosses the roadway for the purpose of extending or shortening the duration of certain pedestrian timing intervals.

title: Section 4I.05 Support 3 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Support 3 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 720

The provisions in this Section place pedestrian push buttons within easy reach of pedestrians who are intending to cross each crosswalk and make it obvious which push button is associated with each crosswalk. These provisions also position push button poles in optimal locations for installation of accessible pedestrian signals (see Chapter 4K). Information regarding reach ranges can be found in the U.S. Department of Justice 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, September 15, 2010, 28 CFR 35 and 36, Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

title: Section 4I.05 Guidance 4 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Guidance 4 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

If pedestrian push buttons are used, they should be capable of easy activation requiring no more than 5 pounds of force, should not require tight grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist, and should be conveniently located near each end of the crosswalks. Except as provided in Paragraphs 5 and 6 of this Section, pedestrian push buttons should be located to meet all of the following criteria (see Figure 4I-2): A. Unobstructed and accessible within one or more of the reach ranges specified in Section 308, and from a clear ground space as specified in Section 305, of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; B. To provide a wheelchair accessible route from the push button to the ramp; C. On the side of the curb ramp which is farthest from the center of the intersection; Figure 4I-2. Preferred Push Button Location Area Notes: 1. The push button detector should be located 5 feet or less from the outside edge of the marked crosswalk farthest from the intersection. 2. The push button detector should be located no farther from the crosswalk than the stop line, if one is present. 3. A 4-foot minimum unobstructed pedestrian access route should be maintained. 4. The maximum (MAX.) and minimum (MIN.) dimensions shown in this figure are recommendations. 5. Two pedestrian push buttons on the same corner should be separated by at least 10 feet. The 10-foot dimension shown in this figure is in reference to the placement of the push buttons within their respective areas. 6. Figure 4I-3 shows typical push button locations. 7. This figure is not drawn to scale. D. Not greater than 10 feet from the edge of the associated curb ramp which is farther from the center of the intersection; E. Not greater than 5 feet from the outside edge of the marked crosswalk farthest from the center of the intersection; F. Not farther from the crosswalk than the stop line is, if present; G. Between 1.5 and 6 feet from the face of the curb or from the outside edge of the shoulder (or if no shoulder exists, from the edge of the pavement); H. With the face of the push button parallel to the crosswalk to be used; I. At a mounting height of approximately 3.5 feet, but no more than 4 feet, above the sidewalk; J. Allowing a minimum 4-foot continuous clear width for a pedestrian access route; and K. Outside the flared side of the curb ramp, if present.

title: Section 4I.05 Guidance 5 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Guidance 5 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

Where there are physical constraints that make it impracticable to place the pedestrian push button adjacent to a level all-weather surface, the surface should be as level as feasible.

title: Section 4I.05 Guidance 6 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Guidance 6 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

Where there are physical constraints that make it impracticable to place the pedestrian push button between 1.5 and 6 feet from the face of the curb or from the outside edge of the shoulder (or if no shoulder exists, from the edge of the pavement), it should not be farther than 10 feet from the face of the curb or from the outside edge of the shoulder (or if no shoulder exists, from the edge of the pavement).

title: Section 4I.05 Guidance 7 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Guidance 7 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

Except as provided in Paragraph 8 of this Section, where two pedestrian push buttons are provided on the same corner of a signalized location, the push buttons should be separated by a distance of at least 10 feet.

title: Section 4I.05 Option 8 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Option 8 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

Where there are physical constraints on a particular corner that make it impracticable to provide the 10-foot separation between the two pedestrian push buttons the push buttons may be placed closer together or on the same pole.

title: Section 4I.05 Support 9 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Support 9 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

Figure 4I-3 shows typical pedestrian push button locations for a variety of situations.

title: Section 4I.05 Standard 10 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Standard 10 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

If a pedestrian push button is provided, a sign (see Section 2B.58) shall also be installed adjacent to the pedestrian push button detector explaining the purpose and use.

title: Section 4I.05 Option 11 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Option 11 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

At certain locations, a supplemental sign in a more visible location may be used to call attention to the pedestrian push button.

title: Section 4I.05 Standard 12 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Standard 12 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

The positioning of pedestrian push buttons and the legends on the pedestrian push button signs shall indicate which crosswalk signal is actuated by each pedestrian push button.

title: Section 4I.05 Standard 13 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Standard 13 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

If the pedestrian clearance time is sufficient only to cross from the curb or shoulder to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait and the signals are pedestrian actuated, an additional pedestrian detector shall be provided in the median.

title: Section 4I.05 Guidance 14 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Guidance 14 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

The use of additional pedestrian detectors on islands or medians where a pedestrian might become stranded should be considered.

title: Section 4I.05 Guidance 15 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Guidance 15 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

If used, special purpose push buttons (to be operated only by authorized persons) should include a housing capable of being locked to prevent access by the general public and do not need an instructional sign.

title: Section 4I.05 Standard 16 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Standard 16 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

If used, a pilot light or other means of indication installed with a pedestrian push button shall not be illuminated until actuation. Once it is actuated, the pilot light shall remain illuminated until the pedestrian’s green or WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication is displayed.

title: Section 4I.05 Option 17 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Option 17 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

At signalized locations with a demonstrated need and subject to equipment capabilities, pedestrians with special needs may be provided with additional crossing time by means of an extended push button press.

title: Section 4I.05 Standard 18 - Pedestrian Detectors
text:
Section 4I.05 Standard 18 - Pedestrian Detectors
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

If additional crossing time is provided by means of an extended push button press, a PUSH BUTTON FOR 2 SECONDS FOR EXTRA CROSSING TIME (R10-32P) plaque (see Figure 2B-27) shall be installed adjacent to the pedestrian push button detector.

title: Section 4I.06 Standard 1 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Standard 1 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 722

At intersections equipped with pedestrian signal heads, the pedestrian signal indications shall be displayed except when the vehicular traffic control signal is being operated in the flashing mode. At those times, the pedestrian signal indications shall not be displayed.

title: Section 4I.06 Standard 2 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Standard 2 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 723

Except as provided in Paragraph 3 of Section 4J.03, when the pedestrian signal heads associated with a crosswalk are displaying either a steady WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) or a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication, a steady red signal indication shall be shown to any conflicting vehicular movement that is approaching the intersection or midblock location perpendicular or nearly perpendicular to the crosswalk. Figure 4I-3. Typical Push Button Locations A - Perpendicular curb ramps with B - Parallel curb ramps crosswalks close together C - Perpendicular curb ramps with shared landing area D - Perpendicular curb ramps with continuous surface between ramps Notes: 1. This figure is not drawn to scale. 2. These drawings are intended to describe the typical locations for pedestrian push button installations. They are not intended to be a guide for the design of curb ramps.

title: Section 4I.06 Standard 3 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Standard 3 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 723

When pedestrian signal heads are used, a WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication shall be displayed only when pedestrians are permitted to leave the curb or shoulder.

title: Section 4I.06 Standard 4 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Standard 4 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 724

A pedestrian change interval consisting of a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall begin immediately following the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication. Following the pedestrian change interval, a buffer interval consisting of a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement. The sum of the time of the pedestrian change interval and the buffer interval shall not be less than the calculated pedestrian clearance time (see Paragraphs 7 through 16 of this Section). The buffer interval shall not begin later than the beginning of the red clearance interval, if used. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 4I.06 Option 5 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Option 5 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 724

During the yellow change interval, the UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DON’T WALK) signal indication may be displayed as either a flashing indication, a steady indication, or a flashing indication for an initial portion of the yellow change interval and a steady indication for the remainder of the interval.

title: Section 4I.06 Support 6 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Support 6 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 724

Figure 4I-4 illustrates the pedestrian intervals and their possible relationships with associated vehicular signal phase intervals.

title: Section 4I.06 Guidance 7 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Guidance 7 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 724

Except as provided in Paragraph 8 of this Section, the pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian crossing in the crosswalk who left the curb or edge of pavement at the end of the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication to travel at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second to at least the far side of the traveled way or to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait.

title: Section 4I.06 Option 8 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Option 8 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 724

A walking speed of up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate the sufficiency of the pedestrian clearance time at locations where an extended push button press function has been installed to provide slower pedestrians an opportunity to request and receive a longer pedestrian clearance time. Passive pedestrian detection may also be used to automatically adjust the pedestrian clearance time based on the pedestrian’s actual walking speed or actual clearance of the crosswalk.

title: Section 4I.06 Option 9 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Option 9 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

The additional time provided by an extended push button press to satisfy pedestrian clearance time needs may be added to either the walk interval or the pedestrian change interval. Figure 4I-4. Pedestrian Intervals * The countdown display is optional for Pedestrian Change Intervals of 7 seconds or less. ** The Walk Interval may be reduced under some conditions (see Section 4I.06). *** The Buffer Interval, which shall always be provided and displayed, may be used to help Rev. 1 satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time, or may begin after the calculated pedestrian clearance time has ended. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 4I.06 Guidance 10 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Guidance 10 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

Where pedestrians who walk slower than 3.5 feet per second, or pedestrians who use wheelchairs, routinely use the crosswalk, a walking speed of less than 3.5 feet per second should be considered in determining the pedestrian clearance time.

title: Section 4I.06 Guidance 11 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Guidance 11 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

Except as provided in Paragraph 12 of this Section, the walk interval should be at least 7 seconds in length so that pedestrians will have adequate opportunity to leave the curb or shoulder before the pedestrian clearance time begins.

title: Section 4I.06 Option 12 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Option 12 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

If pedestrian volumes and characteristics do not require a 7-second walk interval, walk intervals as short as 4 seconds may be used.

title: Section 4I.06 Support 13 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Support 13 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

The walk interval is intended for pedestrians to start their crossing. The pedestrian clearance time is intended to allow pedestrians who started crossing during the walk interval to complete their crossing. Longer walk intervals are often used when the duration of the vehicular green phase associated with the pedestrian crossing is long enough to allow it.

title: Section 4I.06 Guidance 14 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Guidance 14 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

The total of the walk interval and pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian crossing in the crosswalk who left the pedestrian detector (or, if no pedestrian detector is present, a location 6 feet behind the face of the curb or 6 feet behind the edge of the pavement) at the beginning of the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication to travel at a walking speed of 3 feet per second to the far side of the traveled way being crossed or to the median if a two-stage pedestrian crossing sequence is used. Any additional time that is required to satisfy the conditions of this paragraph should be added to the walk interval.

title: Section 4I.06 Option 15 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Option 15 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

On a street with a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait, a pedestrian clearance time that allows the pedestrian to cross only from the curb or shoulder to the median may be provided.

title: Section 4I.06 Standard 16 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Standard 16 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

Where the pedestrian clearance time is sufficient only for crossing from the curb or shoulder to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait, median-mounted pedestrian signals, with pedestrian detectors (see Sections 4I.05 and 4K.01) if actuated operation is used, shall be provided and signing such as the R10-3d sign (see Section 2B.58) shall be provided to notify pedestrians to cross only to the median to await the next WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication.

title: Section 4I.06 Support 17 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Support 17 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

Accessible pedestrian signals (see Chapter 4K) where median-mounted pedestrian signals and detectors are used provide information in non-visual formats (such as audible tones and/or speech messages, and vibrating surfaces) so that a pedestrian with vision disabilities can know when to resume crossing the street after crossing to the median.

title: Section 4I.06 Option 18 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Option 18 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

During the transition into preemption, the walk interval and the pedestrian change interval may be shortened or omitted as described in Section 4F.19.

title: Section 4I.06 Option 19 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Option 19 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

At intersections with high pedestrian volumes and high conflicting left-turning or right-turning vehicle volumes, a brief leading pedestrian interval, during which an advance WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) indication is displayed for the crosswalk while red indications continue to be displayed to parallel through and/or turning traffic, may be used to reduce conflicts between pedestrians and turning vehicles.

title: Section 4I.06 Support 20 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Support 20 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

Accessible pedestrian signals (see Chapter 4K) where leading pedestrian intervals are used provide information in non-visual formats (such as audible tones and/or speech messages, and vibrating surfaces) so that a pedestrian with vision disabilities can know when to cross the street in the absence of the audible cues normally provided when the onset of the vehicular and pedestrian movements coincide.

title: Section 4I.06 Support 21 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Support 21 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

If a leading pedestrian interval is used without accessible features, pedestrians with vision disabilities might begin crossing at the onset of the vehicular movement when vehicle operators are not expecting them to begin crossing.

title: Section 4I.06 Guidance 22 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Guidance 22 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 725

If a leading pedestrian interval is used, it should be at least 3 seconds in duration and should be timed to allow pedestrians to cross at least one lane of traffic or, in the case of a large corner radius, to travel far enough for pedestrians to establish their position ahead of the turning traffic before the turning traffic is released.

title: Section 4I.06 Guidance 23 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Guidance 23 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 726

If a leading pedestrian interval is used, consideration should be given to prohibiting turns across the crosswalk during the leading pedestrian interval. December 2025

title: Section 4I.06 Guidance 24 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Guidance 24 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 726

At locations where a leading pedestrian interval is used, the minimum time for the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) indication should be the time provided for the leading pedestrian interval plus 7 seconds.

title: Section 4I.06 Support 25 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
text:
Section 4I.06 Support 25 - Pedestrian Intervals and Signal Phases
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4I. Pedestrian Control Features
Page: 727

At intersections with pedestrian volumes that are so high that drivers have difficulty finding an opportunity to turn across the crosswalk, the duration of the green interval for a parallel concurrent vehicular movement is sometimes intentionally set to extend beyond the pedestrian clearance time to provide turning drivers additional green time to make their turns while the pedestrian signal head is displaying a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication after pedestrians have had time to complete their crossings.

title: Section 4J.01 Support 1 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Support 1 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 727

A pedestrian hybrid beacon is a special type of hybrid beacon used to warn and control traffic at an unsignalized location to assist pedestrians in crossing a street or highway at a marked crosswalk.

title: Section 4J.01 Option 2 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Option 2 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 727

A pedestrian hybrid beacon may be considered for installation to facilitate pedestrian crossings at a location that does not meet traffic signal warrants (see Chapter 4C), or at a location that meets traffic signal warrants under Sections 4C.05 and/or 4C.06 but a decision is made to not install a traffic control signal.

title: Section 4J.01 Standard 3 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Standard 3 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 727

If used, pedestrian hybrid beacons shall be used in conjunction with signs and pavement markings (see Section 4J.02) to warn and control traffic at locations where pedestrians enter or cross a street or highway. A pedestrian hybrid beacon shall only be installed at a marked crosswalk.

title: Section 4J.01 Guidance 4 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Guidance 4 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 727

If one of the signal warrants of Chapter 4C is met and a traffic control signal is justified by an engineering study, and if a decision is made to install a traffic control signal, it should be installed based upon the provisions of Chapters 4D through 4I and 4K.

title: Section 4J.01 Guidance 5 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Guidance 5 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 727

If a traffic control signal is not justified under the signal warrants of Chapter 4C and if gaps in traffic are not adequate to permit pedestrians to cross, or if the speed for vehicles approaching on the major street is too high to permit pedestrians to cross, or if pedestrian delay is excessive, the need for a pedestrian hybrid beacon should be considered on the basis of an engineering study that considers major-street volumes, speeds, widths, and gaps in conjunction with pedestrian volumes, walking speeds, and delay.

title: Section 4J.01 Guidance 6 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Guidance 6 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 727

For a major street where the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed is 35 mph or less, the need for a pedestrian hybrid beacon should be considered if the engineering study finds that the plotted point representing the vehicles per hour on the major street (total of both approaches) and the corresponding total of all pedestrians crossing the major street for 1 hour (any four consecutive 15-minute periods) of an average day falls above the applicable curve in Figure 4J-1 for the length of the crosswalk.

title: Section 4J.01 Guidance 7 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Guidance 7 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 728

For a major street where the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed exceeds 35 mph, the need for a pedestrian hybrid beacon should be considered if the engineering study finds that the plotted point representing the vehicles per hour on the major street (total of both approaches) and the corresponding total of all pedestrians crossing the major street for 1 hour (any four consecutive 15-minute periods) of an average day falls above the applicable curve in Figure 4J-2 for the length of the crosswalk. Figure 4J-1. Guidelines for the Installation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons on Low-Speed Roadways * Note: 20 pph applies as the lower threshold volume Figure 4J-2. Guidelines for the Installation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons on High-Speed Roadways * Note: 20 pph applies as the lower threshold volume

title: Section 4J.01 Guidance 8 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Guidance 8 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 728

For crosswalks that have lengths other than the four that are specifically shown in Figures 4J-1 and 4J-2, the values should be interpolated between the curves.

title: Section 4J.01 Option 9 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Option 9 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 728

The criteria for the pedestrian volume crossing the major street shown in Figures 4J-1 and 4J-2 may be reduced as much as 50 percent if the 15th-percentile crossing speed of pedestrians is less than 3.5 feet per second.

title: Section 4J.01 Option 10 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.01 Option 10 - Application of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 728

Where there is a divided street having a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait, the criteria for the major-street traffic volume shown in Figures 4J-1 and 4J-2 may be applied separately to each direction of vehicular traffic.

title: Section 4J.02 Standard 1 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Standard 1 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 728

Except as otherwise provided in this Section, a pedestrian hybrid beacon shall meet the provisions of Chapters 4D through 4G, 4I, and 4J.

title: Section 4J.02 Standard 2 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Standard 2 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 728

A pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall consist of three signal sections, with a CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indication centered below two horizontally-aligned CIRCULAR RED signal indications (see Figure 4J-3).

title: Section 4J.02 Standard 3 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Standard 3 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 728

When an engineering study finds that installation of a pedestrian hybrid beacon is justified, then: A. At least two pedestrian hybrid beacon faces shall be installed for each approach of the major street; B. A stop line shall be installed for each approach to the crosswalk; C. A pedestrian signal head complying with the provisions set forth in Chapter 4I shall be installed at each end of the marked crosswalk; D. The pedestrian hybrid beacon shall be pedestrian actuated; and E. If the pedestrian hybrid beacon is installed at or immediately adjacent to an intersection with a minor street, a STOP sign shall be installed for each minor-street approach.

title: Section 4J.02 Guidance 4 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Guidance 4 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

When an engineering study finds that installation of a pedestrian hybrid beacon is justified, then: A. Parking and other sight obstructions should be prohibited for at least 100 feet in advance of and at least 20 feet beyond the marked crosswalk, or site accommodations should be made through curb extensions or other techniques to provide adequate sight distance; and B. If installed within a signal system, the pedestrian hybrid beacon should be coordinated. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 4J-3. Sequence for a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon 1. Dark Until Activated 2. Flashing Yellow Upon Activation 3. Steady Yellow 4. Steady Red During Pedestrian Walk Interval 5. Alternating Flashing Red During Pedestrian Change Interval 6. Dark Again Until Activated Note: An optional steady red clearance interval may be added after Interval 3, and an optional short buffer interval (alternating flashing red while the pedestrian signal heads are displaying a steady UPRAISED HAND) may be added after Interval 5.

title: Section 4J.02 Guidance 5 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Guidance 5 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

On approaches having posted or statutory speed limits or 85th-percentile speeds in excess of 35 mph and on approaches having traffic or operating conditions that would tend to obscure visibility of roadside hybrid beacon face locations, both of the minimum of two pedestrian hybrid beacon faces should be installed over the roadway.

title: Section 4J.02 Guidance 6 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Guidance 6 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

On multi-lane approaches having posted or statutory speed limits or 85th-percentile speeds of 35 mph or less, either a pedestrian hybrid beacon face should be installed on each side of the approach (if a median of sufficient width exists) or at least one of the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces should be installed over the roadway.

title: Section 4J.02 Guidance 7 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Guidance 7 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

A pedestrian hybrid beacon should comply with the signal face location provisions described in Sections 4D.05 through 4D.10.

title: Section 4J.02 Option 8 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Option 8 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

A CROSSWALK-STOP ON RED (symbolic circular red) (R10-23) or a STOP ON RED-YIELD ON FLASHING RED AFTER STOP (R10-23a) sign (see Section 2B.59) may be installed facing each major street approach. Rev. 1

title: Section 4J.02 Option 9 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Option 9 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

A W11-2 (Pedestrian), S1-1 (School), or W11-15 (Trail) crossing warning sign with an AHEAD (W16-9P) supplemental plaque may be placed in advance of a pedestrian hybrid beacon. A Warning Beacon may be installed to supplement the W11-2, S1-1, or W11-15 sign.

title: Section 4J.02 Option 10 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Option 10 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

Backplates (see Section 4D.06) may be used with pedestrian hybrid beacons.

title: Section 4J.02 Support 11 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Support 11 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

Accessible pedestrian signals (see Chapter 4K) where a pedestrian hybrid beacon is used provide information in non-visual formats (such as audible tones and/or speech messages, and vibrating surfaces) so that a pedestrian with vision disabilities can know when to cross the street.

title: Section 4J.02 Guidance 12 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Guidance 12 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

If a Warning Beacon supplements a W11-2 sign in advance of a pedestrian hybrid beacon, it should be programmed to flash only when the pedestrian hybrid beacon is not in the dark mode.

title: Section 4J.02 Standard 13 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Standard 13 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

If a Warning Beacon is installed to supplement the W11-2 sign, the design and location of the Warning Beacon shall comply with the provisions of Sections 4S.01 and 4S.03.

title: Section 4J.02 Standard 14 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.02 Standard 14 - Design of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

Bicycle signal faces (see Chapter 4H) shall not be used at a pedestrian hybrid beacon.

title: Section 4J.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 729

Pedestrian hybrid beacon indications shall be dark (not illuminated) during periods between actuations.

title: Section 4J.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

Following an actuation by a pedestrian, a pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall display a flashing CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by a steady CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by both steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian walk interval, followed by alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian change interval (see Figure 4J-3). Upon December 2025 termination of the pedestrian change interval, the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces shall revert to a dark (not illuminated) condition.

title: Section 4J.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, the pedestrian signal heads shall continue to display a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication when the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces are either dark or displaying flashing or steady CIRCULAR yellow signal indications. The pedestrian signal heads shall display a WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication when the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces are displaying steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications. The pedestrian signal heads shall display a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication when the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces are displaying alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications. Upon termination of the pedestrian change interval, the pedestrian signal heads shall revert to a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication.

title: Section 4J.03 Option 4 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Option 4 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

Where the pedestrian hybrid beacon is installed adjacent to a roundabout to facilitate crossings by pedestrians with vision disabilities and an engineering study determines that pedestrians without vision disabilities can be allowed to cross the roadway without actuating the pedestrian hybrid beacon, the pedestrian signal heads may be dark (not illuminated) when the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces are dark.

title: Section 4J.03 Guidance 5 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Guidance 5 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

The duration of the flashing yellow interval should be determined by engineering judgment.

title: Section 4J.03 Guidance 6 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Guidance 6 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

The duration of the flashing yellow interval should not vary on a cycle-by-cycle basis.

title: Section 4J.03 Guidance 7 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Guidance 7 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

If the pedestrian hybrid beacon is coordinated as a part of a signal system, it should remain in the dark condition after a pedestrian actuation has been received until the point in the background cycle when the predetermined duration of the flashing yellow interval needs to be initiated in order to achieve the appropriate coordinated offset.

title: Section 4J.03 Option 8 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Option 8 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

If a minimum dark time between activations of the pedestrian hybrid beacon has been set on the controller, the pedestrian hybrid beacon may remain in the dark condition after a pedestrian actuation has been received until the minimum dark time has been provided.

title: Section 4J.03 Support 9 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Support 9 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

The minimum dark time is a preprogrammed time set in the controller that provides time between the pedestrian actuation and beginning of the flashing yellow interval. At locations in coordinated signal systems, the dark time can be variable based on when the pedestrian actuation occurs in the coordinated signal timing sequence.

title: Section 4J.03 Standard 10 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Standard 10 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

The duration of the steady yellow change interval shall be determined using engineering practices in accordance with the provisions in Section 4F.17.

title: Section 4J.03 Guidance 11 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Guidance 11 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

A steady yellow change interval should have a minimum duration of 3 seconds and a maximum duration of 6 seconds (see Section 4F.17). The longer intervals should be reserved for use on approaches with higher speeds.

title: Section 4J.03 Option 12 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Option 12 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

A steady red clearance interval may be used after the steady yellow change interval.

title: Section 4J.03 Option 13 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Option 13 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

The alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications may continue to flash for a short period after the pedestrian change interval has terminated to provide a buffer interval for pedestrians.

title: Section 4J.03 Guidance 14 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Guidance 14 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 730

A pedestrian hybrid beacon that is located 200 feet or less from an active grade crossing should be preempted in accordance with the applicable provisions in Sections 4F.19 and 8D.09.

title: Section 4J.03 Standard 15 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4J.03 Standard 15 - Operation of Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4J. Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
Page: 731

If a pedestrian hybrid beacon is placed into a flashing mode by a conflict monitor (malfunction management unit) or by a manual switch, the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces shall display flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indications to each approach of the major street and the pedestrian signal heads shall revert to a dark (not illuminated) condition.

title: Section 4K.01 Support 1 - General
text:
