Section 4K.01 Support 1 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

Accessible pedestrian signals and detectors provide information in non-visual formats (such as audible tones and/or speech messages, and vibrating surfaces). The decision of when to use accessible pedestrian signals is subject to requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Support 2 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Support 2 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

The primary technique that pedestrians with vision disabilities use to cross streets at signalized locations is to initiate their crossing when they hear the traffic in front of them stop and the traffic alongside them begin to move, which often corresponds to the onset of the green interval. The existing environment is often not sufficient to provide the information that pedestrians with vision disabilities need to cross a roadway at a signalized location.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Support 3 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Support 3 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

The following factors are relevant in determining whether a particular signalized location presents difficulties for pedestrians with vision disabilities to cross the roadway: A. Potential demand for accessible pedestrian signals; B. A request for accessible pedestrian signals; C. Traffic volumes during times when pedestrians might be present, including periods of low traffic volumes or high turn-on-red volumes; D. The complexity of the traffic signal phasing (such as split phases, protected turn phases, leading pedestrian intervals, and exclusive pedestrian phases); and E. The complexity of the intersection geometry.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Support 4 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Support 4 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

The factors that make crossing at a signalized location difficult for pedestrians with vision disabilities include: increasingly quiet vehicles, turns on red (which mask the beginning of the through phase), continuous turning movements, complex signal operations, circular intersections, and wide streets. In addition, low traffic volumes might make it difficult for pedestrians with vision disabilities to discern signal phase changes.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Support 5 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Support 5 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

State and local organizations providing support services to pedestrians with vision and/or hearing disabilities can provide advice to the traffic engineer on site-specific accessibility decisions. In addition, orientation and mobility specialists or similar staff can provide advice to inform such decisions. The U.S. Access Board (www. access-board.gov) provides technical assistance for making pedestrian signal information accessible to persons with vision disabilities.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Standard 6 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Standard 6 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

When used, accessible pedestrian signals shall be used in combination with pedestrian signal timing.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Standard 7 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Standard 7 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

The information provided by an accessible pedestrian signal shall indicate which pedestrian crossing is served by each device.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Standard 8 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Standard 8 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

Under steady (stop-and-go) operation, accessible pedestrian signals shall not be limited in operation by the time of day or day of week.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Option 9 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Option 9 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

Accessible pedestrian signal detectors may be push buttons or passive detection devices.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Option 10 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Option 10 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

At locations with pretimed traffic control signals or non-actuated approaches, pedestrian push buttons may be used to activate the accessible pedestrian signals.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Support 11 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Support 11 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

Accessible pedestrian signals are typically integrated into the pedestrian detector (push button), so the audible tones and/or messages come from the push button housing. They have a push button locator tone and a vibrotactile arrow, and can include audible beaconing and other special features.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Option 12 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Option 12 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

The name of the street to be crossed may also be provided in accessible format, such as Braille or raised characters. Tactile maps of crosswalks may also be provided.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Support 13 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Support 13 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 731

Specifications regarding Braille or raised characters can be found in the U.S. Department of Justice 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, September 15, 2010, 28 CFR 35 and 36, Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.01 Standard 14 - General
text:
Section 4K.01 Standard 14 - General
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

At accessible pedestrian signal locations where pressing the pedestrian push button is necessary to activate the walk interval, pressing the pedestrian push button shall activate both the walk interval and the accessible pedestrian signals.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Support 1 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Support 1 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

Technology that provides different sounds for each non-concurrent signal phase has frequently been found to provide ambiguous information. Research indicates that a rapid percussive tone for each crossing coming from accessible pedestrian signal devices on separated poles located close to each crosswalk provides unambiguous information to pedestrians with vision disabilities. Vibrotactile indications provide information to pedestrians who are blind and deaf and are also used by pedestrians who are blind or who have low vision to confirm the walk signal in noisy situations.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 2 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 2 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

Accessible pedestrian signals shall have both audible and vibrotactile walk indications.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 3 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 3 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

Vibrotactile walk indications shall be provided by a vibrotactile arrow that is located on the push button (see Paragraph 1 in Section 4K.04). The vibrotactile arrow shall vibrate during the walk interval.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 4 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 4 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

Accessible pedestrian signals shall have an audible walk indication during the walk interval only.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 5 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 5 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

The audible walk indication shall be audible at the beginning of the associated crosswalk. The accessible walk indication shall have the same duration as the pedestrian walk signal except when the pedestrian signal rests in walk.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Guidance 6 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Guidance 6 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

If the pedestrian signal rests in walk, the accessible walk indication should be limited to the first 7 seconds of the walk interval. The accessible walk indication should be recalled by a button press during the walk interval provided that the crossing time remaining is longer than the pedestrian change interval.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 7 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 7 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

Where two accessible pedestrian signals on one corner, or in a median, that are associated with different phases are placed less than 10 feet apart, the audible walk indication shall be a speech walk message (see Paragraph 3 in Section 4K.02). In all other cases, including at midblock crossings, on corners where only one accessible pedestrian signal is present, in a median, and on corners where two accessible pedestrian signals are separated by a distance of at least 10 feet, the audible walk indication shall be a percussive tone.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 8 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 8 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 732

Audible tone walk indications shall repeat at eight to ten ticks per second. Audible tones used as walk indications shall consist of multiple frequencies with a dominant component at 880 Hz.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Guidance 9 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Guidance 9 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

The volume of audible walk indications and push button locator tones (see Section 4K.04) should be set to be a maximum of 5 dBA louder than ambient sound, except when audible beaconing is provided in response to an extended push button press.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 10 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 10 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

Automatic volume adjustment up to a maximum volume of 100 dBA in response to ambient traffic sound level shall be provided.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Guidance 11 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Guidance 11 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

The sound level of audible walk indications and push button locator tones should be adjusted to be low enough to avoid misleading pedestrians with vision disabilities when the following conditions exist: A. Where there is an island that allows unsignalized right turns across a crosswalk between the island and the sidewalk. B. Where multi-leg approaches or complex signal phasing require more than two pedestrian phases, such that it might be unclear which crosswalk is served by each audible tone. C. At intersections where a diagonal pedestrian crossing is allowed, or where one street receives a WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication simultaneously with another street.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Option 12 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Option 12 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

An alert tone, which is a very brief burst of high-frequency sound at the beginning of the audible walk indication that rapidly decays to the frequency of the walk tone, may be used to alert pedestrians to the beginning of the walk interval.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Support 13 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Support 13 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

An alert tone can be particularly useful if the walk tone is not easily audible in some traffic conditions.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Support 14 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Support 14 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

Speech walk messages communicate to pedestrians which street has the walk interval. To be a useful system, the words and their meaning need to be correctly understood by all users in the context of the street environment where they are used. Because of this, tones are the preferred means of providing audible walk indications except where two accessible pedestrian signals on one corner are not separated by a distance of at least 10 feet.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Support 15 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Support 15 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

If speech walk messages are used, pedestrians have to know the names of the streets that they are crossing in order for the speech walk messages to be unambiguous. In getting directions to travel to a new location, pedestrians with vision disabilities do not always get the name of each street to be crossed. Therefore, it is desirable to give users of accessible pedestrian signals the name of the street controlled by the push button. This can be done by means of a speech push button information message (see Section 4K.05) during the flashing or steady UPRAISED HAND intervals, or by raised print and Braille labels on the push button housing.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Support 16 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Support 16 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

By combining the information from the push button message or Braille label, the vibrotactile arrow aligned in the direction of travel on the relevant crosswalk, and the speech walk message, pedestrians with vision disabilities are able to correctly respond to speech walk messages even if there are two push buttons on the same pole.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 17 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 17 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

If speech walk messages are used to communicate the walk interval, they shall provide a clear message that the walk interval is in effect, as well as to which crossing it applies.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Guidance 18 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Guidance 18 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

Speech walk messages that are used at intersections having pedestrian phasing that is concurrent with vehicular phasing should be patterned after the model: “Broadway. Walk sign is on to cross Broadway.”

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Guidance 19 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Guidance 19 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

Speech walk messages that are used at intersections having exclusive pedestrian phasing should be patterned after the model: “Walk sign is on for all crossings.”

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Guidance 20 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Guidance 20 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

Speech walk messages should not contain any additional information, except they should include designations such as “Street” or “Avenue” where this information is necessary to avoid ambiguity at a particular location.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Guidance 21 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Guidance 21 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

Speech walk messages should not state or imply a command to the pedestrian, such as “Cross Broadway now.” Speech walk messages should not tell pedestrians that it is “safe to cross,” because it is always the pedestrian’s responsibility to check actual traffic conditions.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 22 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 22 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 733

A speech walk message is not required at times when the walk interval is not timing, but, if provided: A. It shall begin with the term “wait.” B. It need not be repeated for the entire time that the walk interval is not timing.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 23 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 23 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

If a pilot light (see Section 4I.05) is used at an accessible pedestrian signal location, each actuation shall be accompanied by the speech message “wait.”

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Option 24 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Option 24 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

Accessible pedestrian signals that provide speech walk messages may provide similar messages in languages other than English, if needed.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.03 Standard 25 - Walk Indications
text:
Section 4K.03 Standard 25 - Walk Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

If used, speech walk messages in a language other than English shall be stated first in English, and then repeated in the second language, alternating back and forth while the walk interval is timing.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Standard 1 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Standard 1 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

To enable pedestrians with vision disabilities to distinguish and locate the appropriate push button at an accessible pedestrian signal location, and to help them align with the crosswalk, each push button shall clearly indicate by means of a vibrotactile arrow which crosswalk signal is actuated by the push button. Vibrotactile arrows shall be located on the button of the push button assembly, shall have high visual contrast (light on dark or dark on light), and shall be aligned parallel to the direction of travel on the associated crosswalk.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Standard 2 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Standard 2 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

A locator tone shall be incorporated into the accessible pedestrian signal equipment to help pedestrians with vision disabilities locate the vibrotactile arrow, and the associated push button if a push button is provided.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Support 3 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Support 3 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

A push button locator tone is a repeating sound that informs approaching pedestrians that a push button to actuate pedestrian timing or receive additional information exists, and that enables pedestrians with vision disabilities to locate the push button.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Standard 4 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Standard 4 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

Push button locator tones shall have a duration of 0.15 seconds or less, and except as provided in Paragraph 5 of this Section, push button locator tones shall repeat at 1-second intervals at all times that the audible walk indication is not active, including during the pedestrian change interval and during the time that the pedestrian signal is resting in walk (see Paragraph 6 in Section 4K.03).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Option 5 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Option 5 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

The push button locator tone may default to a deactivated mode during periods when the steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication is being displayed for the associated crosswalk if a passive pedestrian detection system is implemented that activates the locator tone at all times (other than when the audible walk indication is active) that a pedestrian is present within a 12-foot radius from the push button location. Where pedestrian facilities (such as sidewalks) are present, the passive detection requirement may be reduced such that it only applies to pedestrians who are on the pedestrian facilities within the 12-foot radius from the push button location.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Standard 6 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Standard 6 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

Push button locator tones shall be deactivated when the traffic control signal or pedestrian hybrid beacon is operating in a flashing mode. This requirement shall not apply to traffic control signals or pedestrian hybrid beacons that are activated from a flashing or dark mode to a steady (stop-and-go) mode by pedestrian actuations.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Standard 7 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Standard 7 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

Push button locator tones shall be intensity responsive to ambient sound.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.04 Guidance 8 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
text:
Section 4K.04 Guidance 8 - Vibrotactile Arrows and Locator Tones
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

Push button locator tones should be audible 6 to 12 feet from the push button, or to the building line, whichever is less.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Option 1 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Option 1 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 734

Pedestrians may be provided with additional features such as increased crossing time, audible beaconing, or a speech push button information message as a result of an extended push button press.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Standard 2 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Standard 2 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

If an extended push button press (see Paragraph 18 in Section 4I.05) is used to provide any additional feature(s), a push button press of less than one second shall actuate only the pedestrian timing and any associated accessible walk indication, and a push button press of one second or more shall actuate the pedestrian timing, any associated accessible walk indication, and any additional feature(s).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Standard 3 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Standard 3 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

If additional crossing time is provided by means of an extended push button press, a PUSH BUTTON FOR 2 SECONDS FOR EXTRA CROSSING TIME (R10-32P) plaque (see Section 4I.05) shall be installed adjacent to the pedestrian push button detector.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Support 4 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Support 4 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

Audible beaconing is the use of an audible signal in such a way that pedestrians with vision disabilities can home in on the signal that is located on the far end of the crosswalk as they cross the street.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Support 5 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Support 5 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

Not all crosswalks at an intersection need audible beaconing. Audible beaconing is not appropriate at locations with channelized turns or split phasing, because of the possibility of confusion.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Guidance 6 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Guidance 6 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

Audible beaconing should be considered following an engineering study at: A. Crosswalks longer than 70 feet, unless those crosswalks are divided by a median that has another accessible pedestrian signal with a locator tone; B. Crosswalks that are skewed; C. Intersections with irregular geometry, such as more than four legs; D. Crosswalks where audible beaconing is requested by a person with vision disabilities; or E. Other locations where a study indicates audible beaconing would be beneficial.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Guidance 7 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Guidance 7 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

If audible beaconing is used, it should be initiated by an extended push button press.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Standard 8 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Standard 8 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

If audible beaconing is used, the volume of the push button locator tone during the pedestrian change interval of the called pedestrian phase shall be increased up to a maximum of 100 dBA, and shall come from a loudspeaker that is mounted at the far end of the crosswalk at a height of 7 to 10 feet above the pavement.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Guidance 9 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Guidance 9 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

The audible beaconing loudspeaker mounted at the far end of the crosswalk should be within the width of the crosswalk.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Support 10 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Support 10 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

When the locator tone is active during the pedestrian change interval at a traffic control signal or pedestrian hybrid beacon where audible beaconing is used, the locator tone from the audible beaconing loudspeaker is at an elevated volume, while the locator tone from the accessible pedestrian signal is at its normal, quiet setting.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Option 11 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Option 11 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

The sound level of the accessible pedestrian signal walk indication and subsequent push button locator tone may be increased by an extended push button press.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Option 12 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Option 12 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

Speech push button information messages may provide intersection identification, as well as information about unusual intersection signalization and geometry, such as notification regarding exclusive pedestrian phasing, leading pedestrian intervals, split phasing, diagonal crosswalks, and medians or islands.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Standard 13 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Standard 13 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

If speech push button information messages are made available by actuating the accessible pedestrian signal detector, they shall only be actuated when the walk interval is not timing. They shall begin with the term “Wait,” followed by intersection identification information modeled after: “Wait to cross Broadway at Grand.” If information on intersection signalization or geometry is also given, it shall follow the intersection identification information.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Guidance 14 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Guidance 14 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 735

Speech push button information messages should not be used to provide landmark information or to inform pedestrians with vision disabilities about detours or temporary traffic control situations.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4K.05 Support 15 - Extended Push Button Press Features
text:
Section 4K.05 Support 15 - Extended Push Button Press Features
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors
Page: 736

Additional information on the structure and wording of speech push button information messages is included in the Institute of Transportation Engineers’ “Electronic Toolbox for Making Intersections More Accessible for Pedestrians Who Are Blind or Visually Impaired.” MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4K. Accessible Pedestrian Signals And Detectors

title: Section 4L.01 Option 1 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.01 Option 1 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

A pedestrian-activated and/or bicyclist-activated rectangular rapid flashing beacon (RRFB) may be used to provide supplemental emphasis to pedestrian, school, and trail warning signs at marked crosswalks across uncontrolled approaches.

metadata.section_title: Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.01 Standard 2 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.01 Standard 2 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

An RRFB shall only be installed to function as a Warning Beacon (see Section 4S.03). Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter, all other provisions of the MUTCD applicable to Warning Beacons shall apply to RRFBs.

metadata.section_title: Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.01 Standard 3 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.01 Standard 3 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

An RRFB shall only be used to supplement a post-mounted W11-2 (Pedestrian), S1-1 (School), or W11-15 (Trail) crossing warning sign with a diagonal downward arrow (W16-7P) plaque, or an overhead- mounted W11-2 , S1-1, or W11-15 crossing warning sign, located at a marked crosswalk. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.01 Standard 4 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.01 Standard 4 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

Except for crosswalks across the approach to or egress from a roundabout, or crosswalks across free-flow turn lanes separated by a channelizing island, an RRFB shall not be used for crosswalks across approaches controlled by YIELD signs, STOP signs, traffic control signals, or pedestrian hybrid beacons.

metadata.section_title: Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.01 Option 5 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.01 Option 5 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

An additional RRFB may be installed on that approach in advance of the crosswalk, as a Warning Beacon to supplement a W11-2 (Pedestrian), S1-1 (School), or W11-15 (Trail) crossing warning sign with an AHEAD (W16-9P) or distance (W16-2P or W16-2aP) plaque.

metadata.section_title: Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.01 Standard 6 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.01 Standard 6 - Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

If an additional RRFB is installed on the approach in advance of the crosswalk, it shall be supplemental to and not a replacement for the RRFB at the crosswalk itself.

metadata.section_title: Application of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 1 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 1 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

Each RRFB unit shall consist of two rapidly-flashed rectangular-shaped yellow indications, each with an LED-array based pulsing light source. The size of each RRFB indication shall be at least 5 inches wide by at least 2 inches high.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 2 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 2 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

The two RRFB indications for each RRFB unit shall be aligned horizontally, with the longer dimension horizontal and with a minimum space between the two indications of at least 7 inches, measured from nearest edge of one indication to the nearest edge of the other indication. The outside edges of the RRFB indications, including any housings, shall not project beyond the outside edges of the W11-2, S1-1, or W11-15 sign that it supplements.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 3 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 3 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

An RRFB unit shall not be installed independent of the crossing warning signs for the approach that the RRFB faces. If the RRFB unit is supplementing a post-mounted sign, the RRFB unit shall be installed on the same support as the associated W11-2, S1-1, or W11-15 crossing warning sign and plaque. If the RRFB unit is supplementing an overhead-mounted sign, the RRFB unit shall be mounted directly above the top of sign or below the bottom of the sign.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Option 4 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Option 4 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

As a specific exception to Paragraph 6 of Section 4S.01, the RRFB unit associated with a post-mounted sign and plaque may be located between and immediately adjacent to the bottom of the crossing warning sign and the top of the supplemental downward diagonal arrow plaque (or, in the case of a supplemental advance sign, the AHEAD or distance plaque) or within 12 inches above the crossing warning sign, rather than the recommended minimum of 12 inches above or below the sign assembly.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Option 5 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Option 5 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 736

Signal visors and backplates, with or without a yellow retroreflective strip, may be used with RRFB units based on provisions in Section 4D.06.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 6 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 6 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 737

For any approach on which RRFBs are used to supplement post-mounted signs, at least two W11-2 , S1-1, or W11-15 crossing warning signs (each with an RRFB unit and a W16-7P plaque) shall be installed at the crosswalk, one on the right-hand side of the roadway and one on the left-hand side of the roadway. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Guidance 7 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Guidance 7 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 737

On a divided highway, the left-hand side RRFB assembly should be installed on the median, if practicable, rather than on the far left side of the highway.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 8 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 8 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 737

For any approach on which RRFBs are used to supplement an overhead-mounted sign, at least one W11-2 , S1-1, or W11-15 crossing warning sign (without a W16-7P plaque) located approximately over the center of the lanes of the approach (or where optimum visibility can be achieved) shall be installed at the crosswalk.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 9 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 9 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 737

If used at intersections, the design of the RRFBs shall conform to the requirements for post-mounted or overhead placement described in Paragraph 3 of this Section.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Option 10 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Option 10 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 737

RRFBs may be installed at intersections with more than one crosswalk on the same uncontrolled approach (see Figure 4L-1).

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Option 11 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Option 11 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

If used at intersections with two crosswalks on an uncontrolled approach, post-mounted RRFBs may be installed to face only one direction of travel at the first crosswalk that traffic encounters (see Figure 4L-1). Figure 4L-1. Example of RRFBs at Uncontrolled, Marked Crosswalks at an Intersection Rev. 1 Rev. 1 Notes: 1. When activated, the RRFBs on both approaches shall simultaneously commence operation of their rapid flashing indications and shall cease operation simultaneously. 2. If placed overhead, follow the requirements of Paragraph 8 of Section 4L.02, except that the signs may be placed approximately over the center of the intersection. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 12 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 12 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

The light intensity of the yellow indications during daytime conditions shall meet the minimum specifications for Class 1 yellow peak luminous intensity in the publication “Directional Flashing Optical Warning Devices for Authorized Emergency, Maintenance, and Service Vehicles J595,” 2005, Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE).

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Option 13 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Option 13 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

If the RRFB indications are so bright that they cause excessive glare during nighttime conditions, an automatic signal dimming device may be used to reduce the brilliance of the RRFB indications during nighttime conditions.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.02 Standard 14 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.02 Standard 14 - Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

If pedestrian push button detectors (rather than passive detection) are used to actuate the RRFB indications, a PUSH BUTTON FOR WARNING LIGHTS/WAIT FOR GAP IN TRAFFIC (R10-25) sign (see Section 2B.58) shall be installed explaining the purpose and use of the pedestrian push button detector.

metadata.section_title: Design of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

The RRFB shall be normally dark, shall initiate operation only upon pedestrian actuation, and shall cease operation at a predetermined time after the pedestrian actuation or, with passive detection, after the pedestrian clears the crosswalk.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

All RRFB units associated with a given crosswalk (including those with an advance crossing sign, if used) shall, when activated, simultaneously commence operation of their rapid flashing indications and shall cease operation simultaneously.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Guidance 3 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Guidance 3 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

The minimum duration of a predetermined period of operation of the RRFBs following each actuation should be based on the procedures for the timing of pedestrian clearance times for pedestrian signals (see Section 4I.06).

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Support 4 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Support 4 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

One consideration for lengthening the duration of the predetermined period of operation of the RRFBs is adding the perception/reaction time for pedestrians to confirm that a vehicle will yield or stop.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Standard 5 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Standard 5 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

The predetermined flash period shall be immediately initiated each and every time that a pedestrian is detected either through passive detection or as a result of a pedestrian pressing a push button detector, including when pedestrians are detected while the RRFBs are already flashing and when pedestrians are detected immediately after the RRFBs have ceased flashing.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Standard 6 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Standard 6 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 738

When activated, the two yellow indications in each RRFB unit shall flash in a rapidly flashing sequence. As a specific exception to the requirements for the flash rate of beacons provided in Paragraph 3 of Section 4S.01, RRFBs shall use a much faster flash rate and shall provide 75 flashing sequences per minute.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Standard 7 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Standard 7 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 739

Except as provided in Paragraph 8 of this Section, during each 800-millisecond flashing sequence, the left and right RRFB indications shall operate using the following sequence: A. The RRFB indication on the left-hand side shall be illuminated for approximately 50 milliseconds. B. Both RRFB indications shall be dark for approximately 50 milliseconds. C. The RRFB indication on the right-hand side shall be illuminated for approximately 50 milliseconds. D. Both RRFB indications shall be dark for approximately 50 milliseconds. E. The RRFB indication on the left-hand side shall be illuminated for approximately 50 milliseconds. F. Both RRFB indications shall be dark for approximately 50 milliseconds. G. The RRFB indication on the right-hand side shall be illuminated for approximately 50 milliseconds. December 2025 H. Both RRFB indications shall be dark for approximately 50 milliseconds. I. Both RRFB indications shall be illuminated for approximately 50 milliseconds. J. Both RRFB indications shall be dark for approximately 50 milliseconds. K. Both RRFB indications shall be illuminated for approximately 50 milliseconds. L. Both RRFB indications shall be dark for approximately 250 milliseconds.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Standard 8 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Standard 8 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 739

The flash rate of each individual RRFB indication, as applied over the full flashing sequence, shall not be more than 5 flashes per second, to avoid frequencies that might cause seizures.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Standard 9 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Standard 9 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 739

If an audible information device is used in conjunction with an RRFB, the audible information device shall not use vibrotactile indications or percussive indications.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4L.03 Guidance 10 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4L.03 Guidance 10 - Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4L. Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons
Page: 740

If an audible information device is used in conjunction with an RRFB, the audible message should be a speech message that says, “Warning lights are flashing.” The audible message should be spoken twice.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4M.01 Support 1 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.01 Support 1 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

An emergency-vehicle traffic control signal is a special traffic control signal that directs all conflicting traffic to stop in order to permit the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle to proceed into the roadway or intersection.

metadata.section_title: Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.01 Option 2 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.01 Option 2 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

An emergency-vehicle traffic control signal may be installed at a location that does not meet other traffic signal warrants such as at an intersection or other location to permit direct access from a building housing the emergency vehicle.

metadata.section_title: Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.01 Option 3 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.01 Option 3 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

An emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon may be installed instead of an emergency-vehicle traffic control signal under the conditions described in Section 4N.01.

metadata.section_title: Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.01 Guidance 4 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.01 Guidance 4 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

If a traffic control signal is not justified under the signal warrants of Chapter 4C and if gaps in traffic are not adequate to permit the timely entrance of emergency vehicles, or the stopping sight distance for vehicles approaching on the major street is insufficient for emergency vehicles, installing an emergency-vehicle traffic control signal should be considered. If one of the signal warrants of Chapter 4C is met and a traffic control signal is justified by an engineering study, and if a decision is made to install a traffic control signal, it should be installed based upon the provisions of Chapters 4D through 4I and 4K.

metadata.section_title: Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.01 Guidance 5 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.01 Guidance 5 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

The sight distance determination should be based on the location of the visibility obstruction for the critical approach lane for each street or drive and the posted or statutory speed limit or 85th-percentile speed on the major street, whichever is higher.

metadata.section_title: Application of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Standard 1 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Standard 1 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

Except as otherwise provided in this Section, an emergency-vehicle traffic control signal shall meet the requirements of this Manual.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Standard 2 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Standard 2 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

An Emergency Vehicle (W11-8) sign (see Section 2C.54) with an EMERGENCY SIGNAL AHEAD (W11-12P) supplemental plaque shall be placed in advance of all emergency-vehicle traffic control signals. If a Warning Beacon is installed to supplement the W11-8 sign, the design and location of the beacon shall comply with the Standards of Sections 4S.01 and 4S.03.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Guidance 3 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Guidance 3 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

At least one of the two required signal faces for each approach on the major street should be located over the roadway.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Guidance 4 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Guidance 4 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

The following size signal indications should be used for emergency-vehicle traffic control signals: 12-inch diameter for steady red and steady yellow circular signal indications and any arrow indications, and 8-inch diameter for green or flashing yellow circular signal indications.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Standard 5 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Standard 5 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

An EMERGENCY SIGNAL (R10-13) sign (see Section 2B.59) shall be installed facing each major- street approach.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Standard 6 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Standard 6 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

If an overhead signal face is provided, the EMERGENCY SIGNAL sign shall be mounted adjacent to the overhead signal face.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Option 7 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Option 7 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

An approach that only serves emergency vehicles may be provided with only one signal face consisting of one or more signal sections.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.02 Option 8 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.02 Option 8 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

Besides using an 8-inch diameter signal indication, other appropriate means to reduce the flashing yellow light output may be used.

metadata.section_title: Design of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 740

Green signal indications for emergency vehicles at signalized locations operating in the steady (stop- and-go) mode shall be obtained as provided in Section 4F.19.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 741

As a minimum, the signal indications, sequence, and manner of operation of an emergency-vehicle traffic control signal installed at a midblock location shall be as follows: A. The signal indication, between emergency-vehicle actuations, shall be either green or flashing yellow. If the flashing yellow signal indication is used instead of the green signal indication, it shall be displayed in the normal position of the green signal indication, while the steady red and steady yellow signal indications shall be displayed in their normal positions. B. When an emergency-vehicle actuation occurs, a steady yellow change interval followed by a steady red interval shall be displayed to traffic on the major street. C. A yellow change interval is not required following the green interval for the emergency- vehicle driveway.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.03 Guidance 3 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.03 Guidance 3 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 741

Emergency-vehicle traffic control signals located at intersections should either be operated in the flashing mode (see Sections 4G.01 and 4G.03) between emergency-vehicle actuations or be full-actuated or semi-actuated to accommodate normal vehicular and pedestrian traffic on the streets.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.03 Guidance 4 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.03 Guidance 4 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 741

Warning Beacons, if used with an emergency-vehicle traffic control signal, should be flashed only: A. For an appropriate time in advance of and during the steady yellow change interval for the major street, and B. During the steady red interval for the major street.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.03 Guidance 5 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.03 Guidance 5 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 741

The duration of the steady red interval for traffic on the major street should be determined by on-site test- run time studies, but should not exceed 1.5 times the time required for the emergency vehicle to clear the path of conflicting vehicles.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4M.03 Option 6 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 4M.03 Option 6 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

An emergency-vehicle traffic control signal sequence may be initiated manually from a local control point such as a fire station or law enforcement headquarters or from an emergency vehicle equipped for remote operation of the signal.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Traffic Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4M. Traffic Control Signals For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.01 Standard 1 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.01 Standard 1 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

Emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons shall be used only in conjunction with signs to warn and control traffic at an unsignalized location where emergency vehicles enter or cross a street or highway. Emergency- vehicle hybrid beacons shall be actuated only by authorized emergency or maintenance personnel.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.01 Guidance 2 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.01 Guidance 2 - Application of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

Emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons should only be used when all of the following criteria are satisfied: A. The conditions justifying an emergency-vehicle traffic control signal (see Section 4M.01) are met; B. An engineering study, considering the road width, approach speeds, and other pertinent factors, determines that emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons can be designed and located in compliance with the requirements contained in this Chapter and in Section 4S.01, such that they effectively warn and control traffic at the location; and C. The location is not at or within 100 feet from an intersection or driveway where the side road or driveway is controlled by a STOP or YIELD sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Standard 1 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Standard 1 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

Except as otherwise provided in this Section, an emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon shall meet the requirements of this Manual.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Standard 2 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Standard 2 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

An emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon face shall consist of three signal sections, with a CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indication centered below two horizontally-aligned CIRCULAR RED signal indications (see Figure 4N-1).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Standard 3 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Standard 3 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

At least two emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon faces shall be installed for each approach of the major street.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Guidance 4 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Guidance 4 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

On approaches having posted or statutory speed limits or 85th-percentile speeds in excess of 40 mph, and on approaches having traffic or operating conditions that would tend to obscure visibility of roadside beacon faces, both of the minimum of two emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon faces should be installed over the roadway.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Guidance 5 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Guidance 5 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

On multi-lane approaches having posted or statutory speed limits or 85th-percentile speeds of 40 mph or less, either an emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon face should be installed on each side of the approach (if a median of sufficient width exists) or at least one of the emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon faces should be installed over the roadway.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Guidance 6 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Guidance 6 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 742

An emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon should comply with the signal face location provisions described in Sections 4D.05 through 4D.10.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Standard 7 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Standard 7 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

Stop lines and EMERGENCY SIGNAL-STOP ON FLASHING RED (R10-14 or R10-14a) signs (see Section 2B.59) shall be used with emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons for each approach of the major street. Figure 4N-1. Sequence for an Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacon Note: An optional steady red clearance interval may be used after Interval 3 and before Interval 4.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Option 8 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Option 8 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

If needed for extra emphasis, a STOP HERE ON FLASHING RED (R10-14b) sign (see Section 2B.59) may be installed with an emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Option 9 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Option 9 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

Emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons may be equipped with a light or other display visible to the operator of the egressing emergency vehicle to provide confirmation that the beacons are operating.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Option 10 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Option 10 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

Emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons may be supplemented with an advance warning sign, which may also be supplemented with a Warning Beacon (see Section 4S.03).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.02 Guidance 11 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.02 Guidance 11 - Design of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

If a Warning Beacon is used to supplement the advance warning sign, it should be programmed to flash only when the emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon is not in the dark mode.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

Emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons shall be placed in a dark mode (no indications displayed) during periods between actuations.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

Upon actuation by authorized emergency personnel, the emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon faces shall each display a flashing yellow signal indication, followed by a steady yellow change interval, prior to displaying two CIRCULAR RED signal indications in an alternating flashing array for a duration of time adequate for egress of the emergency vehicles (see Figure 4N-1). The alternating flashing red signal indications shall only be displayed when it is required that drivers on the major street stop and then proceed subject to the rules applicable after making a stop at a STOP sign. Upon termination of the flashing red signal indications, the emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons shall revert to a dark mode (no indications displayed) condition.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Guidance 3 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Guidance 3 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

The duration of the flashing yellow interval should be determined by engineering judgment.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Standard 4 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Standard 4 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

The duration of the steady yellow change interval shall be determined using engineering practices in accordance with the provisions in Section 4F.17.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Guidance 5 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Guidance 5 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

A yellow change interval should have a minimum duration of 3 seconds and a maximum duration of 6 seconds (see Section 4F.17). The longer intervals should be reserved for use on approaches with higher speeds.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Option 6 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Option 6 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
