Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

A steady red clearance interval may be used after the steady yellow change interval.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Guidance 7 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Guidance 7 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 743

An emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon that is located 200 feet or less from an active grade crossing should be preempted in accordance with the applicable provisions in Sections 4F.19 and 8D.09.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4N.03 Standard 8 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
text:
Section 4N.03 Standard 8 - Operation of Emergency-Vehicle Hybrid Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access
Page: 744

If an emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon is placed into a flashing mode by a conflict monitor (malfunction management unit) or by a manual switch, the emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon faces shall display flashing yellow signal indications to each approach of the major street.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4N. Hybrid Beacons For Emergency-Vehicle Access

title: Section 4O.01 Support 1 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.01 Support 1 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 744

A traffic control signal at a narrow bridge, tunnel, or roadway section that is not of sufficient width for two opposing vehicles to pass is a special signal that alternates which direction of travel is permitted to proceed.

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4O.01 Support 2 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.01 Support 2 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 744

Temporary traffic control signals (see Sections 4D.11 and 6L.01) are the most frequent application of traffic control signals for one-lane, two-way facilities.

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4O.01 Guidance 3 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.01 Guidance 3 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 744

Sight distance across or through the one-lane, two-way facility should be considered as well as the approach speed and sight distance approaching the facility when determining whether traffic control signals should be installed.

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4O.01 Option 4 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.01 Option 4 - Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 744

At a narrow bridge, tunnel, or roadway section where a traffic control signal is not justified under the conditions of Chapter 4C, a traffic control signal may be used if gaps in opposing traffic do not permit the flow of traffic through the one-lane section of roadway.

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4O.02 Standard 1 - Design of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.02 Standard 1 - Design of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 744

The provisions of Chapters 4D through 4G shall apply to traffic control signals for one-lane, two-way facilities, except that: A. The durations of the red clearance intervals shall be adequate to clear the one-lane section of conflicting vehicles; and B. Adequate means, such as interconnection, shall be provided to prevent conflicting signal indications, such as green and green, at opposite ends of the section.

metadata.section_title: Design of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4O.03 Guidance 1 - Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.03 Guidance 1 - Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 744

Traffic control signals at one-lane, two-way facilities should operate in a manner consistent with traffic requirements.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4O.03 Guidance 2 - Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.03 Guidance 2 - Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 744

Adequate time should be provided to allow traffic to clear the narrow facility before opposing traffic is allowed to move. Engineering judgment should be used to determine the proper timing for the signal.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4O.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
text:
Section 4O.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
Page: 745

When in the flashing mode, the signal indications shall flash red.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Traffic Control Signals for One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4O. Traffic Control Signals For One-Lane, Two-Way Facilities

title: Section 4P.01 Support 1 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.01 Support 1 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

Ramp control signals are traffic control signals that control the flow of traffic entering the freeway facility. This is often referred to as “ramp metering.”

metadata.section_title: Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.01 Support 2 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.01 Support 2 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

Freeway entrance ramp control signals are sometimes used if controlling traffic entering the freeway could reduce the total expected delay to traffic in the freeway corridor, including freeway ramps and local streets.

metadata.section_title: Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.01 Guidance 3 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.01 Guidance 3 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

The installation of ramp control signals should be preceded by an engineering study of the physical and traffic conditions on the highway facilities likely to be affected. The study should include the ramps and ramp connections and the surface streets that would be affected by the ramp control, as well as the freeway section concerned.

metadata.section_title: Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.01 Support 4 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.01 Support 4 - Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

Information on conditions that might justify freeway entrance ramp control signals, factors to be evaluated in traffic engineering studies for ramp control signals, design of ramp control signals, and operation of ramp control signals can be found in the FHWA’s “Ramp Management and Control Handbook.”

metadata.section_title: Application of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Standard 1 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Standard 1 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

Ramp control signals shall meet all of the standard design specifications for traffic control signals, except as otherwise provided in this Section.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Standard 2 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Standard 2 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

The signal face for freeway entrance ramp control signals shall be either a two-section signal face containing red and green signal indications or a three-section signal face containing red, yellow, and green signal indications.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Option 3 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Option 3 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

Ramp control signals may be placed in the dark mode (no indications displayed) when not in use.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Option 4 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Option 4 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

Ramp control signals may be used to control some, but not all, lanes on a ramp, such as when non-metered HOV bypass lanes are provided on a ramp.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Standard 5 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Standard 5 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

If only one controlled lane is present on an entrance ramp, or if more than one controlled lane is present on an entrance ramp and the ramp control signals are operated such that green signal indications are always displayed simultaneously to all of the controlled lanes on the ramp, then a minimum of two signal faces per ramp shall face entering traffic.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Standard 6 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Standard 6 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

If two controlled lanes are present on an entrance ramp and the ramp control signals are operated such that green signal indications are not always displayed simultaneously to both of the controlled lanes on the ramp, then one signal face shall be provided over the approximate center of each separately-controlled lane.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Standard 7 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Standard 7 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

If three or more controlled lanes are present on an entrance ramp and the ramp control signals are operated such that green signal indications are not always displayed simultaneously to all of the controlled lanes on the ramp, then one signal face shall be provided over the approximate center of each separately- controlled lane.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Guidance 8 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Guidance 8 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

Additional side-mounted signal faces should be considered for ramps with three or more separately- controlled lanes.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Option 9 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Option 9 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

For entrance ramps with only one controlled lane, the two required signal faces may both be mounted at the side of the roadway on a single pole (as a specific exception to the normal 8-foot minimum lateral separation of signal faces required by Section 4D.07), with the lower signal face installed at a minimum mounting height of 4.5 feet.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Option 10 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Option 10 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 745

For entrance ramps with two or more controlled lanes, if two signal faces are installed for the right-hand lane or for the left-hand lane, the two signal faces for that lane may both be mounted at the closest side of the roadway on a single pole (as a specific exception to the normal 8-foot minimum lateral separation of signal faces required by Section 4D.07), with the lower signal face installed at a minimum mounting height of 4.5 feet.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Guidance 11 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Guidance 11 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 746

Ramp control signals should be located and designed to minimize their viewing by mainline freeway traffic.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Guidance 12 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Guidance 12 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 746

Regulatory signs with legends appropriate to the control, such as XX VEHICLE(S) PER GREEN or XX VEHICLE(S) PER GREEN EACH LANE (see Section 2B.61), should be installed.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.02 Guidance 13 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.02 Guidance 13 - Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 746

When ramp control signals are installed on a freeway-to-freeway ramp, special consideration should be given to assuring adequate visibility of the ramp control signals, and multiple advance warning signs with flashing Warning Beacons should be installed to warn road users of the metered operation.

metadata.section_title: Design of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.03 Guidance 1 - Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.03 Guidance 1 - Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 746

Operational strategies for ramp control signals, such as periods of operation, metering rates and algorithms, and queue management, should be determined by the operating agency prior to the installation of the ramp control signals and should be closely monitored and adjusted as needed thereafter.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.03 Guidance 2 - Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.03 Guidance 2 - Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 746

When the ramp control signals are operated only during certain periods of the day, a RAMP METERED WHEN FLASHING (W3-8) sign (see Section 2C.37) should be installed in advance of the ramp control signal near the entrance to the ramp, or on the arterial on the approach to the ramp, to alert road users to the presence and operation of ramp meters.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4P.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
text:
Section 4P.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps
Page: 747

The RAMP METERED WHEN FLASHING sign shall be supplemented with a Warning Beacon (see Section 4S.03) that flashes when the ramp control signal is in operation (controlling the flow of traffic entering the freeway). Flashing light-emitting diode (LED) units shall not be used within the legend or border of the sign.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Freeway Entrance Ramp Control Signals
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4P. Traffic Control Signals For Freeway Entrance Ramps

title: Section 4Q.01 Support 1 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
text:
Section 4Q.01 Support 1 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Traffic signals for movable bridges are a special type of highway traffic signal installed at movable bridges to notify road users to stop because of a road closure rather than alternately controlling the flow of conflicting traffic movements. The signals are operated in coordination with the opening and closing of the movable bridge, and with the operation of movable bridge warning and resistance gates, or other devices and features used to warn, control, and stop traffic.

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.01 Support 2 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
text:
Section 4Q.01 Support 2 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Movable bridge warning gates installed at movable bridges decrease the likelihood of vehicles and pedestrians passing the stop line and entering an area where potential hazards exist because of bridge operations.

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.01 Support 3 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
text:
Section 4Q.01 Support 3 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

A movable bridge resistance gate is sometimes used at movable bridges and located downstream of the movable bridge warning gate. A movable bridge resistance gate provides a physical deterrent to road users when placed in the appropriate position. The movable bridge resistance gates are considered a design feature and not a traffic control device; requirements for them are contained in AASHTO’s “Standard Specifications for Movable Highway Bridges.”

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.01 Standard 4 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
text:
Section 4Q.01 Standard 4 - Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Traffic control at movable bridges shall include both signals and gates, except in the following cases: A. Neither is required if other traffic control devices or measures considered appropriate are used under either of the following conditions: 1. On low-volume roads (roads of less than 400 vehicles average daily traffic), or 2. At manually-operated bridges if electric power is not available. B. Only signals are required in urban areas if intersecting streets or driveways make gates ineffective. C. Only movable bridge warning gates are required if a traffic control signal that is controlled as part of the bridge operations exists within 500 feet of the movable bridge resistance gates and no intervening traffic entrances exist.

metadata.section_title: Application of Traffic Control for Movable Bridges
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Standard 1 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Standard 1 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

The signal faces and mountings of movable bridge signals shall comply with the provisions of Chapters 4D through 4G except as provided in this Section.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Standard 2 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Standard 2 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Signal faces with 12-inch diameter signal indications shall be used for all new movable bridge signals.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Option 3 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Option 3 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Existing signal faces with 8-inch diameter lenses may be retained for the remainder of their useful service life.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Standard 4 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Standard 4 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Since movable bridge operations cover a variable range of time periods between openings, the signal faces shall be one of the following types: A. Three-section signal faces with red, yellow, and green signal indications; or B. Two one-section signal faces with red signal indications in a vertical array separated by a STOP HERE ON RED (R10-6) sign (see Section 2B.59).

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Standard 5 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Standard 5 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Regardless of which signal type is selected, at least two signal faces shall be provided for each approach to the movable span and a stop line (see Section 3B.19) shall be installed to indicate the point behind which vehicles are required to stop.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 6 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 6 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

If movable bridge operation is frequent, the use of three-section signal faces should be considered.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 7 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 7 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 747

Insofar as practicable, the height and lateral placement of signal faces should comply with the requirements for other traffic control signals in accordance with Chapter 4D. They should be located no more than 50 feet in advance of the movable bridge warning gate.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Option 8 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Option 8 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

Movable bridge signals may be supplemented with audible warning devices to provide additional warning to drivers and pedestrians.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 9 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 9 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

A DRAW BRIDGE (W3-6) sign (see Section 2C.36) should be used in advance of movable bridge signals and gates to give warning to road users, except in urban conditions where such signing would not be practical.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Standard 10 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Standard 10 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

If physical conditions prevent a road user from having a continuous view of at least two signal indications for the distance specified in Table 4D-2, an auxiliary device (either a supplemental signal face or the DRAW BRIDGE (W3-6) sign to which has been added a Warning Beacon that is interconnected with the movable bridge controller unit) shall be provided in advance of movable bridge signals and gates.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Option 11 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Option 11 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

The DRAW BRIDGE (W3-6) sign may be supplemented by a Warning Beacon (see Section 4S.03).

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Support 12 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Support 12 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

If two sets of gates (both a warning and a resistance gate) are used for a single direction, highway traffic signals are not required to accompany the resistance gate nearest the span opening.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Standard 13 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Standard 13 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

Movable bridge warning gates, if used, shall be at least standard railroad size, striped with 16-inch alternate vertical, fully-reflectorized red and white stripes. Flashing red lights in accordance with the Standards for those on railroad gates (see Section 8D.03) shall be included on the gate arm and they shall only be operated if the gate is closed or in the process of being opened or closed.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 14 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 14 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

In the horizontal position, the top of the gate should be approximately 4 feet above the pavement.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 15 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 15 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

Movable bridge warning gates should be of lightweight construction. In its normal upright position, the gate arm should provide adequate lateral clearance.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Option 16 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Option 16 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

The movable bridge resistance gates may be delineated, if practical, in a manner similar to the movable bridge warning gate.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 17 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 17 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

Movable bridge warning gates, if used, should extend at least across the full width of the approach lanes if movable bridge resistance gates are used. On divided highways in which the roadways are separated by a barrier median, movable bridge warning gates, if used, should extend across all roadway lanes approaching the span openings.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 18 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 18 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

If movable bridge resistance gates are not used on undivided highways, movable bridge warning gates, if used, should extend across the full width of the roadway.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Option 19 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Option 19 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

A single full-width gate or two half-width gates may be used.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Support 20 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Support 20 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

The locations of movable bridge signals and gates are determined by the location of the movable bridge resistance gate (if used) rather than by the location of the movable spans. The movable bridge resistance gates for high-speed highways are preferably located 50 feet or more from the span opening except for bascule and lift bridges, where they are often attached to, or are a part of, the structure.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 21 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 21 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

Except where physical conditions make it impracticable, movable bridge warning gates should be located 100 feet or more from the movable bridge resistance gates or, if movable bridge resistance gates are not used, 100 feet or more from the movable span.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 22 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 22 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

On bridges or causeways that cross a long reach of water and that might be hit by large marine vessels, within the limits of practicality, traffic should not be halted on a section of the bridge or causeway that is subject to impact.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 23 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 23 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 748

In cases where it is impractical to halt traffic on a span that is not subject to impact, traffic should be halted at least one span from the opening. If traffic is halted by signals and gates more than 330 feet from the movable bridge warning gates (or from the span opening if movable bridge warning gates are not used), a second set of gates should be installed approximately 100 feet from the gate or span opening.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.02 Guidance 24 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.02 Guidance 24 - Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 749

If the movable bridge is close to a grade crossing and traffic might possibly be stopped on the crossing as a result of the bridge opening, a traffic control device should notify the road users to not stop on the railroad tracks.

metadata.section_title: Design and Location of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.03 Standard 1 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 749

Traffic control devices at movable bridges shall be coordinated with the movable spans, so that the signals, gates, and movable spans are controlled by the bridge tender through an interlocked control.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.03 Standard 2 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 749

If the three-section type of signal face is used, the green signal indication shall be displayed at all times between bridge openings, except that if the bridge is not expected to open during continuous periods in excess of 5 hours, a flashing yellow signal indication shall be permitted to be used. The signal shall display a steady red signal indication when traffic is required to stop. The duration of the yellow change interval between the display of the green and steady red signal indications, or flashing yellow and steady red signal indications, shall be determined using engineering practices (see Section 4F.17).

metadata.section_title: Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.03 Standard 3 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 749

If the vertical array of red signal indications is the type of signal face selected, the red signal indications shall flash alternately only when traffic is required to stop.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4Q.03 Guidance 4 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
text:
Section 4Q.03 Guidance 4 - Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges
Page: 750

Traffic control signals on adjacent streets and highways should be interconnected with the movable bridge control if indicated by engineering judgment. When such interconnection is provided, the traffic control signals at adjacent intersections should be preempted by the operation of the movable bridge in the manner described in Section 4F.19.

metadata.section_title: Operation of Movable Bridge Signals and Gates
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4Q. Traffic Control For Movable Bridges

title: Section 4R.01 Standard 1 - Traffic Signals at Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.01 Standard 1 - Traffic Signals at Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

Traffic control signals or devices that closely resemble traffic control signals that use red or green circular indications shall not be used at toll plazas to indicate the open or closed status of the toll plaza lanes.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.01 Guidance 2 - Traffic Signals at Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.01 Guidance 2 - Traffic Signals at Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

Traffic control signals or devices that closely resemble traffic control signals that use red or green circular indications should not be used for new or reconstructed installations at toll plazas to indicate the success or failure of electronic toll payments or to alternately direct drivers making cash toll payments to stop and then proceed.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.02 Standard 1 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.02 Standard 1 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

Lane-use control signals used at toll plazas shall comply with the provisions of Chapter 4T except as otherwise provided in this Section.

metadata.section_title: Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.02 Standard 2 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.02 Standard 2 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

At toll plazas with multiple lanes where one or more lanes is sometimes closed to traffic, a lane-use control signal shall be installed above the center of each toll plaza lane to indicate the open or closed status of the controlled lane.

metadata.section_title: Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.02 Option 3 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.02 Option 3 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

The bottom of the signal housing of a lane-use control signal above a toll plaza lane having a canopy may be mounted lower than 15 feet above the pavement, but not lower than the vertical clearance of the canopy structure.

metadata.section_title: Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.02 Option 4 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.02 Option 4 - Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

Lane-use control signals may also be used to indicate the open or closed status of an Open-Road ETC lane as a supplement to other devices used for the temporary closure of a lane (see Part 6).

metadata.section_title: Lane-Use Control Signals at or Near Toll Plazas
metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.03 Standard 1 - Warning Beacons at Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.03 Standard 1 - Warning Beacons at Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

Warning Beacons used at toll plazas shall comply with the provisions of Chapter 4S except as otherwise provided in this Section.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.03 Guidance 2 - Warning Beacons at Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.03 Guidance 2 - Warning Beacons at Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 750

Warning Beacons, if used with a toll plaza canopy sign (see Section 2F.16) to assist drivers of such vehicles in locating the dedicated ETC Account-Only lane(s), should be installed in a manner such that the beacons are distinctly separate from the lane-use control signals (see Section 4T.01) for the toll plaza lane.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4R.03 Option 3 - Warning Beacons at Toll Plazas
text:
Section 4R.03 Option 3 - Warning Beacons at Toll Plazas
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas
Page: 751

Warning Beacons that are mounted on toll plaza islands, behind impact attenuators in front of toll plaza islands, and/or on toll booth pylons (ramparts) to identify them as objects in the roadway may be mounted at a height that is appropriate for viewing in a toll plaza context, even if that height is lower than the normal minimum of 8 feet above the pavement.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 4R. Highway Traffic Signals At Toll Plazas

title: Section 4S.01 Support 1 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Support 1 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

A flashing beacon is a highway traffic signal with one or more signal sections that operates in a flashing mode. It can provide traffic control when used as an intersection control beacon (see Section 4S.02) or it can provide warning when used in other applications (see Sections 4S.03, 4S.04, and 4S.05).

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.01 Standard 2 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Standard 2 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

Flashing beacon units, their mountings, signal visors, and backplates shall comply with the provisions of Chapters 4D and 4E, except as otherwise provided in this Chapter.

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.01 Standard 3 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Standard 3 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

Beacons shall be flashed at a rate of not less than 50 or more than 60 times per minute. The illuminated period of each flash shall be a minimum of ½ and a maximum of ²⁄³ of the total cycle.

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.01 Standard 4 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Standard 4 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

A beacon shall not be included within the border of a sign except for Interchange Exit Direction signs with advisory speed panels (see Section 2E.25).

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.01 Standard 5 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Standard 5 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

There shall be two nominal diameter sizes for flashing beacon signal indications: 8 inches and 12 inches.

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.01 Guidance 6 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Guidance 6 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

If used to supplement a warning or regulatory sign, the edge of the beacon signal housing should normally be located no closer than 12 inches outside of the nearest edge of the sign or from the nearest edge of any of the signs and plaques in a sign assembly.

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.01 Option 7 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Option 7 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

An automatic dimming device may be used to reduce the brilliance of flashing yellow signal indications during night operation.

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.01 Option 8 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
text:
Section 4S.01 Option 8 - General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

Backplates (see Section 4D.06) may be used with flashing beacons.

metadata.section_title: General Design and Operation of Flashing Beacons

title: Section 4S.02 Standard 1 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Standard 1 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

An Intersection Control Beacon shall consist of one or more signal faces directed toward each approach to an intersection. Each signal face shall consist of one or more signal sections of a standard traffic signal face, with flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW or CIRCULAR RED signal indications in each signal face. They shall be installed and used only at an intersection to control two or more directions of travel.

title: Section 4S.02 Standard 2 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Standard 2 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

Application of Intersection Control Beacon signal indications shall be limited to the following: A. Yellow on one route (normally the major street) and red for the remaining approaches that are controlled by STOP signs, or B. Red for all approaches (if all of the intersection approaches are controlled by STOP signs).

title: Section 4S.02 Standard 3 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Standard 3 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

Flashing yellow signal indications shall not face conflicting vehicular approaches.

title: Section 4S.02 Standard 4 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Standard 4 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

A STOP sign (see Section 2B.04) shall be used on approaches to which a flashing red signal indication is displayed on an Intersection Control Beacon.

title: Section 4S.02 Standard 5 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Standard 5 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

If two horizontally-aligned red signal indications are used on an approach for an Intersection Control Beacon, they shall be flashed simultaneously to avoid being confused with grade crossing flashing-light signals. If two vertically-aligned red signal indications that have a physical separation between them are used on an approach for an Intersection Control Beacon, they shall be flashed alternately.

title: Section 4S.02 Standard 6 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Standard 6 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

Twelve-inch signal indications shall be used for Intersection Control Beacons facing approaches where: A. Road users view both Intersection Control Beacon and lane-use control signal indications simultaneously; or B. The nearest Intersection Control Beacon signal face is more than 120 feet beyond the stop line, unless a supplemental near-side Intersection Control Beacon signal face is provided.

title: Section 4S.02 Guidance 7 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Guidance 7 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 751

Twelve-inch signal indications should be used for Intersection Control Beacons facing approaches where: A. The posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile approach speed is higher than 40 mph, or B. Where only post-mounted flashing beacon signal faces are used.

title: Section 4S.02 Guidance 8 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Guidance 8 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

An Intersection Control Beacon should not be mounted on a pedestal in the roadway unless the pedestal is within the confines of a traffic or pedestrian island. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 4S.02 Option 9 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Option 9 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

Supplemental signal indications may be used on one or more approaches in order to provide adequate visibility to approaching road users.

title: Section 4S.02 Option 10 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Option 10 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

Intersection Control Beacons may be used at intersections where traffic or physical conditions do not justify conventional traffic control signals but crash rates indicate the possibility of a special need.

title: Section 4S.02 Option 11 - Intersection Control Beacon
text:
Section 4S.02 Option 11 - Intersection Control Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

An Intersection Control Beacon is generally located over the center of an intersection; however, it may be used at other suitable locations.

title: Section 4S.03 Support 1 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Support 1 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

Typical applications of Warning Beacons include the following: A. As supplemental emphasis to signs or object markers on or in front of obstructions that are in or immediately adjacent to the roadway; B. As supplemental emphasis to warning signs; C. As emphasis for midblock crosswalks; D. As supplemental emphasis to regulatory signs, except STOP, DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and SPEED LIMIT signs; and E. In conjunction with a regulatory or warning sign that includes the phrase WHEN FLASHING in its legend or on a supplemental plaque to indicate that the regulation is in effect or that the condition is present only at certain times. Section 2A.12 prohibits the use flashing light-emitting diode (LED) units within the legend or border of the sign in conjunction with the phrase WHEN FLASHING in its legend or on a supplemental plaque.

title: Section 4S.03 Standard 2 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Standard 2 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

A Warning Beacon shall consist of one or more signal sections of a standard traffic signal face with a flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indication in each signal section.

title: Section 4S.03 Standard 3 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Standard 3 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

A Warning Beacon shall be used only to supplement an appropriate warning or regulatory sign or marker.

title: Section 4S.03 Standard 4 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Standard 4 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

Warning Beacons, if used at intersections, shall not face conflicting vehicular approaches.

title: Section 4S.03 Guidance 5 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Guidance 5 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

The condition or regulation justifying Warning Beacons should largely govern their location with respect to the roadway.

title: Section 4S.03 Guidance 6 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Guidance 6 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

If an obstruction is in or adjacent to the roadway, illumination of the lower portion or the beginning of the obstruction or illumination of the sign on or in front of the obstruction, in addition to the beacon, should be considered.

title: Section 4S.03 Guidance 7 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Guidance 7 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

Warning Beacons should be operated only during those periods or times when the condition or regulation exists.

title: Section 4S.03 Option 8 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Option 8 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

If Warning Beacons have more than one signal section, they may be flashed either alternately or simultaneously.

title: Section 4S.03 Option 9 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Option 9 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

A Warning Beacon interconnected with a traffic signal controller assembly may be used with a BE PREPARED TO STOP (W3-4) sign and a WHEN FLASHING (W16-13P) plaque (see Section 2C.35).

title: Section 4S.03 Option 10 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Option 10 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

Warning Beacons that are actuated by pedestrians, bicyclists, or other road users may be used as appropriate to provide additional warning to vehicles approaching a crossing or other location.

title: Section 4S.03 Guidance 11 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Guidance 11 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

An audible information device should be used with pedestrian-actuated Warning Beacons to assist pedestrians with vision disabilities.

title: Section 4S.03 Standard 12 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Standard 12 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

If an audible information device is used in conjunction with a pedestrian-actuated Warning Beacon at a pedestrian crossing, the audible information device shall not use vibrotactile indications or percussive indications.

title: Section 4S.03 Guidance 13 - Warning Beacon
text:
Section 4S.03 Guidance 13 - Warning Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 752

If an audible information device is used in conjunction with a pedestrian-actuated Warning Beacon at a pedestrian crossing, the audible message should be a speech message that says, “Warning lights are flashing.” The audible message should be spoken twice.

title: Section 4S.04 Standard 1 - Speed Limit Sign Beacon
text:
Section 4S.04 Standard 1 - Speed Limit Sign Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 753

A Speed Limit Sign Beacon shall be used only to supplement a Speed Limit sign.

title: Section 4S.04 Standard 2 - Speed Limit Sign Beacon
text:
Section 4S.04 Standard 2 - Speed Limit Sign Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 753

A Speed Limit Sign Beacon shall consist of one or more signal sections of a standard traffic control signal face, with a flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indication in each signal section. If two or more signal indications are used, they shall be alternately flashed.

title: Section 4S.04 Option 3 - Speed Limit Sign Beacon
text:
Section 4S.04 Option 3 - Speed Limit Sign Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 753

A Speed Limit Sign Beacon may be used with a fixed or variable Speed Limit sign. If applicable, a flashing Speed Limit Sign Beacon (with an appropriate accompanying sign) may be used to indicate that the displayed speed limit is in effect.

title: Section 4S.05 Standard 1 - Stop Beacon
text:
Section 4S.05 Standard 1 - Stop Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 753

A Stop Beacon shall be used only to supplement a STOP sign, a DO NOT ENTER sign, or a WRONG WAY sign.

title: Section 4S.05 Standard 2 - Stop Beacon
text:
Section 4S.05 Standard 2 - Stop Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 753

A Stop Beacon shall consist of one or more signal sections of a standard traffic signal face with a flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indication in each signal section. If two horizontally-aligned signal indications are used for a Stop Beacon, they shall be flashed simultaneously to avoid being confused with grade crossing flashing-light signals. If two vertically-aligned signal indications are used for a Stop Beacon, they shall be flashed alternately.

title: Section 4S.05 Guidance 3 - Stop Beacon
text:
Section 4S.05 Guidance 3 - Stop Beacon
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4S. Flashing Beacons
Page: 754

The edge of the signal housing of a Stop Beacon should be not less than 12 inches or more than 24 inches from the nearest edge of the STOP sign, DO NOT ENTER sign, or WRONG WAY sign that it supplements.

title: Section 4T.01 Support 1 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.01 Support 1 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 754

Lane-use control signals are special overhead signals that permit or prohibit the use of specific lanes of a street or highway or that indicate the impending prohibition of their use. Lane-use control signals are distinguished by placement of special signal faces over a certain lane or lanes of the roadway, over a shoulder where driving is permitted at certain times, and by their distinctive shapes and symbols. Supplementary signs are sometimes used to explain their meaning and intent.

title: Section 4T.01 Support 2 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.01 Support 2 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 754

Lane-use control signals are most commonly used for reversible lane control, but are also used in certain non- reversible-lane applications and for toll plaza lanes (see Section 4R.02).

title: Section 4T.01 Guidance 3 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.01 Guidance 3 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 754

An engineering study should be conducted to determine whether a reversible lane operation can be controlled satisfactorily by static signs (see Section 2B.34) or whether lane-use control signals are necessary. Lane-use control signals should be used to control reversible lane operations if any of the following conditions are present: A. More than one lane is reversed in direction; B. Two-way or one-way left turns are allowed during peak-period reversible operations, but those turns are from a different lane than used during off-peak periods; C. Other unusual or complex operations are included in the reversible lane pattern; D. Demonstrated crash experience occurring with reversible lane operation controlled by static signs that can be corrected by using lane-use control signals at the times of transition between peak and off-peak patterns; and/or E. An engineering study indicates that the safety and efficiency of the traffic operations of a reversible lane system would be improved by lane-use control signals.

title: Section 4T.01 Standard 4 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.01 Standard 4 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 754

Pavement markings (see Section 3B.04) shall be used in conjunction with reversible lane control signals.

title: Section 4T.01 Option 5 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.01 Option 5 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 754

Lane-use control signals may also be used if there is no intent or need to reverse lanes, but there is a need to indicate the open or closed status of one or more lanes, such as: A. On a freeway, if it is desired to close certain lanes at certain hours to facilitate the merging of traffic from a ramp or other freeway; B. On a freeway, near its terminus, to indicate a lane that ends; C. On a freeway or long bridge, to indicate that a lane may be temporarily blocked by a crash, breakdown, construction or maintenance activities, or similar temporary conditions; and D. On a conventional road or driveway, at access or egress points to or from a facility, such as a parking garage, where one or more lanes of the access or egress are opened or closed at various times.

title: Section 4T.01 Option 6 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.01 Option 6 - Application of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 754

A USE LANE(S) WITH GREEN ARROW (R10-8) sign (see Section 2B.59) may be used in conjunction with lane-use control signals.

title: Section 4T.02 Standard 1 - Meaning of Lane-Use Control Signal Indications
text:
Section 4T.02 Standard 1 - Meaning of Lane-Use Control Signal Indications
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

The meanings of lane-use control signal indications (see Figure 4T-1) shall be as follows: A. A steady DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW signal indication shall mean that the lane which the arrow signal indication is located over is open to vehicle travel in that direction. B. A steady YELLOW X signal indication shall mean that the lane which the Yellow X signal indication is located over is about to be closed to vehicle traffic in that direction and shall be followed by a steady RED X signal indication (either within the same signal face or in a downstream signal face). C. A steady RED X signal indication shall mean that the lane which the Red X signal indication is located over is closed to vehicle traffic in the direction viewed by the road user. D. A steady WHITE TWO-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW signal indication shall mean that the lane which the turning arrows indication is located over is open to traffic making a left turn from either direction of travel, but not for through travel. E. A steady WHITE ONE-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW signal indication shall mean that the lane which the turning arrow indication is located over is open to traffic making a left turn in that direction (without opposing turns in the same lane), but not for through travel. Figure 4T-1. Lane-Use Control Signal Indications

metadata.section_title: Meaning of Lane-Use Control Signal Indications

title: Section 4T.03 Standard 1 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Standard 1 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

All lane-use control signal indications shall be in units with rectangular signal faces and shall have opaque backgrounds. Except as provided in Paragraph 13 of this Section, the nominal minimum height and width of each DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW, YELLOW X, and RED X signal face shall be 18 inches for typical applications. Except as provided in Paragraph 13 of this Section, the WHITE TWO-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW and WHITE ONE-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW signal faces shall have a nominal minimum height and width of 30 inches.

title: Section 4T.03 Standard 2 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Standard 2 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

Each lane to be reversed or closed shall have signal faces with at least a DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW and a RED X symbol.

title: Section 4T.03 Standard 3 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Standard 3 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

Each reversible-lane that also operates as a two-way or one-way left-turn lane during certain periods shall have signal faces that also include the applicable WHITE TWO-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW or WHITE ONE-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW symbol.

title: Section 4T.03 Standard 4 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Standard 4 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

Each non-reversible-lane immediately adjacent to a reversible-lane shall have signal indications that display a DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW to traffic traveling in the permitted direction and a RED X to traffic traveling in the opposite direction.

title: Section 4T.03 Standard 5 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Standard 5 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

If in separate signal sections, the relative positions, from left to right, of the signal indications shall be RED X, YELLOW X, DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW, WHITE TWO-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW, WHITE ONE-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW.

title: Section 4T.03 Guidance 6 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Guidance 6 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

The color of lane-use control signal indications should be clearly visible for at least 2,300 feet at all times under normal atmospheric conditions, unless otherwise physically obstructed.

title: Section 4T.03 Guidance 7 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Guidance 7 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

Lane-use control signal faces should be located approximately over the center of the controlled lane.

title: Section 4T.03 Guidance 8 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Guidance 8 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

If the area to be controlled is more than 2,300 feet in length, or if the vertical or horizontal alignment is curved, intermediate lane-use control signal faces should be located over each controlled lane at frequent intervals. This location should be such that road users will at all times be able to see at least one signal indication and preferably two along the roadway, and will have a definite indication of the lanes specifically reserved for their use.

title: Section 4T.03 Guidance 9 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Guidance 9 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

All lane-use control signal faces should be located in a straight line across the roadway approximately at right angles to the roadway alignment.

title: Section 4T.03 Guidance 10 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Guidance 10 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

On roadways having intersections controlled by traffic control signals, the lane-use control signal face should be located sufficiently far in advance of or beyond such traffic control signals to prevent them from being misconstrued as traffic control signals.

title: Section 4T.03 Standard 11 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Standard 11 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

Except as provided in Paragraph 12 of this Section, the bottom of the signal housing of any lane-use control signal face shall be a minimum of 15 feet and a maximum of 19 feet above the pavement grade.

title: Section 4T.03 Option 12 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Option 12 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 755

The bottom of a lane-use control signal housing may be lower than 15 feet above the pavement if it is mounted on a canopy or other structure over the pavement, but not lower than the vertical clearance of the structure.

title: Section 4T.03 Option 13 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Option 13 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 756

Except for lane-use control signals at toll plazas (see Section 4R.02), lane-use control signal faces with nominal height and width of 12 inches for the DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW, YELLOW X, and RED X signal faces, and lane-use control signal faces with nominal height and width of 18 inches for the WHITE TWO-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW and WHITE ONE-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW signal faces may be used in areas with minimal visual clutter and with speeds of less than 40 mph.

title: Section 4T.03 Option 14 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Option 14 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 756

Other sizes of lane-use control signal faces larger than 18 inches with proportional dimensions and with message recognition distances appropriate to signal spacing may be used for the DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW, YELLOW X, and RED X signal faces.

title: Section 4T.03 Option 15 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Option 15 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 756

Non-reversible lanes not immediately adjacent to a reversible-lane on any street so controlled may also be provided with signal indications that display a DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW to traffic traveling in the permitted direction and a RED X to traffic traveling in the opposite direction.

title: Section 4T.03 Option 16 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.03 Option 16 - Design of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 756

The signal indications provided for each lane may be in separate signal sections or may be superimposed in the same signal section.

title: Section 4T.04 Standard 1 - Operation of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.04 Standard 1 - Operation of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 756

All lane-use control signals shall be coordinated so that all the signal indications along the controlled section of roadway are operated uniformly and consistently. The lane-use control signal system shall be designed to reliably guard against showing any prohibited combination of signal indications to any traffic at any point in the controlled lanes.

title: Section 4T.04 Standard 2 - Operation of Lane-Use Control Signals
text:
Section 4T.04 Standard 2 - Operation of Lane-Use Control Signals
Part: Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals
Chapter: Chapter 4T. Lane-Use Control Signals
Page: 756

For reversible lane control signals, the following combination of signal indications shall not be simultaneously displayed over the same lane to both directions of travel: A. DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW in both directions, B. YELLOW X in both directions, C. WHITE ONE-WAY LEFT-TURN ARROW in both directions, D. DOWNWARD GREEN ARROW in one direction and YELLOW X in the other direction, E.
