Equally as important as the safety of road users traveling through the TTC zone is the safety of workers. TTC zones present temporary and constantly changing conditions that are unexpected by road users. This creates an even higher degree of vulnerability for workers on or near the roadway.

title: Section 6C.04 Support 2 - Worker Safety Considerations
text:
Section 6C.04 Support 2 - Worker Safety Considerations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 781

Maintaining TTC zones with road user flow inhibited as little as possible, and using TTC devices that get the road users’ attention and provide positive direction are of particular importance. Likewise, equipment and vehicles moving within the activity area create a risk to workers on foot. When possible, the separation of moving equipment and construction vehicles from workers on foot provides the operators of these vehicles with a greater separation clearance and improved sight lines to minimize exposure to the hazards of moving vehicles and equipment.

title: Section 6C.04 Guidance 3 - Worker Safety Considerations
text:
Section 6C.04 Guidance 3 - Worker Safety Considerations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 781

The following are the key elements of worker safety and TTC management that should be considered to improve worker safety: A. Training-all workers should be trained on how to work next to motor vehicle traffic in ways that minimize their vulnerability. Workers having specific TTC responsibilities should be trained in TTC techniques, device usage, and placement. B. Temporary Traffic Barriers-temporary traffic barriers should be placed along the work space depending on factors such as lateral clearance of workers from adjacent traffic, speed of traffic, duration and type of operations, time of day, and volume of traffic. C. Speed Management-reducing the speed of vehicular traffic, mainly through regulatory speed zoning, funneling, lane reduction, and/or the use of speed safety cameras, uniformed law enforcement officers, or flaggers should be considered. D. Activity Area-operations entering and departing the work space, and within the work space, should be planned to minimize backing maneuvers by construction vehicles and equipment to minimize the risk of run-over and back-over crashes. E. Worker Safety Planning-a trained person designated by the employer should conduct a basic hazard assessment for the worksite and job classifications required in the activity area. This safety professional should determine whether engineering, administrative, or personal protection measures should be implemented. This plan should be in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, as amended, “General Duty Clause” Section 5(a)(1) - Public Law 91-596, 84 Stat. 1590, December 29, 1970, as amended, and with the requirement to assess worker risk exposures for each job site and job classification, as per 29 CFR 1926.20 (b)(2) of “Occupational Safety and Health Administration Regulations, General Safety and Health Provisions.”

title: Section 6C.04 Option 4 - Worker Safety Considerations
text:
Section 6C.04 Option 4 - Worker Safety Considerations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

The following are additional elements of TTC management that may be considered to improve worker safety: A. Shadow Vehicle-in the case of mobile and constantly moving operations, such as pothole patching and striping operations, a shadow vehicle, equipped with appropriate lights and warning signs, may be used to protect the workers from impacts by errant vehicles. The shadow vehicle may be equipped with a rear- mounted impact attenuator. B. Road Closure-if alternate routes are available to handle road users, the road may be closed temporarily to facilitate project completion and thus further reduce worker vulnerability. C. Law Enforcement Use-in highly vulnerable work situations, particularly those of relatively short- duration, law enforcement units may be stationed to heighten the awareness of passing vehicular traffic and to improve safety through the TTC zone. D. Lighting-for nighttime work, the TTC zone and approaches may be lighted. E. Special Devices-these include rumble strips, changeable message signs, hazard identification beacons, flags, and warning lights. Intrusion warning devices may be used to alert workers to the approach of errant vehicles.

title: Section 6C.04 Support 5 - Worker Safety Considerations
text:
Section 6C.04 Support 5 - Worker Safety Considerations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

Judicious use of the special devices described in Item E in Paragraph 4 of this Section might be helpful for certain difficult TTC situations, but misuse or overuse of special devices or techniques might lessen their effectiveness.

title: Section 6C.05 Standard 1 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
text:
Section 6C.05 Standard 1 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

For daytime and nighttime activity, all workers, including emergency responders, within the right- of-way who are within the TTC zone shall wear high-visibility safety apparel that meets the Performance Class 2 or 3 requirements of the ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 publication entitled “American National Standard for High-Visibility Safety Apparel and Headwear,” or equivalent revisions, except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section. A person designated by the employer to be responsible for worker safety shall make the selection of the appropriate class of garment.

title: Section 6C.05 Standard 2 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
text:
Section 6C.05 Standard 2 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

The apparel background (outer) material color shall be fluorescent orange-red, fluorescent yellow-green, or a combination of the two as defined in the ANSI standard. The retroreflective material shall be orange, yellow, white, silver, yellow-green, or a fluorescent version of these colors.

title: Section 6C.05 Standard 3 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
text:
Section 6C.05 Standard 3 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

When uniformed law enforcement personnel are used to direct traffic, to investigate crashes, or to handle lane closures, obstructed roadways, and disasters, high-visibility safety apparel as described in this Section shall be worn by the law enforcement personnel.

title: Section 6C.05 Option 4 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
text:
Section 6C.05 Option 4 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

Emergency and incident responders and law enforcement personnel within the TTC zone may wear high- visibility safety apparel that meets the performance requirements of the ANSI/ISEA 207-2006 publication entitled “American National Standard for High-Visibility Public Safety Vests,” or equivalent revisions, and labeled as ANSI 207-2006, in lieu of ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 apparel.

title: Section 6C.05 Standard 5 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
text:
Section 6C.05 Standard 5 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

Except as provided in Paragraph 6 of this Section, firefighters or other emergency responders working within the right-of-way shall wear high-visibility safety apparel as described in this Section.

title: Section 6C.05 Option 6 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
text:
Section 6C.05 Option 6 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 782

Firefighters or other emergency responders working within the right-of-way and engaged in emergency operations that directly expose them to flame, fire, heat, and/or hazardous materials may wear retroreflective turn- out gear that is specified and regulated by other organizations, such as the National Fire Protection Association.

title: Section 6C.05 Guidance 7 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
text:
Section 6C.05 Guidance 7 - High-Visibility Safety Apparel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6C. Pedestrian And Worker Safety
Page: 783

For flagger wear during nighttime activity, high-visibility safety apparel that meets the Performance Class 3 requirements of the ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 publication entitled “American National Standard for High- Visibility Apparel and Headwear,” or equivalent revision, and labeled as meeting the ANSI 107-2015 standard performance for Class 3 risk exposure should be worn.

title: Section 6D.01 Guidance 1 - Qualifications for Flaggers
text:
Section 6D.01 Guidance 1 - Qualifications for Flaggers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

Because flaggers are responsible for public safety and make the greatest number of contacts with the public of all highway workers, they should be trained in proper traffic control practices and public contact techniques. Flaggers should be able to satisfactorily demonstrate the following abilities: A. Ability to receive and communicate specific instructions clearly, firmly, and courteously; B. Ability to move and maneuver quickly in order to avoid danger from errant vehicles; C. Ability to control signaling devices (such as paddles and flags) in order to provide clear and positive guidance to drivers approaching a TTC zone in frequently changing situations; D. Ability to understand and apply proper traffic control practices, sometimes in stressful or emergency situations; and E. Ability to recognize dangerous traffic situations and warn workers in sufficient time to avoid injury.

title: Section 6D.02 Guidance 1 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Guidance 1 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

The STOP/SLOW paddle (see Figure 6D-1 and Table 6G-1) should be the primary and preferred hand- signaling device because the STOP/SLOW paddle gives road users more positive guidance than red flags.

title: Section 6D.02 Standard 2 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Standard 2 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

The STOP/SLOW paddle (R1-1 and W20-8) shall have an octagonal shape on a rigid handle. When used at night, the STOP/SLOW paddle shall be retroreflectorized. Option

title: Section 6D.02 Standard 3 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Standard 3 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

A STOP/STOP or a SLOW/SLOW paddle may be used in certain situations (see Section 6D.05), provided the device meets the size and shape requirements for the STOP/SLOW paddle.

title: Section 6D.02 Guidance 4 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Guidance 4 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

The STOP/SLOW paddle should be fabricated from light semi-rigid material.

title: Section 6D.02 Support 5 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Support 5 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

The optimum method of displaying a STOP or SLOW message is to place the STOP/SLOW paddle on a rigid staff that is tall enough that when the end of the staff is resting on the ground, the message is high enough to be seen by approaching or stopped traffic.

title: Section 6D.02 Option 6 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Option 6 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

The STOP/SLOW paddle may be modified to improve conspicuity by incorporating either white or red flashing lights on the STOP face, and either white or yellow flashing lights on the SLOW face. The flashing lights may be arranged in any of the following patterns: A. Two white or red lights, one centered vertically above and one centered vertically below the STOP legend; and/or two white or yellow lights, one centered vertically above and one centered vertically below the SLOW legend; B. Two white or red lights, one centered horizontally on each side of the STOP legend; and/or two white or yellow lights, one centered horizontally on each side of the SLOW legend; C. One white or red light centered below the STOP legend; and/or one white or yellow light centered below the SLOW legend; D. A series of eight or more small white or red lights no larger than ¼ inch in diameter along the outer edge of the paddle, arranged in an octagonal pattern at the eight corners of the border of the STOP face; and/ or a series of eight or more small white or yellow lights no larger than ¼ inch in diameter along the outer edge of the paddle, arranged in a diamond pattern along the border of the SLOW face; or E. A series of white lights forming the shapes of the letters in the legend.

title: Section 6D.02 Standard 7 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Standard 7 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

If flashing lights are used on the STOP face of the paddle, their colors shall be all white or all red. If flashing lights are used on the SLOW face of the paddle, their colors shall be all white or all yellow.

title: Section 6D.02 Standard 8 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Standard 8 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 783

If more than eight flashing lights are used, the lights shall be arranged such that they clearly convey the octagonal shape of the STOP face of the paddle and/or the diamond shape of the SLOW face of the paddle.

title: Section 6D.02 Standard 9 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.02 Standard 9 - STOP/SLOW Paddle for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

If flashing lights are used on the STOP/SLOW paddle, the flash rate shall be at least 50, but not more than 60, flashes per minute. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 6D-1. Use of Hand-Signaling Devices by Flaggers PREFERRED METHOD EMERGENCY SITUATIONS ONLY Rev. 1 STOP/SLOW Paddle Flag December 2025

title: Section 6D.03 Guidance 1 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.03 Guidance 1 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

Use of flags should be limited to emergency situations.

title: Section 6D.03 Standard 2 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.03 Standard 2 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

Flags, when used, shall be red or fluorescent orange-red in color, shall be a minimum of 24 inches square, and shall be securely fastened to a staff that is approximately 36 inches in length.

title: Section 6D.03 Guidance 3 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.03 Guidance 3 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

The free edge of a flag should be weighted so the flag will hang vertically, even in heavy winds.

title: Section 6D.03 Standard 4 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.03 Standard 4 - Flag for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

When used at nighttime, flags shall be retroreflectorized.

title: Section 6D.04 Option 1 - Flashlight for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.04 Option 1 - Flashlight for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

When flagging in an emergency situation at night in a non-illuminated flagger station, a flagger may use a flashlight with a red glow cone to supplement the STOP/SLOW paddle or flag.

title: Section 6D.04 Standard 2 - Flashlight for Hand-Signaling
text:
Section 6D.04 Standard 2 - Flashlight for Hand-Signaling
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

When a flashlight is used for flagging in an emergency situation at night in a non-illuminated flagger station, the flagger shall hold the flashlight in the left hand, shall hold the paddle or flag in the right hand as shown in Figure 6D-1, and shall use the flashlight in the following manner to control approaching road users: A. To inform road users to stop, the flagger shall hold the flashlight with the left arm extended and pointed down toward the ground, and then shall slowly wave the flashlight in front of the body in a slow arc from left to right such that the arc reaches no farther than 45 degrees from vertical. B. To inform road users to proceed, the flagger shall point the flashlight at the vehicle’s bumper, slowly aim the flashlight toward the open lane, then hold the flashlight in that position. The flagger shall not wave the flashlight. C. To alert or slow traffic, the flagger shall point the flashlight toward oncoming traffic and quickly wave the flashlight in a Figure eight motion.

title: Section 6D.05 Support 1 - Flagger Procedures
text:
Section 6D.05 Support 1 - Flagger Procedures
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

The use of paddles and flags by flaggers is illustrated in Figure 6D-1.

title: Section 6D.05 Standard 2 - Flagger Procedures
text:
Section 6D.05 Standard 2 - Flagger Procedures
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

Flaggers shall use a STOP/SLOW paddle, a flag, or an Automated Flagger Assistance Device (AFAD) (see Sections 6L.02 through 6L.04) to control road users approaching a TTC zone. The use of hand movements alone without a paddle, flag, or AFAD to control road users shall be prohibited when controlling traffic in a one-lane two-way operation except when the control is provided by emergency responders at incident scenes as described in Section 6O.01 or provided by uniformed law enforcement officers.

title: Section 6D.05 Standard 3 - Flagger Procedures
text:
Section 6D.05 Standard 3 - Flagger Procedures
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

The following methods of signaling with a paddle shall be used: A. To stop road users, the flagger shall face road users and aim the STOP paddle face toward road users in a stationary position with the arm extended horizontally away from the body. The free arm shall be held with the palm of the hand above shoulder level toward approaching traffic. B. To direct stopped road users to proceed, the flagger shall face road users with the SLOW paddle face aimed toward road users in a stationary position with the arm extended horizontally away from the body. The flagger shall motion with the free hand for road users to proceed. C. To alert or slow traffic, the flagger shall face road users with the SLOW paddle face aimed toward road users in a stationary position with the arm extended horizontally away from the body.

title: Section 6D.05 Option 4 - Flagger Procedures
text:
Section 6D.05 Option 4 - Flagger Procedures
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 785

To further alert or slow traffic, the flagger holding the SLOW paddle face toward road users may motion up and down with the free hand, palm down.

title: Section 6D.05 Standard 5 - Flagger Procedures
text:
Section 6D.05 Standard 5 - Flagger Procedures
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 786

The following methods of signaling with a flag shall be used: A. To stop road users, the flagger shall face road users and extend the flag staff horizontally across the road users’ lane in a stationary position so that the full area of the flag is visibly hanging below the staff. The free arm shall be held with the palm of the hand above shoulder level toward approaching traffic. B. To direct stopped road users to proceed, the flagger shall face road users with the flag and arm lowered from the view of the road users, and shall motion with the free hand for road users to proceed. Flags shall not be used to signal road users to proceed. C. To alert or slow traffic, the flagger shall face road users and slowly wave the flag in a sweeping motion of the extended arm from shoulder level to straight down without raising the arm above a horizontal position. The flagger shall keep the free hand down.

title: Section 6D.05 Guidance 6 - Flagger Procedures
text:
Section 6D.05 Guidance 6 - Flagger Procedures
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 786

The flagger should stand either on the shoulder adjacent to the road user being controlled or in the closed lane prior to stopping road users. A flagger should only stand in the lane being used by moving road users after road users have stopped. The flagger should be clearly visible to the first approaching road user at all times. The flagger also should be visible to other road users. The flagger should be stationed sufficiently in advance of the workers to warn them (for example, with audible warning devices such as horns or whistles) of approaching danger by out-of-control vehicles. The flagger should stand alone, away from other workers, work vehicles, or equipment.

title: Section 6D.05 Option 7 - Flagger Procedures
text:
Section 6D.05 Option 7 - Flagger Procedures
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 786

In certain conditions, it may be more appropriate for a flagger to use a STOP/STOP or a SLOW/SLOW paddle to convey the appropriate message to approaching road users and avoid confusing those that are approaching the operation from the opposing direction.

title: Section 6D.06 Standard 1 - Flagger Stations
text:
Section 6D.06 Standard 1 - Flagger Stations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 786

Except as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section, flagger stations shall be located such that approaching road users will have sufficient distance to stop at an intended stopping point.

title: Section 6D.06 Option 2 - Flagger Stations
text:
Section 6D.06 Option 2 - Flagger Stations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 786

If sufficient stopping sight distance is not achievable, the location of the flagger station may be modified based on engineering judgment.

title: Section 6D.06 Option 3 - Flagger Stations
text:
Section 6D.06 Option 3 - Flagger Stations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 786

The distances shown in Table 6B-2, which provides information regarding the stopping sight distance as a function of speed, may be used for the location of a flagger station. These distances may be increased for downgrades and other conditions that affect stopping distance.

title: Section 6D.06 Guidance 4 - Flagger Stations
text:
Section 6D.06 Guidance 4 - Flagger Stations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 786

Flagger stations should be located such that an errant vehicle has additional space to stop without entering the work space. The flagger should identify an escape route that can be used to avoid being struck by an errant vehicle.

title: Section 6D.06 Standard 5 - Flagger Stations
text:
Section 6D.06 Standard 5 - Flagger Stations
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6D. Flagger Control
Page: 787

Except in emergency situations, flagger stations shall be preceded by an advance warning sign or signs. Except in emergency situations, flagger stations shall be illuminated when flagging is used at night.

title: Section 6E.01 Standard 1 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
text:
Section 6E.01 Standard 1 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, when traffic in both directions must use a single lane for a limited distance, movements from each end shall be coordinated.

title: Section 6E.01 Guidance 2 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
text:
Section 6E.01 Guidance 2 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

Provisions should be made for alternate one-way movement through the constricted section via methods such as flagger control, a flag transfer, a pilot car, traffic control signals, or stop or yield control.

title: Section 6E.01 Guidance 3 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
text:
Section 6E.01 Guidance 3 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

Control points at each end should be chosen to permit easy passing of opposing lanes of vehicles.

title: Section 6E.01 Option 4 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
text:
Section 6E.01 Option 4 - One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

If the work space on a low-volume street or road is short and road users from both directions are able to see the traffic approaching from the opposite direction through and beyond the worksite, the movement of traffic through a one-lane, two-way constriction may be self-regulating.

title: Section 6E.02 Guidance 1 - Flagger Method
text:
Section 6E.02 Guidance 1 - Flagger Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

Except as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section, traffic should be controlled by a flagger at each end of a constricted section of roadway. One of the flaggers should be designated as the coordinator. To provide coordination of the control of the traffic, the flaggers should be able to communicate with each other orally, electronically, or with manual signals. These manual signals should not be mistaken for flagging signals.

title: Section 6E.02 Option 2 - Flagger Method
text:
Section 6E.02 Option 2 - Flagger Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

When a one-lane, two-way TTC zone is short enough to allow a flagger to see from one end of the zone to the other, traffic may be controlled by either a single flagger or by a flagger at each end of the section.

title: Section 6E.02 Guidance 3 - Flagger Method
text:
Section 6E.02 Guidance 3 - Flagger Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

When a single flagger is used, the flagger should be stationed on the shoulder opposite the constriction or work space, or in a position where good visibility and traffic control can be maintained at all times. When good visibility and traffic control cannot be maintained by one flagger station, traffic should be controlled by a flagger at each end of the section.

title: Section 6E.03 Support 1 - Flag Transfer Method
text:
Section 6E.03 Support 1 - Flag Transfer Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

The driver of the last vehicle proceeding into the one-lane section is given a red flag (or other token) and instructed to deliver it to the flagger at the other end. The opposite flagger, upon receipt of the flag, then knows that traffic can be permitted to move in the other direction. A variation of this method is to replace the use of a flag with an official pilot car that follows the last road user vehicle proceeding through the section.

title: Section 6E.03 Guidance 2 - Flag Transfer Method
text:
Section 6E.03 Guidance 2 - Flag Transfer Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

The flag transfer method should be employed only where the one-way traffic is confined to a relatively short length of a road, usually no more than 1 mile in length.

title: Section 6E.04 Option 1 - Pilot Car Method
text:
Section 6E.04 Option 1 - Pilot Car Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

A pilot car may be used to guide a queue of vehicles through the TTC zone or detour.

title: Section 6E.04 Guidance 2 - Pilot Car Method
text:
Section 6E.04 Guidance 2 - Pilot Car Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

The pilot car should have the name of the contractor or contracting authority prominently displayed.

title: Section 6E.04 Standard 3 - Pilot Car Method
text:
Section 6E.04 Standard 3 - Pilot Car Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

The PILOT CAR FOLLOW ME (G20-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall be mounted on the top or on the rear of the pilot vehicle (see Section 6H.37).

title: Section 6E.04 Standard 4 - Pilot Car Method
text:
Section 6E.04 Standard 4 - Pilot Car Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 787

The pilot car operation shall be coordinated with flagging operations or other methods of control at each end of the one lane section of the work zone.

title: Section 6E.04 Standard 5 - Pilot Car Method
text:
Section 6E.04 Standard 5 - Pilot Car Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 788

If an Automated Flagger Assistance Device (AFAD) (see Section 6L.02) is used in pilot car operations, the AFAD shall be operated by a flagger positioned near and within the line of sight of the AFAD. The AFAD shall not be left unattended at any time that the AFAD is being used.

title: Section 6E.04 Guidance 6 - Pilot Car Method
text:
Section 6E.04 Guidance 6 - Pilot Car Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 788

If temporary traffic control signals are used in pilot car operations and long wait times will be encountered by road users, consideration should be given to using signs to notify drivers of the wait time and/or pilot car operation, based on engineering judgment.

title: Section 6E.05 Option 1 - Temporary Traffic Control Signal Method
text:
Section 6E.05 Option 1 - Temporary Traffic Control Signal Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 788

Traffic control signals may be used to control vehicular traffic movements in one-lane, two-way TTC zones (see Figure 6P-12 and Chapter 4O).

title: Section 6E.06 Option 1 - Stop or Yield Control Method
text:
Section 6E.06 Option 1 - Stop or Yield Control Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 788

STOP or YIELD signs may be used to control traffic on low-volume roads at a one-lane, two-way TTC zone when drivers are able to see the other end of the one-lane, two-way operation and have sufficient visibility of approaching vehicles.

title: Section 6E.06 Guidance 2 - Stop or Yield Control Method
text:
Section 6E.06 Guidance 2 - Stop or Yield Control Method
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6E. One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control
Page: 789

If the STOP or YIELD sign is installed for only one direction, then the STOP or YIELD sign should face road users who are driving on the side of the roadway that is closed for the work activity area.

title: Section 6F.01 Support 1 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Support 1 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

TTC zone signs convey both general and specific messages by means of words, symbols, and/or arrows and have the same three categories as all road user signs: regulatory, warning, and guide.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Option 2 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Option 2 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

Where the color orange is required, the fluorescent orange color may also be used.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Support 3 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Support 3 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

The fluorescent version of orange provides higher conspicuity than standard orange, especially during twilight.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Option 4 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Option 4 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

Standard orange flags, flashing beacons, and/or flashing warning lights may be used in conjunction with signs.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Standard 5 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Standard 5 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

When standard orange flags, flashing beacons, and/or flashing warning lights are used in conjunction with a sign, they shall not block the sign face.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Standard 6 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Standard 6 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

Except as provided in Section 2A.07, the sizes for TTC signs and plaques shall be as shown in Tables 6G-1, 6H-1, and 6I-1. The sizes in the minimum column shall only be used on low-volume rural roads, local streets, or roadways where the operating speed is 30 mph or less.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Option 7 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Option 7 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

The dimensions of signs and plaques shown in Tables 6G-1, 6H-1, and 6I-1 may be increased wherever necessary for greater legibility or emphasis.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Guidance 8 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Guidance 8 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

Deviations from standard sizes as prescribed in this Manual should be in 6-inch increments.

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.01 Support 9 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
text:
Section 6F.01 Support 9 - General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

Sign design details are contained in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05).

metadata.section_title: General Characteristics of TTC Zone Signs
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Guidance 1 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Guidance 1 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

Signs should be located on the right-hand side of the roadway unless otherwise provided in this Manual.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Option 2 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Option 2 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

Where special emphasis is needed, signs may be placed on both the left-hand and right-hand sides of the roadway. Signs mounted on portable supports may be placed within the roadway itself. Signs may also be mounted on or above barricades.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Support 3 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Support 3 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 789

The provisions of this Section regarding mounting height apply unless otherwise provided for a particular sign elsewhere in this Manual.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Standard 4 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Standard 4 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 790

The minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road in rural areas shall be 5 feet (see Figure 6F-1).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Standard 5 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Standard 5 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 790

The minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the top of the curb, or in the absence of curb, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way, of signs installed at the side of the road in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, shall be 7 feet (see Figure 6F-1).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Standard 6 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Standard 6 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 790

The minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the sidewalk, of signs installed above sidewalks shall be 7 feet.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Standard 7 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Standard 7 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 790

The bottom of a sign mounted on a barricade, or other portable support, shall be at least 1 foot above the traveled way.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Option 8 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Option 8 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 790

The height to the bottom of a secondary sign mounted below another sign may be 1 foot less than the height provided in Paragraphs 4 through 6 of this Section.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Guidance 9 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Guidance 9 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 790

Neither portable nor permanent sign supports should be located on sidewalks, bicycle facilities, or areas designated for pedestrians or bicyclists.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Standard 10 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Standard 10 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 790

Signs shall be mounted and placed in accordance with Section 307 of the U.S. Department of Justice 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, September 15, 2010, 28 CFR 35 and 36, Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Guidance 11 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Guidance 11 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

Except as provided in Paragraph 12 of this Section, signs mounted on portable sign supports that do not meet the minimum mounting heights provided in Part 2 should not be used for a duration of more than 3 days. Figure 6F-1. Height and Lateral Location of Signs-Typical Installations B - Rural area with advisory speed plaque A - Rural area C - Business, commercial, D - Business, commercial, or residential or residential area area (without curb)

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Option 12 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Option 12 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

The R9-8 through R9-11a series, R11 series, W1-6 through W1-8 series, M4-10, E5-1, or other similar type signs (see Figures 6G-1, 6H-1, and 6I-1) may be used on portable sign supports that do not meet the minimum mounting heights provided in Part 2 for longer than 3 days.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Support 13 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Support 13 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

Methods of mounting signs other than on posts are illustrated in Figure 6F-2.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Guidance 14 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Guidance 14 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

Signs mounted on Type 3 Barricades should not cover more than 50 percent of the top two rails or 33 percent of the total area of the three rails.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Standard 15 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Standard 15 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

Signs and sign supports used together shall be crashworthy (see Section 6A.04). Where large signs having an area exceeding 50 square feet are installed on multiple breakaway posts, the clearance from the ground to the bottom of the sign shall be at least 7 feet.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.02 Option 16 - Sign Placement
text:
Section 6F.02 Option 16 - Sign Placement
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

For mobile operations, a sign may be mounted on a work vehicle, a shadow vehicle, or a trailer stationed in advance of the TTC zone or moving along with it.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.03 Guidance 1 - Sign Maintenance
text:
Section 6F.03 Guidance 1 - Sign Maintenance
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

Signs should be properly maintained for cleanliness, visibility, retroreflectivity, and correct positioning.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6F.03 Guidance 2 - Sign Maintenance
text:
Section 6F.03 Guidance 2 - Sign Maintenance
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General
Page: 791

Signs that have lost significant legibility should be promptly replaced.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6F. Temporary Traffic Control Zone Signs – General

title: Section 6G.01 Support 1 - Regulatory Sign Authority
text:
Section 6G.01 Support 1 - Regulatory Sign Authority
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

Regulatory signs such as those shown in Figure 6G-1 inform road users of traffic laws or regulations and indicate the applicability of legal requirements that would not otherwise be apparent.

title: Section 6G.01 Standard 2 - Regulatory Sign Authority
text:
Section 6G.01 Standard 2 - Regulatory Sign Authority
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

Regulatory signs shall be authorized by the public agency or official having jurisdiction and shall conform with Chapter 2B.

title: Section 6G.02 Standard 1 - Regulatory Sign Design and Size
text:
Section 6G.02 Standard 1 - Regulatory Sign Design and Size
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

TTC regulatory signs shall comply with the Standards for regulatory signs presented in Part 2 and in the FHWA’s “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05).

title: Section 6G.02 Standard 2 - Regulatory Sign Design and Size
text:
Section 6G.02 Standard 2 - Regulatory Sign Design and Size
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

The sizes for TTC regulatory signs shall be as shown in Table 6G-1.

title: Section 6G.03 Standard 1 - Regulatory Sign Applications
text:
Section 6G.03 Standard 1 - Regulatory Sign Applications
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

If a TTC zone requires regulatory measures different from those existing, the existing permanent regulatory devices shall be removed or covered and superseded by the appropriate temporary regulatory signs. This change shall be made in compliance with applicable ordinances or statutes of the jurisdiction.

title: Section 6G.04 Guidance 1 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
text:
Section 6G.04 Guidance 1 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

The ROAD CLOSED (R11-2) sign (see Figure 6G-1) should be used when the roadway is closed to all road users except contractors’ equipment or officially authorized vehicles. The R11-2 sign should be accompanied by appropriate warning and detour signing.

title: Section 6G.04 Option 2 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
text:
Section 6G.04 Option 2 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

STREET CLOSED (R11-2a), BRIDGE OUT (R11-2b), or PATH CLOSED (R11-2c) signs may be substituted for Road Closed signs where applicable.

title: Section 6G.04 Guidance 3 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
text:
Section 6G.04 Guidance 3 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

Road Closed signs should be installed at or near the center of the roadway on or above a Type 3 Barricade that closes the roadway (see Section 6K.07).

title: Section 6G.04 Standard 4 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
text:
Section 6G.04 Standard 4 - Road Closed Signs (R11-2 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

Road Closed signs shall not be used where road user flow is maintained through the TTC zone with a reduced number of lanes on the existing roadway or where the actual closure is some distance beyond the sign.

title: Section 6G.05 Guidance 1 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
text:
Section 6G.05 Guidance 1 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

The Local Traffic Only signs (see Figure 6G-1) should be used where road users follow detours to avoid a closure some distance beyond the sign, but where local road users can use the roadway to the point of closure. These signs should be accompanied by appropriate warning and detour signing. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)

title: Section 6G.05 Guidance 2 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
text:
Section 6G.05 Guidance 2 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

In rural applications, the Local Traffic Only sign should have the legend ROAD CLOSED XX MILES AHEAD, LOCAL TRAFFIC ONLY (R11-3).

metadata.section_title: Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)

title: Section 6G.05 Option 3 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
text:
Section 6G.05 Option 3 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

In urban areas, a ROAD (STREET) CLOSED TO THRU TRAFFIC (R11-4) sign or the legend ROAD CLOSED, LOCAL TRAFFIC ONLY may be used.

metadata.section_title: Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)

title: Section 6G.05 Option 4 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
text:
Section 6G.05 Option 4 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

In urban areas, a word message that includes the name of an intersecting street name or well-known destination may be substituted for the words XX MILES AHEAD on the R11-3 sign where applicable.

metadata.section_title: Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)

title: Section 6G.05 Option 5 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
text:
Section 6G.05 Option 5 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 793

A STREET CLOSED (R11-3a) or BRIDGE OUT (R11-3b) sign may be substituted for an R11-3 sign, where applicable.

metadata.section_title: Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)

title: Section 6G.05 Option 6 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
text:
Section 6G.05 Option 6 - Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 795

The words BRIDGE OUT, BRIDGE CLOSED, or STREET CLOSED may be substituted for the words ROAD CLOSED on the R11-4 sign where applicable. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 6G-1. Regulatory Signs and Plaques in Temporary Traffic Control Zones (Sheet 1 of 2) Rev. 1 Rev. 1 Note: See Chapter 2B for information on the application of these signs. December 2025 Figure 6G-1. Regulatory Signs and Plaques in Temporary Traffic Control Zones (Sheet 2 of 2) Note: See Chapter 2B for information on the application of these signs.

metadata.section_title: Local Traffic Only Signs (R11-3 Series and R11-4)

title: Section 6G.06 Standard 1 - Weight Limit Signs (R12-1, R12-2, and R12-5)
text:
Section 6G.06 Standard 1 - Weight Limit Signs (R12-1, R12-2, and R12-5)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 795

A Weight Limit sign (see Figure 6G-1), which shows the gross weight or axle weight that is permitted on the roadway or bridge, shall be consistent with State or local regulations and shall not be installed without the approval of the authority having jurisdiction over the highway.

metadata.section_title: Weight Limit Signs (R12-1, R12-2, and R12-5)

title: Section 6G.06 Standard 2 - Weight Limit Signs (R12-1, R12-2, and R12-5)
text:
Section 6G.06 Standard 2 - Weight Limit Signs (R12-1, R12-2, and R12-5)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 795

When weight restrictions are imposed because of the activity in a TTC zone, a marked detour shall be provided for vehicles weighing more than the posted limit.

metadata.section_title: Weight Limit Signs (R12-1, R12-2, and R12-5)

title: Section 6G.07 Option 1 - STAY IN LANE Signs (R4-9 and R4-9a)
text:
Section 6G.07 Option 1 - STAY IN LANE Signs (R4-9 and R4-9a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 795

A STAY IN LANE (R4-9) sign (see Figure 6G-1) may be used where a multi-lane shift has been incorporated as part of the TTC on a highway to direct road users around road work that occupies part of the roadway on a multi-lane highway.

metadata.section_title: STAY IN LANE Signs (R4-9 and R4-9a)

title: Section 6G.07 Guidance 2 - STAY IN LANE Signs (R4-9 and R4-9a)
text:
Section 6G.07 Guidance 2 - STAY IN LANE Signs (R4-9 and R4-9a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 795

A STAY IN LANE TO MERGE POINT (R4-9a) sign (see Figure 6G-1) should be used during late merge operations (see Section 6N.19) to direct traffic to use all available lanes until the merge point is reached.

metadata.section_title: STAY IN LANE Signs (R4-9 and R4-9a)

title: Section 6G.08 Option 1 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
text:
Section 6G.08 Option 1 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 795

A WORK ZONE (G20-5aP) plaque (see Figure 6G-1) may be mounted above a Speed Limit sign to emphasize that a reduced speed limit is in effect within a TTC zone. An END WORK ZONE SPEED LIMIT (R2-12) sign (see Figure 6G-1) may be installed at the downstream end of the reduced speed limit zone.

metadata.section_title: Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques

text:

Page: 797

title: Section 6G.08 Option 3 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
text:
Section 6G.08 Option 3 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

Alternate legends such as BEGIN (or END) DOUBLE FINES ZONE may also be used for the R2-10 and R2-11 signs.

metadata.section_title: Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques

title: Section 6G.08 Option 4 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
text:
Section 6G.08 Option 4 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

A FINES HIGHER, FINES DOUBLE, or $XX FINE plaque (see Section 2B.25 and Figure 6G-1) may be mounted below the Speed Limit sign if increased fines are imposed for traffic violations within the TTC zone.

metadata.section_title: Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques

title: Section 6G.08 Option 5 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
text:
Section 6G.08 Option 5 - Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

Individual signs and plaques for work zone speed limits and higher fines may be combined into a single sign or may be displayed as an assembly of signs and plaques.

metadata.section_title: Work Zone and Higher Fines Signs and Plaques

title: Section 6G.09 Option 1 - PEDESTRIAN CROSSWALK Sign (R9-8)
text:
Section 6G.09 Option 1 - PEDESTRIAN CROSSWALK Sign (R9-8)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

The PEDESTRIAN CROSSWALK (R9-8) sign (see Figure 6G-1) may be used to indicate where a temporary crosswalk has been established.

title: Section 6G.09 Standard 2 - PEDESTRIAN CROSSWALK Sign (R9-8)
text:
Section 6G.09 Standard 2 - PEDESTRIAN CROSSWALK Sign (R9-8)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

If a temporary crosswalk is established, it shall be accessible to pedestrians with disabilities in accordance with Section 6C.03.

title: Section 6G.10 Guidance 1 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
text:
Section 6G.10 Guidance 1 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

SIDEWALK CLOSED signs (see Figure 6G-1) should be used where pedestrian flow is restricted. Bicyclist/ Pedestrian Detour (M4-9a) signs or Pedestrian Detour (M4-9b) signs should be used where pedestrian flow is rerouted (see Section 6I.02).

metadata.section_title: SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)

title: Section 6G.10 Guidance 2 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
text:
Section 6G.10 Guidance 2 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

The SIDEWALK CLOSED (R9-9) sign should be installed at the beginning of the closed sidewalk, at the intersections preceding the closed sidewalk, and elsewhere along the closed sidewalk as needed.

metadata.section_title: SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)

title: Section 6G.10 Guidance 3 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
text:
Section 6G.10 Guidance 3 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

The SIDEWALK CLOSED, (ARROW) USE OTHER SIDE (R9-10) sign should be installed at the beginning of the restricted sidewalk when a parallel sidewalk exists on the other side of the roadway.

metadata.section_title: SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)

title: Section 6G.10 Guidance 4 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
text:
Section 6G.10 Guidance 4 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

The SIDEWALK CLOSED AHEAD, (ARROW) CROSS HERE (R9-11) sign should be used to indicate to pedestrians that sidewalks beyond the sign are closed and to direct them to open crosswalks, sidewalks, or other travel paths.

metadata.section_title: SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)

title: Section 6G.10 Guidance 5 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
text:
Section 6G.10 Guidance 5 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

The SIDEWALK CLOSED, (ARROW) CROSS HERE (R9-11a) sign should be installed just beyond the point to which pedestrians are being redirected.

metadata.section_title: SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)

title: Section 6G.10 Support 6 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
text:
Section 6G.10 Support 6 - SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

These signs are typically mounted on a detectable barricade to encourage compliance and to communicate with pedestrians that the sidewalk is closed. Printed signs are not useful to many pedestrians with vision disabilities. A barrier or barricade detectable by a person with a vision disability is sufficient to indicate that a sidewalk is closed. If the barrier is continuous with detectable channelizing devices for an alternate route, accessible signing might not be necessary.

metadata.section_title: SIDEWALK CLOSED Signs (R9-9, R9-10, R9-11, and R9-11a)

title: Section 6G.11 Standard 1 - TURN OFF 2-WAY RADIO AND CELL PHONE Sign (R22-2)
text:
Section 6G.11 Standard 1 - TURN OFF 2-WAY RADIO AND CELL PHONE Sign (R22-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

The TURN OFF 2-WAY RADIO AND CELL PHONE (R22-2) sign (see Figure 6G-1) shall be used to require road users to turn off mobile radio transmitters and cellular telephones where blasting operations occur.

metadata.section_title: TURN OFF 2-WAY RADIO AND CELL PHONE Sign (R22-2)

title: Section 6G.12 Option 1 - Other Regulatory Signs
text:
Section 6G.12 Option 1 - Other Regulatory Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 797

Regulatory word message signs other than those classified and specified in this Manual and the “Standard Highways Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05) may be developed and used based on engineering judgment to aid the enforcement of other laws or regulations in TTC zones.

title: Section 6G.12 Guidance 2 - Other Regulatory Signs
text:
Section 6G.12 Guidance 2 - Other Regulatory Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6G. Ttc Zone Regulatory Signs
Page: 798

Special regulatory signs should comply with the general requirements of color, shape, and alphabet size and series. The sign message should be brief, legible, and clear. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 6H.01 Support 1 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Support 1 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

TTC zone warning signs (see Figure 6H-1) notify road users of specific situations or conditions on or adjacent to a roadway that might not otherwise be apparent.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Standard 2 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Standard 2 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

TTC warning signs shall comply with the Standards for warning signs presented in Part 2 and in the FHWA’s “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05).

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Standard 3 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Standard 3 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

The sizes for TTC warning signs shall be as shown in Table 6H-1.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Standard 4 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Standard 4 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Except as provided in Paragraphs 5-9 of this Section, TTC warning signs shall be diamond-shaped with a black legend and border on an orange background, except for the Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1) sign, which shall have a black legend and border on a yellow background.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Option 5 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Option 5 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Warning signs that are required or recommended in Parts 2 or 7 to have a fluorescent yellow-green background may have that color background in TTC zones.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Option 6 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Option 6 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Existing warning signs with a yellow background that are still applicable may remain in place.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Option 7 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Option 7 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Warning signs used for TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Option 8 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Option 8 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Mounting or space considerations may justify a change from the standard diamond shape to a rectangular shape.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Option 9 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Option 9 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

In emergencies, available warning signs having yellow backgrounds may be used if signs with orange or fluorescent pink backgrounds are not at hand.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Guidance 10 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Guidance 10 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Where roadway or road user conditions require greater emphasis, larger than standard size warning signs should be used, with the symbol or legend enlarged approximately in proportion to the outside dimensions.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Guidance 11 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Guidance 11 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Where any part of the roadway is obstructed or closed by work activities or incidents, advance warning signs should be installed to alert road users well in advance of these obstructions or restrictions.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Guidance 12 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Guidance 12 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Where road users include pedestrians, the provision of supplemental audible information or detectable barriers or barricades should be provided for people with vision disabilities.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Support 13 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Support 13 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Detectable barriers or barricades communicate very clearly to pedestrians who have vision disabilities that they can no longer proceed in the direction that they are traveling.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Option 14 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Option 14 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Advance warning signs may be used singly or in combination.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.01 Option 15 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
text:
Section 6H.01 Option 15 - Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Where distances are not displayed on warning signs as part of the message, a supplemental plaque with the distance legend may be mounted immediately below the sign on the same support.

metadata.section_title: Warning Sign Function, Design, and Application

title: Section 6H.02 Guidance 1 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.02 Guidance 1 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Where highway conditions permit, warning signs should be placed in advance of the transition and activity areas at varying distances depending on roadway type, condition, and posted speed. Table 6B-1 contains information regarding the spacing of advance warning signs. Where a series of two or more advance warning signs is used, the closest sign to the transition and activity areas should be placed approximately 100 feet for low-speed urban streets to 1,000 feet or more for freeways and expressways.

title: Section 6H.02 Guidance 2 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.02 Guidance 2 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Where multiple advance warning signs are needed on the approach to a transition and activity area, the ROAD WORK AHEAD (W20-1) sign should be the first advance warning sign encountered by road users.

title: Section 6H.02 Support 3 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.02 Support 3 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 798

Various conditions, such as limited sight distance or obstructions that might require a driver to reduce speed or stop, might require additional advance warning signs.

title: Section 6H.02 Option 4 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.02 Option 4 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

As an alternative to a specific distance on advance warning signs, the word AHEAD may be used. December 2025 Figure 6H-1. Figure 6H-1. Warning Signs and Plaques in Temporary Traffic Control Zones (Sheet 4 of 4) Note: See Chapter 2C for information on the application of these signs.

title: Section 6H.02 Support 5 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.02 Support 5 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

At TTC zones on lightly-traveled roads, all of the advance warning signs prescribed for major construction might not be needed.

title: Section 6H.02 Option 6 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.02 Option 6 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

Utility work, maintenance, or minor construction can occur within the TTC zone limits of a major construction project, and additional warning signs may be needed.

title: Section 6H.02 Guidance 7 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.02 Guidance 7 - Position of Advance Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

Utility, maintenance, and minor construction signing and TTC should be coordinated with appropriate authorities so that road users are not confused or misled by the additional TTC devices.

title: Section 6H.03 Guidance 1 - ROAD (STREET) WORK Sign (W20-1)
text:
Section 6H.03 Guidance 1 - ROAD (STREET) WORK Sign (W20-1)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

The ROAD (STREET) WORK (W20-1) sign (see Figure 6H-1), which serves as a general warning of obstructions or restrictions, should be located in advance of the work space or any detour, on the road where the work is taking place.

title: Section 6H.03 Guidance 2 - ROAD (STREET) WORK Sign (W20-1)
text:
Section 6H.03 Guidance 2 - ROAD (STREET) WORK Sign (W20-1)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

Where traffic can enter a TTC zone from a crossroad or a major (high-volume) driveway, an advance warning sign should be used on the crossroad or major driveway.

title: Section 6H.03 Option 3 - ROAD (STREET) WORK Sign (W20-1)
text:
Section 6H.03 Option 3 - ROAD (STREET) WORK Sign (W20-1)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

The legend STREET may be substituted for ROAD and the distance legend may be either XX FEET, XX MILES, or AHEAD.

title: Section 6H.04 Guidance 1 - DETOUR Sign (W20-2)
text:
Section 6H.04 Guidance 1 - DETOUR Sign (W20-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 802

The DETOUR (W20-2) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used in advance of a road user detour over a different roadway or route.

title: Section 6H.04 Option 2 - DETOUR Sign (W20-2)
text:
Section 6H.04 Option 2 - DETOUR Sign (W20-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805
