title: Section 6H.05 Guidance 1 - ROAD (STREET) CLOSED Sign (W20-3)
text:
Section 6H.05 Guidance 1 - ROAD (STREET) CLOSED Sign (W20-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The ROAD (STREET) CLOSED (W20-3) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used in advance of the point where a highway is closed to all road users, or to all but local road users.

title: Section 6H.05 Option 2 - ROAD (STREET) CLOSED Sign (W20-3)
text:
Section 6H.05 Option 2 - ROAD (STREET) CLOSED Sign (W20-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The legend STREET may be substituted for ROAD and the distance legend may be either XX FEET, XX MILES, or AHEAD.

title: Section 6H.06 Standard 1 - ONE LANE ROAD Sign (W20-4)
text:
Section 6H.06 Standard 1 - ONE LANE ROAD Sign (W20-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The ONE LANE ROAD (W20-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall be used only in advance of that point where motor vehicle traffic in both directions must use a common single lane (see Section 6E.01).

title: Section 6H.06 Option 2 - ONE LANE ROAD Sign (W20-4)
text:
Section 6H.06 Option 2 - ONE LANE ROAD Sign (W20-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The distance legend may be either XX FEET, XX MILES, or AHEAD.

title: Section 6H.07 Standard 1 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
text:
Section 6H.07 Standard 1 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The Lane(s) Closed sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall be used in advance of that point where one or more through lanes of a multi-lane roadway are closed.

metadata.section_title: Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)

title: Section 6H.07 Standard 2 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
text:
Section 6H.07 Standard 2 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

For a single lane closure, the Lane Closed (W20-5) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall use the legend RIGHT (LEFT) LANE CLOSED. Where two or more adjacent lanes are closed, the W20-5a sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall use the legend XX RIGHT (LEFT) LANES CLOSED.

metadata.section_title: Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)

title: Section 6H.07 Option 3 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
text:
Section 6H.07 Option 3 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The distance legend may be either XX FEET, XX MILES, or AHEAD.

metadata.section_title: Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)

title: Section 6H.07 Guidance 4 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
text:
Section 6H.07 Guidance 4 - Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The Interior Lane Shift (W9-3) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used in advance of that point where work occupies an interior lane(s) and approaching motor vehicle traffic is directed to the right or left of the work zone in the lane(s) by using a shifting taper to route traffic around the closed interior lane(s).

metadata.section_title: Lane(s) Closed Signs (W20-5, W20-5a, and W9-3)

title: Section 6H.08 Option 1 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-2a)
text:
Section 6H.08 Option 1 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-2a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The Lane Ends (W4-2) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used to warn drivers of the reduction in the number of lanes for moving motor vehicle traffic in the direction of travel on a multi-lane roadway.

title: Section 6H.08 Guidance 2 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-2a)
text:
Section 6H.08 Guidance 2 - Lane Ends Signs (W4-2 and W9-2a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The MERGE HERE TAKE TURNS (W9-2a) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used to identify the merge point at which vehicles from alternate lanes take turns merging during Late Merge applications (see Section 6N.19).

title: Section 6H.09 Guidance 1 - ON RAMP Plaque (W13-4P)
text:
Section 6H.09 Guidance 1 - ON RAMP Plaque (W13-4P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

When work is being done on a ramp, but the ramp remains open, the ON RAMP (W13-4P) plaque (see Figure 6H-1) should be used to supplement the advance ROAD WORK sign.

title: Section 6H.10 Guidance 1 - RAMP NARROWS Sign (W5-4)
text:
Section 6H.10 Guidance 1 - RAMP NARROWS Sign (W5-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 805

The RAMP NARROWS (W5-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used in advance of the point where work on a ramp reduces the normal width of the ramp along a part or all of the ramp.

title: Section 6H.11 Option 1 - SLOW TRAFFIC AHEAD Sign (W23-1)
text:
Section 6H.11 Option 1 - SLOW TRAFFIC AHEAD Sign (W23-1)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

The SLOW TRAFFIC AHEAD (W23-1) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used on a shadow vehicle, usually mounted on the rear of the most upstream shadow vehicle, along with other appropriate signs for mobile operations to warn of slow moving work vehicles. A ROAD WORK (W20-1) sign may also be used with the SLOW TRAFFIC AHEAD sign. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 6H.12 Option 1 - EXIT OPEN and EXIT CLOSED Signs (E5-2 and E5-2a)
text:
Section 6H.12 Option 1 - EXIT OPEN and EXIT CLOSED Signs (E5-2 and E5-2a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

An EXIT OPEN (E5-2) or EXIT CLOSED (E5-2a) sign (see Figure 6I-1) may be used to supplement other warning signs where work is being conducted in the vicinity of an exit ramp and where the exit maneuver for vehicular traffic using the ramp is different from the normal condition. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: EXIT OPEN and EXIT CLOSED Signs (E5-2 and E5-2a)

title: Section 6H.13 Option 1 - EXIT ONLY Sign (E5-3)
text:
Section 6H.13 Option 1 - EXIT ONLY Sign (E5-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

An EXIT ONLY (E5-3) sign (see Figure 6I-1) may be used to supplement other warning signs where work is being conducted in the vicinity of an exit ramp and where the exit maneuver for vehicular traffic using the ramp is different from the normal condition. Rev. 1

title: Section 6H.14 Option 1 - NEW TRAFFIC PATTERN AHEAD Sign (W23-2)
text:
Section 6H.14 Option 1 - NEW TRAFFIC PATTERN AHEAD Sign (W23-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

A NEW TRAFFIC PATTERN AHEAD (W23-2) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used on the approach to an intersection or along a section of roadway to provide advance warning of a change in traffic patterns, such as revised lane usage, roadway geometry, or signal phasing.

title: Section 6H.14 Guidance 2 - NEW TRAFFIC PATTERN AHEAD Sign (W23-2)
text:
Section 6H.14 Guidance 2 - NEW TRAFFIC PATTERN AHEAD Sign (W23-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

To retain its effectiveness, the W23-2 sign should be displayed for up to 2 weeks, and then it should be covered or removed until it is needed again.

title: Section 6H.15 Guidance 1 - Flagger Signs (W20-7 and W20-7a)
text:
Section 6H.15 Guidance 1 - Flagger Signs (W20-7 and W20-7a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

The Flagger (W20-7) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used in advance of any point where a flagger is stationed to control road users.

title: Section 6H.15 Option 2 - Flagger Signs (W20-7 and W20-7a)
text:
Section 6H.15 Option 2 - Flagger Signs (W20-7 and W20-7a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

A distance legend may be displayed on a supplemental plaque below the Flagger sign. The sign may be used with appropriate legends or in conjunction with other warning signs, such as the BE PREPARED TO STOP (W3-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1).

title: Section 6H.15 Option 3 - Flagger Signs (W20-7 and W20-7a)
text:
Section 6H.15 Option 3 - Flagger Signs (W20-7 and W20-7a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

The FLAGGER (W20-7a) word message sign with a distance legend may be substituted for the Flagger (W20-7) sign.

title: Section 6H.16 Guidance 1 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
text:
Section 6H.16 Guidance 1 - Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

When one roadway of a normally-divided highway is closed, with two-way vehicular traffic maintained on the other roadway, the Two-Way Traffic (W6-3) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used at the beginning of the two- way vehicular traffic section and at intervals to remind road users of opposing vehicular traffic.

title: Section 6H.17 Standard 1 - Narrow Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-4)
text:
Section 6H.17 Standard 1 - Narrow Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

The Narrow Two-Way Traffic (W6-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall be an upright, retroreflective orange- colored sign placed on a flexible support and sized at least 12 inches wide by 18 inches high.

title: Section 6H.17 Support 2 - Narrow Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-4)
text:
Section 6H.17 Support 2 - Narrow Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

The Narrow Two-Way Traffic (W6-4) sign is intended for mounting only on a flexible support in a series along the center line to separate opposing vehicular traffic on a two-lane, two-way operation.

title: Section 6H.17 Standard 3 - Narrow Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-4)
text:
Section 6H.17 Standard 3 - Narrow Two-Way Traffic Sign (W6-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

Narrow Two-Way Traffic signs shall not be placed within pedestrian crossings.

title: Section 6H.18 Option 1 - Workers Signs (W21-1 and W21-1a)
text:
Section 6H.18 Option 1 - Workers Signs (W21-1 and W21-1a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 806

A Workers (W21-1) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used to alert road users of workers in or near the roadway.

title: Section 6H.18 Guidance 2 - Workers Signs (W21-1 and W21-1a)
text:
Section 6H.18 Guidance 2 - Workers Signs (W21-1 and W21-1a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

In the absence of other warning devices, a Workers sign should be used when workers are in the roadway. December 2025

title: Section 6H.18 Option 3 - Workers Signs (W21-1 and W21-1a)
text:
Section 6H.18 Option 3 - Workers Signs (W21-1 and W21-1a)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

The WORKERS (W21-1a) word message sign may be used as an alternate to the Workers (W21-1) symbol sign.

title: Section 6H.19 Guidance 1 - FRESH OIL (TAR) Sign (W21-2)
text:
Section 6H.19 Guidance 1 - FRESH OIL (TAR) Sign (W21-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

The FRESH OIL (TAR) (W21-2) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used to warn road users of the surface treatment.

title: Section 6H.20 Option 1 - ROAD MACHINERY AHEAD Sign (W21-3)
text:
Section 6H.20 Option 1 - ROAD MACHINERY AHEAD Sign (W21-3)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

The ROAD MACHINERY AHEAD (W21-3) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used to warn of machinery operating in or adjacent to the roadway.

title: Section 6H.21 Option 1 - Motorized Traffic Signs (W8-6 and W11-10)
text:
Section 6H.21 Option 1 - Motorized Traffic Signs (W8-6 and W11-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

Motorized Traffic (W8-6 and W11-10) signs may be used to alert road users to locations where unexpected travel on the roadway or entries into or departures from the roadway by construction vehicles might occur. The TRUCK CROSSING (W8-6) word message sign may be used as an alternate to the Truck (W11-10) symbol sign (see Figure 6H-1) where there is an established construction vehicle crossing of the roadway.

title: Section 6H.21 Support 2 - Motorized Traffic Signs (W8-6 and W11-10)
text:
Section 6H.21 Support 2 - Motorized Traffic Signs (W8-6 and W11-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

These locations might be relatively confined or might occur randomly over a segment of roadway.

title: Section 6H.22 Support 1 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
text:
Section 6H.22 Support 1 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

Shoulder Work signs (see Figure 6H-1) warn of maintenance, reconstruction, or utility operations on the highway shoulder where the roadway is unobstructed.

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)

title: Section 6H.22 Standard 2 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
text:
Section 6H.22 Standard 2 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

The Shoulder Work sign shall have the legend SHOULDER WORK (W21-5), RIGHT (LEFT) SHOULDER CLOSED (W21-5a), or RIGHT (LEFT) SHOULDER CLOSED XX FT or AHEAD (W21-5b).

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)

title: Section 6H.22 Option 3 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
text:
Section 6H.22 Option 3 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

The Shoulder Work sign may be used in advance of the point on a non-limited access highway where there is shoulder work. It may be used singly or in combination with a ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES or ROAD WORK AHEAD sign.

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)

title: Section 6H.22 Guidance 4 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
text:
Section 6H.22 Guidance 4 - Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

On freeways and expressways, the RIGHT (LEFT) SHOULDER CLOSED XX FT or AHEAD (W21-5b) sign followed by RIGHT (LEFT) SHOULDER CLOSED (W21-5a) sign should be used in advance of the point where the shoulder work occurs and should be preceded by a ROAD WORK AHEAD sign.

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Work Signs (W21-5, W21-5a, and W21-5b)

title: Section 6H.23 Guidance 1 - SURVEY CREW Sign (W21-6)
text:
Section 6H.23 Guidance 1 - SURVEY CREW Sign (W21-6)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

The SURVEY CREW (W21-6) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used to warn of surveying crews working in or adjacent to the roadway.

title: Section 6H.24 Option 1 - UTILITY WORK Sign (W21-7)
text:
Section 6H.24 Option 1 - UTILITY WORK Sign (W21-7)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

The UTILITY WORK (W21-7) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used as an alternate to the ROAD (STREET) WORK (W20-1) sign for utility operations on or adjacent to a highway.

title: Section 6H.24 Support 2 - UTILITY WORK Sign (W21-7)
text:
Section 6H.24 Support 2 - UTILITY WORK Sign (W21-7)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 807

Typical examples of where the UTILITY WORK sign is used appear in Figures 6P-4, 6P-6, 6P-10, 6P-15, 6P-18, 6P-21, 6P-22, 6P-26, and 6P-33.

title: Section 6H.24 Option 3 - UTILITY WORK Sign (W21-7)
text:
Section 6H.24 Option 3 - UTILITY WORK Sign (W21-7)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The distance legend may be either XX FEET, XX MILES, or AHEAD. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 6H.25 Support 1 - Signs for Blasting Areas
text:
Section 6H.25 Support 1 - Signs for Blasting Areas
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

Radio-Frequency (RF) energy can cause the premature firing of electric detonators (blasting caps) used in TTC zones.

title: Section 6H.25 Standard 2 - Signs for Blasting Areas
text:
Section 6H.25 Standard 2 - Signs for Blasting Areas
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

Road users shall be warned where blasting operations occur. A sequence of signs shall be prominently displayed to warn all road users of blasting operations and to direct operators of mobile radio equipment, including cellular telephones, to turn off transmitters in a blasting area. These signs shall be covered or removed when there are no explosives in the area or the area is otherwise secured.

title: Section 6H.25 Standard 3 - Signs for Blasting Areas
text:
Section 6H.25 Standard 3 - Signs for Blasting Areas
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The BLASTING ZONE AHEAD (W22-1) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall be used in advance of any TTC zone where explosives are being used. The TURN OFF 2-WAY RADIO AND CELL PHONE (R22-2) and END BLASTING ZONE (W22-3) signs shall be used in sequence with this sign.

title: Section 6H.25 Standard 4 - Signs for Blasting Areas
text:
Section 6H.25 Standard 4 - Signs for Blasting Areas
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The TURN OFF 2-WAY RADIO AND CELL PHONE (R22-2) sign (see Section 6G.11 and Figure 6G-1) shall follow the BLASTING ZONE AHEAD (W22-1) sign and shall be placed at least 1,000 feet before the beginning of the blasting zone.

title: Section 6H.25 Standard 5 - Signs for Blasting Areas
text:
Section 6H.25 Standard 5 - Signs for Blasting Areas
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The END BLASTING ZONE (W22-3) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall be placed a minimum of 1,000 feet past the blasting zone.

title: Section 6H.25 Option 6 - Signs for Blasting Areas
text:
Section 6H.25 Option 6 - Signs for Blasting Areas
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The END BLASTING ZONE sign may be placed either with or preceding the END ROAD WORK sign.

title: Section 6H.26 Option 1 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
text:
Section 6H.26 Option 1 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The SOFT SHOULDER (W8-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used to warn of a soft shoulder condition.

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)

title: Section 6H.26 Option 2 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
text:
Section 6H.26 Option 2 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The LOW SHOULDER (W8-9) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used to warn of a shoulder condition where there is an elevation difference of 3 inches or less between the shoulder and the travel lane.

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)

title: Section 6H.26 Guidance 3 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
text:
Section 6H.26 Guidance 3 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The Shoulder Drop-Off (W8-17) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used when an unprotected shoulder drop-off, adjacent to the travel lane, exceeds 3 inches in depth for a continuous length along the roadway, based on engineering judgment.

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)

title: Section 6H.26 Option 4 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
text:
Section 6H.26 Option 4 - Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

A SHOULDER DROP-OFF (W8-17P) supplemental plaque (see Figure 6H-1) may be mounted below the W8-17 sign.

metadata.section_title: Shoulder Signs and Plaque (W8-4, W8-9, W8-17, and W8-17P)

title: Section 6H.27 Guidance 1 - UNEVEN LANES Sign (W8-11)
text:
Section 6H.27 Guidance 1 - UNEVEN LANES Sign (W8-11)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The UNEVEN LANES (W8-11) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used during operations that create a difference in elevation between adjacent lanes that are open to travel.

title: Section 6H.28 Option 1 - STEEL PLATE AHEAD Sign (W8-24)
text:
Section 6H.28 Option 1 - STEEL PLATE AHEAD Sign (W8-24)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

A STEEL PLATE AHEAD (W8-24) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used to warn road users that the presence of a temporary steel plate(s) might make the road surface uneven and might create slippery conditions during wet weather.

title: Section 6H.29 Guidance 1 - NO CENTER LINE Sign (W8-12)
text:
Section 6H.29 Guidance 1 - NO CENTER LINE Sign (W8-12)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 808

The NO CENTER LINE (W8-12) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used when the work obliterates the center line pavement markings. This sign should be placed at the beginning of the TTC zone and repeated at 2-mile intervals in long TTC zones.

title: Section 6H.30 Guidance 1 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
text:
Section 6H.30 Guidance 1 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

In order to give road users advance notice of a lane shift, a Reverse Curve (W1-4, W1-4b, or W1-4c) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used when a lane (or lanes) is being shifted to the left or right. If the design speed of the curves is 30 mph or less, a Reverse Turn (W1-3) sign should be used.

title: Section 6H.30 Standard 2 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
text:
Section 6H.30 Standard 2 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

If a Reverse Curve (or Turn) sign is used, the direction of the reverse curve (or turn) shall be appropriately illustrated. Except as provided in Paragraph 3 of this Section, the number of lanes illustrated on the sign shall be the same as the number of through lanes available to road users.

title: Section 6H.30 Option 3 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
text:
Section 6H.30 Option 3 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

Where two or more lanes are being shifted, a W1-4 (or W1-3) sign with an ALL LANES (W24-1cP) plaque (see Figure 6H-1) may be used instead of a sign that illustrates the number of lanes.

title: Section 6H.30 Option 4 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
text:
Section 6H.30 Option 4 - Reverse Curve Signs (W1-4 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

Where more than three lanes are being shifted, the Reverse Curve (or Turn) sign may be rectangular.

title: Section 6H.31 Option 1 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
text:
Section 6H.31 Option 1 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

The Double Reverse Curve (W24-1, W24-1a, or W24-1b) sign (see Figure 6H-1) may be used where the tangent distance between two reverse curves is less than 600 feet, thus making it difficult for a second Reverse Curve (W1-4 series) sign to be placed between the curves. If the design speed of the curves is 30 mph or less, Double Reverse Turn signs may be used.

title: Section 6H.31 Standard 2 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
text:
Section 6H.31 Standard 2 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

If a Double Reverse Curve (or Turn) sign is used, the direction of the double reverse curve (or turn) shall be appropriately illustrated. Except as provided in Paragraph 3 of this Section, the number of lanes illustrated on the sign shall be the same as the number of through lanes available to road users.

title: Section 6H.31 Option 3 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
text:
Section 6H.31 Option 3 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

Where two or more lanes are being shifted, a W24-1 (or Double Reverse Turn sign showing one lane) sign with an ALL LANES (W24-1cP) plaque (see Figure 6H-1) may be used instead of a sign that illustrates the number of lanes.

title: Section 6H.31 Option 4 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
text:
Section 6H.31 Option 4 - Double Reverse Curve Signs (W24-1 Series)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

Where more than three lanes are being shifted, the Double Reverse Curve (or Turn) sign may be rectangular.

title: Section 6H.32 Option 1 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
text:
Section 6H.32 Option 1 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

In combination with a warning sign, an Advisory Speed (W13-1P) plaque (see Figure 6H-1) may be used to indicate a recommended speed through the TTC zone.

title: Section 6H.32 Standard 2 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
text:
Section 6H.32 Standard 2 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

The Advisory Speed plaque shall not be used in conjunction with any sign other than a warning sign, nor shall it be used alone. When used with orange TTC zone signs, this plaque shall have a black legend and border on an orange background. Except in emergencies, an Advisory Speed plaque shall not be mounted until the recommended speed is determined by the highway agency.

title: Section 6H.32 Support 3 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
text:
Section 6H.32 Support 3 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

Warning signs with advisory speed plaques (see Section 2C.59) inform drivers of the recommended operating speed based on temporary conditions within a TTC zone. Examples include narrow lanes, temporary diversion (reverse curves), lane shifts, sight distance restrictions, rough road surface, bumps, low/no shoulder, workers on foot, work vehicles or equipment close to the open travel lane, or other conditions that indicate the need for reduced speed.

title: Section 6H.32 Support 4 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
text:
Section 6H.32 Support 4 - Advisory Speed Plaque (W13-1P)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 809

AASHTO and ITE design documents contain established engineering practices for the determination of the recommended advisory speeds for horizontal curves or locations with limited sight distance.

title: Section 6H.33 Option 1 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
text:
Section 6H.33 Option 1 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

In combination with a warning sign, a Supplementary Distance (W7-3aP) plaque (see Figure 6H-1) with the legend NEXT XX MILES may be used to indicate the length of highway over which a work activity is being conducted, or over which a condition exists in the TTC zone. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 6H.33 Option 2 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
text:
Section 6H.33 Option 2 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

In long TTC zones, Supplementary Distance plaques with the legend NEXT XX MILES may be placed in combination with warning signs at regular intervals within the zone to indicate the remaining length of highway over which the TTC work activity or condition exists.

title: Section 6H.33 Standard 3 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
text:
Section 6H.33 Standard 3 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

The Supplementary Distance plaque with the legend NEXT XX MILES shall not be used in conjunction with any sign other than a warning sign, nor shall it be used alone. When used with orange TTC zone signs, this plaque shall have a black legend and border on an orange background. The plaque shall be at least 30 x 24 inches in size when used with a sign that is 36 x 36 inches or larger.

title: Section 6H.33 Guidance 4 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
text:
Section 6H.33 Guidance 4 - Supplementary Distance Plaque (W7-3aP)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

When used in TTC zones, the Supplementary Distance plaque with the legend NEXT XX MILES should be placed below the initial warning sign designating that, within the approaching zone, a temporary work activity or condition exists.

title: Section 6H.34 Option 1 - Motorcycle Plaque (W8-15aP)
text:
Section 6H.34 Option 1 - Motorcycle Plaque (W8-15aP)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

A Motorcycle (W8-15aP) plaque (see Figure 6H-1) may be mounted below a LOOSE GRAVEL (W8-7) sign, a GROOVED PAVEMENT (W8-15) sign, a METAL BRIDGE DECK (W8-16) sign, or a STEEL PLATE AHEAD (W8-24) sign if the warning is intended to be directed primarily to motorcyclists. Rev. 1

title: Section 6H.35 Guidance 1 - ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)
text:
Section 6H.35 Guidance 1 - ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

The ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES (G20-1) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be installed in advance of TTC zones that are more than 2 miles in length.

metadata.section_title: ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)

title: Section 6H.35 Option 2 - ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)
text:
Section 6H.35 Option 2 - ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

The ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES sign may be mounted on a Type 3 Barricade. The sign may also be used for TTC zones of shorter length.

metadata.section_title: ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)

title: Section 6H.35 Standard 3 - ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)
text:
Section 6H.35 Standard 3 - ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

The distance displayed on the ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES sign shall be stated to the nearest whole mile.

metadata.section_title: ROAD WORK NEXT XX MILES Sign (G20-1)

title: Section 6H.36 Guidance 1 - END ROAD WORK Sign (G20-2)
text:
Section 6H.36 Guidance 1 - END ROAD WORK Sign (G20-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

When used, the END ROAD WORK (G20-2) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be placed near the downstream end of the termination area, as determined by engineering judgment.

title: Section 6H.36 Option 2 - END ROAD WORK Sign (G20-2)
text:
Section 6H.36 Option 2 - END ROAD WORK Sign (G20-2)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

The END ROAD WORK sign may be installed on the back of a warning sign facing the opposite direction of road users or on the back of a Type 3 Barricade.

title: Section 6H.37 Standard 1 - PILOT CAR FOLLOW ME Sign (G20-4)
text:
Section 6H.37 Standard 1 - PILOT CAR FOLLOW ME Sign (G20-4)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

The PILOT CAR FOLLOW ME (G20-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1) shall be mounted in a conspicuous position on the top or on the rear of a vehicle used for guiding one-way vehicular traffic through or around a TTC zone (see Section 6E.04).

title: Section 6H.38 Option 1 - Other Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.38 Option 1 - Other Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

Advance warning signs may be used by themselves or with other advance warning signs.

title: Section 6H.38 Option 2 - Other Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.38 Option 2 - Other Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

Besides the warning signs specifically related to TTC zones, several other warning signs in Part 2 may apply in TTC zones.

title: Section 6H.38 Option 3 - Other Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.38 Option 3 - Other Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

Word message warning signs other than those classified and specified in this Manual and the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05) may be developed and used based on engineering judgment to warn of special conditions in TTC zones.

title: Section 6H.38 Standard 4 - Other Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.38 Standard 4 - Other Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 810

Except as provided in Sections 6F.01 and 6H.01, other warning signs that are used in TTC zones shall have black legends and borders on an orange background.

title: Section 6H.38 Guidance 5 - Other Warning Signs
text:
Section 6H.38 Guidance 5 - Other Warning Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6H. Ttc Zone Warning Signs
Page: 811

Other warning signs should comply with the general requirements of color, shape, and alphabet size and series. The sign message should be brief, legible, and clear. December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 6I.01 Support 1 - Guide Signs – General
text:
Section 6I.01 Support 1 - Guide Signs – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

Guide signs along highways provide road users with information to help them along their way through the TTC zone. The design of guide signs is presented in Part 2.

title: Section 6I.01 Guidance 2 - Guide Signs – General
text:
Section 6I.01 Guidance 2 - Guide Signs – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

The following guide signs should be used in TTC zones as needed: A. Standard route markings where temporary route changes are necessary, B. Directional signs and street name signs, and C. Special guide signs relating to the condition or work being done.

title: Section 6I.01 Standard 3 - Guide Signs – General
text:
Section 6I.01 Standard 3 - Guide Signs – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

If additional temporary guide signs are used in TTC zones, they shall have a black legend and border on an orange background.

title: Section 6I.01 Option 4 - Guide Signs – General
text:
Section 6I.01 Option 4 - Guide Signs – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

Guide signs used in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background.

title: Section 6I.01 Option 5 - Guide Signs – General
text:
Section 6I.01 Option 5 - Guide Signs – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

When temporary directional signs and temporary street name signs are used in conjunction with detour routing, these signs may have a black legend and border on an orange background.

title: Section 6I.01 Option 6 - Guide Signs – General
text:
Section 6I.01 Option 6 - Guide Signs – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

When permanent directional signs or permanent street name signs are used in conjunction with detour signing, they may have a white legend on a green background (see Sections 2D.35 and 2D.45).

title: Section 6I.01 Standard 7 - Guide Signs – General
text:
Section 6I.01 Standard 7 - Guide Signs – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

The sizes for TTC guide signs shall be as shown in Table 6I-1.

title: Section 6I.02 Standard 1 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Standard 1 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

Each detour shall be adequately marked with standard temporary route signs and destination signs.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Option 2 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Option 2 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

Detour signs in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Option 3 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Option 3 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 811

The Detour Arrow (M4-10) sign (see Figure 6I-1) may be used where a detour route has been established.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Option 4 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Option 4 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

The DETOUR (M4-8P) plaque (see Figure 6I-1) may be mounted at the top of a route sign assembly to mark a temporary route that detours from a highway, bypasses a section closed by a TTC zone, and rejoins the highway beyond the TTC zone. metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Guidance 5 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Guidance 5 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

The Detour Arrow (M4-10) sign should normally be mounted just below the ROAD CLOSED (R11-2, R11-3a, or R11-4) sign. The Detour Arrow sign should include a horizontal arrow pointed to the right or left as required.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Guidance 6 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Guidance 6 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

The DETOUR (M4-9) sign (see Figure 6I-1) should be used for unnumbered highways, for emergency situations, for periods of short durations, or where, over relatively short distances, road users are guided along the detour and back to the desired highway without route signs.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Guidance 7 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Guidance 7 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

A Street Name sign should be placed above, or the street name should be incorporated into, a DETOUR (M4-9) sign to indicate the name of the street being detoured.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Option 8 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Option 8 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

The END DETOUR (M4-8a) sign or the END (M4-8bP) plaque (see Figure 6I-1) may be used to indicate that the detour has ended.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Guidance 9 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Guidance 9 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

When the END DETOUR sign is used on a numbered highway, the sign should be mounted above a route sign after the downstream end of the detour.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Guidance 10 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Guidance 10 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

The Pedestrian/Bicyclist Detour (M4-9a) sign (see Figure 6I-1) should be used where a pedestrian/bicyclist detour route has been established because of the closing of a pedestrian/bicycle facility to through traffic.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Standard 11 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Standard 11 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

If used, the Pedestrian/Bicyclist Detour sign shall have an arrow pointing in the appropriate direction.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Option 12 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Option 12 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

The arrow on a Pedestrian/Bicyclist Detour sign may be on the sign face or on a supplemental plaque.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.02 Option 13 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
text:
Section 6I.02 Option 13 - Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 812

The Pedestrian Detour (M4-9b) sign or Bicyclist Detour (M4-9c) sign (see Figure 6I-1) may be used where a pedestrian or a bicyclist detour route (not both) has been established because of the closing of the pedestrian or bicycle facility to through traffic.

metadata.section_title: Detour Signs and Plaques (M4-8P, M4-8a, M4-8bP, M4-9, M4-9a, M4-9b, M4-9c, and M4-10)

title: Section 6I.03 Guidance 1 - EXIT CLOSED Panel
text:
Section 6I.03 Guidance 1 - EXIT CLOSED Panel
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6I. Ttc Zone Guide Signs
Page: 813

When an exit ramp is closed, an EXIT CLOSED sign panel with a black legend and border on an orange background should be placed diagonally across the interchange/intersection guide signs.

title: Section 6J.01 Support 1 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
text:
Section 6J.01 Support 1 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Pavement markings are installed or existing markings are maintained or enhanced in TTC zones to provide road users with a clearly defined path for travel through the TTC zone in day, night, and twilight periods under both wet and dry pavement conditions.

title: Section 6J.01 Guidance 2 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
text:
Section 6J.01 Guidance 2 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

The work should be planned and staged to provide for the placement and removal of the pavement markings in a way that minimizes the disruption to traffic flow approaching and through the TTC zone during the placement and removal process.

title: Section 6J.01 Standard 3 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
text:
Section 6J.01 Standard 3 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Existing pavement markings shall be maintained in all long-term stationary (see Section 6N.01) TTC zones in accordance with Chapters 3A and 3B, except as otherwise provided for temporary pavement markings in Section 6J.02. Pavement markings shall match the alignment of the markings in place at both ends of the TTC zone. Pavement markings shall be placed along the entire length of any paved detour or temporary roadway prior to the detour or roadway being opened to road users.

title: Section 6J.01 Guidance 4 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
text:
Section 6J.01 Guidance 4 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

For long-term stationary operations, pavement markings in the temporary traveled way that are no longer applicable should be removed or obliterated as soon as practical. Pavement marking obliteration should remove the non-applicable pavement marking material, and the obliteration method should minimize pavement scarring.

title: Section 6J.01 Standard 5 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
text:
Section 6J.01 Standard 5 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Painting over existing pavement markings with black paint or spraying with asphalt shall not be accepted as a substitute for removal or obliteration.

title: Section 6J.01 Option 6 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
text:
Section 6J.01 Option 6 - Pavement Markings in TTC Zones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Removable, non-reflective, preformed tape that is approximately the same color as the pavement surface may be used where markings need to be covered temporarily.

title: Section 6J.02 Support 1 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Support 1 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Temporary markings are those pavement markings or devices that are placed within TTC zones to provide road users with a clearly defined path of travel through the TTC zone when the permanent markings are either removed or obliterated during the work activities. Temporary markings are typically needed during the reconstruction of a road while it is open to traffic, such as overlays or surface treatments or where lanes are temporarily shifted on pavement that is to remain in place.

title: Section 6J.02 Guidance 2 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Guidance 2 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Unless justified based on engineering judgment, temporary pavement markings should not remain in place for more than 14 days after the application of the pavement surface treatment or the construction of the final pavement surface on new roadways or over existing pavements.

title: Section 6J.02 Guidance 3 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Guidance 3 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

The temporary use of edge lines, channelizing lines, lane-reduction transitions, gore markings, and other longitudinal markings, and the various non-longitudinal markings (such as stop lines, railroad crossings, crosswalks, words, symbols, or arrows) should be in accordance with the State’s or highway agency’s policy.

title: Section 6J.02 Standard 4 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Standard 4 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Warning signs, channelizing devices, and delineation shall be used to indicate required road user paths in TTC zones where it is not possible to provide a clear path by pavement markings.

title: Section 6J.02 Standard 5 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Standard 5 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 813

Except as otherwise provided in this Section, all temporary pavement markings for no-passing zones shall comply with the requirements of Chapters 3A and 3B. All temporary broken line pavement markings shall use the same cycle length as permanent markings and shall have line segments that are at least 2 feet long.

title: Section 6J.02 Guidance 6 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Guidance 6 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

All pavement markings and devices used to delineate road user paths should be reviewed during daytime and nighttime periods.

title: Section 6J.02 Option 7 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Option 7 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

Half-cycle lengths with a minimum of 2-foot stripes may be used on roadways with severe curvature (see Section 3A.04) for broken line center lines in passing zones and for lane lines.

title: Section 6J.02 Option 8 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Option 8 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

For temporary situations of 14 days or less, for a two- or three-lane road, no-passing zones may be identified by using DO NOT PASS (R4-1), PASS WITH CARE (R4-2), and NO PASSING ZONE (W14-3) signs (see Sections 2B.36, 2B.37, and 2C.53) rather than pavement markings. Also, DO NOT PASS, PASS WITH CARE, and NO PASSING ZONE signs may be used instead of pavement markings on roads with low volumes for longer periods in accordance with the State’s or highway agency’s policy.

title: Section 6J.02 Guidance 9 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Guidance 9 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

If used, the DO NOT PASS, PASS WITH CARE, and NO PASSING ZONE signs should be placed in accordance with Sections 2B.36, 2B.37, and 2C.53.

title: Section 6J.02 Guidance 10 - Temporary Markings
text:
Section 6J.02 Guidance 10 - Temporary Markings
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

If used, the NO CENTER LINE sign should be placed in accordance with Section 6H.29.

title: Section 6J.03 Option 1 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
text:
Section 6J.03 Option 1 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

Retroreflective or internally illuminated raised pavement markers, or non-retroreflective raised pavement markers supplemented by retroreflective or internally illuminated markers, may be substituted for markings of other types in TTC zones.

title: Section 6J.03 Standard 2 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
text:
Section 6J.03 Standard 2 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

If used, the color and pattern of the raised pavement markers shall simulate the color and pattern of the markings for which they substitute.

title: Section 6J.03 Standard 3 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
text:
Section 6J.03 Standard 3 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

If temporary raised pavement markers are used to substitute for broken line segments, a group of at least three retroreflective markers equally spaced at no greater than 5 feet shall be installed every 40 feet.

title: Section 6J.03 Standard 4 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
text:
Section 6J.03 Standard 4 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

If temporary raised pavement markers are used to substitute for solid lines, the markers shall be equally spaced at no greater than 10 feet, with retroreflective or internally illuminated units at a spacing no greater than 20 feet.

title: Section 6J.03 Option 5 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
text:
Section 6J.03 Option 5 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

Temporary raised pavement markers may be used to substitute for broken line segments by using at least two retroreflective markers placed at each end of a segment of 2 to 5 feet in length, using the same cycle length as permanent markings.

title: Section 6J.03 Guidance 6 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
text:
Section 6J.03 Guidance 6 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

Raised pavement markers should be considered for use along surfaced detours or temporary roadways, and other changed or new travel-lane alignments.

title: Section 6J.03 Option 7 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
text:
Section 6J.03 Option 7 - Temporary Raised Pavement Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

Retroreflective or internally illuminated raised pavement markers, or non-retroreflective raised pavement markers supplemented by retroreflective or internally illuminated markers, may also be used in TTC zones to supplement markings as prescribed in Chapters 3A and 3B.

title: Section 6J.04 Option 1 - Delineators
text:
Section 6J.04 Option 1 - Delineators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

Delineators may be used in TTC zones to indicate the alignment of the roadway and to outline the required vehicle path through the TTC zone.

title: Section 6J.04 Standard 2 - Delineators
text:
Section 6J.04 Standard 2 - Delineators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 814

When used, delineators shall combine with or supplement other TTC devices. They shall be mounted on crashworthy supports and shall be in accordance with Chapter 3G.

title: Section 6J.04 Guidance 3 - Delineators
text:
Section 6J.04 Guidance 3 - Delineators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6J. Ttc Zone Pavement Markings
Page: 815

Spacing along roadway curves should be as set forth in Section 3G.04 and should be such that several delineators are visible to an approaching driver.

title: Section 6K.01 Standard 1 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Standard 1 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

Designs of various channelizing devices shall be as shown in Figure 6K-1. All channelizing devices shall be crashworthy (see definition in Section 1C.02).

title: Section 6K.01 Support 2 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Support 2 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

The function of channelizing devices is to warn road users of conditions created by work activities in or near the roadway and to guide road users. Channelizing devices include cones, tubular markers, vertical panels, drums, barricades, and longitudinal channelizing devices.

title: Section 6K.01 Support 3 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Support 3 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

Channelizing devices provide for smooth and gradual vehicular traffic flow from one lane to another, onto a bypass or detour, or into a narrower traveled way. They are also used to channelize traffic away from the work space, pavement drop-offs, pedestrian or shared-use paths, bicycle facilities, or opposing directions of vehicular traffic.

title: Section 6K.01 Guidance 4 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Guidance 4 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

The spacing between cones, tubular markers, vertical panels, drums, and barricades should not exceed a distance in feet equal to 1 times the speed limit in mph when used for taper channelization, and should not exceed a distance in feet equal to 2 times the speed limit in mph when used for tangent channelization.

title: Section 6K.01 Guidance 5 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Guidance 5 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

When channelizing devices have the potential of leading vehicular traffic out of the intended vehicular traffic space as shown in Figure 6P-39, the channelizing devices should be extended a distance in feet of 2 times the speed limit in mph beyond the downstream end of the transition area.

title: Section 6K.01 Option 6 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Option 6 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

A gap not exceeding 2 inches between the bottom rail and the ground surface may be used to facilitate drainage.

title: Section 6K.01 Option 7 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Option 7 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

Warning lights (see Section 6L.07) may be added to channelizing devices in areas with frequent fog, snow, or severe roadway curvature, or where visual distractions are present.

title: Section 6K.01 Option 8 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Option 8 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

A series of sequential flashing warning lights may be placed on channelizing devices that form a merging taper in order to increase driver detection and recognition of the merging taper.

title: Section 6K.01 Support 9 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Support 9 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

The flashing rates and patterns for warning lights used on channelizing devices are specified in Section 6L.07.

title: Section 6K.01 Standard 10 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Standard 10 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

The retroreflective material used on channelizing devices shall display a similar color day or night.

title: Section 6K.01 Standard 11 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Standard 11 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

Except as provided in Paragraph 12 of this Section, information identifying the owner or manufacturer of the channelizing device shall not be displayed on any portion of the device that can be seen by road users approaching the device.

title: Section 6K.01 Option 12 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Option 12 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

The name and telephone number of the highway agency, contractor, or supplier may be displayed on the non- retroreflective surface of all types of channelizing devices.

title: Section 6K.01 Standard 13 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Standard 13 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

The area containing the name and telephone number shall be non-retroreflective and not over 2 inches in height.

title: Section 6K.01 Guidance 14 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Guidance 14 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

Particular attention should be given to maintaining the channelizing devices to keep them clean, visible, and properly positioned at all times.

title: Section 6K.01 Standard 15 - Channelizing Devices – General
text:
Section 6K.01 Standard 15 - Channelizing Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 815

Channelizing devices that are no longer serviceable (see definition in Section 1C.02) shall be replaced.

title: Section 6K.02 Support 1 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Support 1 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 817

Pedestrian channelizing devices indicate a suitable path of pedestrian travel around or through the work zone. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 6K-1. Examples of Channelizing Devices DRUM TUBULAR MARKERS Rev. 1 CONES VERTICAL PANEL TYPE 1 BARRICADE TYPE 2 BARRICADE TYPE 3 BARRICADE DIRECTION INDICATOR BARRICADE * Warning lights (optional) ** Rail stripe widths shall be 6 inches, except that 4-inch wide stripes may be used if rail lengths are less than 36 inches. The sides of barricades facing traffic shall have retroreflective rail faces. December 2025

title: Section 6K.02 Guidance 2 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Guidance 2 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 817

Pedestrian channelizing devices should be provided when work activities impact sidewalks or other pedestrian facilities or when the design of the temporary pedestrian facility does not otherwise include accessibility features consistent with the features in the existing pedestrian facility.

title: Section 6K.02 Guidance 3 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Guidance 3 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 817

The pedestrian channelizing devices should be used both to close sidewalks and to delineate an alternate route.

title: Section 6K.02 Support 4 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Support 4 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 817

An example of a pedestrian channelizing device is depicted in Figure 6K-2.

title: Section 6K.02 Standard 5 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Standard 5 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 817

Pedestrian channelizing devices shall be crashworthy (see definition in Section 1C.02) when exposed to vehicular traffic.

title: Section 6K.02 Standard 6 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Standard 6 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 817

Devices used to channelize pedestrians shall be detectable to users of long canes and visible to pedestrians with vision disabilities.

title: Section 6K.02 Standard 7 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Standard 7 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

When used as a sidewalk closure, the device shall cover the entire width of the sidewalk. Figure 6K-2. Pedestrian Channelizing Device Notes: 1. There should be at least a 2-inch gap between the hand-trailing edge and its support. 2. A maximum 2-inch gap between the bottom portion of the bottom rail and the walkway may be used to provide drainage. 3. Striping on sheeting panels may be either vertical or at a 45-degree angle. 4. Hand-trailing edge and/or detection plates are optional for continuous walls.

title: Section 6K.02 Standard 8 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Standard 8 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

Pedestrian channelizing devices shall have continuous detection plates and hand-trailing edges. The bottom of the detection plate shall be no higher than 2 inches above the walkway. The top edge of the detection plate shall be at least 8 inches above the walkway. The top of the hand-trailing edge shall be no lower than 32 inches and no higher than 38 inches above the walkway. The top surface of the hand-trailing edge shall be smooth to optimize hand trailing. Both the detection plate and the hand-trailing edge shall share a common vertical plane.

title: Section 6K.02 Guidance 9 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Guidance 9 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

When pedestrian channelizing devices are combined in a series, the gap between devices should not exceed 1 inch.

title: Section 6K.02 Support 10 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Support 10 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

The hand-trailing edge is the upper rail on a pedestrian channelizing device, as shown in Figure 6K-2. It is provided to allow pedestrians with vision disabilities to follow the pedestrian channelizing device with their hand. The hand-trailing edge is not a weight-bearing railing.

title: Section 6K.02 Guidance 11 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Guidance 11 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

There should be at least a 2-inch gap between the hand-trailing edge and its support.

title: Section 6K.02 Standard 12 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Standard 12 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

When visible to vehicular traffic the detection plate and the hand-trailing edge of the pedestrian channelizing device shall have retroreflective sheeting complying with Paragraph 10 of Section 6K.01.

title: Section 6K.02 Guidance 13 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Guidance 13 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

When not visible to vehicular traffic, the pedestrian channelizing device should have a contrasting pattern in alternating light and dark colors to provide visual contrast on the upper surface consisting of a minimum of 6 inches of sheeting or other contrasting materials.

title: Section 6K.02 Option 14 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Option 14 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

Non-retroreflective materials may be used on the pedestrian side of the pedestrian channelizing device.

title: Section 6K.02 Option 15 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Option 15 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

The sheeting on the pedestrian side of the pedestrian channelizing device may have stripes that are oriented either vertically or at a 45-degree angle.

title: Section 6K.02 Support 16 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.02 Support 16 - Pedestrian Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

The contrast of the light and dark stripes on the barricade sheeting assists pedestrians with vision disabilities in following the designated detour.

title: Section 6K.03 Standard 1 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Standard 1 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

Cones (see Figure 6K-1) shall be predominantly orange and shall be made of a material that can be struck without causing damage to the impacting vehicle. For daytime and low-speed roadways, cones shall be not less than 18 inches in height. When cones are used on freeways and other high-speed highways or at night on all highways, or when more conspicuous guidance is needed, cones shall be a minimum of 28 inches in height.

title: Section 6K.03 Standard 2 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Standard 2 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 818

For nighttime use, cones shall be retroreflectorized or equipped with lighting devices for maximum visibility. Retroreflectorization of cones that are 28 to 36 inches in height shall be provided by a 6-inch wide white band located 3 to 4 inches from the top of the cone and an additional 4-inch wide white band located approximately 2 inches below the 6-inch band.

title: Section 6K.03 Standard 3 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Standard 3 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Retroreflectorization of cones that are more than 36 inches in height shall be provided by horizontal, circumferential, alternating orange and white retroreflective stripes that are 4 to 6 inches wide. Each cone shall have a minimum of two orange and two white stripes with the top stripe being orange. Any non- retroreflective spaces between the retroreflective stripes shall not exceed 3 inches in width.

title: Section 6K.03 Option 4 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Option 4 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Traffic cones may be used to channelize road users, divide opposing vehicular traffic lanes, divide lanes when two or more lanes are kept open in the same direction, and delineate short-duration maintenance and utility work.

title: Section 6K.03 Guidance 5 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Guidance 5 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Steps should be taken to minimize the possibility of cones being blown over or displaced by wind or moving vehicular traffic.

title: Section 6K.03 Option 6 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Option 6 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Cones may be doubled up to increase their weight.

title: Section 6K.03 Support 7 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Support 7 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Some cones are constructed with bases that can be filled with ballast. Others have specially weighted bases, or weight such as sandbag rings, that can be dropped over the cones and onto the base to provide added stability.

title: Section 6K.03 Guidance 8 - Cones
text:
Section 6K.03 Guidance 8 - Cones
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Ballast should be kept to the minimum amount needed.

title: Section 6K.04 Standard 1 - Tubular Markers
text:
Section 6K.04 Standard 1 - Tubular Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Tubular markers (see Figure 6K-1) shall be predominantly orange for TTC zone applications and shall be not less than 18 inches high and 2 inches wide facing road users. They shall be made of a material that can be struck without causing damage to the impacting vehicle.

title: Section 6K.04 Standard 2 - Tubular Markers
text:
Section 6K.04 Standard 2 - Tubular Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Tubular markers shall be a minimum of 28 inches in height when they are used on freeways and other high-speed highways, on all highways during nighttime, or whenever more conspicuous guidance is needed.

title: Section 6K.04 Standard 3 - Tubular Markers
text:
Section 6K.04 Standard 3 - Tubular Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

For nighttime use, tubular markers shall be retroreflectorized. Retroreflectorization of tubular markers that have a height of less than 42 inches shall be provided by two 3-inch wide white bands placed a maximum of 2 inches from the top with a maximum of 6 inches between the bands. Retroreflectorization of tubular markers that have a height of 42 inches or more shall be provided by four 4-inch to 6-inch wide alternating orange and white stripes with the top stripe being orange.

title: Section 6K.04 Guidance 4 - Tubular Markers
text:
Section 6K.04 Guidance 4 - Tubular Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Tubular markers have less visible area than other devices and should be used only where space restrictions do not allow for the use of other more visible devices.

title: Section 6K.04 Guidance 5 - Tubular Markers
text:
Section 6K.04 Guidance 5 - Tubular Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Tubular markers should be stabilized by affixing them to the pavement, by using weighted bases, or by using weights such as sandbag rings that can be dropped over the tubular markers and onto the base to provide added stability. Ballast should be kept to the minimum amount needed.

title: Section 6K.04 Option 6 - Tubular Markers
text:
Section 6K.04 Option 6 - Tubular Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Tubular markers may be used effectively to divide opposing lanes of road users, divide vehicular traffic lanes when two or more lanes of moving vehicular traffic are kept open in the same direction, and to delineate the edge of a pavement drop off where space limitations do not allow the use of larger devices.

title: Section 6K.04 Standard 7 - Tubular Markers
text:
Section 6K.04 Standard 7 - Tubular Markers
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

A tubular marker shall be attached to the pavement to display the minimum 2-inch width to the approaching road users.

title: Section 6K.05 Standard 1 - Vertical Panels
text:
Section 6K.05 Standard 1 - Vertical Panels
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Vertical panels (see Figure 6K-1) shall have retroreflective striped material that is 8 to 12 inches in width and at least 24 inches in height. They shall have alternating diagonal orange and white retroreflective stripes sloping downward at an angle of 45 degrees in the direction vehicular traffic is to pass.

title: Section 6K.05 Standard 2 - Vertical Panels
text:
Section 6K.05 Standard 2 - Vertical Panels
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Where the height of the retroreflective material on the vertical panel is 36 inches or more, a stripe width of 6 inches shall be used.

title: Section 6K.05 Option 3 - Vertical Panels
text:
Section 6K.05 Option 3 - Vertical Panels
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 819

Where the height of the retroreflective material on the vertical panel is less than 36 inches, a stripe width of 4 inches may be used.

title: Section 6K.05 Option 4 - Vertical Panels
text:
Section 6K.05 Option 4 - Vertical Panels
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Where space is limited, vertical panels may be used to channelize vehicular traffic, divide opposing lanes, or replace barricades.

title: Section 6K.06 Standard 1 - Drums
text:
Section 6K.06 Standard 1 - Drums
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Drums (see Figure 6K-1) used for road user warning or channelization shall be constructed of lightweight, deformable materials.
