They shall be a minimum of 36 inches in height and have at least an 18-inch minimum width regardless of orientation. Metal drums shall not be used. The markings on drums shall be horizontal, circumferential, alternating orange and white retroreflective stripes 4 to 6 inches wide. Each drum shall have a minimum of two orange and two white stripes with the top stripe being orange. Any non-retroreflectorized spaces between the horizontal orange and white stripes shall not exceed 3 inches wide. Drums shall have closed tops that will not allow collection of construction debris or other debris.

title: Section 6K.06 Support 2 - Drums
text:
Section 6K.06 Support 2 - Drums
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Drums are highly visible, have good target value, give the appearance of being formidable obstacles and, therefore, command the respect of road users. They are portable enough to be shifted from place to place within a TTC zone in order to accommodate changing conditions, but are generally used in situations where they will remain in place for a prolonged period of time.

title: Section 6K.06 Option 3 - Drums
text:
Section 6K.06 Option 3 - Drums
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Although drums are most commonly used to channelize or delineate road user flow, they may also be used alone or in groups to mark specific locations.

title: Section 6K.06 Guidance 4 - Drums
text:
Section 6K.06 Guidance 4 - Drums
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Drums should not be weighted with sand, water, or any material to the extent that would make them hazardous to road users or workers when struck. Drums used in regions susceptible to freezing should have drain holes in the bottom so that water will not accumulate and freeze causing a hazard if struck by a road user.

title: Section 6K.06 Standard 5 - Drums
text:
Section 6K.06 Standard 5 - Drums
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Ballast shall not be placed on the top of a drum.

title: Section 6K.07 Support 1 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Support 1 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

A barricade is a portable or fixed device having from one to three rails with appropriate markings and is used to control road users by closing, restricting, or delineating all or a portion of the right-of-way.

title: Section 6K.07 Support 2 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Support 2 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

As shown in Figure 6K-1, barricades are classified as Type 1, Type 2, or Type 3.

title: Section 6K.07 Standard 3 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Standard 3 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Stripes on barricade rails shall be alternating orange and white retroreflective stripes sloping downward at an angle of 45 degrees in the direction road users are to pass. Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, the stripes shall be 6 inches wide.

title: Section 6K.07 Option 4 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Option 4 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

When rail lengths are less than 36 inches, 4-inch wide stripes may be used.

title: Section 6K.07 Standard 5 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Standard 5 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

The minimum length for Type 1 and Type 2 Barricades shall be 24 inches, and the minimum length for Type 3 Barricades shall be 48 inches. Each barricade rail shall be 8 to 12 inches wide. Barricades used on freeways, expressways, and other high-speed roadways shall have a minimum of 270 square inches of retroreflective area facing road users.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 6 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 6 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Where barricades extend entirely across a roadway, the stripes should slope downward in the direction toward which road users must turn.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 7 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 7 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Where both right and left turns are provided, the barricade stripes should slope downward in both directions from the center of the barricade or barricades.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 8 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 8 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Where no turns are intended, the stripes should be positioned to slope downward toward the center of the barricade or barricades.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 9 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 9 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 820

Barricade rails should be supported in a manner that will allow them to be seen by the road user, and in a manner that provides a stable support that is not easily blown over or displaced.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 10 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 10 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

The width of the existing pedestrian facility should be provided for the temporary facility if practical. Traffic control devices and other construction materials and features should not intrude into the usable width of the sidewalk, temporary pathway, or other pedestrian facility. When it is not possible to maintain a minimum width of 60 inches throughout the entire length of the pedestrian pathway, a 60 x 60-inch passing space should be provided at least every 200 feet to allow individuals in wheelchairs to pass.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 11 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 11 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Barricade rail supports should not project into pedestrian circulation routes more than 4 inches from the support between 27 and 80 inches from the surface as described in Section 307 of the U.S. Department of Justice 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, September 15, 2010, 28 CFR 35 and 36, Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

title: Section 6K.07 Option 12 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Option 12 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

For Type 1 Barricades, the support may include other unstriped horizontal rails necessary to provide stability.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 13 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 13 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

On high-speed expressways or in other situations where barricades might be susceptible to overturning in the wind, ballasting should be used.

title: Section 6K.07 Option 14 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Option 14 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Sandbags may be placed on the lower parts of the frame or the stays of barricades to provide the required ballast.

title: Section 6K.07 Support 15 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Support 15 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Type 1 or Type 2 Barricades are intended for use in situations where road user flow is maintained through the TTC zone.

title: Section 6K.07 Option 16 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Option 16 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Barricades may be used alone or in groups to mark a specific condition or they may be used in a series for channelizing road users.

title: Section 6K.07 Option 17 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Option 17 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Type 1 Barricades may be used on conventional roads or urban streets.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 18 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 18 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Type 2 or Type 3 Barricades should be used on freeways and expressways or other high-speed roadways. Type 3 Barricades should be used to close or partially close a road.

title: Section 6K.07 Option 19 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Option 19 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Type 3 Barricades used at a road closure may be placed completely across a roadway or from curb to curb.

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 20 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 20 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Where provision is made for access of authorized equipment and vehicles, the responsibility for Type 3 Barricades should be assigned to a person who will provide proper closure at the end of each work day.

title: Section 6K.07 Support 21 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Support 21 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

When a highway is legally closed but access must still be allowed for local road users, barricades usually are not extended completely across the roadway.

title: Section 6K.07 Standard 22 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Standard 22 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

A sign shall be installed with the appropriate legend concerning permissible use by local road users (see Section 6G.05).

title: Section 6K.07 Guidance 23 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Guidance 23 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Adequate visibility of the barricades from both directions should be provided.

title: Section 6K.07 Option 24 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
text:
Section 6K.07 Option 24 - Type 1, 2, or 3 Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

Signs may be installed on barricades (see Section 6F.02).

title: Section 6K.08 Standard 1 - Direction Indicator Barricades
text:
Section 6K.08 Standard 1 - Direction Indicator Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

The Direction Indicator Barricade (see Figure 6K-1) shall consist of a One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign mounted above a diagonal striped, horizontally-aligned, retroreflective rail.

title: Section 6K.08 Standard 2 - Direction Indicator Barricades
text:
Section 6K.08 Standard 2 - Direction Indicator Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

The One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign shall have a black legend and border on an orange background. The stripes on the bottom rail shall be alternating orange and white retroreflective stripes sloping downward at an angle of 45 degrees in the direction road users are to pass. The stripes shall be 4 inches wide. The One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign shall be 24 x 12 inches. The bottom rail shall have a length of 24 inches and a height of 8 inches.

title: Section 6K.08 Option 3 - Direction Indicator Barricades
text:
Section 6K.08 Option 3 - Direction Indicator Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 821

The Direction Indicator Barricade may be used in tapers, transitions, and other areas where specific directional guidance to drivers is necessary.

title: Section 6K.08 Guidance 4 - Direction Indicator Barricades
text:
Section 6K.08 Guidance 4 - Direction Indicator Barricades
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

If used, Direction Indicator Barricades should be used in a series to direct the driver through the transition and into the intended travel lane.

title: Section 6K.09 Support 1 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.09 Support 1 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Temporary traffic barriers (see Section 6M.02) are not TTC devices in themselves; however, when placed in a position identical to a line of channelizing devices and marked and/or equipped with appropriate channelization features to provide guidance and warning both day and night, they serve as TTC devices.

metadata.section_title: Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices

title: Section 6K.09 Standard 2 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.09 Standard 2 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Temporary traffic barriers serving as TTC devices shall comply with requirements for such devices as set forth throughout Part 6.

metadata.section_title: Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices

title: Section 6K.09 Standard 3 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.09 Standard 3 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Temporary traffic barriers (see Section 6M.02) shall not be used solely to channelize road users, but also to protect the work space. If used to channelize vehicular traffic, the temporary traffic barrier shall be supplemented with delineation, pavement markings, or channelizing devices for improved daytime and nighttime visibility.

metadata.section_title: Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices

title: Section 6K.09 Guidance 4 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.09 Guidance 4 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Temporary traffic barriers should not be used for a merging taper except in low-speed urban areas.

metadata.section_title: Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices

title: Section 6K.09 Guidance 5 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.09 Guidance 5 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

When it is necessary to use a temporary traffic barrier for a merging taper in low-speed urban areas or for a constricted/restricted TTC zone, the taper length should be designed to optimize road user operations considering the available geometric conditions.

metadata.section_title: Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices

title: Section 6K.09 Standard 6 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.09 Standard 6 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

When it is necessary to use a temporary traffic barrier for a merging taper in low-speed urban areas or for a constricted/restricted TTC zone, the taper shall be delineated using channelizing devices, and/or an edge line, and/or delineators on the barrier.

metadata.section_title: Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices

title: Section 6K.09 Guidance 7 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.09 Guidance 7 - Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

When used for channelization, temporary traffic barriers should be of a light color for increased visibility.

metadata.section_title: Temporary Traffic Barriers as Channelizing Devices

title: Section 6K.10 Support 1 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Support 1 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Longitudinal channelizing devices are lightweight, deformable devices that are highly visible, have good target value, and can be connected together.

title: Section 6K.10 Standard 2 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Standard 2 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

If used singly as Type 1, 2, or 3 barricades, longitudinal channelizing devices shall comply with the general size, color, stripe pattern, retroreflectivity, and placement characteristics established for the devices described in this Chapter.

title: Section 6K.10 Guidance 3 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Guidance 3 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

If used to channelize vehicular traffic at night, longitudinal channelizing devices should be supplemented with retroreflective material or delineation for improved nighttime visibility.

title: Section 6K.10 Option 4 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Option 4 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Longitudinal channelizing devices may be used instead of a line of cones, drums, or barricades.

title: Section 6K.10 Option 5 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Option 5 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Longitudinal channelizing devices may be hollow and filled with water as a ballast.

title: Section 6K.10 Option 6 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Option 6 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Longitudinal channelizing devices may be used for pedestrian traffic control.

title: Section 6K.10 Standard 7 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Standard 7 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

If used for pedestrian traffic control, longitudinal channelizing devices shall be interlocked to delineate or channelize flow. The interlocking devices shall not have gaps that allow pedestrians to stray from the channelizing path.

title: Section 6K.10 Guidance 8 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.10 Guidance 8 - Longitudinal Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 822

Longitudinal channelizing devices have not met the crashworthy requirements for temporary traffic barriers and should not be used to shield obstacles or provide positive protection for pedestrians or workers.

title: Section 6K.11 Option 1 - Temporary Lane Separators
text:
Section 6K.11 Option 1 - Temporary Lane Separators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 823

Temporary lane separators may be used to channelize road users, to divide opposing vehicular traffic lanes, and to divide lanes when two or more lanes are open in the same direction.

title: Section 6K.11 Standard 2 - Temporary Lane Separators
text:
Section 6K.11 Standard 2 - Temporary Lane Separators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 823

Temporary lane separators shall consist of a longitudinal base component with a maximum height of 4 inches and a maximum width of 1 foot. The longitudinal base shall have sloping sides in order to facilitate crossover by emergency vehicles. One or more types of channelizing devices, such as tubular markers, vertical panels, or a Narrow Two-Way Traffic (W6-4) sign (see Section 6H.17) mounted on flexible supports, shall be affixed to the longitudinal base.

title: Section 6K.11 Standard 3 - Temporary Lane Separators
text:
Section 6K.11 Standard 3 - Temporary Lane Separators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 823

Channelizing devices affixed to the longitudinal base of a temporary lane separator shall be retroreflectorized to provide nighttime visibility.

title: Section 6K.11 Guidance 4 - Temporary Lane Separators
text:
Section 6K.11 Guidance 4 - Temporary Lane Separators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 823

A temporary lane separator should be stabilized by affixing it to the pavement in a manner suitable to its design, while allowing the unit to be intentionally moved from place to place within the TTC zone in order to accommodate changing conditions.

title: Section 6K.11 Guidance 5 - Temporary Lane Separators
text:
Section 6K.11 Guidance 5 - Temporary Lane Separators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 823

Temporary Lane Separators should not be used to shield obstacles or provide positive protection for pedestrians or workers because these devices have not met the crashworthy requirements for temporary traffic barriers.

title: Section 6K.11 Standard 6 - Temporary Lane Separators
text:
Section 6K.11 Standard 6 - Temporary Lane Separators
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 823

At pedestrian crossing locations, temporary lane separators shall have an opening or be shortened to provide a pathway that is at least 60 inches wide for crossing pedestrians.

title: Section 6K.12 Option 1 - Other Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.12 Option 1 - Other Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 823

Channelizing devices other than those described in this Chapter may be used in special situations based on an engineering study.

title: Section 6K.12 Guidance 2 - Other Channelizing Devices
text:
Section 6K.12 Guidance 2 - Other Channelizing Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6K. Ttc Zone Channelizing Devices
Page: 824

Other channelizing devices should comply with the general size, color, stripe pattern, retroreflection, and placement characteristics established for the devices described in this Chapter.

title: Section 6L.01 Standard 1 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Standard 1 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

Temporary traffic control signals (see Section 4D.11) used to control road user movements through TTC zones and in other TTC situations shall comply with the applicable provisions of Part 4.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Support 2 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Support 2 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

Temporary traffic control signals are typically used in TTC zones such as temporary haul road crossings; temporary one-way operations along a one-lane, two-way highway; temporary one-way operations on bridges, reversible lanes, and intersections.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Standard 3 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Standard 3 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

A temporary traffic control signal that is used to control traffic through a one-lane, two-way section of roadway shall comply with the provisions of Section 4O.02.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Guidance 4 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Guidance 4 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

When temporary traffic control signals are used, conflict monitors typical of traditional traffic control signal operations should be used.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Support 5 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Support 5 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

Where pedestrians are detoured to a temporary traffic control signal, an accessible pedestrian signal (see Chapter 4K) provides information in non-visual formats (such as audible tones and/or speech messages, and vibrating surfaces) so that a pedestrian with vision disabilities can know when to cross the street along the alternate route.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Option 6 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Option 6 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

Temporary traffic control signals may be portable or temporarily mounted on fixed supports.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Guidance 7 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Guidance 7 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

Temporary traffic control signals should only be used in situations where temporary traffic control signals are preferable to other means of traffic control, such as changing the work staging or work zone size to eliminate one-way vehicular traffic movements, using flaggers to control one-way or crossing movements, using STOP or YIELD signs, and using warning devices alone.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Support 8 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Support 8 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 824

Factors related to the design and application of temporary traffic control signals include the following: A. Safety and road user needs; B. Work staging and operations; C. The feasibility of using other TTC strategies (for example, flaggers, providing space for two lanes, or detouring road users, including bicyclists and pedestrians); D. Sight distance restrictions; E. Human factors considerations (for example, lack of driver familiarity with temporary traffic control signals); F. Road-user volumes including roadway and intersection capacity; G. Affected side streets and driveways; H. Vehicle speeds; I. The placement of other TTC devices; J. Parking; K. Turning restrictions; L. Pedestrians; M. The nature of adjacent land uses (such as residential or commercial); N. Legal authority; O. Signal phasing and timing requirements; P. Full-time or part-time operation; Q. Actuated, fixed-time, or manual operation; R. Power failures or other emergencies; S. Inspection and maintenance needs; T. Need for detailed placement, timing, and operation records; and U. Operation by contractors or by others.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Support 9 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Support 9 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

Although temporary traffic control signals can be mounted on trailers or lightweight portable supports, fixed supports offer superior resistance to displacement or damage by severe weather, vehicle impact, and vandalism.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Guidance 10 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Guidance 10 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

Other TTC devices should be used to supplement temporary traffic control signals, including warning and regulatory signs, pavement markings, and channelizing devices.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Guidance 11 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Guidance 11 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

Temporary traffic control signals not in use should be covered or removed.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Guidance 12 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Guidance 12 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

If a temporary traffic control signal is located within ½ mile of an adjacent traffic control signal, consideration should be given to interconnected operation.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.01 Standard 13 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
text:
Section 6L.01 Standard 13 - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

Temporary traffic control signals shall not be located within 200 feet of a grade crossing unless the temporary traffic control signal is provided with preemption in accordance with Sections 4F.18, 4F.19, and 8D.09, or unless a uniformed officer or flagger is provided at the crossing to prevent vehicles from stopping within the crossing.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Support 1 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Support 1 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

Automated Flagger Assistance Devices (AFADs) enable a flagger(s) to be positioned out of the lane of traffic and are used to control road users through TTC zones. These devices are designed to be remotely operated either by a single flagger at one end of the TTC zone or at a central location, or by separate flaggers near each device’s location.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Support 2 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Support 2 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

There are two types of AFADs: A. An AFAD (see Section 6L.03) that uses a remotely controlled STOP/SLOW sign on either a trailer or a movable cart system to alternately control right-of-way. B. An AFAD (see Section 6L.04) that uses remotely controlled red and yellow lenses and a gate arm to alternately control right-of-way.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Support 3 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Support 3 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

AFADs might be appropriate for short-term and intermediate-term activities (see Section 6N.01). Typical applications include TTC activities such as, but not limited to: A. Bridge maintenance, B. Haul road crossings, and C. Pavement patching.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 4 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 4 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

AFADs shall only be used in situations where there is only one lane of approaching traffic in the direction to be controlled.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 5 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 5 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

When used at night, the AFAD location shall be illuminated in accordance with Section 6D.06.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Guidance 6 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Guidance 6 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

AFADs should not be used for long-term stationary work (see Section 6N.01).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 7 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 7 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

Because AFADs are not traffic control signals, they shall not be used as a substitute for or a replacement for a continuously operating temporary traffic control signal as described in Section 6L.01.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 8 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 8 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

AFADs shall meet the crashworthy (see definition in Section 1C.02) performance criteria contained in Section 6A.04.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Guidance 9 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Guidance 9 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

If used, AFADs should be located in advance of one-lane, two-way tapers and downstream from the point where approaching traffic is to stop in response to the device.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 10 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 10 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

If used, AFADs shall be placed so that all of the signs and other items controlling traffic movement are readily visible to the driver of the initial approaching vehicle with advance warning signs alerting other approaching traffic to be prepared to stop.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 11 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 11 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

If used, an AFAD shall be operated only by a flagger (see Section 6D.01) who has been trained on the operation of the AFAD. The flagger(s) operating the AFAD(s) shall not leave the AFAD(s) unattended at any time while the AFAD(s) is being used.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 12 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 12 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 825

The use of AFADs shall conform to one of the following methods: A. An AFAD at each end of the TTC zone (Method 1), or B. An AFAD at one end of the TTC zone and a flagger at the opposite end (Method 2).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 13 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 13 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

Except as provided in Paragraph 14 of this Section, two flaggers shall be used when using either Method 1 or Method 2.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Option 14 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Option 14 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

A single flagger may simultaneously operate two AFADs (Method 1) or may operate a single AFAD on one end of the TTC zone while being the flagger at the opposite end of the TTC zone (Method 2) if both of the following conditions are present: A. The flagger has an unobstructed view of the AFAD(s), and B. The flagger has an unobstructed view of approaching traffic in both directions.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Guidance 15 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Guidance 15 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

When an AFAD is used, the advance warning signing should include a ROAD WORK AHEAD (W20-1) sign, a ONE LANE ROAD (W20-4) sign, and a BE PREPARED TO STOP (W3-4) sign.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Standard 16 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Standard 16 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

When the AFAD is not in use, the signs associated with the AFAD, both at the AFAD location and in advance, shall be removed or covered.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.02 Guidance 17 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
text:
Section 6L.02 Guidance 17 - Automated Flagger Assistance Devices – General
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

A State or local agency that elects to use AFADs should adopt a policy, based on engineering judgment, governing AFAD applications. The policy should also consider more detailed and/or more restrictive requirements for AFAD use, such as the following: A. Conditions applicable for the use of Method 1 and Method 2 AFAD operation, B. Volume criteria, C. Maximum distance between AFADs, D. Conflicting lenses/indications monitoring requirements, E. Fail-safe procedures, F. Additional signing and pavement markings, G. Application consistency, H. Larger signs or lenses to increase visibility, and I. Use of backplates.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.03 Standard 1 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.03 Standard 1 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

A STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Device (AFAD) shall include a STOP/SLOW sign that alternately displays the STOP (R1-1) face and the SLOW (W20-8) face of a STOP/SLOW paddle (see Figure 6L-1).

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.03 Standard 2 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.03 Standard 2 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

The AFAD’s STOP/SLOW sign shall have an octagonal shape, shall be fabricated of rigid material, and shall be mounted with the bottom of the sign a minimum of 6 feet above the pavement on an appropriate support. The size of the STOP/SLOW sign shall be at least 24 x 24 inches with letters at least 8 inches high. The background of the STOP face shall be red with white letters and border. The background of the SLOW face shall be diamond-shaped and orange with black letters and border. Both faces of the STOP/SLOW sign shall be retroreflectorized.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.03 Standard 3 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.03 Standard 3 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

The AFAD’s STOP/SLOW sign shall have a means to positively lock, engage, or otherwise maintain the sign assembly in a stable condition when set in the STOP or SLOW position.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.03 Standard 4 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.03 Standard 4 - STOP/SLOW Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 826

The AFAD’s STOP/SLOW sign shall be supplemented with active conspicuity devices by incorporating either: A. White or red flashing lights within the STOP face and white or yellow flashing lights within the SLOW face meeting the provisions contained in Section 6D.02; or B. A Stop Beacon (see Section 4S.05) mounted a maximum of 24 inches above the STOP face and a Warning Beacon (see Section 4S.03) mounted a maximum of 24 inches above, below, or to the side of the SLOW face. The Stop Beacon shall not be flashed or illuminated when the SLOW face is displayed, and the Warning Beacon shall not be flashed or illuminated when the STOP face is displayed. Except for the mounting locations, the beacons shall comply with the provisions of

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 1 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 1 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 828

A Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Device (AFAD) shall alternately display a steadily illuminated CIRCULAR RED lens and a flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW lens to control traffic without the need for a flagger in the immediate vicinity of the AFAD or on the roadway (see Figure 6L-2).

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 2 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 2 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 828

Red/Yellow Lens AFADs shall have at least one set of CIRCULAR RED and CIRCULAR YELLOW lenses that are 12 inches in diameter. Unless otherwise provided in this Section, the lenses and their arrangement, CIRCULAR RED on top and CIRCULAR YELLOW below, shall comply with the applicable provisions for traffic signal indications in Part 4. If the set of lenses is post-mounted, the bottom of the housing (including brackets) shall be at least 7 feet above the pavement. If the set of lenses is located over any portion of the highway that can be used by motor vehicles, the bottom of the housing (including brackets) shall be at least 15 feet above the pavement.

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Option 3 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Option 3 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

Additional sets of CIRCULAR RED and CIRCULAR YELLOW lenses, located over the roadway or on the left-hand side of the approach and operated in unison with the primary set, may be used to improve visibility and/ or conspicuity of the AFAD. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 6L-2. Example of the Use of a Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Device (AFAD) Rev. 1 Notes: 1. See Table 6B-1 for the meanings of the letter codes used in this figure. 2. Shown as Method 2 with one AFAD and a flagger December 2025

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 4 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 4 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

A Red/Yellow Lens AFAD shall include a gate arm that descends to a down position across the approach lane of traffic when the steady CIRCULAR RED lens is illuminated and then ascends to an upright position when the flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW lens is illuminated. The gate arm shall be fully retroreflectorized on both sides, and shall have vertical alternating red and white stripes at 16-inch intervals measured horizontally as shown in Figure 8D-1. When the arm is in the down position blocking the approach lane: A. The minimum vertical aspect of the arm and sheeting shall be 2 inches, and B. The end of the arm shall reach at least to the center of the lane being controlled.

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 5 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 5 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

A Stop Here On Red (R10-6 or R10-6a) sign (see Section 2B.59) shall be installed on the right-hand side of the approach at the point at which drivers are expected to stop when the steady CIRCULAR RED lens is illuminated (see Figure 6L-2).

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 6 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 6 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

To inform road users to stop, the AFAD shall display a steadily illuminated CIRCULAR RED lens and the gate arm shall be in the down position. To inform road users to proceed, the AFAD shall display a flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW lens and the gate arm shall be in the upright position.

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 7 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 7 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

If Red/Yellow Lens AFADs are used to control traffic in a one-lane, two-way TTC zone, safeguards shall be incorporated to prevent the flagger(s) from actuating a simultaneous display of a flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW lens at each end of the TTC zone. Additionally, the flagger shall not actuate the AFAD’s display of the flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW lens until all oncoming vehicles have cleared the one-lane portion of the TTC zone.

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 8 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 8 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

A change interval shall be provided as the transition between the display of the flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW indication and the display of the steady CIRCULAR RED indication. During the change interval, the CIRCULAR YELLOW lens shall be steadily illuminated. The gate arm shall remain in the upright position during the display of the steadily illuminated CIRCULAR YELLOW change interval.

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Standard 9 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Standard 9 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

A change interval shall not be provided between the display of the steady CIRCULAR RED indication and the display of the flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW indication.

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.04 Guidance 10 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
text:
Section 6L.04 Guidance 10 - Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

The steadily illuminated CIRCULAR YELLOW change interval should have a duration of at least 5 seconds, unless a different duration, within the range of durations recommended by Section 4F.17, is justified by engineering judgment.

metadata.section_title: Red/Yellow Lens Automated Flagger Assistance Devices
metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.05 Support 1 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 6L.05 Support 1 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

Portable changeable message signs (PCMS) are TTC devices installed for temporary use with the flexibility to display a variety of messages. In most cases, portable changeable message signs follow the same provisions for design and application as those given for changeable message signs in Chapter 2L. The information in this Section describes situations where the provisions for portable changeable message signs differ from those given in Chapter 2L.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.05 Support 2 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 6L.05 Support 2 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

Portable changeable message signs are used most frequently on high-density urban freeways, but have applications on all types of highways where highway alignment, road user routing problems, or other pertinent conditions require advance warning and information.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.05 Support 3 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 6L.05 Support 3 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

Portable changeable message signs have a wide variety of applications in TTC zones including: roadway, lane, or ramp closures; incident management; width restriction information; speed control or reductions; advisories on work scheduling; road user management and diversion; warning of adverse conditions or special events; and other operational control.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.05 Support 4 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 6L.05 Support 4 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 830

The primary purpose of portable changeable message signs in TTC zones is to advise the road user of unexpected situations. Portable changeable message signs are particularly useful as they are capable of: A. Conveying complex messages, B. Displaying real time information about conditions ahead, and C. Providing information to assist road users in making decisions prior to the point where actions must be taken.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.05 Support 5 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 6L.05 Support 5 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 831

Some typical applications include the following: A. Where the speed of vehicular traffic is expected to drop substantially; B. Where significant queuing and delays are expected; C. Where adverse environmental conditions are present; D. Where there are changes in alignment or surface conditions; E. Where advance notice of ramp, lane, or roadway closures is needed; F. Where crash or incident management is needed; and/or G. Where changes in the road user pattern occur. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.05 Guidance 6 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 6L.05 Guidance 6 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 831

The components of a portable changeable message sign should include: a message sign, control systems, a power source, and mounting and transporting equipment. The front face of the sign should be covered with a protective material.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.05 Standard 7 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
text:
Section 6L.05 Standard 7 - Portable Changeable Message Signs
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 831

Portable changeable message signs shall comply with the applicable design and application principles established in Chapter 2A. Portable changeable message signs shall display only traffic operational, regulatory, warning, and guidance information, and shall not be used for advertising messages.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 1 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 1 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 832

An arrow board shall be a sign with a matrix of elements capable of either flashing or sequential displays. This sign shall provide additional warning and directional information to assist in merging and controlling road users through or around a TTC zone.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 2 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 2 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

An arrow board in the arrow or chevron mode should be used to advise approaching traffic of a lane closure along major multi-lane roadways in situations involving heavy traffic volumes, high speeds, and/or limited sight distances, or at other locations and under other conditions where road users are less likely to expect such lane closures.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 3 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 3 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

If used, an arrow board should be used in combination with appropriate signs, channelizing devices, or other TTC devices.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 4 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 4 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

An arrow board should be placed on the shoulder of the roadway or, if practicable, farther from the traveled lane. It should be delineated with retroreflective TTC devices. When an arrow board is not being used, it should be removed; if not removed, it should be shielded; or if the previous two options are not feasible, it should be delineated with retroreflective TTC devices.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 5 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 5 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

Arrow boards shall meet the minimum size, legibility distance, number of elements, and other specifications shown in Figure 6L-3.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Support 6 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Support 6 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

Type A arrow boards are appropriate for use on low-speed urban streets. Type B arrow boards are appropriate for intermediate-speed facilities and for maintenance or mobile operations on high-speed roadways. Type C arrow boards are intended to be used on high-speed, high-volume motor vehicle traffic control projects. Type D arrow boards are intended for use on vehicles authorized by the State or local agency.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 7 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 7 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

Type A, B, and C arrow boards shall have solid rectangular appearances. A Type D arrow board shall conform to the shape of the arrow.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 8 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 8 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

All arrow boards shall be finished in non-reflective black. The arrow board shall be mounted on a vehicle, a trailer, or other suitable support.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 9 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 9 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

The minimum mounting height, measured vertically from the bottom of the board to the roadway below it or to the elevation of the near edge of the roadway, of an arrow board should be 7 feet, except on vehicle-mounted arrow boards, which should be as high as practicable.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 10 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 10 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

A vehicle-mounted arrow board should be provided with remote controls.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 11 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 11 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

Arrow board elements shall be capable of at least a 50 percent dimming from full brilliance. The dimmed mode shall be used for nighttime operation of arrow boards.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 12 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 12 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

Full brilliance should be used for daytime operation of arrow boards.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 13 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 13 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

The arrow board shall have suitable elements capable of the various operating modes. The color presented by the elements shall be yellow.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 14 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 14 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

If an arrow board consisting of a bulb matrix is used, the elements should be recess-mounted or equipped with an upper hood of not less than 180 degrees.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 15 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 15 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

The minimum element on-time shall be 50 percent for the flashing mode, with equal intervals of 25 percent for each sequential phase. The flashing rate shall be not less than 25 or more than 40 flashes per minute.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 16 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 16 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

An arrow board shall have the following three mode selections: A. A Flashing Arrow, Sequential Arrow, or Sequential Chevron mode; B. A flashing Double Arrow mode; and C. A flashing Caution or Alternating Diamond mode.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 17 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 17 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

An arrow board in the arrow or chevron mode shall be used only for stationary or moving lane closures on multi-lane roadways.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 18 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 18 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

For shoulder work, for blocking the shoulder, for roadside work near the shoulder, or for temporarily closing one lane on a two-lane, two-way roadway, an arrow board shall be used only in the caution mode.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 19 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 19 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 833

For a stationary lane closure, the arrow board should be located on the shoulder at the beginning of the merging taper.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 20 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 20 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 834

Where the shoulder is narrow, the arrow board should be located in the closed lane. Figure 6L-3. Advance Warning Arrow Board Display Specifications Arrow Board Minimum Minimum Legibility Minimum Number Type Size Distance of Elements A 48 x 24 inches 1/2 mile

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 13 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 13 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 834

C 96 x 48 inches 1 mile

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 15 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 15 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 834

D None* 1/2 mile

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 21 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 21 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 834

When arrow boards are used to close multiple lanes, a separate arrow board shall be used for each closed lane.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 22 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 22 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

When arrow boards are used to close multiple lanes, if the first arrow board is placed on the shoulder, the second arrow board should be placed in the first closed lane at the upstream end of the second merging taper (see Figure 6P-37). When the first arrow board is placed in the first closed lane, the second arrow board should be placed in the second closed lane at the downstream end of the second merging taper.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Guidance 23 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Guidance 23 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

For mobile operations where a lane is closed, the arrow board should be located to provide adequate separation from the work operation to allow for appropriate reaction by approaching drivers.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 24 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 24 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

A vehicle displaying an arrow board shall be equipped with high-intensity rotating, flashing, oscillating, or strobe lights.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Standard 25 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Standard 25 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Arrow boards shall only be used to indicate a lane closure. Arrow boards shall not be used to indicate a lane shift.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.06 Option 26 - Arrow Boards
text:
Section 6L.06 Option 26 - Arrow Boards
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

A portable changeable message sign may be used to simulate an arrow board display.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Guidance 1 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Guidance 1 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Lighting devices should be provided in TTC zones based on engineering judgment.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Option 2 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Option 2 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Flashing beacons (see Chapter 4S) and/or warning lights may be used to supplement retroreflectorized signs, barriers, and channelizing devices.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Support 3 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Support 3 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Type A, Type B, Type C, and Type D 360-degree warning lights are portable, powered, yellow, lens-directed, enclosed lights.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 4 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 4 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Warning lights shall comply with the provisions in Chapter 13 of the publication entitled, “Equipment and Materials Standards of the Institute of Transportation Engineers,” 1998, Institute of Transportation Engineers.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 5 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 5 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

When warning lights are used, they shall be mounted on signs or channelizing devices in a manner that, if hit by an errant vehicle, they will not be likely to penetrate the windshield.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Guidance 6 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Guidance 6 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

The maximum spacing for warning lights should be identical to the channelizing device spacing requirements.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Support 7 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Support 7 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

The light weight and portability of warning lights are advantages that make these devices useful as supplements to the retroreflectorization on signs and channelizing devices. The flashing lights are effective in attracting road users’ attention.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Option 8 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Option 8 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Warning lights may be used in either a steady-burn or flashing mode.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 9 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 9 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Warning lights shall flash when placed on channelizing devices used alone or in a cluster to warn of a condition.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 10 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 10 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Except for the sequential flashing warning lights discussed in Paragraph 12 of this Section, warning lights placed on channelizing devices used in a series to channelize road users shall be steady-burn.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 11 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 11 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Except for the sequential flashing warning lights that are described in Paragraph 12 of this Section, flashing warning lights shall not be used for delineation, as a series of flashers fails to identify the desired vehicle path.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 12 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 12 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

If a series of sequential flashing warning lights is used on channelizing devices that form a merging taper, the successive flashing of the lights shall occur from the upstream end of the merging taper to the downstream end of the merging taper in order to identify the desired vehicle path. Each flashing warning light in the sequence shall be flashed at a rate of not less than 55 or more than 75 times per minute.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 13 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 13 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 835

Type A Low-Intensity Flashing warning lights, Type C Steady-Burn warning lights, and Type D 360-degree Steady-Burn warning lights shall be maintained so as to be capable of being visible on a clear night from a distance of 3,000 feet. Type B High-Intensity Flashing warning lights shall be maintained so as to be capable of being visible on a sunny day when viewed without the sun directly on or behind the device from a distance of 1,000 feet.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Standard 14 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Standard 14 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 836

Warning lights shall have a minimum mounting height of 30 inches to the bottom of the lens.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Support 15 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Support 15 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 836

Type A Low-Intensity Flashing warning lights are used to warn road users during nighttime hours that they are approaching or proceeding in a potentially hazardous area.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Option 16 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Option 16 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 836

Type A warning lights may be mounted on channelizing devices.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Support 17 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Support 17 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 836

Type B High-Intensity Flashing warning lights are used to warn road users during both daylight and nighttime hours that they are approaching a potentially hazardous area.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Option 18 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Option 18 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 836

Type B warning lights are designed to operate 24 hours per day and may be mounted on advance warning signs or on independent supports.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Option 19 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Option 19 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 836

Type C Steady-Burn warning lights and Type D 360-degree Steady-Burn warning lights may be used during nighttime hours to delineate the edge of the traveled way.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices

title: Section 6L.07 Guidance 20 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
text:
Section 6L.07 Guidance 20 - Flashing Beacons and Warning Lights
Part: Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control
Chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
Page: 836

When used to delineate a curve, Type C and Type D 360-degree warning lights should only be used on devices on the outside of the curve, and not on the inside of the curve.

metadata.chapter: Chapter 6L. Other Ttc Zone Traffic Control Devices
