metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.05 Standard 14 - School Speed Limit Signs and Plaques
text:
Section 7B.05 Standard 14 - School Speed Limit Signs and Plaques
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 980

If used, the Reduced School Speed Limit Ahead sign shall be followed by a School Speed Limit sign or a School Speed Limit assembly.

metadata.section_title: School Speed Limit Signs and Plaques
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.05 Standard 15 - School Speed Limit Signs and Plaques
text:
Section 7B.05 Standard 15 - School Speed Limit Signs and Plaques
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 980

The speed limit displayed on the Reduced School Speed Limit Ahead sign shall be identical to the speed limit displayed on the subsequent School Speed Limit sign or School Speed Limit assembly.

metadata.section_title: School Speed Limit Signs and Plaques
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Support 1 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Support 1 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 980

The signs and plaques used to inform road users of higher fines zones and their locations depend on whether the fines apply to all traffic violations or only to speeding violations. Their locations also depend on whether the higher fines zone begins and/or ends at the same point as the school zone or school speed limit zone. Figures 7B-4 and 7B-5 show examples of higher fines zones signing.

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Standard 2 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Standard 2 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 980

Where increased fines are imposed for traffic violations within a designated school zone: A. A BEGIN HIGHER FINES ZONE (R2-10) sign (see Figure 7B-1) or a FINES HIGHER (R2-6P), FINES DOUBLE (R2-6aP), or $XX FINE (R2-6bP) plaque (see Figure 7B-1) shall be installed as a supplement to the School Zone (S1-1) sign to identify the beginning point of the higher fines zone (see Figures 7B-4 and 7B-5); and B. An END HIGHER FINES ZONE (R2-11) sign (see Figure 7B-1) or an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) sign (see Figure 7B-1) shall be installed at the downstream end of the zone to notify road users of the termination of the increased fines zone (see Figure 7B-5).

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Standard 3 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Standard 3 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 980

If exceeding the speed limit is the only traffic violation that is subject to higher fines, a FINES HIGHER (R2-6P), FINES DOUBLE (R2-6aP), or $XX FINE (R2-6bP) plaque shall be posted with the School Speed Limit (S5-1) sign and shall not be posted beneath the School Zone (S1-1) sign (see Section 7B.05).

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Standard 4 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Standard 4 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 980

If the portion of the roadway that is subject to higher fines does not begin at the location of the School Zone (S1-1) sign, a BEGIN HIGHER FINES ZONE (R2-10) sign shall be placed at the point where the higher fines begin (see Sheet 2 of Figure 7B-5).

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Option 5 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Option 5 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 980

If a BEGIN HIGHER FINES ZONE (R2-10) sign is used downstream of the School Zone (S1-1) sign, a FINES HIGHER (R2-6P), FINES DOUBLE (R2-6aP), or $XX FINE (R2-6bP) plaque may also be placed beneath the School Zone (S1-1) sign.

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Option 6 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Option 6 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 983

Where appropriate, one of the following plaques may be mounted below the sign that identifies the beginning point of the higher fines zone: A. A S4-1P plaque (see Figure 7B-1) specifying the times that the higher fines are in effect, B. A WHEN CHILDREN ARE PRESENT (S4-2P) plaque (see Figure 7B-1), or C. A WHEN FLASHING (S4-4P) plaque (see Figure 7B-1) if used in conjunction with a yellow flashing beacon. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 7B-5. Example of Signing for a School Zone with Higher Fines for All Traffic Violations (Sheet 1 of 2) A - Higher fines zone begins at the beginning of the school zone Rev. 1 Rev. 1 December 2025 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 7B-5. Example of Signing for a School Zone with Higher Fines for All Traffic Violations (Sheet 2 of 2) B - Higher fines zone begins after the beginning of the school zone Rev. 1 Rev. 1 December 2025

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Guidance 7 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Guidance 7 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 983

If other traffic violations in addition to exceeding the speed limit are subject to higher fines, then the duplicate FINES HIGHER (R2-6P), FINES DOUBLE (R2-6aP), or $XX FINE (R2-6bP) plaque should be omitted from the School Speed Limit When Flashing (S5-1) sign (see Section 7B.05).

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Option 8 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Option 8 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 983

If a higher fines zone ends at the same point as a reduced school speed limit zone, an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) sign may be used instead of a combination of an END HIGHER FINES ZONE (R2-11) sign and an END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) sign (see Figure 7B-5).

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.06 Option 9 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
text:
Section 7B.06 Option 9 - Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 983

Where the higher fines zone is established by statute, the BEGIN HIGHER FINES ZONE (R2-10) sign, FINES HIGHER (R2-6P), FINES DOUBLE (R2-6aP), and $XX FINE (R2-6bP) plaques may be omitted.

metadata.section_title: Higher Fines Zone Signs and Plaques in School Areas
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.07 Option 1 - Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
text:
Section 7B.07 Option 1 - Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 983

Parking and stopping regulatory signs may be used to prevent parked or waiting vehicles from blocking pedestrians’ views, and drivers’ views of pedestrians, and to control vehicles as a part of the school traffic plan.

metadata.section_title: Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.07 Support 2 - Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
text:
Section 7B.07 Support 2 - Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 983

Parking signs and other signs governing the stopping and standing of vehicles in school areas cover a wide variety of regulations. Typical examples of regulations are as follows: A. NO PARKING X:XX AM to X:XX PM SCHOOL DAYS ONLY B. NO STOPPING X:XX AM to X:XX PM SCHOOL DAYS ONLY, C. XX MIN LOADING X:XX AM to X:XX PM SCHOOL DAYS ONLY, and D. NO STANDING X:XX AM to X:XX PM SCHOOL DAYS ONLY.

metadata.section_title: Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7B.07 Support 3 - Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
text:
Section 7B.07 Support 3 - Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7B. Signs
Page: 984

Sections 2B.53 through 2B.55 contain information regarding the signing of parking regulations in school zone areas. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Parking and Stopping (R7 and R8 Series) Signs
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7C.01 Guidance 1 - Crosswalk Markings
text:
Section 7C.01 Guidance 1 - Crosswalk Markings
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7C. Markings
Page: 984

Crosswalks should be marked at all intersections on established routes to a school where there is substantial conflict between motorists, bicyclists, and student movements; where students would not otherwise recognize the proper place to cross; or where motorists or bicyclists might not expect students to cross (see Figure 7A-1). Rev. 1

metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7C.01 Guidance 2 - Crosswalk Markings
text:
Section 7C.01 Guidance 2 - Crosswalk Markings
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7C. Markings
Page: 984

An engineering study considering the factors described in Section 3C.02 should be performed before a marked crosswalk is installed at a location away from a traffic control signal or an approach controlled by a STOP or YIELD sign.

metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7C.01 Guidance 3 - Crosswalk Markings
text:
Section 7C.01 Guidance 3 - Crosswalk Markings
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7C. Markings
Page: 984

Because non-intersection school crossings are generally unexpected by the road user, warning signs (see Section 7B.03) should be installed for all marked school crosswalks at non-intersection locations. Adequate visibility of students by approaching motorists and of approaching motorists by students should be provided by parking prohibitions or other appropriate measures.

metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7C.02 Option 1 - Pavement Word, Symbol, and Arrow Markings
text:
Section 7C.02 Option 1 - Pavement Word, Symbol, and Arrow Markings
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7C. Markings
Page: 984

If used, the SCHOOL word marking may extend to the width of two approach lanes (see Figure 7C-1).

metadata.section_title: Pavement Word, Symbol, and Arrow Markings
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7C.02 Guidance 2 - Pavement Word, Symbol, and Arrow Markings
text:
Section 7C.02 Guidance 2 - Pavement Word, Symbol, and Arrow Markings
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7C. Markings
Page: 984

If the two-lane SCHOOL word marking is used, the letters should be 10 feet or more in height.

metadata.section_title: Pavement Word, Symbol, and Arrow Markings
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.01 Option 1 - Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.01 Option 1 - Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

Adult crossing guards may be used to provide gaps in traffic at school crossings where an engineering study has shown that adequate gaps need to be created, and where authorized by law.

metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.01 Support 2 - Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.01 Support 2 - Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

Adult crossing guards can also add conspicuity at the crossing where children, who are typically smaller in stature, might not be as visible.

metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.01 Support 3 - Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.01 Support 3 - Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

High standards for selection of adult crossing guards are essential because they are responsible for the safety of and the efficient crossing of the street by schoolchildren within and in the immediate vicinity of school crosswalks.

metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.01 Guidance 4 - Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.01 Guidance 4 - Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

Jurisdictions should have policies and procedures for the qualifications, selection, and training of adult crossing guards.

metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.02 Standard 1 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.02 Standard 1 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

Law enforcement officers performing school crossing supervision and adult crossing guards shall wear high-visibility retroreflective safety apparel labeled as ANSI 107-2020 standard performance for Class 2, Type R, as described in Section 6C.05.

metadata.section_title: Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.02 Standard 2 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.02 Standard 2 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

Adult crossing guards shall not direct traffic in the usual law enforcement regulatory sense. In the control of traffic, they shall pick opportune times to create a sufficient gap in the traffic flow. At these times, they shall stand in the roadway to indicate that pedestrians are about to use or are using the crosswalk, and that all vehicular traffic must stop.

metadata.section_title: Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.02 Standard 3 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.02 Standard 3 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

Adult crossing guards shall use a STOP paddle. The STOP paddle shall be the primary hand-signaling device.

metadata.section_title: Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.02 Standard 4 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.02 Standard 4 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 985

The STOP paddle shall comply with the provisions for a STOP/SLOW paddle (see Section 6D.02) except both sides shall be a STOP face.

metadata.section_title: Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 7D.02 Standard 5 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
text:
Section 7D.02 Standard 5 - Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
Part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas
Chapter: Chapter 7D. Crossing Supervision
Page: 987

The paddle shall be retroreflective or illuminated when used during hours of darkness. (This page intentionally left blank) May 2023

metadata.section_title: Operating Procedures for Adult Crossing Guards
metadata.part: Part 7 Traffic Control For School Areas

title: Section 8A.01 Support 1 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 1 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

Where the acronym “LRT” is used in Part 8, it refers to “light rail transit.”

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 2 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 2 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

Chapters 8A, 8B, 8C, and 8D describe the traffic control devices that are used at highway-rail and highway- LRT grade crossings. Unless otherwise provided in the text or on a figure or table, the provisions of Part 8 are applicable to both highway-rail and highway-LRT grade crossings. Where the phrase “grade crossing” is used by itself without the prefix “highway-rail” or “highway-LRT,” it refers to both highway-rail and highway-LRT grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 3 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 3 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

Chapter 8E describes the traffic control devices that are used at pathway and sidewalk grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 4 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 4 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

Traffic control for grade crossings includes all signs, signals, markings, other warning devices, and their supports along highways approaching and at grade crossings. The function of this traffic control is to promote safety and provide effective operation of rail and/or LRT and highway traffic at grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 5 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 5 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

For purposes of design, installation, operation, and maintenance of traffic control devices at grade crossings, it is recognized that the crossing of the highway and rail tracks is situated on a right-of-way available for the joint use of both highway traffic and railroad or LRT traffic.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 6 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 6 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

Grade crossings and the traffic control devices that are associated with them are unique in that in many cases, the highway agency or authority with jurisdiction, the regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable), and the railroad company or transit agency are jointly involved in the development of engineering judgment or the performance of an engineering study. This joint process is accomplished through the efforts of a Diagnostic Team made up of the highway agency with jurisdiction, the regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable), and the railroad company and/or transit agency (if applicable).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 7 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 7 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

In Part 8, the combination of traffic control devices selected or installed at a specific grade crossing is referred to as a “traffic control system.”

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 8 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 8 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

The combination of railroad or LRT active traffic control devices used to inform road users at a grade crossing of the approach or presence of rail traffic and the necessary control equipment for the devices are referred to as a “grade crossing warning system.” The “2023 AREMA Communications and Signals Manual” published by the American Railway Engineering and Maintenance-of-Way Association (AREMA) contains further information about grade crossing warning systems.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Standard 9 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Standard 9 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

Except at grade crossings of privately-owned roadways, pathways, and sidewalks, the traffic control devices, systems, and practices described in this Manual shall be used at all grade crossings open to public travel, consistent with Federal, State, and local laws and regulations.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.01 Support 10 - Introduction
text:
Section 8A.01 Support 10 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 987

23 CFR 655.603 contains information on the applicability of this Manual at private grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Support 1 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Support 1 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 988

Because of the large number of significant variables to be considered, no single standard system of traffic control devices is universally applicable for all grade crossings.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Standard 2 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Standard 2 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 988

Before any new grade crossing traffic control system is installed or before modifications are made to an existing system, approval shall be obtained from the highway agency with jurisdiction, the regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable), and the railroad company and/or transit agency.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Standard 3 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Standard 3 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 988

The Diagnostic Team members shall make a recommendation, documented in an engineering study (see Section 8A.05), on new grade crossing traffic control systems and on proposed changes to an existing grade crossing traffic control system. The Diagnostic Team recommendation shall be made based on the Diagnostic Team’s site visits, meetings, conference calls, or a combination of some or all of these methods.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Standard 4 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Standard 4 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 988

Except as provided in Paragraph 7 of this Section, operational changes made to a grade crossing traffic control system shall be evaluated by a Diagnostic Team.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Standard 5 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Standard 5 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 988

Among the types of changes at a grade crossing for which a Diagnostic Team shall conduct an engineering study are: additions, removals, or modifications of the lanes approaching or traversing the grade crossing; addition or removal of tracks; significant changes in the number or speed of trains; significant changes in the number or speed of vehicles; addition of vehicle access near the grade crossing; additions or modifications to sidewalks; additions or modifications to bicycle lanes, especially if a counter- flow bicycle lane is added on a one-way street; changes to roadway use, including conversion to or from one-way operation or reversible lanes; and the installation of or significant operational changes to traffic control signals that might affect the grade crossing.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Option 6 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Option 6 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 988

A Diagnostic Team may conduct an engineering study and make recommendations as part of the Quiet Zone establishment process (see Section 8A.11).

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Option 7 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Option 7 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 988

Where determined by the responsible public agency, the railroad company, and/or the transit agency, general maintenance activities or minor operational changes to the grade crossing traffic control system that do not have a negative impact on the overall operation of the traffic control system may be made without a review and determination by a Diagnostic Team.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.03 Support 8 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.03 Support 8 - Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

Many other details of grade crossing traffic control systems that are not set forth in Part 8 are contained in publications such as the “2023 AREMA Communications and Signals Manual” published by the American Railway Engineering and Maintenance-of-Way Association (AREMA), the Third Edition of “Highway-Rail Crossing Handbook” published by the FHWA and the FRA, and the 2nd Edition of “Preemption of Traffic Signals Near Railroad Crossings” published by the Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE). Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems and Practices at Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.04 Support 1 - Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.04 Support 1 - Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

The combination of devices selected or installed at a specific highway-LRT grade crossing is referred to as a “Light Rail Transit Traffic Control System.”

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.04 Support 2 - Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.04 Support 2 - Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

The normal rules of the road and traffic control priority identified in the “Uniform Vehicle Code” (see Section 1A.06) govern the order assigned to the movement of vehicles at an intersection unless the local agency determines that it is appropriate to assign a higher priority to LRT vehicles. Examples of different types of LRT priority control include separate traffic control signal phases for LRT movements, restriction of movement of roadway vehicles in favor of LRT operations, and preemption of highway traffic signal control to accommodate LRT movements.

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.04 Standard 3 - Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.04 Standard 3 - Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

Highway-LRT grade crossings in semi-exclusive alignments, except where the tracks are located in the median of a street or highway, shall be equipped with flashing-light signals, with or without automatic gates, unless a Diagnostic Team determines that the use of Crossbuck Assemblies, traffic control signals (see Section 8D.04), STOP signs alone, or YIELD signs alone would be adequate. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Traffic Control Systems at Highway-LRT Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.05 Standard 1 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.05 Standard 1 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

The appropriate traffic control system to be used at a grade crossing shall be determined based on an engineering study conducted by a Diagnostic Team involving the highway agency with jurisdiction, the regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable), and the railroad company and/or transit agency (as applicable).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.05 Option 2 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.05 Option 2 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

The regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable) may approve the grade crossing traffic control system.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.05 Guidance 3 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.05 Guidance 3 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

Among the factors that should be considered in the determination by a Diagnostic Team of which traffic control devices would be appropriate to install at a grade crossing are road geometrics, stopping sight distance, clearing sight distance, the proximity of nearby roadway intersections (including the traffic control devices at the intersections), adjacent driveways, traffic volume across the grade crossing, extent of queuing upstream or downstream from the grade crossing, train volume, pedestrian and bicycle volumes, operation of passenger trains, presence of nearby passenger station stops, maximum allowable train speeds, variable train speeds, accelerating and decelerating trains, multiple tracks, high-speed train operation, number of school buses or hazardous material haul vehicles, and the crash history at or near the location.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.05 Option 4 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.05 Option 4 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

The engineering study may include the Highway-Rail Intersection (HRI) components of the National Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) architecture, which is a USDOT accepted method for linking the highway, vehicles, and traffic management systems with rail operations and wayside equipment.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.05 Support 5 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.05 Support 5 - Engineering Studies at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

More detail on Highway-Rail Intersection components is available from the USDOT’s Federal Railroad Administration, 1200 New Jersey Avenue, SE, Washington, DC 20590, or www.fra.dot.gov.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.06 Standard 1 - Uniform Provisions
text:
Section 8A.06 Standard 1 - Uniform Provisions
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

All signs used in grade crossing traffic control systems shall be retroreflective or illuminated as described in Section 2A.21 to show the same shape and similar color to an approaching road user during both day and night.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.06 Standard 2 - Uniform Provisions
text:
Section 8A.06 Standard 2 - Uniform Provisions
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

No sign or signal shall be located in the center of an undivided highway, unless it is crashworthy (breakaway, yielding, or shielded with a longitudinal barrier or crash cushion) or unless it is placed on a raised island.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.06 Guidance 3 - Uniform Provisions
text:
Section 8A.06 Guidance 3 - Uniform Provisions
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 989

Any signs or signals placed on a raised island in the center of an undivided highway should be installed with a clearance of at least 2 feet from the outer edge of the raised island to the nearest edge of the sign or signal, except as permitted in Section 2A.16.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.06 Guidance 4 - Uniform Provisions
text:
Section 8A.06 Guidance 4 - Uniform Provisions
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

Where a raised median island is installed supplemental to an automatic gate to discourage road users from driving around a lowered gate, the Diagnostic Team should consider the length of the vehicle queues that typically form on the approach to the grade crossing when determining how far in advance of the grade crossing to extend the island. Month 2023 December 2025

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.06 Guidance 5 - Uniform Provisions
text:
Section 8A.06 Guidance 5 - Uniform Provisions
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

If the roadway at a grade crossing includes a two-way left-turn lane (see Section 3B.05), the two-way left- turn lane should be discontinued in the immediate vicinity of the grade crossing by installing median islands, by designating the lane for left turns in one direction only, or by installing yellow diagonal markings in the lane (see Figure 3B-5). If yellow diagonal markings are used, the use of channelizing devices (see Section 3I.01), such as supplemental tubular markers, should also be considered.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.06 Option 6 - Uniform Provisions
text:
Section 8A.06 Option 6 - Uniform Provisions
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

If yellow diagonal markings are used, extending the automatic gate across the lane may be considered.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.07 Support 1 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
text:
Section 8A.07 Support 1 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

The upstream point of the minimum track clearance distance is determined in the following manner: A. If an automatic gate is present on the approach, the upstream point is the portion of the automatic gate arm that is farthest from the nearest rail. B. If an automatic gate is not present on the approach, the upstream point is the portion of the stop line that is farthest from the nearest rail. C. If the roadway is not paved, the upstream point is the point that is farthest from the nearest rail that is 10 feet measured perpendicular from the nearest rail.

metadata.section_title: Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.07 Support 2 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
text:
Section 8A.07 Support 2 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

The downstream point of the minimum track clearance distance is 6 feet beyond the track(s) or the edge of the downstream highway-highway intersection, whichever is closer, and is measured perpendicular to the farthest rail, along the center line or edge line of the highway, as appropriate, to obtain the longer distance. Where an Exit Gate system (see Section 8D.05) is present, the downstream point is the point where the rear of the vehicle would be clear of the exit gate arm. In cases where the exit gate arm is not perpendicular to the highway, the distance is measured either along the center line or edge line of the highway, as appropriate, to obtain the longer distance.

metadata.section_title: Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.07 Support 3 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
text:
Section 8A.07 Support 3 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

Where two adjacent grade crossings (see Section 8A.08) are located within 200 feet of each other as measured along the highway, the minimum track clearance distance is measured from a point that is upstream of the first grade crossing to a point that is downstream from the second grade crossing.

metadata.section_title: Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.07 Support 4 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
text:
Section 8A.07 Support 4 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

Where a highway-highway intersection is located beyond a grade crossing, the clear storage distance defines on a lane-by-lane basis the area of the roadway between the downstream point of the minimum track clearance distance and the intersection stop line, yield line, or normal stopping point on the highway.

metadata.section_title: Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.07 Support 5 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
text:
Section 8A.07 Support 5 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

The Highway-Rail Crossing Handbook contains an illustration of the minimum track clearance distance and the clear storage distance.

metadata.section_title: Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.07 Support 6 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
text:
Section 8A.07 Support 6 - Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

The minimum track clearance distance and the clear storage distance are used by the Diagnostic Team to determine the appropriate traffic control devices and/or roadway treatments to be used at the grade crossing, and to determine the queue start-up and queue clearance time necessary where a traffic signal or hybrid beacon is interconnected with a grade crossing active warning system.

metadata.section_title: Minimum Track Clearance Distance and Clear Storage Distance
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.08 Support 1 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.08 Support 1 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

Adjacent grade crossings sometimes exist within 200 feet of each other as measured along the highway between the inside rails. These closely-spaced grade crossings sometimes result from separate railroads or from a railroad and an LRT alignment operating in parallel corridors.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.08 Guidance 2 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.08 Guidance 2 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

Where adjacent grade crossings are located within 200 feet of each other along the highway as measured along the highway between the inside rails, the Diagnostic Team should consider the possibility that rail traffic might arrive at a grade crossing when rail traffic is already occupying the adjacent grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.08 Guidance 3 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.08 Guidance 3 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

Where the shortest distance between the tracks at adjacent grade crossings, measured along the highway between the inside rails, is 100 feet or less, the grade crossings should be treated as one individual grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.08 Guidance 4 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.08 Guidance 4 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 990

Where the shortest distance between the tracks at adjacent grade crossings, measured along the highway between the inside rails, is more than 100 feet and less than 200 feet, additional signs or other appropriate traffic control devices should be used to inform approaching road users of the long distance to cross the tracks.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.08 Guidance 5 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.08 Guidance 5 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Where active traffic control devices are installed between adjacent grade crossings that are more than 100 feet apart and less than 200 feet apart as measured along the highway between the inside rails, the operation of the devices should provide additional time for vehicles to clear the extended minimum track clearance distance (see Section 8A.07) that results from the closely-spaced grade crossings. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.08 Guidance 6 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.08 Guidance 6 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Where the shortest distance between the tracks at adjacent grade crossings, measured along the highway between the inside rails, is more than 200 feet, the grade crossings should be treated as individual grade crossings and traffic control devices should be installed between the grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.08 Support 7 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.08 Support 7 - Adjacent Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

The “2023 AREMA Communications and Signals Manual” published by the American Railway Engineering and Maintenance-of-Way Association (AREMA) contains further information and recommendations about the location and operation of active traffic control devices at adjacent grade crossings that are located within 200 feet of each other.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Option 1 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Option 1 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

If a particular grade crossing appears to be redundant or unnecessary for motor vehicle, pedestrian, and bicycle traffic, an engineering study may be conducted to determine the costs and benefits of eliminating the crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Guidance 2 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Guidance 2 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

If an engineering study is conducted, any necessary improvements to adjacent grade crossings and the surrounding roadway network to accommodate diverted traffic should also be included in the analysis.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Guidance 3 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Guidance 3 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

If the conclusion of the engineering study is that the grade crossing should be eliminated, a Diagnostic Team should use the engineering study to determine the appropriate steps that need to be taken to accomplish the grade crossing elimination.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Standard 4 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Standard 4 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Where a grade crossing is eliminated, the traffic control devices for the crossing shall be removed, and shall be covered or turned from view in the interim period prior to removal.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Guidance 5 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Guidance 5 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

If the existing traffic control devices at a multiple-track grade crossing become improperly placed or are no longer applicable because of the removal of some of the tracks, the existing devices should be relocated and/ or modified.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Guidance 6 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Guidance 6 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Where a roadway is removed from a grade crossing, the roadway approaches in the railroad or LRT right- of-way should also be removed and appropriate signs and object markers should be placed at the roadway end in accordance with Section 2C.73.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Guidance 7 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Guidance 7 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Where a railroad or LRT is eliminated at a grade crossing, the tracks should be removed or paved over.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.09 Option 8 - Grade Crossing Elimination
text:
Section 8A.09 Option 8 - Grade Crossing Elimination
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Based on engineering judgment, the TRACKS OUT OF SERVICE (R8-9) sign (see Figure 8B-1) may be temporarily installed until the tracks are removed or covered. The length of time before the tracks will be removed or covered may be considered in making the decision as to whether to install the sign.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.10 Support 1 - Illumination at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.10 Support 1 - Illumination at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Illumination is sometimes installed at or adjacent to a grade crossing in order to provide better nighttime visibility of trains or LRT equipment and the grade crossing (for example, where a substantial amount of railroad or LRT operations are conducted at night, where grade crossings are blocked for extended periods of time, or where crash history indicates that road users experience difficulty in seeing trains or LRT equipment or traffic control devices during hours of darkness).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.10 Support 2 - Illumination at Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.10 Support 2 - Illumination at Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

Recommended types and locations of luminaires for illuminating grade crossings are contained in the American National Standards Institute’s “ANSI/IES RP-8-22, Recommended Practice: Lighting Roadway and Parking Facilities,” which is available from the Illuminating Engineering Society.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.11 Support 1 - Quiet Zone Treatments at Highway-Rail Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.11 Support 1 - Quiet Zone Treatments at Highway-Rail Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 991

49 CFR Part 222 (Use of Locomotive Horns at Highway-Rail Grade Crossings; Final Rule) prescribes Quiet Zone requirements and treatments.

metadata.section_title: Quiet Zone Treatments at Highway-Rail Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.11 Standard 2 - Quiet Zone Treatments at Highway-Rail Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8A.11 Standard 2 - Quiet Zone Treatments at Highway-Rail Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Any traffic control device and its application, where used as part of a Quiet Zone, shall comply with all applicable provisions of the MUTCD. Rev. 1 Month 2023 December 2025

metadata.section_title: Quiet Zone Treatments at Highway-Rail Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.12 Support 1 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
text:
Section 8A.12 Support 1 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

At circular intersections, such as roundabouts and traffic circles, that include or are within close proximity to a grade crossing, a queue of vehicular traffic could cause motor vehicles to stop on the grade crossing.

metadata.section_title: Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.12 Standard 2 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
text:
Section 8A.12 Standard 2 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Where circular intersections include or are within 200 feet of a grade crossing, an engineering study shall be made to determine if queuing could impact the grade crossing.

metadata.section_title: Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.12 Guidance 3 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
text:
Section 8A.12 Guidance 3 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

The Diagnostic Team should review the findings of the engineering study and determine the appropriate measures to clear highway traffic from the grade crossing prior to the arrival of rail traffic.

metadata.section_title: Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.12 Support 4 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
text:
Section 8A.12 Support 4 - Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Among the actions that can be taken to keep the grade crossing clear of traffic or to clear traffic from the grade crossing prior to the arrival of rail traffic are the following: A. Grade crossing regulatory and warning devices; B. Highway traffic signals; C. Traffic metering devices; D. Activated signs; E. Geometric design revisions, including reconstruction or elimination of the circular intersection; or F. A combination of these or other actions.

metadata.section_title: Grade Crossings within or in Close Proximity to Circular Intersections
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.13 Support 1 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
text:
Section 8A.13 Support 1 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Temporary traffic control planning provides for continuity of operations (such as movement of motor vehicle traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists, transit operations, and access to property/utilities) when the normal function of a roadway at a grade crossing is suspended because of temporary traffic control operations. Temporary traffic control planning is also needed when traffic is detoured over an existing grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.13 Standard 2 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
text:
Section 8A.13 Standard 2 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Traffic controls for temporary traffic control zones that include grade crossings shall be as provided in Part 6.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.13 Guidance 3 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
text:
Section 8A.13 Guidance 3 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Where a temporary traffic control zone extends over an active grade crossing (see Section 6N.17), and where the direction of traffic in any lane is reversed over the grade crossing, the railroad company or transit agency should be part of the temporary traffic control planning process. Where a grade crossing warning system is not modified to support the temporary traffic control operation, at least one uniformed law enforcement officer should be in place at all times that rail traffic might approach or occupy the grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.13 Guidance 4 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
text:
Section 8A.13 Guidance 4 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Where traffic is detoured over an existing passive grade crossing, a temporary traffic control plan (see Section 6B.01) should be prepared.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.13 Guidance 5 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
text:
Section 8A.13 Guidance 5 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Public and private agencies, emergency services, businesses, and railroad companies or transit agencies should meet to plan appropriate traffic detours and the necessary signing, marking, signalization, and flagging requirements for operations during temporary traffic control zone activities or during the period when traffic is being detoured over an existing passive grade crossing. Consideration should be given to the length of time that the grade crossing is to be closed, the length of time that a detour is to be in place, the type of rail or LRT and highway traffic affected, the time of day, and the materials and techniques of repair.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.13 Guidance 6 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
text:
Section 8A.13 Guidance 6 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

The agencies responsible for the operation of the LRT and highway should be contacted when the initial planning begins for any temporary traffic control zone that might directly or indirectly influence the flow of traffic on facilities where LRT vehicles operate on a mixed-use alignment.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8A.13 Guidance 7 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
text:
Section 8A.13 Guidance 7 - Temporary Traffic Control Zones
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8A. General
Page: 992

Temporary traffic control operations should minimize the inconvenience, delay, and crash potential to affected traffic. Prior notice should be given to affected public or private agencies, emergency services, businesses, railroad companies or transit agencies, and road users before the free movement of road users or rail traffic is infringed upon or blocked.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.01 Support 1 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 8B.01 Support 1 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 993

Passive traffic control systems, consisting of signs and pavement markings only, identify and direct attention to the location of a grade crossing and advise road users to reduce their speed or stop at the grade crossing as necessary in order to yield to any rail traffic occupying, or approaching and in proximity to, the grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.01 Support 2 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 8B.01 Support 2 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 993

Signs and markings regulate, warn, and guide the road users so that they, as well as LRT vehicle operators on mixed-use alignments, can take appropriate action when approaching a grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.01 Support 3 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 8B.01 Support 3 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 993

Unless otherwise provided in this Chapter, the provisions of Part 2 are applicable to the design and location of signs at grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.02 Standard 1 - Sizes of Grade Crossing Signs
text:
Section 8B.02 Standard 1 - Sizes of Grade Crossing Signs
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 993

The minimum sizes of grade crossing signs shall be as shown in Table 8B-1.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.02 Option 2 - Sizes of Grade Crossing Signs
text:
Section 8B.02 Option 2 - Sizes of Grade Crossing Signs
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 993

Signs larger than those shown in Table 8B-1 may be used (see Section 2A.07).

title: Section 8B.03 Standard 1 - Grade Crossing (Crossbuck) Sign (R15-1) and Number of Tracks Plaque (R15-2P) at Active and Passive Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.03 Standard 7 - Grade Crossing (Crossbuck) Sign (R15-1) and Number of Tracks Plaque (R15-2P) at Active and Passive Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8B.03 Standard 7 - Grade Crossing (Crossbuck) Sign (R15-1) and Number of Tracks Plaque (R15-2P) at Active and Passive Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 993

On each approach to a highway-rail grade crossing and, if used, on each approach to a highway- LRT grade crossing, the Crossbuck sign shall be installed on the right-hand side of the highway on each approach to the grade crossing. Where restricted sight distance or unfavorable highway geometry exists on an approach to a grade crossing, or where there is a one-way multi-lane approach, an additional Crossbuck sign shall be installed on the left-hand side of the highway, possibly placed back-to-back with the Crossbuck sign for the opposite approach, or otherwise located so that two Crossbuck signs are displayed for that approach.

title: Section 8B.04 Standard 1 - Crossbuck Assemblies with YIELD or STOP Signs at Passive Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8B.04 Standard 1 - Crossbuck Assemblies with YIELD or STOP Signs at Passive Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 995

A Crossbuck Assembly shall consist of a Crossbuck (R15-1) sign, and a Number of Tracks (R15-2P) plaque if two or more tracks are present, that complies with the provisions of Section 8B.03, and either a YIELD (R1-2) or STOP (R1-1) sign installed on the same support, except as provided in Paragraph 10 of this Section. YIELD or STOP signs used at passive grade crossings shall be installed in compliance with the provisions of Section 2B.18, and Figures 8B-2 and 8B-3.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.04 Standard 2 - Crossbuck Assemblies with YIELD or STOP Signs at Passive Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8B.04 Standard 2 - Crossbuck Assemblies with YIELD or STOP Signs at Passive Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 995

At all public highway-rail grade crossings that are not equipped with the active traffic control systems that are described in Chapter 8D, except crossings where road users are directed by an authorized person on the ground to not enter the crossing at all times that an approaching train is about to occupy the crossing, a Crossbuck Assembly shall be installed on the right-hand side of the highway on each approach to the highway-rail grade crossing.

text:
Section 8B.04 Standard 3 - Crossbuck Assemblies with YIELD or STOP Signs at Passive Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 995

If a Crossbuck sign is used on a highway approach to a public highway-LRT grade crossing that is not equipped with the active traffic control systems that are described in Chapter 8D, a Crossbuck Assembly shall be installed on the right-hand side of the highway on each approach to the highway-LRT grade crossing.

metadata.section_title: Crossbuck Assemblies with YIELD or STOP Signs at Passive Grade Crossings
