title: Section 8B.16 Guidance 1 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Guidance 1 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

If the highway profile conditions are sufficiently abrupt to create a hang-up situation for long wheelbase vehicles or for trailers with low ground clearance, the Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing (W10-5) sign (see Figure 8B-4) should be installed in advance of the grade crossing.

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Standard 2 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Standard 2 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

Because this symbol might not be readily recognizable by the public, the Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing (W10-5) warning sign shall be accompanied by a LOW GROUND CLEARANCE (W10-5P) educational plaque. The LOW GROUND CLEARANCE educational plaque shall remain in place for at least 3 years after the initial installation of the W10-5 sign (see Section 2A.09).

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Guidance 3 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Guidance 3 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

Because other vehicle types and combinations also face the potential risk of hanging up at a grade crossing, word message warning signs and selective exclusion regulatory signs (see Section 2B.45) for specific vehicle types and combinations should be used in addition to, or in place of, the Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing (W10-5) sign.

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Support 4 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Support 4 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

While not all inclusive, some potential low ground clearance vehicles and combinations include single-unit trucks, buses, motor coaches, low-boy trailers, car carriers, and recreational vehicles.

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Guidance 5 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Guidance 5 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

Auxiliary plaques such as AHEAD, NEXT CROSSING, or USE NEXT CROSSING (with appropriate arrows), or a supplemental distance plaque should be placed below the W10-5 sign at the nearest intersecting highway where a vehicle can detour or at a point on the highway wide enough to permit a U-turn.

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Guidance 6 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Guidance 6 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

If engineering judgment of roadway geometric and operating conditions confirms that motor vehicle speeds across the tracks should be below the posted speed limit, a W13-1P advisory speed plaque should be posted.

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Guidance 7 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Guidance 7 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

A signed detour should be installed to guide potential hang-up vehicles to alternate nearby crossings to avoid the potential hang-up condition.

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Support 8 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Support 8 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

Information on ground clearance requirements at grade crossings is available in the “Communications and Signals Manual,” 2023 Edition, AREMA, or in “A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets,” 2018 Edition, AASHTO. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.16 Support 9 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
text:
Section 8B.16 Support 9 - Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

An inventory of crossings with low ground clearance concerns, including a list of potential vehicle types that could hang up on the crossing, can be useful in tracking locations of low ground clearance crossings. Specific geometric conditions, known incidents, or anecdotal evidence of vehicle hang-ups can also be used to identify crossings with low ground clearance concerns.

metadata.section_title: Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing Sign (W10-5)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.17 Support 1 - Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
text:
Section 8B.17 Support 1 - Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

The Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out (W10-7) warning sign (see Figure 8B-4) supplements the traffic control devices to warn road users crossing the tracks of approaching LRT equipment.

metadata.section_title: Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.17 Option 2 - Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
text:
Section 8B.17 Option 2 - Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

A Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out warning sign may be used at signalized intersections near highway-LRT grade crossings or at crossings controlled by STOP signs or automatic gates.

metadata.section_title: Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.17 Support 3 - Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
text:
Section 8B.17 Support 3 - Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1005

The provisions contained in Chapter 2L for blank-out signs are applicable to the W10-7 sign.

metadata.section_title: Light Rail Transit Approaching-Activated Blank-Out Warning Sign (W10-7)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.18 Support 1 - Another Train Coming Sign (W10-16)
text:
Section 8B.18 Support 1 - Another Train Coming Sign (W10-16)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

Conflicts between vehicles or vulnerable road users and multiple trains can occur at multi-track crossings on sidewalks, pathways, and at crossings in station areas where grade crossing users might not consider the arrival of another train on a different track. Month 2023 December 2025

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.18 Guidance 2 - Another Train Coming Sign (W10-16)
text:
Section 8B.18 Guidance 2 - Another Train Coming Sign (W10-16)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

The decision to provide notification of another train should be made by a Diagnostic Team. In making this determination, the Diagnostic Team should consider the pedestrian usage, pedestrian collision history, train speeds and volumes, operating plans and/or schedules, and the presence of a nearby station or transit center.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.18 Option 3 - Another Train Coming Sign (W10-16)
text:
Section 8B.18 Option 3 - Another Train Coming Sign (W10-16)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

An ANOTHER TRAIN COMING (W10-16) train-activated blank-out sign (see Figure 8B-4) may be used to provide notification of another train coming. For added sign conspicuity, a Warning Beacon may be used in accordance with the requirements of Section 4S.03.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.19 Guidance 1 - TRAINS MAY EXCEED 80 MPH Sign (W10-8)
text:
Section 8B.19 Guidance 1 - TRAINS MAY EXCEED 80 MPH Sign (W10-8)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

Where trains are permitted to travel at speeds exceeding 80 mph, a TRAINS MAY EXCEED 80 MPH (W10-8) sign (see Figure 8B-4) should be installed facing road users approaching the highway-rail grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.19 Guidance 2 - TRAINS MAY EXCEED 80 MPH Sign (W10-8)
text:
Section 8B.19 Guidance 2 - TRAINS MAY EXCEED 80 MPH Sign (W10-8)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

If used, the TRAINS MAY EXCEED 80 MPH signs should be installed between the Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1 through W10-4) sign (see Figure 8B-4) and the highway-rail grade crossing on all approaches to the highway-rail grade crossing. The locations should be determined based on specific site conditions.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.20 Standard 1 - NO TRAIN HORN Sign or Plaque (W10-9 and W10-9P)
text:
Section 8B.20 Standard 1 - NO TRAIN HORN Sign or Plaque (W10-9 and W10-9P)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

Either a NO TRAIN HORN (W10-9) sign (see Figure 8B-4) or a NO TRAIN HORN (W10-9P) plaque (see Figure 8B-4) shall be installed in each direction at each highway-rail grade crossing where a Quiet Zone has been established in compliance with 49 CFR Part 222. If a W10-9P plaque is used, it shall supplement and be mounted directly below the Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1 through W10-4) sign (see Figure 8B-4).

metadata.section_title: NO TRAIN HORN Sign or Plaque (W10-9 and W10-9P)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.21 Guidance 1 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
text:
Section 8B.21 Guidance 1 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

A Storage Space (W10-11) sign supplemented by a word message Storage Space Ahead (W10-11a) sign (see Figure 8B-4) should be used where there is a highway intersection in close proximity to the grade crossing and the Diagnostic Team determines that adequate space is not available to store a design vehicle(s) between the highway intersection and the train or LRT equipment dynamic envelope.

metadata.section_title: Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.21 Guidance 2 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
text:
Section 8B.21 Guidance 2 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

The Storage Space (W10-11 and W10-11a) signs should be mounted in advance of the grade crossing at an appropriate location to advise drivers of the space available for motor vehicle storage between the highway intersection and the grade crossing.

metadata.section_title: Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.21 Option 3 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
text:
Section 8B.21 Option 3 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

A word message Storage Space Behind (W10-11b) sign (see Figure 8B-4) may be mounted beyond the grade crossing at the highway intersection under the STOP or YIELD sign or just prior to the signalized intersection to remind drivers of the storage space between the tracks and the highway intersection.

metadata.section_title: Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.21 Standard 4 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
text:
Section 8B.21 Standard 4 - Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

A Storage Space (W10-11) sign shall not be used as a replacement for the required Advance Warning (W10-1) sign. If used, the Storage Space sign shall be used in addition to the W10-1 sign and shall be mounted on a separate post.

metadata.section_title: Storage Space Signs (W10-11, W10-11a, and W10-11b)
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.22 Option 1 - Skewed Crossing Sign (W10-12)
text:
Section 8B.22 Option 1 - Skewed Crossing Sign (W10-12)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

The Skewed Crossing (W10-12) sign (see Figure 8B-4) may be used at a skewed grade crossing to warn road users that the tracks are not perpendicular to the highway.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.22 Guidance 2 - Skewed Crossing Sign (W10-12)
text:
Section 8B.22 Guidance 2 - Skewed Crossing Sign (W10-12)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1006

If the Skewed Crossing sign is used, the symbol should show the direction of the crossing (near left to far right as shown on the sign image in Figure 8B-4, or the mirror image if the track goes from far left to near right).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.22 Standard 3 - Skewed Crossing Sign (W10-12)
text:
Section 8B.22 Standard 3 - Skewed Crossing Sign (W10-12)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

The Skewed Crossing sign shall not be used as a replacement for the required Advance Warning (W10-1) sign. If used, the Skewed Crossing sign shall be used in addition to the W10-1 sign and shall be mounted on a separate post. Month 2023

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.23 Option 1 - NO GATES OR LIGHTS Plaque (W10-13P)
text:
Section 8B.23 Option 1 - NO GATES OR LIGHTS Plaque (W10-13P)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

The NO GATES OR LIGHTS (W10-13P) plaque (see Figure 8B-4) may be mounted below the Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1 through W10-4) sign at grade crossings that are not equipped with automatic gates or automated signals.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.24 Option 1 - Next Crossing Plaques (W10-14P and W10-14aP)
text:
Section 8B.24 Option 1 - Next Crossing Plaques (W10-14P and W10-14aP)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

The NEXT CROSSING (W10-14P) plaque (see Figure 8B-4) may be mounted below the Low Ground Clearance (W10-5) sign (see Section 8B.16) or Skewed Crossing (W10-12) sign to indicate to a road user that the warning is associated with the next grade crossing. This plaque may be used where multiple grade crossings exist in close proximity to one another.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.24 Option 2 - Next Crossing Plaques (W10-14P and W10-14aP)
text:
Section 8B.24 Option 2 - Next Crossing Plaques (W10-14P and W10-14aP)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

Where recommended by a Diagnostic Team, the USE NEXT CROSSING (W10-14aP) plaque (see Figure 8B-4) may be mounted below the Low Ground Clearance (W10-5) sign (see Section 8B.16) to advise a road user with a low clearance load to use the crossing after the upcoming crossing to avoid encountering a low ground clearance situation.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.25 Option 1 - ROUGH CROSSING Plaque (W10-15P)
text:
Section 8B.25 Option 1 - ROUGH CROSSING Plaque (W10-15P)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

The ROUGH CROSSING (W10-15P) plaque (see Figure 8B-4) may be mounted below the Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1 through W10-4) sign on the approach to a grade crossing to provide supplemental information that the surface or condition of the grade crossing might require a reduced speed or some other appropriate action by the road user.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.25 Option 2 - ROUGH CROSSING Plaque (W10-15P)
text:
Section 8B.25 Option 2 - ROUGH CROSSING Plaque (W10-15P)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

If the grade crossing is rough, word message signs such as BUMP, DIP, or ROUGH CROSSING may be installed. A W13-1P advisory speed plaque may be installed below the word message sign in advance of rough crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.26 Option 1 - Light Rail Transit Station Sign (I3-8)
text:
Section 8B.26 Option 1 - Light Rail Transit Station Sign (I3-8)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

The Light Rail Transit Station (I3-8) sign (see Section 2H.01) may be used to direct road users to an LRT station or boarding location. It may be supplemented by the name of the transit system and by arrows as provided in Section 2D.08.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Standard 1 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Standard 1 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

The Emergency Notification System (I13-1) sign (see Figure 8B-5) shall be installed on each approach at all highway-rail grade crossings, and at all highway-LRT grade crossings with automatic gates or flashing light-signals, to provide information to road users so that they can notify the railroad company or transit agency about emergencies or malfunctioning traffic control devices.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Standard 2 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Standard 2 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

At a highway-rail grade crossing, the Emergency Notification System sign shall, at a minimum, include the USDOT grade crossing inventory number and the emergency contact telephone number.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Standard 3 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Standard 3 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

Where Emergency Notification System signs are used at a highway-LRT grade crossing, they shall, at a minimum, include a unique crossing identifier and the emergency contact telephone number. Figure 8B-5. Example of an Emergency Notification System Sign

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Standard 4 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Standard 4 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

The minimum width of the Emergency Notification System sign shall be 12 inches and the minimum height shall be 9 inches. The lettering on Emergency Notification System signs for the telephone number, the grade crossing inventory number, and the explanation of the purpose of the sign shall be composed of numerals and upper-case letters that are at least 1 inch in height.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Standard 5 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Standard 5 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1007

Emergency Notification System signs shall be retroreflective.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Standard 6 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Standard 6 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

Except as provided in Paragraph 7 of this Section, Emergency Notification System signs shall have a white legend and border on a blue background. Month 2023

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Option 7 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Option 7 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

The seven-character grade crossing inventory number may be shown on the sign as a black legend on a white rectangular background.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Guidance 8 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Guidance 8 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

Except as provided in Paragraph 12 of this Section, Emergency Notification System signs should be attached to the Crossbuck Assemblies or grade crossing signal masts on the right-hand side of each roadway approach to the grade crossing rather than on the railroad or LRT signal control equipment housings. Emergency Notification System signs should be oriented so the face of the sign is approximately parallel or approximately perpendicular to the edge of the roadway or pathway and is visible to road users or pathway users. The visibility of the Emergency Notification System sign should not be obstructed by automatic gates in either the vertical or horizontal position.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Guidance 9 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Guidance 9 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

The Emergency Notification System signs should be positioned so as to not obstruct any traffic control devices or limit the view of rail traffic approaching the grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Guidance 10 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Guidance 10 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

Emergency Notification System signs mounted on Crossbuck Assemblies or signal masts should only be large enough to provide the necessary contact information. Use of larger signs on Crossbuck Assemblies or signal masts that might obstruct the view of rail traffic or other motor vehicles should be avoided.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Guidance 11 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Guidance 11 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

At station crossings, Emergency Notification System signs or information should be posted in a conspicuous location.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Option 12 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Option 12 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

Emergency Notification System signs may be located on a separate post. Where located on a separate post, the size of the Emergency Notification System sign may be increased for improved visibility.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Option 13 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Option 13 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1008

Where the improvement of the conspicuity of an Emergency Notification System sign is desired, a solid yellow rectangular header panel with a legend of “NOTICE” in black letters may be used (see Section 2A.11).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8B.27 Option 14 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
text:
Section 8B.27 Option 14 - Emergency Notification System Sign (I13-1)
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8B. Signs
Page: 1009

Additional Emergency Notification System signs may be installed at a grade crossing. Month 2023

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.01 Support 1 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 8C.01 Support 1 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Passive traffic control systems, consisting of signs and pavement markings only, identify and direct attention to the location of a grade crossing and advise road users to reduce their speed or stop at the grade crossing as necessary in order to yield to any rail traffic occupying, or approaching and in proximity to, the grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.01 Support 2 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 8C.01 Support 2 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Signs and pavement markings regulate, warn, and guide the road users so that they, as well as LRT vehicle operators on mixed-use alignments, can take appropriate action when approaching a grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.01 Support 3 - Purpose and Application
text:
Section 8C.01 Support 3 - Purpose and Application
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Unless otherwise provided in this Chapter, the provisions of Part 3 are applicable to the design and location of pavement markings at grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Standard 1 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Standard 1 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

On paved roadways, grade crossing pavement markings shall consist of an X, the letters RR, a no- passing zone marking (on two-lane, two-way highways with center line markings in compliance with Section 3B.01), and certain transverse lines as shown with detailed dimensions in Figures 8C-1 and 8C-2.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Standard 2 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Standard 2 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Except as provided in Paragraphs 3 and 4 of this Section, grade crossing pavement markings shall be placed in each approach lane on all paved approaches to highway-rail grade crossings where signals or automatic gates are located, and at all other grade crossings where the posted or statutory highway speed is 40 mph or higher.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Standard 3 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Standard 3 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Grade crossing pavement markings shall not be required at highway-rail grade crossings where the posted or statutory highway speed is less than 40 mph if the Diagnostic Team determines that other installed devices provide suitable warning and control.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Standard 4 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Standard 4 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Grade crossing pavement markings shall not be required at highway-rail grade crossings in urban areas if the Diagnostic Team determines that other installed devices provide suitable warning and control.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Standard 5 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Standard 5 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Grade crossing pavement markings shall be placed in each approach lane on all paved approaches to highway-LRT grade crossings where a Crossbuck sign is placed at the grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Standard 6 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Standard 6 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

If grade crossing pavement markings are used on a multi-lane approach to a grade crossing, identical markings shall be placed in each approach lane that crosses the tracks.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Standard 7 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Standard 7 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

All grade crossing pavement markings shall be retroreflective white. All other markings shall be in accordance with Part 3.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Guidance 8 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Guidance 8 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Where grade crossing pavement markings are used, a portion of the X symbol should be directly opposite the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Option 9 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Option 9 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

Where determined by the Diagnostic Team, supplemental pavement marking symbol(s) may be placed between the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign and the grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.02 Guidance 10 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.02 Guidance 10 - Grade Crossing Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

If supplemental pavement marking symbol(s) are placed between the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign and the grade crossing, the downstream transverse line should be at least 50 feet upstream from the stop or yield line at the grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.03 Guidance 1 - Stop and Yield Lines
text:
Section 8C.03 Guidance 1 - Stop and Yield Lines
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1009

On paved roadway approaches to passive grade crossings where a STOP sign is installed in conjunction with the Crossbuck sign, a stop line should be installed to indicate the point behind which motor vehicles are required to stop or as near to that point as practicable.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.03 Option 2 - Stop and Yield Lines
text:
Section 8C.03 Option 2 - Stop and Yield Lines
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

On paved roadway approaches to passive grade crossings where a YIELD sign is installed in conjunction with the Crossbuck sign, a yield line (see Section 3B.19) or a stop line may be installed to indicate the point behind which motor vehicles are required to yield or stop or as near to that point as practicable. Month 2023 Figure 8C-1. Example of Placement of Warning Signs and Pavement Markings at Grade Crossings * When used, a portion of the pavement marking symbol should be directly opposite the Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1) sign. If needed, supplemental pavement marking symbol(s) may be placed between the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign and the grade crossing, but should be at least 50 feet from the stop or yield line. Note: In an effort to simplify the figure to show warning sign and pavement marking placement, not all required traffic control devices are shown. Month 2023 Figure 8C-2. Grade Crossing Pavement Markings A - Grade crossing pavement marking symbol B - Grade crossing alternative (narrow) pavement marking symbol Note: Refer to Figure 8C-1 for placement Month 2023

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.03 Guidance 3 - Stop and Yield Lines
text:
Section 8C.03 Guidance 3 - Stop and Yield Lines
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

If a yield line (see Figure 3B-16) or stop line is used at a passive grade crossing, it should be a transverse line at a right angle to the traveled way and should be placed no closer than 15 feet in advance of the nearest rail.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.03 Standard 4 - Stop and Yield Lines
text:
Section 8C.03 Standard 4 - Stop and Yield Lines
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

On paved roadways at grade crossings that are equipped with active control devices such as flashing- light signals, automatic gates, or traffic control signals, a stop line (see Section 3B.19) shall be installed to indicate the point behind which motor vehicles are or might be required to stop.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.03 Guidance 5 - Stop and Yield Lines
text:
Section 8C.03 Guidance 5 - Stop and Yield Lines
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

If a stop line is used at an active grade crossing where road users are controlled by flashing-light signals, it should be a transverse line at a right angle to the traveled way and should be placed approximately 8 feet in advance of the flashing-light signals or automatic gate (if present), whichever is farther from the track(s), but no closer than 15 feet in advance of the nearest rail (see Figure 8C-1).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.03 Guidance 6 - Stop and Yield Lines
text:
Section 8C.03 Guidance 6 - Stop and Yield Lines
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

If a stop line is used at an active grade crossing where road users are controlled by a traffic control signal, it should be a transverse line at a right angle to the traveled way and should be placed no closer than 15 feet in advance of the nearest rail.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.03 Standard 7 - Stop and Yield Lines
text:
Section 8C.03 Standard 7 - Stop and Yield Lines
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

If a stop line is used at an active grade crossing where road users are controlled by a traffic control signal, it shall be placed such that the lateral and longitudinal positions of the signal faces for the approach comply with the provisions of Sections 4D.07 and 4D.08.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.04 Standard 1 - Lane-Use Arrow Markings
text:
Section 8C.04 Standard 1 - Lane-Use Arrow Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

Lane-use arrow markings (see Section 3B.23) that indicate that a turning movement must be made or is permitted to be made from a lane that crosses a grade crossing shall not be placed between the stop line for the grade crossing and the track(s).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.04 Guidance 2 - Lane-Use Arrow Markings
text:
Section 8C.04 Guidance 2 - Lane-Use Arrow Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1012

Lane-use arrow markings that indicate that a turning movement must be made or is permitted to be made from a lane that crosses a grade crossing should not be placed less than 100 feet upstream from the stop line for the grade crossing or less than 20 feet beyond the farthest rail.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.06 Option 1 - Dynamic Envelope and Do Not Block Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.06 Option 1 - Dynamic Envelope and Do Not Block Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1013

Dynamic envelope markings may be installed at a grade crossing to mark the edges of the train dynamic envelope.

metadata.section_title: Dynamic Envelope and Do Not Block Pavement Markings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8C.06 Standard 2 - Dynamic Envelope and Do Not Block Pavement Markings
text:
Section 8C.06 Standard 2 - Dynamic Envelope and Do Not Block Pavement Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8C. Markings
Page: 1013

If used, pavement markings for indicating the dynamic envelope shall comply with the provisions of

metadata.section_title: Dynamic Envelope and Do Not Block Pavement Markings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

title: Section 8D.01 Support 1 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Support 1 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Active traffic control systems inform road users of the approach or presence of rail traffic at grade crossings. These systems include Exit Gate systems, automatic gates, flashing-light signals, traffic control signals, actuated blank-out and variable message signs, and other active traffic control devices that are used in conjunction with the signs and pavement markings that are described in Chapters 8B and 8C, respectively.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Support 2 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Support 2 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Figure 8D-1 shows a post-mounted flashing-light signal (two light units mounted in a horizontal line), a flashing-light signal mounted on an overhead structure, and an automatic gate assembly.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Support 3 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Support 3 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Where LRT speed is cited in this Part, it refers to the maximum speed at which LRT equipment is permitted to traverse a particular grade crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Option 4 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Option 4 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Post-mounted and overhead flashing-light signals may be used separately or in combination with each other as determined by the Diagnostic Team. Also, flashing-light signals may be used without automatic gate assemblies, as determined by the Diagnostic Team.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Standard 5 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Standard 5 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

The meaning of flashing-light signals and automatic gates shall be as stated in Sections 11-701 and 11-703 of the Uniform Vehicle Code (see Section 1A.06).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Standard 6 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Standard 6 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Location for flashing-light signals and automatic gates shall be as shown in Figure 8D-1.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Standard 7 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Standard 7 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Where there is a curb, a horizontal offset of at least 2 feet shall be provided from the face of the vertical curb to the nearest part of the signal or automatic gate arm in its upright position. Where a cantilevered- arm flashing-light signal is used, the vertical clearance shall be at least 17 feet above the crown of the highway to the lowest point of the signal unit.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Standard 8 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Standard 8 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Where there is a shoulder, but no curb, a horizontal offset of at least 2 feet from the edge of a paved shoulder shall be provided, with an offset of at least 6 feet from the edge of the traveled way.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Standard 9 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Standard 9 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Where there is no curb or shoulder, the minimum horizontal offset shall be 6 feet from the edge of the traveled way.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Standard 10 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Standard 10 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Minimum clearance dimensions for flashing-light signals and automatic gates relative to the closest track shall conform to standards provided by the railroad company and/or transit agency, and the regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable).

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Guidance 11 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Guidance 11 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Equipment housings (controller cabinets) should have a lateral offset of at least 30 feet from the edge of the highway, and where railroad or LRT property and conditions allow, at least 25 feet from the nearest rail.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Guidance 12 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Guidance 12 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

If a pedestrian route is provided, sufficient clearance from supports, posts, and automatic gate mechanisms should be maintained for pedestrian travel.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Guidance 13 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Guidance 13 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Where determined by the Diagnostic Team, a lateral escape route to the right-hand side of the highway in advance of the grade crossing traffic control devices should be kept free of guardrail or other ground obstructions. Where guardrail is not deemed necessary or appropriate, barriers should not be used for protecting signal supports.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Guidance 14 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Guidance 14 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

The same lateral offset and roadside safety features should apply to flashing-light signal and automatic gate locations on both the right-hand and left-hand sides of the roadway.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Option 15 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Option 15 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

In industrial or other areas involving only low-speed highway traffic or where signals are vulnerable to damage by turning truck traffic, guardrail may be installed to provide protection for the signal assembly.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Guidance 16 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Guidance 16 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1016

Where both traffic control signals and flashing-light signals (with or without automatic gates) are in operation at the same highway-LRT grade crossing, the operation of the devices should be coordinated to avoid any display of conflicting signal indications.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.01 Option 17 - Introduction
text:
Section 8D.01 Option 17 - Introduction
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1018

If highway traffic signals must be located within close proximity to the flashing-light signals, the highway traffic signals may be mounted on the same overhead structure as the flashing-light signals. Month 2023 Figure 8D-1. Composite Drawing of Active Traffic Control Devices for Grade Crossings Showing Clearances *For locating this reference line on an approach that does not have a curb, see Section 8D.01. Notes: 1. Where gates are located in the median, additional median width may be required to provide the minimum clearance for the counterweight supports. 2. The top of the signal foundation should be no more than 4 inches above the surface of the ground and should be at the same elevation as the crown of the roadway. Where site conditions would not allow this to be achieved, the shoulder side slope should be re-graded or the height of the signal post should be adjusted to meet the 17-foot vertical clearance requirement. Month 2023

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.03 Support 1 - Automatic Gates
text:
Section 8D.03 Support 1 - Automatic Gates
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1019

An automatic gate is a traffic control device used in conjunction with flashing-light signals.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.03 Standard 2 - Automatic Gates
text:
Section 8D.03 Standard 2 - Automatic Gates

title: Section 8D.03 Standard 3 - Automatic Gates
text:
Section 8D.03 Standard 3 - Automatic Gates
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1019

In the normal sequence of operation, unless constant warning time detection or other advanced system requires otherwise, the flashing-light signals and the lights on the gate arm (in its normal upright position) shall be activated immediately upon detection of approaching rail traffic. The gate arm shall start its downward motion not less than 3 seconds after the flashing-light signals start to operate, shall reach its horizontal position at least 5 seconds before the arrival of the rail traffic, and shall remain in the down position until the rail traffic completely clears the grade crossing.

The width (which becomes the height of the retroreflective sheeting when the automatic gate is in the down position) of the retroreflective sheeting on the front of the gate arm shall be at least 4 inches for the first 32 feet of gate arm length measured from the center of the gate mast. The front of the gate arm beyond 32 feet to the tip of the gate arm shall have retroreflective sheeting at least 2 inches in width.

Page: 1021

In the normal sequence of operation, unless constant warning time detection or other advanced system requires otherwise, the flashing-light signals and the lights on the gate arms (in their normal upright positions) shall be activated immediately upon the detection of approaching rail traffic. The entrance gate arms shall start their downward motion not less than 3 seconds after the flashing-light signals start to operate and shall reach their horizontal position at least 5 seconds before the arrival of the rail traffic. Exit gate arm activation and downward motion shall be based on detection or timing requirements established by a Diagnostic Team. If an Exit Gate system is present, the exit gate clearance time (see AREMA Manual) shall be long enough to permit the exit gate arm to lower after a design vehicle of maximum length is clear of the minimum track clearance distance (see Section 8A.07). The gate arms shall remain in the down position as long as the rail traffic occupies the grade crossing. Rev. 1

title: Section 8D.09 Support 1 - Preemption of Highway Traffic Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8D.09 Support 1 - Preemption of Highway Traffic Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1024

Traffic signal preemption for grade crossings is a complex topic that requires a specific understanding of grade crossing warning systems and highway traffic signal operations. While most traffic signal operations are governed only by the traffic signal controller unit and the associated traffic signal equipment, preemption for grade crossings is also governed by the grade crossing warning system. Active grade crossing warning systems include flashing- light signals and possibly automatic gates, as well as various types of train detection equipment. Where the traffic signal controller unit is interconnected with the grade crossing warning system for the purpose of preemption, a combined system is created. It is the combined system that requires a thorough understanding of the design and operating parameters in order to provide proper operation of the preemption system.

The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) has issued two documents that provide additional information relating to preemption of highway traffic signals at or near grade crossings. The first document is “Technical Bulletin S-12-01, Guidance Regarding the Appropriate Process for the Inspection of Highway-Rail Grade Crossing Warning System Pre-emption Interconnections with Highway Traffic Signals” and the second document is “Safety Advisory 2010-02, Signal Recording Devices for Highway-Rail Grade Crossing Active Warning Systems that are Interconnected with Highway Traffic Signal Systems.”

Coordination with the flashing-light signals, such as using queue detection and queue cutter signals, blank- out signs, or other alternatives, should be considered where a traffic control signal, a pedestrian hybrid beacon, or an emergency-vehicle hybrid beacon is located more than 200 feet from the grade crossing. Factors to be considered should include traffic volumes, highway vehicle mix, highway vehicle and train approach speeds, frequency of trains, presence of midblock driveways or unsignalized intersections, and the potential for vehicular queues resulting from an adjacent downstream grade crossing or highway traffic signal to extend into the minimum track clearance distance (see Section 8A.07).

At a signalized intersection that is located within 100 feet of a grade crossing and the intersection traffic control signals are preempted by the approach of rail traffic, all existing permissive-only turning movements toward the grade crossing should be prohibited, steady red arrow signal indications should be shown to all existing protected/permissive and protected-only turning movements toward the grade crossing, and red signal indications should be shown to the straight-through movement toward the grade crossing during the signal preemption sequences. The pre-signal phase sequencing may be timed with an offset from the downstream signalized intersection such that the pre-signal’s green signal indication terminates prior to the downstream intersection’s green signal indication to minimize the possibility of stopping motor vehicles within the minimum track clearance distance (see Section 8A.07) and the clear storage distance .

In such cases, drivers that are in the turn lane are required to make a straight-through movement when they cross the track(s) and then are required to make a turning movement when they reach the downstream signalized intersection. The storage area for the turn lane extends from the downstream signalized intersection back to and across the grade crossing, and B. The green interval for the turning movement at the downstream intersection does not always begin and end simultaneously with the green interval for the adjacent through movement at the downstream intersection.

Shall be visibility-limited from the adjacent through movement, or B. A LEFT (RIGHT) LANE SIGNAL (R10-10b) sign (see Figure 8B-1) shall be mounted adjacent to the separate signal face controlling traffic in a single turn lane or in the turn lane that is farthest from the adjacent through lane(s) if multiple turn lanes are present for a particular turning movement, and a LEFT (RIGHT) TURN LANE SIGNAL (R10-10c) sign (see Figure 8B-1) shall be mounted adjacent to the separate signal face controlling traffic in the other turn lanes if multiple turn lanes are present for a particular turning movement.

This means that the provisions in Sections 4D.05 through 4D.08 regarding the number of signal faces, the visibility and aiming of the signal faces, and the lateral and longitudinal positioning of the signal faces apply separately to the approach to the pre-signal.

title: Section 8D.12 Support 1 - Queue Cutter Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8D.12 Support 1 - Queue Cutter Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1030

A queue cutter signal is a traffic control signal that controls one direction of traffic at a grade crossing to minimize the possibility of vehicles stopping within the minimum track clearance distance (see Section 8A.07). Although a queue cutter signal has a similar purpose as a pre-signal (see Section 8D.11), the difference is that a queue cutter signal is independent from the downstream signalized intersection, whereas a pre-signal is part of the downstream signal.

Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1030

At grade crossing locations where the queue from a bottleneck (usually a signalized intersection) that is downstream from the grade crossing frequently extends back to and across the grade crossing, a queue cutter signal may be installed.

text:

Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1030

A queue cutter signal may be operated in one of the following modes: A. Actuated mode - the queue cutter signal operation is dependent on downstream detection of a growing queue. B. Non-actuated mode - the queue cutter signal operates on a time-of-day plan based on anticipated downstream queues. This mode could be similar to the functional operation of a pre-signal. C. Variable mode - the queue cutter signal operation varies between the actuated mode and the non-actuated mode based on the time of day, on queue detection, or both.

A non-actuated queue cutter signal is generally used where the grade crossing is located between 200 feet and 400 feet from a downstream bottleneck. An actuated queue cutter signal is generally used where the grade crossing is located more than 400 feet from a downstream bottleneck. Section 8D.11 contains information for grade crossings located less than 200 feet from a downstream signalized intersection.

Where a queue cutter signal operates in an actuated mode based on vehicle presence detection, the queue detector should be located to provide adequate distance to detect a growing queue, permit the queue cutter signal to complete any programmed minimum green or yellow change interval time, and then allow a design vehicle that lawfully crosses the queue cutter signal’s stop line during the yellow change interval to clear the minimum track clearance distance (see Section 8A.07) before the growing queue extends to the grade crossing.

A queue cutter signal that is operating in an actuated mode and that is displaying CIRCULAR RED signal indications should continue to display CIRCULAR RED signal indications as long as the downstream detection system continues to detect the presence of a vehicular queue at the detection point on the departure side of the grade crossing.

Where a queue cutter signal operates in actuated mode based on vehicle presence detection, consideration should be given to the potential for turning movements between the grade crossing and the downstream bottleneck that could create an intermediate queue of vehicles. Supplemental queue detectors should be considered to detect the formation of these intermediate queues to activate the queue cutter signal.

title: Section 8D.12 Standard 19 - Queue Cutter Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8D.12 Standard 19 - Queue Cutter Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1031

When a queue cutter signal that is displaying straight-through GREEN ARROW signal indications (when operating in a steady, stop-and-go mode) or flashing CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indications (when operating in a programmed flashing mode) is preempted by the approach of rail traffic, it shall immediately display steady CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indications during the yellow change interval (see Section 4F.17) followed by steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications. The queue cutter signal shall continue to display the steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications until the rail traffic clears the grade crossing and no other rail traffic is detected.

metadata.section_title: Queue Cutter Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

title: Section 8D.12 Standard 20 - Queue Cutter Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
text:
Section 8D.12 Standard 20 - Queue Cutter Signals at or Near Grade Crossings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals
Page: 1031

A queue cutter signal operating in an actuated mode shall display straight-through GREEN ARROW signal indications except when it receives an actuation from the downstream vehicle presence detection system or is preempted by the approach of rail traffic. When it receives an actuation from the vehicle presence detection system, the queue cutter signal shall finish timing any active minimum green interval, if used, and then display steady CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indications during the yellow change interval (see Section 4F.17) followed by steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications. When no preemption call is present and the queue length is such that no vehicles are detected in the detection zone of the downstream vehicle presence detection system, the queue cutter signal shall finish timing any active minimum red interval, if used, and then return to the display of straight-through GREEN ARROW signal indications.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

text:

Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8D. Flashing-Light Signals, Automatic Gates, And Traffic Control Signals

The failure modes of the queue cutter signal control system and vehicle presence detection circuitry shall be evaluated and accounted for in the design of any such system. Fail-safe design techniques shall be used in the system design. If a queue detector fails, the queue cutter signal shall display flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications until the normal functioning of the detection system is restored.

The storage area for mandatory left-turn and right-turn lanes at signalized intersections that are downstream from grade crossings sometimes extends from the signalized intersection back to and across the grade crossing. In such cases, drivers that are in the turn lane are required to make a straight-through movement when they cross the track(s) and then are required to make a turning movement when they reach the downstream signalized intersection.

A separate queue cutter signal face for the mandatory left-turn lane and/or right-turn lane should be provided in addition to the queue cutter signal faces provided for the through movement where both of the following conditions are met: A. The storage area for the turn lane extends from the downstream signalized intersection back to and across the grade crossing, and B. The green interval for the turning movement at the downstream intersection does not always begin and end simultaneously with the green interval for the adjacent through movement at the downstream intersection.

If a separate signal face is provided at a queue cutter signal for separate control of a mandatory left- turn and/or right-turn lane that extends from the downstream signalized intersection back to and across the grade crossing, the separate signal face shall be devoted exclusively to controlling traffic in the turn lane separately from adjacent lanes, and: A. Shall be visibility-limited from the adjacent through movement, or B. A LEFT (RIGHT) LANE SIGNAL (R10-10b) sign (see Figure 8B-1) shall be mounted adjacent to the separate signal face controlling traffic in a single turn lane or in the turn lane that is farthest from the adjacent through lane(s) if multiple turn lanes are present for a particular turning movement, and a LEFT (RIGHT) TURN LANE SIGNAL (R10-10c) sign (see Figure 8B-1) shall be mounted adjacent to the separate signal face controlling traffic in the other turn lanes if multiple turn lanes are present for a particular turning movement. This means that the provisions in Sections 4D.05 through 4D.08 regarding the number of signal faces, the visibility and aiming of the signal faces, and the lateral and longitudinal positioning of the signal faces apply separately to the approach to the queue cutter signal.

Most of the warning signs that are used at or on an approach to a grade crossing warn of physical conditions that exist at the grade crossing regardless of whether rail traffic is approaching or occupying the grade crossing. In these cases, a Warning Beacon or LED-enhanced sign would typically be operated continuously to enhance the conspicuity of the sign.

Some warning signs, such as a BE PREPARED TO STOP (W3-4) sign (see Section 2C.35), if used in advance of a grade crossing and supplemented with a WHEN FLASHING (W16-13P) plaque, provide information that is typically not applicable except when rail traffic is approaching or occupying the grade crossing. Likewise, a special word message sign (see Section 2A.04) with a legend such as TRAIN WHEN FLASHING provides notice of a condition that only exists when rail traffic is approaching or occupying the grade crossing. These signs would not typically be operated continuously, but instead only when the condition is present.

title: Section 8E.01 Support 4 - Purpose
text:
Section 8E.01 Support 4 - Purpose
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1035

Figure 8E-1 illustrates the difference between a pathway grade crossing and a sidewalk grade crossing. A pathway is frequently placed in its own right-of-way on an alignment that is independent of any roadway. If a pathway is built parallel to a roadway, it is physically separated from the roadway by an open space or barrier such that the traffic control devices for the roadway grade crossing do not exert an influence over or provide adequate warning to pathway users. A sidewalk runs parallel to a roadway within the highway right-of-way and is close enough to the edge of the roadway’s traveled way that the traffic control devices for the roadway grade crossing can frequently exert an influence over or provide adequate warning to sidewalk users. Pathways are typically used by both pedestrians and bicyclists, whereas sidewalks are typically used only by pedestrians.

Page: 1035

The pathway or sidewalk user’s ability to detect the presence of approaching rail traffic should be considered in determining the type and placement of traffic control devices at pathway or sidewalk grade crossings.

Page: 1035

The traffic control devices, including the appropriate traffic control system to be used, and other physical treatments at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing should be determined by a Diagnostic Team that includes the agency with jurisdiction over the pathway or sidewalk.

Page: 1035

At skewed grade crossings, the adjustment, re-alignment, or relocation of existing sidewalk grade crossings should be considered when determining the placement of traffic control devices for roadway users.

title: Section 8E.02 Support 4 - Use of Standard Devices, Systems, and Practices
text:
Section 8E.02 Support 4 - Use of Standard Devices, Systems, and Practices
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1036

The safety of pathway and sidewalk users is enhanced when pathways and sidewalks are designed such that they do not cross the tracks at a narrow angle. The casters of wheelchairs and the wheels of bicycles could fall into and might be constrained in the flangeway gap at a skewed crossing. The flangeway gap is typically 2.5 inches wide at LRT grade crossings and 3 inches wide at railroad grade crossings. Figure 8E-1. Illustration of the Difference between a Pathway Grade Crossing and a Sidewalk Grade Crossing A - Pathway grade crossing B - Sidewalk grade crossing Month 2023

title: Section 8E.02 Support 5 - Use of Standard Devices, Systems, and Practices
text:
Section 8E.02 Support 5 - Use of Standard Devices, Systems, and Practices
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1036

It is desirable that pathways and sidewalks be designed such that they maintain a relatively consistent horizontal alignment and profile from the nearest rail to the detectable warning (if present) or from the nearest rail to the stop line (if present) on each approach to the crossing. Providing a pedestrian refuge area in advance of the stop line or the detectable warning surface so that pedestrians have a place to wait while rail traffic approaches and occupies the crossing can be beneficial to pedestrian safety.

Page: 1036

When designing new sidewalk grade crossings, placing the sidewalk outside of the area occupied by grade crossing traffic control devices for vehicular traffic is desirable (see Figure 8E-2). This includes making sure that the counterweights and support arms for the automatic gates for vehicular traffic do not obstruct the sidewalk when the gate is fully lowered. Figure 8E-2. Additional information regarding the design of pathways and sidewalks is contained in the U.S. Department of Justice 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, September 15, 2010, 28 CFR 35 and 36, Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Notes: The dimension “a” is the distance from the edge of the sidewalk grade crossing to the center of the traffic control warning devices at the grade crossing. If a ≤ 25 feet, flashing-light signals may be omitted at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing (see Section 8E.07).

The minimum sizes of sidewalk grade crossing signs that are intended to be viewed only by sidewalk users and of pathway grade crossing signs shall be as shown in the shared-use path column in Table 9A-1.

text:
Section 8E.03 Guidance 3 - Pathway and Sidewalk Grade Crossing Signs and Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1036

No portion of a traffic control device or its support should protrude into the pathway or sidewalk grade crossing. Sidewalk and pathway grade crossing traffic control devices should be located such that all physical features of the device, including the support hardware, conform to clearance requirements provided by the railroad company and/or transit agency, and the regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable).
