Section 8E.03 Guidance 4 - Pathway and Sidewalk Grade Crossing Signs and Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1036

The minimum mounting height for post-mounted signs adjacent to pathways and sidewalks should be 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pathway or sidewalk surface (see Figure 9A-1).

Section 8E.03 Guidance 5 - Pathway and Sidewalk Grade Crossing Signs and Markings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1036

If overhead traffic control devices are placed above pathways, the clearance from the bottom of the device to the pathway surface directly under the sign or device should be at least 8 feet.

Page: 1036

If overhead traffic control devices are placed above pathways that are used by equestrians, the clearance from the bottom of the device to the pathway surface directly under the sign or device should be at least 10 feet.

If overhead traffic control devices are placed above sidewalks, the clearance from the bottom of the device to the sidewalk surface directly under the sign or device shall be at least 7 feet.

Traffic control devices mounted adjacent to pathways at a height of less than 8 feet measured vertically from the bottom of the device to the elevation of the near edge of the pathway surface should have a minimum lateral offset of 2 feet from the near edge of the device to the near edge of the pathway (see Figure 9A-1).

If pathway users include those who travel faster than pedestrians, such as bicyclists or skaters, warning signs should be installed in advance of the pathway grade crossing (see Figure 8E-3). If a LOOK (R15-8) sign is used at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing, it should be mounted on a separate post that is farther from the pathway or sidewalk than the Crossbuck sign or Crossbuck Assembly.

Page: 1037

A stop line may be provided at a sidewalk grade crossing if the surface where the marking is to be applied is capable of retaining the application of the marking.

text:
Section 8E.04 Guidance 3 - Stop Lines, Edge Lines, and Detectable Warnings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1037

If used at pathway or sidewalk grade crossings, the stop line should be a transverse line that extends across the full width of the pathway or sidewalk at the point where a pathway or sidewalk user is to stop. If no detectable warning is provided, the stop line should be placed at least 2 feet in advance of the automatic gate, counterweight, flashing-light signals, or Crossbuck Assembly (if any of these are present), and at least 12 feet from the nearest rail.

Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1037

Edge lines (see Section 3B.09) to delineate the designated user route may be used on the approach to and across the tracks at a pathway grade crossing, a sidewalk grade crossing, or a station crossing if the surface where the marking is to be applied is capable of retaining the application of the marking.

Page: 1037

Edge line delineation can be beneficial where the distance across the tracks is long, commonly because of a skewed grade crossing or because of multiple tracks, or where the pathway or sidewalk surface is immediately adjacent to a traveled way.

Page: 1038

Page: 1038

Detectable warnings (see Chapter 3C) shall be used at pathway grade crossings where pedestrian travel is permitted and at sidewalk grade crossings and shall extend across the full width of the pathway or sidewalk.

Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1038

The dimension of the detectable warning in the direction of pedestrian travel should be at least 2 feet.

text:
Section 8E.04 Guidance 9 - Stop Lines, Edge Lines, and Detectable Warnings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1038

Detectable warnings should be placed immediately beyond the pathway or sidewalk stop line (if a stop line is present) or should be incorporated into and made a part of the stop line. The downstream edge of the detectable warning should be located at least 2 feet upstream from the automatic gate, counterweight, flashing-light signals, or Crossbuck Assembly (if any of these are present) and at least 12 feet from the nearest rail (see Figures 8E-2 and 8E-3).

Section 8E.04 Guidance 10 - Stop Lines, Edge Lines, and Detectable Warnings
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1038

If the distance between the nearest rail of two adjacent tracks at a sidewalk or pathway grade crossing is 30 feet or more, additional detectable warnings should be used to designate the limits of the pedestrian refuge area (see Figure 8E-4).

Page: 1038

At pathway-LRT and sidewalk-LRT grade crossings, the downstream edge of the detectable warning may be located less than 12 feet from the nearest rail.

The downstream edge of the detectable warning at pathway-LRT and sidewalk-LRT grade crossings should be located at least 2 feet upstream from the automatic gate, counterweight, flashing-light signals, or Crossbuck Assembly (if any of these are present), at least 6 feet from the nearest rail, and in accordance with the requirements of the railroad company and/or transit agency, and regulatory agency with statutory authority (if applicable). text:
Section 8E.05 Standard 1 - Passive Traffic Control Devices – Crossbuck Assemblies
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1039

Where the nearest edge of a passive pathway or sidewalk grade crossing is located more than 25 feet from the center of the nearest traffic control warning device at the grade crossing, a Crossbuck Assembly (see Figure 8E-5) shall be installed on each approach to the pathway or sidewalk grade crossing. The distance shall be measured perpendicular to the traveled way from the center of the support post of a Crossbuck Assembly at a passive grade crossing or from the center of the mast of an active traffic control warning device at an active grade crossing to the nearest edge of the pathway or sidewalk surface where it crosses the track(s) (see Figure 8E-2).

Page: 1039

A Crossbuck Assembly may be installed on the approaches to a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing where the nearest edge of the pathway or sidewalk is located 25 feet or less from the center of the nearest traffic control warning device at a grade crossing.

The retroreflective strip on the back of the support may be omitted on the Crossbuck support at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing.

text:
Section 8E.05 Standard 5 - Passive Traffic Control Devices – Crossbuck Assemblies
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1039

The minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the YIELD or STOP sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pathway or sidewalk, of Crossbuck Assemblies installed on pathways or sidewalks shall be 4 feet where the lateral offset to the nearest edge of the sign is 2 feet or more and shall be 7 feet where the lateral offset to the nearest edge of the sign is less than 2 feet (see Figure 8E-5). * ** Mounting height shall be at least 7 feet for sidewalks where the lateral offset is less than 2 feet, at least 4 feet for sidewalks where the lateral offset is 2 feet or more, and at least 4 feet for pathways. Measured to the elevation at the near edge of the pathway or sidewalk. Notes: YIELD or STOP signs are used only at passive crossings. A STOP sign is used only if an engineering study determines that it is appropriate for that particular approach.

If used at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing, an active traffic control system (see Section 8D.01) should include an audible device such as a bell that is operated in conjunction with the flashing-light signals.

Section 8E.07 Option 5 - Active Traffic Control Systems

Flashing-light signals, bells, and other audible warning devices may be omitted at pathway or sidewalk grade crossings that are located within 25 feet of an active warning device at a grade crossing that is equipped with those devices.

Additional pairs of flashing-light signals, bells, or other audible warning devices may be installed on the active traffic control devices at a grade crossing for pathway or sidewalk users approaching the grade crossing from the back side of those devices.

text:
Section 8E.07 Guidance 7 - Active Traffic Control Systems
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1042

Where railroad or LRT tracks in a semi-exclusive alignment are parallel and immediately adjacent to a roadway and if adequate space exists, a pedestrian refuge area or island should be provided between the tracks and the roadway to permit pedestrians to stand clear of the tracks while waiting to cross the roadway and to stand clear of the roadway while waiting to cross the tracks. If a pedestrian refuge area or island is provided at a signalized crossing of the roadway, additional pedestrian features (see Chapter 4I), such as signal heads, signing, and detectors, should be installed in the refuge area or on the island. Month 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

title: Section 8E.08 Support 1 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Signals
text:
Section 8E.08 Support 1 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Signals
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1042

Pedestrian signal heads are typically used at highway-highway intersections where pedestrians have an expectation that other roadway users will sometimes be legally required to yield the right-of-way to them. At grade crossings where rail traffic does not stop, pedestrians will not have the right-of-way yielded to them. Therefore, pedestrian signal heads are not an appropriate traffic control device to use at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing where rail traffic does not stop. Instead, the universal application of horizontally-aligned, alternately-flashing red lights is the uniform active traffic control device for all grade crossings where rail traffic does not stop including pathway and sidewalk grade crossings.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings

Except as provided in Paragraph 3 of this Section, pedestrian signal heads as described in Chapter 4I comprised of Upraised Hand and Walking Person symbols shall not be used at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing.

Pedestrian signal heads may be used at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing where the movement of LRT vehicles is controlled by a traffic control signal or by special LRT signals (see Section 8D.15).

Section 8E.08 Standard 4 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Signals

Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1042

If used at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing, flashing-light signals shall be aligned horizontally, and the light units shall have a diameter of at least 4 inches. For 4-inch diameter light units, the light centers shall be spaced approximately 16 inches apart and, if used, the flashing light unit backgrounds shall be at least 8 inches in diameter. Rev. 1

Section 8E.08 Standard 5 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Signals
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1042

Each red signal unit in the flashing-light signal shall flash alternately. The number of flashes per minute for each lamp shall be 35 minimum and 65 maximum. Each lamp shall be illuminated for approximately the same length of time. The total time of illumination of each pair of lamps shall be the entire operating time.

The minimum mounting height of the flashing-light signals shall be 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom edge of the lights to the elevation of the near edge of the pathway or sidewalk surface.

At station, pathway, or sidewalk grade crossings with multiple tracks, traffic control devices may be installed between the tracks in compliance with any railroad clearance requirements.

Page: 1042

The mounting height for flashing-light signals that are installed between the tracks at multiple-track crossings shall be a minimum of 1 foot, measured vertically from the bottom edge of the lights to the elevation of the near edge of the pathway surface.

Section 8E.08 Guidance 9 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Signals

Page: 1042

If a Diagnostic Team finds that a flashing-light signal with a Crossbuck sign and an audible device is still not resulting in appropriate pedestrian behavior, consideration should be given to also installing an automatic pedestrian gate (see Section 8E.09).

text:
Section 8E.08 Guidance 10 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Signals
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1042

Flashing-light signals (see Figure 8E-7) with a Crossbuck (R15-1) sign and an audible device should be installed along semi-exclusive LRT alignments at station, pathway, or sidewalk grade crossings where the Diagnostic Team has determined that the sight distance is not sufficient for pathway or sidewalk users to complete their crossing prior to the arrival of LRT traffic at the crossing.

metadata.part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
metadata.chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings

text:
Section 8E.08 Guidance 11 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Signals
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1042

If the Diagnostic Team determines that flashing-light signals with a Crossbuck sign and an audible device would not provide sufficient notice of approaching LRT traffic, consideration should be given to also installing an automatic pedestrian gate (see Section 8E.09) with appropriate channelization or fencing.

Section 8E.09 Option 1 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Automatic Pedestrian Gates

Automatic pedestrian gates (see Figures 8E-6, 8E-8, 8E-9, 8E-11,and 8E-12) may be used at pathway or sidewalk grade crossings.

Section 8E.09 Standard 2 - Active Traffic Control Devices – Automatic Pedestrian Gates
Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1043

A pathway or sidewalk grade crossing across tracks where trains are permitted to travel at speeds of 80 mph or higher shall be equipped with a system of automatic pedestrian gates and an escape area with swing gates and fencing installed in the vicinity of the crossing to direct users to the pathway or sidewalk grade crossing (see Figure 8E-6) unless the Diagnostic Team determines that other safety treatments for the crossing would be more appropriate. Month 2023 December 2025

Part: Part 8 Traffic Control For Railroad And Light Rail Transit Grade Crossings
Chapter: Chapter 8E. Pathway And Sidewalk Grade Crossings
Page: 1043

Where automatic pedestrian gates are installed across a pathway or sidewalk at a grade crossing, or where a sidewalk is located between the edge of a roadway and the support for an automatic gate arm that extends across the sidewalk and into the roadway, an emergency escape route (see Figures 8E-9 and 8E-10) should be provided to allow pedestrians to egress away from the track area when the automatic pedestrian gates are activated.

Page: 1043

Except as provided in Paragraph 6 of this Section, automatic pedestrian gate arms shall be provided with at least one red light as shown in Figures 8E-6, 8E-8, 8E-9, 8E-11, and 8E-12. This light shall be continuously illuminated whenever the warning system is active.

Page: 1043

If any red lights in addition to the continuously-illuminated red light that is required in Paragraph 4 of this Section are provided on the automatic pedestrian gate arm, they shall be installed in pairs and shall be flashed alternately in unison with the other flashing-light units at the crossing.

The red light on an automatic pedestrian gate arm may be omitted if the pathway or sidewalk grade crossing is located within 25 feet of the traveled way at a highway-rail or highway-LRT grade crossing that is equipped with active warning devices (see Figure 8E-11). Page: 1044

If used at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing, the gate configuration, which might include a combination of automatic pedestrian gates and swing gates, should provide for full-width coverage of the pathway or sidewalk on each approach to the crossing.

Page: 1045

Except as provided in Paragraph 11 of this Section, if a separate automatic pedestrian gate is used for a sidewalk at a highway-rail or highway-LRT grade crossing, instead of a supplemental or auxiliary gate arm installed as a part of the same mechanism as the vehicular gate, a separate mechanism (see Figure 8E-11) should be provided for the separate automatic pedestrian gate so that if a pedestrian manually raises the pedestrian gate arm, it will have no effect on the vehicular gate.

Page: 1045

A horizontal hanging bar (see Figure 8E-12) may be attached to an automatic pedestrian gate at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing to inform pedestrians with vision disabilities that the automatic pedestrian gate is in the down position and to reduce the likelihood that pedestrians will violate a lowered crossing gate.

All signs installed on bikeways shall be retroreflective, including those on shared-use paths and bicycle lane facilities.

text:
Section 9A.02 Standard 4 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1047

Where signs serve both bicyclists and other road users, vertical mounting height and lateral placement shall be as provided in Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 of this manual.

title: Section 9A.02 Guidance 5 - Standardization of Application for Signing
text:
Section 9A.02 Guidance 5 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1047

Where used on a shared-use path, no portion of a sign or its support should be placed less than 2 feet laterally from the near edge of the path, or less than 8 feet vertically over the entire width of the shared-use path (see Figure 9A-1).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9A.02 Guidance 6 - Standardization of Application for Signing
text:
Section 9A.02 Guidance 6 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1047

Mounting height for post-mounted signs on shared-use paths should be a minimum of 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the path surface (see Figure 9A-1).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9A.02 Guidance 7 - Standardization of Application for Signing
text:
Section 9A.02 Guidance 7 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1047

Signs for the exclusive use of bicyclists should be located so that other road users are not confused by them.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9A.02 Guidance 8 - Standardization of Application for Signing
text:
Section 9A.02 Guidance 8 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

The clearance for overhead signs on shared-use paths should be adjusted when appropriate to accommodate path users requiring more clearance, such as equestrians, or typical maintenance or emergency vehicles. December 2025 Figure 9A-1. Sign Placement on Shared-Use Paths

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

Section 9A.02 Standard 9 - Standardization of Application for Signing

Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

If the sign or plaque applies to motorists and bicyclists, then the size shall be as shown for conventional roads in Tables 2B-1, 2C-1, 2D-1, and 8B-1, as applicable.

text:
Section 9A.02 Standard 10 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

The minimum sign and plaque sizes for signs specific to bicycle-only facilities and shared-use paths shall be those shown in Table 9A-1. These sizes shall be used only for signs and plaques installed specifically for bicyclist applications.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

text:
Section 9A.02 Option 11 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

Larger sizes of signs and plaques may be used on bicycle facilities when appropriate (see Section 2A.07).

text:
Section 9A.02 Option 12 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

Any diamond-shaped warning sign that is placed such that it is applicable only to bicyclists or pedestrians on shared-use paths or separated bicycle lanes may be 18” x 18”.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

text:
Section 9A.02 Guidance 13 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

Except for size, the design of signs and plaques for bicycle facilities should be identical to that provided in this Manual for signs and plaques for streets and highways.

text:
Section 9A.02 Support 14 - Standardization of Application for Signing
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

Uniformity in design of bicycle signs and plaques includes shape, color, symbols, arrows, wording, lettering, and illumination or retroreflectivity.

text:
Section 9A.03 Support 1 - Standardization of Application for Markings
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1048

Markings indicate the separation of the lanes for road users, assist the bicyclist by indicating assigned travel paths, indicate correct position for traffic control signal actuation, and provide advance information for turning and crossing maneuvers.

Section 9A.03 Guidance 2 - Standardization of Application for Markings

Page: 1048

Pavement marking word messages, symbols, and/or arrows should be used in bikeways where appropriate.

title: Section 9A.03 Standard 4 - Standardization of Application for Markings
text:
Section 9A.03 Standard 4 - Standardization of Application for Markings
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1051

Pavement markings on bicycle facilities that must be visible at night or in low-light conditions shall be retroreflective unless the markings are adequately visible under provided lighting.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9A.03 Standard 5 - Standardization of Application for Markings
text:
Section 9A.03 Standard 5 - Standardization of Application for Markings
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9A. General
Page: 1051

The colors, width of lines, patterns of lines, symbols, and arrows used for marking bicycle facilities shall be as defined in Part 3.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Standard 1 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Standard 1 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1052

STOP (R1-1) signs (see Figure 9B-1) shall be installed on bicycle facilities at points where bicyclists are required to stop.

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Standard 2 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Standard 2 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1052

YIELD (R1-2) signs (see Figure 9B-1) shall be installed on bicycle facilities at points where bicyclists have an adequate view of conflicting traffic as they approach the sign, and where bicyclists are required to yield the right-of-way to that conflicting traffic.

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Standard 3 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Standard 3 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1053

A STOP sign or a YIELD sign shall not be installed in conjunction with a bicycle signal face (see Chapter 4H). Figure 9B-1. Regulatory Signs and Plaques for Bicycle Facilities (Sheet 1 of 2) Figure 9B-1. Regulatory Signs and Plaques for Bicycle Facilities (Sheet 2 of 2)

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Option 4 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Option 4 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1053

Larger signs may be used on shared-use paths and separated bikeways for added emphasis.

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Guidance 5 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Guidance 5 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1054

Where conditions require shared-use path users or bicyclists on separated bikeways, but not roadway users, to stop or yield, the STOP or YIELD sign should be placed or shielded so that it is not readily visible to roadway users. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Guidance 6 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Guidance 6 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1054

When the placement of STOP or YIELD signs is being considered, the priority at a shared-use path/roadway intersection should be assigned with consideration of the following: A. Relative speeds of shared-use path and roadway users, B. Relative volumes of shared-use path and roadway traffic, and C. Relative importance of shared-use path and roadway.

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Guidance 7 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Guidance 7 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1054

Speed should not be the sole factor used to determine priority, as it is sometimes appropriate to give priority to a high-volume shared-use path that crosses a low-volume street, or to a regional shared-use path that crosses a minor collector street.

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.01 Guidance 8 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
text:
Section 9B.01 Guidance 8 - STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1054

When priority is assigned (see Sections 2B.06 and 2B.08), the least-restrictive control that is appropriate should be placed on the lower-priority approaches. STOP signs should not be used where YIELD signs would provide adequate control.

metadata.section_title: STOP and YIELD Signs (R1-1 and R1-2)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.02 Support 1 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Regulatory Plaque (R3-7bP)
text:
Section 9B.02 Support 1 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Regulatory Plaque (R3-7bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1054

There are circumstances where it might be appropriate to exempt bicyclists from regulatory restrictions applied to other traffic.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.02 Guidance 2 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Regulatory Plaque (R3-7bP)
text:
Section 9B.02 Guidance 2 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Regulatory Plaque (R3-7bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1054

Where an engineering study or engineering judgment demonstrates that it is appropriate to exempt bicyclists from the provisions of a regulatory sign, the EXCEPT BICYCLES (R3-7bP) regulatory plaque (see Figure 9B-1) should be used.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.02 Support 3 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Regulatory Plaque (R3-7bP)
text:
Section 9B.02 Support 3 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Regulatory Plaque (R3-7bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1054

Figure 9B-2 shows examples of how the EXCEPT BICYCLES (R3-7bP) regulatory plaque can be applied. Rev. 1

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.03 Option 1 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Option 1 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

Advance Intersection Lane Control (R3-8 series) signs (see Section 2B.30) may display the arrangement of a conventional or buffer-separated bicycle lane in relation to other lanes in the same direction that are present on a roadway approach to an intersection.

metadata.section_title: Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.03 Support 2 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Support 2 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

The number and combination of permissible movements by both the motor vehicle and the bicycle on the same approach to an intersection might be practically limited by the amount of information that can be legibly displayed on signs or in signing sequences and still be readily comprehended by road users. The excessive display of all movements by more than one mode can result in unwieldy signs that are difficult to locate and install.

metadata.section_title: Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.03 Guidance 3 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Guidance 3 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

On an approach to an intersection with complex geometry that can include multiple through lanes and multiple turn lanes and also includes a bicycle lane, consideration should be given to displaying all allowable movements on separate signs, such as using Mandatory Movement Lane Control (R3-5) signs (see Section 2B.28) for the through lanes and Mandatory Movement Lane Control (R3-7) signs (see Section 2B.28) for the turn lanes, and guide signs for bicycle routes (see Section 9D.02 through 9D.07) and Bicycle Route Sign auxiliary plaques (see Section 9D.08) for the bicycle movement.

metadata.section_title: Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.03 Standard 4 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Standard 4 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

The portion of the sign face for the bicycle lane shall be limited to the relationship of the bicycle lane to the other lanes on the roadway approach to the intersection. The portion of the sign face for the bicycle lane shall not be modified to display specific, supplementary information about the bicycle lane such as bicycle lane extensions, contiguous buffer spaces, or other ancillary bicycle operations such as two-stage turn boxes or bicycle boxes.

metadata.section_title: Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.03 Standard 5 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Standard 5 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

Counter-flow bicycle lanes shall not be displayed on Advance Intersection Lane Control signs.

title: Section 9B.03 Standard 6 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Standard 6 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

The shared-lane marking symbol shall not be displayed on Advance Intersection Lane Control signs.

metadata.section_title: Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.03 Standard 7 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Standard 7 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

Shared-use paths shall not be displayed on Advance Intersection Lane Control signs.

metadata.section_title: Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.03 Standard 8 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
text:
Section 9B.03 Standard 8 - Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

Advance Intersection Lane Control signs that display the bicycle lane shall use a contrasting white legend on a black background for the bicycle lane (see Figure 2B-4). The portion of the display for the bicycle lane shall not use the color green on the sign face in an attempt to be consistent with the green- colored pavement that might be present on the intersection approach.

metadata.section_title: Advance Intersection Lane Control Signs (R3-8 Series) for Bicycle Lanes
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.04 Standard 1 - Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
text:
Section 9B.04 Standard 1 - Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

The Bike Lane (R3-17) sign and the BIKE LANE (R3-5hP), AHEAD (R3-17aP), and ENDS (R3-17bP) plaques (see Figure 9B-1) shall be used only in conjunction with marked bicycle lanes as described in Sections 9E.01, 9E.06, and 9E.07.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.04 Guidance 2 - Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
text:
Section 9B.04 Guidance 2 - Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1055

If used, Bicycle Lane signs and plaques should be located at the beginning of the bicycle lane and in advance of the downstream end of the bicycle lane.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.04 Option 3 - Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
text:
Section 9B.04 Option 3 - Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

Additional Bicycle Lane signs and plaques may be used at periodic intervals along the bicycle lane as determined by engineering judgment based on the operating speed of bicycle and other traffic, block length, distances from adjacent intersections, and other considerations.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Signs and Plaques (R3-17, R3-5hP, R3-17aP, and R3-17bP)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.05 Option 1 - BEGIN RIGHT TURN LANE YIELD TO BIKES Sign (R4-4)
text:
Section 9B.05 Option 1 - BEGIN RIGHT TURN LANE YIELD TO BIKES Sign (R4-4)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

Where motor vehicles entering a mandatory right-turn lane must weave across bicyclists in bicycle lanes, the BEGIN RIGHT TURN LANE YIELD TO BIKES (R4-4) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used to inform both the motorist and the bicyclist of this weaving maneuver (see Figures 9E-3 and 9E-4).

metadata.section_title: BEGIN RIGHT TURN LANE YIELD TO BIKES Sign (R4-4)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.05 Guidance 2 - BEGIN RIGHT TURN LANE YIELD TO BIKES Sign (R4-4)
text:
Section 9B.05 Guidance 2 - BEGIN RIGHT TURN LANE YIELD TO BIKES Sign (R4-4)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

The R4-4 sign should not be used when bicyclists need to move left because of a right-turn lane drop situation.

metadata.section_title: BEGIN RIGHT TURN LANE YIELD TO BIKES Sign (R4-4)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.06 Option 1 - Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
text:
Section 9B.06 Option 1 - Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

The Bicycle WRONG WAY (R5-1b) sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC (R9-3cP) plaque (see Figure 9B-1) may be placed facing wrong-way bicyclists, such as on the left-hand side of a roadway.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.06 Option 2 - Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
text:
Section 9B.06 Option 2 - Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

This sign and plaque may be mounted back-to-back with other signs to minimize visibility to other traffic.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.06 Guidance 3 - Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
text:
Section 9B.06 Guidance 3 - Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

The RIDE WITH TRAFFIC plaque should be used only in conjunction with the Bicycle WRONG WAY sign, and should be mounted directly below the Bicycle WRONG WAY sign.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Wrong Way Sign and RIDE WITH TRAFFIC Plaque (R5-1b and R9-3cP)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.07 Option 1 - NO MOTOR VEHICLES Sign (R5-3)
text:
Section 9B.07 Option 1 - NO MOTOR VEHICLES Sign (R5-3)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

The NO MOTOR VEHICLES (R5-3) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be installed at the entrance to a shared-use path.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.08 Option 1 - Selective Exclusion Signs
text:
Section 9B.08 Option 1 - Selective Exclusion Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

Selective Exclusion signs (see Figure 9B-1) may be installed at the entrance to a roadway or facility to notify road or facility users that designated types of traffic are excluded from using the roadway or facility.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.08 Support 2 - Selective Exclusion Signs
text:
Section 9B.08 Support 2 - Selective Exclusion Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1056

Typical exclusion messages include: A. No Bicycles (R5-6); B. No Pedestrians (R9-3); C. No Skaters (R9-13); D. No Equestrians (R9-14); E. No Snowmobiles (R9-15); and F. No All-Terrain Vehicles (R9-16).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.08 Option 3 - Selective Exclusion Signs
text:
Section 9B.08 Option 3 - Selective Exclusion Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1057

Where bicyclists, pedestrians, and motor-driven cycles are all prohibited, the R5-10a word message sign (see Section 2B.45) may be used.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.09 Standard 1 - No Parking Bike Lane Signs (R7-9 and R7-9a)
text:
Section 9B.09 Standard 1 - No Parking Bike Lane Signs (R7-9 and R7-9a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1057

If the installation of signs is necessary to restrict parking, standing, or stopping in a bicycle lane, appropriate signs as described in Sections 2B.53 through 2B.55, or the No Parking Bike Lane (R7-9 or R7-9a) signs (see Figure 9B-1) shall be installed.

metadata.section_title: No Parking Bike Lane Signs (R7-9 and R7-9a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.10 Option 1 - Back-In Parking Sign (R7-10)
text:
Section 9B.10 Option 1 - Back-In Parking Sign (R7-10)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1057

The Back-In Parking (R7-10) sign (see Section 2B.52 and Figure 9B-1) may be used where back-in parking is required by motor vehicles in the presence of a bicycle lane or movement.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.10 Support 2 - Back-In Parking Sign (R7-10)
text:
Section 9B.10 Support 2 - Back-In Parking Sign (R7-10)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1057

Angled back-in curb parking is commonly applied on streets where a bicycle lane is present so that the scanning behavior of a motorist associated with the back-in angle parking task, both entering and exiting the parking space, would place a bicyclist in a bicycle lane in a more direct view of the motor vehicle operator.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.10 Support 3 - Back-In Parking Sign (R7-10)
text:
Section 9B.10 Support 3 - Back-In Parking Sign (R7-10)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1057

Figure 9B-3 shows an example of the use of back-in parking signs in conjunction with bicycle lanes.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.11 Option 1 - Bicycles Use Ped Signal Sign (R9-5)
text:
Section 9B.11 Option 1 - Bicycles Use Ped Signal Sign (R9-5)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1057

The Bicycles Use Ped Signal (R9-5) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used where the crossing of a street by bicyclists is controlled by pedestrian signal indications.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.11 Option 2 - Bicycles Use Ped Signal Sign (R9-5)
text:
Section 9B.11 Option 2 - Bicycles Use Ped Signal Sign (R9-5)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1057

In order to remind drivers who are making turns to yield to or stop for pedestrians or bicyclists, a Turning Vehicles Yield to Pedestrians (R10-15) sign, Turning Vehicles Stop for Pedestrians (R10-15a) sign (see Section 2B.59), or Left Turn Yield to Bicycles (R10-12b) sign (see Section 9B.21) may be used.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.11 Guidance 3 - Bicycles Use Ped Signal Sign (R9-5)
text:
Section 9B.11 Guidance 3 - Bicycles Use Ped Signal Sign (R9-5)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

If used, the R9-5 sign should be installed in the vicinity of where bicyclists will be crossing the street. Figure 9B-3. Examples of Bicycle Facilities Adjacent to Back-In Parking

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.12 Option 1 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
text:
Section 9B.12 Option 1 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycles Yield to Peds (R9-6) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used at locations where a bicyclist is required to cross or share a facility used by pedestrians and is required to yield to the pedestrians.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.12 Standard 2 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
text:
Section 9B.12 Standard 2 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

Where the Bicycles Yield to Peds sign is supported by a yield line pavement marking (see Section 3B.19) to establish the yielding point, the sign and the pavement marking shall be installed adjacent to each other.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.12 Standard 3 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
text:
Section 9B.12 Standard 3 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycles Yield to Peds sign shall not be used in bicycle corridors to establish a programmatic regulation where no yielding point exists.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.12 Standard 4 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
text:
Section 9B.12 Standard 4 - Bicycles Yield to Peds Sign (R9-6)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycles Yield to Peds sign shall not be used in conjunction with a STOP or YIELD sign, Yield Here to Pedestrians Sign, or a Stop Here for Pedestrians Sign.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.13 Option 1 - Shared-Use Path Restriction Sign (R9-7)
text:
Section 9B.13 Option 1 - Shared-Use Path Restriction Sign (R9-7)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Shared-Use Path Restriction (R9-7) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be installed to supplement a solid white pavement marking line (see Section 9E.13) on facilities that are to be shared by pedestrians and bicyclists in order to provide a separate designated pavement area for each mode of travel. The symbols may be transposed as appropriate.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.13 Guidance 2 - Shared-Use Path Restriction Sign (R9-7)
text:
Section 9B.13 Guidance 2 - Shared-Use Path Restriction Sign (R9-7)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

If two-way operation is allowed on the facility for pedestrians and/or bicyclists, the designated pavement area that is provided for each two-way mode of travel should be wide enough to accommodate both directions of travel for that mode.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.14 Support 1 - Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
text:
Section 9B.14 Support 1 - Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Uniform Vehicle Code (UVC) defines a “substandard width lane” as a “lane that is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the same lane.”

metadata.section_title: Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.14 Option 2 - Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
text:
Section 9B.14 Option 2 - Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane (R9-20) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used on roadways where no bicycle lanes or adjacent shoulders usable by bicycles are present and where travel lanes are too narrow for bicycles and motor vehicles to operate side-by-side.

metadata.section_title: Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.14 Option 3 - Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
text:
Section 9B.14 Option 3 - Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane sign may be used in locations where it is important to inform road users that bicyclists might occupy the travel lane.

metadata.section_title: Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane Sign (R9-20)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.15 Option 1 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
text:
Section 9B.15 Option 1 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycle Passing Clearance (R4-19) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used in jurisdictions that have defined in law or ordinance a specific clearance to be provided by motor vehicles when they pass bicycles.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.15 Option 2 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
text:
Section 9B.15 Option 2 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The specific clearance displayed on the Bicycle Passing Clearance (R4-19) sign may be adjusted to reflect the applicable law or ordinance.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.15 Standard 3 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
text:
Section 9B.15 Standard 3 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycle Passing Clearance (R4-19) sign shall not be used in jurisdictions that do not have a specific passing clearance to be provided by motor vehicles passing bicycles, as defined in law or ordinance.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.15 Guidance 4 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
text:
Section 9B.15 Guidance 4 - Bicycle Passing Clearance Sign (R4-19)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycle Passing Clearance (R4-19) sign should not be used on roadways with bicycle lanes or with shoulders usable for bicycle travel.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.16 Option 1 - Bicycles Use Shoulder Only Sign (R9-21)
text:
Section 9B.16 Option 1 - Bicycles Use Shoulder Only Sign (R9-21)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycles Use Shoulder Only (R9-21) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used to designate locations on a freeway or expressway where bicycles are allowed, but must remain on an available and usable shoulder.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.16 Guidance 2 - Bicycles Use Shoulder Only Sign (R9-21)
text:
Section 9B.16 Guidance 2 - Bicycles Use Shoulder Only Sign (R9-21)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1058

The Bicycles Use Shoulder Only sign should be limited to use on freeways and expressways.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.16 Guidance 3 - Bicycles Use Shoulder Only Sign (R9-21)
text:
Section 9B.16 Guidance 3 - Bicycles Use Shoulder Only Sign (R9-21)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

The Bicycles Use Shoulder Only sign should be placed adjacent to the entrance ramp or entrance to the freeway at or near the location where the full-width shoulder resumes beyond the entrance ramp taper.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.17 Standard 1 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 9B.17 Standard 1 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

The Bicycles Must Exit (R9-22) sign (see Figure 9B-1) shall be used in advance of a location where a freeway or expressway becomes prohibited to bicycle travel, and shall be placed in advance of the intersection or exit ramp prior to the prohibited segment of roadway (see Figure 9B-4).

metadata.section_title: Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.17 Option 2 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 9B.17 Option 2 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

The Bicycles Must Exit sign may be used below a post-mounted Exit Direction sign.

metadata.section_title: Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.17 Standard 3 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 9B.17 Standard 3 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

If the Bicycles Must Exit sign is used, a No Bicycles (R5-6) sign (see Figure 9B-1) shall be placed downstream from the intersection or exit ramp departure point where the prohibited segment of freeway or expressway begins. The No Bicycles sign shall not be placed below the Exit Gore sign.

metadata.section_title: Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.17 Option 4 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
text:
Section 9B.17 Option 4 - Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

The ON FREEWAY (R5-10dP) plaque (see Figure 9B-1) may be used with an appropriate Selective Exclusion sign to indicate a prohibition along ramps leading to an adjacent or parallel freeway.

metadata.section_title: Signing for Bicycles on Freeways and Expressways
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.18 Support 1 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
text:
Section 9B.18 Support 1 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

Where two-stage bicycle turn boxes are provided in an intersection, the design of an approach to that intersection will determine whether the use of a two-stage bicycle turn box is required by bicycles to facilitate a turn.

metadata.section_title: Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.18 Support 2 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
text:
Section 9B.18 Support 2 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

Situations in which a two-stage bicycle turn box might be necessary to facilitate turns include, but are not limited to, those in which: A. A separated bicycle facility is provided where upstream access to a lane used to facilitate turns by motor vehicle traffic is physically inaccessible to bicycles; B. Left turns are prohibited from the left-most lane, or right turns are prohibited from the right-most lane, at an intersection; or C. Locations where physical or operational conditions make it impracticable or unsafe for a bicyclist to merge and make the appropriate turn as would any other vehicle.

metadata.section_title: Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.18 Standard 3 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
text:
Section 9B.18 Standard 3 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

Where bicycles are required to use a two-stage bicycle turn box (see Figure 9B-5), the Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box regulatory sign series (see Figure 9B-5) shall be used.

metadata.section_title: Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.18 Standard 4 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
text:
Section 9B.18 Standard 4 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1059

Where bicycles are required to use a two-stage bicycle turn box, the Bicycles All Turns from Bike Lane (R9-23) or Bicycle Left Turn from Bike Lane (R9-23a) advance regulatory sign shall be mounted in advance of the intersection, and at least one Bicycle Turn Must Use Turn Box (R9-23b or R9-23c) sign shall be used at the intersection.

metadata.section_title: Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.18 Standard 5 - Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box Regulatory Signing (R9-23 Series)
text:

Page: 1059

Where use of a two-stage bicycle turn box is optional, the Two-Stage Bicycle Turn Box guide sign series (see Section 9D.13) may be used to provide directional information.

Page: 1059

If used, an appropriately sized Street Name (D3-1) sign (see Section 2D.45) may be installed below the All Turns from Bike Lane sign or Left Turn from Bike Lane sign to identify the crossroad where the turn box will be available.

title: Section 9B.19 Support 1 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
text:
Section 9B.19 Support 1 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1062

Bicycle jughandle turns allow bicycles to use the traffic control provided for the crossroad for facilitating a left turn, right turn, or U-turn.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

Section 9B.19 Option 2 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1062

The R9-23 sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used in advance of where bicyclists are required to use the bicycle jughandle turn in order to facilitate all turns.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1062

The R9-24 series sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used where bicyclists are required to use the bicycle jughandle turn in order to facilitate all turns.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.19 Option 4 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
text:
Section 9B.19 Option 4 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1062

The R9-25 series sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used where bicyclists are required to use a bicycle jughandle turn to facilitate U-turns and left turns and where right-turning bicyclists are exempted or the right turn is not available or possible (see Figure 9B-6).

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.19 Option 5 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
text:
Section 9B.19 Option 5 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1062

The R9-26 series sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used where bicyclists are required to use a jughandle to facilitate U-turns and where left-turning and right-turning bicyclists are exempted or the left turn or right turn is not available or possible.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.19 Option 6 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
text:
Section 9B.19 Option 6 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

The R9-27 series sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used where bicyclists are required to use a jughandle to facilitate left turns and where U-turning and right-turning bicyclists are exempted or the U-turn or right turn is not available or possible. Figure 9B-6. Example of Application of Bicycle Jughandle Sign Note: The use of green-colored pavement is optional. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.19 Option 7 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
text:
Section 9B.19 Option 7 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

A Bicycle Jughandle sign may be used to indicate a jughandle turn initially made by a left turn for a bicycle lane on the left-hand side of a one-way street or for a counter-flow bicycle lane. The legend RIGHT may be substituted for the legend LEFT on Bicycle Jughandle signs to represent bicycle facilities on the left-hand side of the roadway where facilitating a right turn would be applicable.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.19 Guidance 8 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
text:
Section 9B.19 Guidance 8 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

Applications of Bicycle Jughandle signs should be limited to brief independent alignments either through physical separation or islands formed by pavement markings. Bicycle Jughandle signs should not be used for a turning movement facilitated by a two-stage turn box (see Section 9B.18).

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

Section 9B.19 Support 9 - Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

Bicycle Jughandle signs are designed to be mounted below guide signs.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Jughandle Signs (R9-24, R9-25, R9-26, and R9-27 Series)

text:
Section 9B.20 Option 1 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

Where bicycles are not controlled by pedestrian signal indications, the R10-4, R10-24, or R10-26 sign (see Section 2B.58) may be used.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.20 Guidance 2 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
text:
Section 9B.20 Guidance 2 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

If used, the R10-4, R10-24, or R10-26 signs (see Figure 9B-1) should be installed in the vicinity of where bicycles will be crossing the street.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.20 Option 3 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
text:
Section 9B.20 Option 3 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

If bicycles are crossing a roadway where In-Roadway Warning Lights (see Section 4U.02) or other warning lights or beacons have been provided, the R10-25 (see Figure 9B-1) sign may be used. Rev. 1

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.20 Option 4 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
text:
Section 9B.20 Option 4 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

The Bicycle Detector (R10-22) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be installed at signalized intersections where pavement markings are used to indicate the location where a bicycle is to be positioned to actuate the signal (see Section 9E.15).

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
