text:
Section 9B.20 Guidance 5 - Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

If the Bicycle Detector sign is installed, it should be placed at the roadside adjacent to the marking to emphasize the location of the marking.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Actuation Signs (R10-4, R10-22, R10-24, R10-25, and R10-26)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.21 Option 1 - Left Turn Yield to Bicycles Sign (R10-12b)
text:
Section 9B.21 Option 1 - Left Turn Yield to Bicycles Sign (R10-12b)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

The Left Turn Yield to Bicycles (R10-12b) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be used to emphasize the requirement for motorists to yield to bicyclists in situations where the motorist is turning across a bicycle movement that may be unexpected in direction, location, or some other quality that would be inconsistent with the typical bicycle lane.

metadata.section_title: Left Turn Yield to Bicycles Sign (R10-12b)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.22 Support 1 - Bicycle Signal Signs (R10-40, R10-40a, R10-41, R10-41a, R10-41b, and R10-41c)
text:
Section 9B.22 Support 1 - Bicycle Signal Signs (R10-40, R10-40a, R10-41, R10-41a, R10-41b, and R10-41c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1063

The purposes of the Bicycle Signal signs (see Figure 9B-1) are to inform road users that the signal indications in the bicycle signal face are intended only for bicyclists, and to inform bicyclists which specific bicycle movements are controlled by the bicycle signal face.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Signal Signs (R10-40, R10-40a, R10-41, R10-41a, R10-41b, and R10-41c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.23 Option 1 - LOOK Sign (R15-8)
text:
Section 9B.23 Option 1 - LOOK Sign (R15-8)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1064

At railroad or LRT grade crossings with shared-use paths or separated bikeways, the LOOK (R15-8) sign (see Figure 9B-1) may be mounted on the Crossbuck support below the Crossbuck (R15-1) sign or any other signs, or on a separate post in the immediate vicinity of the grade crossing on the railroad or LRT right-of-way.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.23 Guidance 2 - LOOK Sign (R15-8)
text:
Section 9B.23 Guidance 2 - LOOK Sign (R15-8)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1064

A LOOK sign should not be mounted on a Crossbuck Assembly that has a YIELD or STOP sign mounted on the same support as the Crossbuck.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9B.24 Option 1 - Other Regulatory Signs
text:
Section 9B.24 Option 1 - Other Regulatory Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9B. Regulatory Signs
Page: 1065

Other regulatory signs described in Chapters 2B and 8B may be installed on bicycle facilities as appropriate.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9C.01 Guidance 1 - Turn or Curve Warning Signs (W1 Series)
text:
Section 9C.01 Guidance 1 - Turn or Curve Warning Signs (W1 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1065

To warn bicyclists of unexpected changes in shared-use path direction, appropriate Turn, Curve, or Large Arrow (W1-1 through W1-7) signs (see Figure 9C-1) should be used.

metadata.section_title: Turn or Curve Warning Signs (W1 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.01 Guidance 2 - Turn or Curve Warning Signs (W1 Series)
text:
Section 9C.01 Guidance 2 - Turn or Curve Warning Signs (W1 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

The W1-1 through W1-5 signs should be installed at least 50 feet in advance of the beginning of the change of alignment. Figure 9C-1. Warning Signs and Plaques and Object Markers for Bicycle Facilities (Sheet 1 of 2) * A fluorescent yellow-green background color may be used for this sign or plaque. The background color of the plaque should match the color of the warning sign that it supplements. Figure 9C-1. Warning Signs and Plaques and Object Markers for Bicycle Facilities (Sheet 2 of 2) * A fluorescent yellow-green background color may be used for this sign or plaque. The background color of the plaque should match the color of the warning sign that it supplements.

metadata.section_title: Turn or Curve Warning Signs (W1 Series)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.02 Option 1 - Intersection Warning Signs (W2 Series)
text:
Section 9C.02 Option 1 - Intersection Warning Signs (W2 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

Intersection Warning (W2-1 through W2-5) signs (see Figure 9C-1) may be used on a roadway, street, or shared-use path in advance of an intersection to indicate the presence of an intersection and the possibility of turning or entering traffic.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.02 Guidance 2 - Intersection Warning Signs (W2 Series)
text:
Section 9C.02 Guidance 2 - Intersection Warning Signs (W2 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

When engineering judgment determines that the visibility of the intersection is limited on the shared-use path approach, Intersection Warning signs should be used.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.02 Guidance 3 - Intersection Warning Signs (W2 Series)
text:
Section 9C.02 Guidance 3 - Intersection Warning Signs (W2 Series)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

Intersection Warning signs should not be used where the shared-use path approach to the intersection is controlled by a STOP sign, a YIELD sign, or a traffic control signal.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.03 Option 1 - Bicycle Surface Condition Warning Sign (W8-10)
text:
Section 9C.03 Option 1 - Bicycle Surface Condition Warning Sign (W8-10)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

The Bicycle Surface Condition Warning (W8-10) sign (see Figure 9C-1) may be installed where roadway or shared-use path conditions could cause a bicyclist to lose control of the bicycle.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.03 Option 2 - Bicycle Surface Condition Warning Sign (W8-10)
text:
Section 9C.03 Option 2 - Bicycle Surface Condition Warning Sign (W8-10)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

Signs warning of other conditions that might be of concern to bicyclists, including BUMP (W8-1), DIP (W8-2), PAVEMENT ENDS (W8-3), and any other word message that describes conditions that are of concern to bicyclists, may also be used (see Figure 9C-1).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.03 Option 3 - Bicycle Surface Condition Warning Sign (W8-10)
text:
Section 9C.03 Option 3 - Bicycle Surface Condition Warning Sign (W8-10)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

A supplemental plaque may be used to clarify the specific type of surface condition.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.04 Support 1 - Bicycle Warning and Trail Crossing Signs (W11-1 and W11-15)
text:
Section 9C.04 Support 1 - Bicycle Warning and Trail Crossing Signs (W11-1 and W11-15)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1066

The Bicycle Warning (W11-1) sign (see Figure 9C-1) alerts the road user to unexpected entries into the roadway by bicyclists, and other crossing activities that might cause conflicts. These conflicts might be relatively confined, or might occur randomly over a segment of roadway.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Warning and Trail Crossing Signs (W11-1 and W11-15)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.05 Option 1 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Warning Plaque (W16-20P)
text:
Section 9C.05 Option 1 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Warning Plaque (W16-20P)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

Where it might be advantageous to notify bicyclists that the conditions or hazards depicted by a warning sign are not applicable to bicycles, the EXCEPT BICYCLES (W16-20P) warning plaque (see Figure 9C-1) may be used.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.05 Support 2 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Warning Plaque (W16-20P)
text:
Section 9C.05 Support 2 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Warning Plaque (W16-20P)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

Examples of warning signs where an EXCEPT BICYCLES warning plaque can be mounted include DEAD END (W14-1) and NO OUTLET (W14-2) signs (see Section 2C.24).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.05 Support 3 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Warning Plaque (W16-20P)
text:
Section 9C.05 Support 3 - EXCEPT BICYCLES Warning Plaque (W16-20P)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

Sections 2C.57 and 2C.58 contain information on the design of supplemental warning plaques.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.06 Standard 1 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
text:
Section 9C.06 Standard 1 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

When used, the Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic (W16-21P) warning plaque (see Figure 9C-1) shall be installed below a STOP or YIELD sign.

metadata.section_title: Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.06 Option 2 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
text:
Section 9C.06 Option 2 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

The Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic warning plaque may be used below STOP or YIELD signs on crossroads and driveways to alert road users of an unexpected bicycle movement.

metadata.section_title: Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.06 Support 3 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
text:
Section 9C.06 Support 3 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

The Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic warning plaque can help minimize overuse or misapplication of other warning signs such as the Bicycle Warning (W11-1) sign.

metadata.section_title: Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.06 Guidance 4 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
text:
Section 9C.06 Guidance 4 - Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

The Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic warning plaque should be used in combination with a STOP or YIELD sign when a counter-flow or two-way bicycle facility has an approach that is counter to the customary scanning behavior of a motorist at that location.

metadata.section_title: Two-Way Bicycle Cross Traffic Warning Plaque (W16-21P)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.07 Support 1 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
text:
Section 9C.07 Support 1 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

Where a warning sign is appropriate, the Bicycle Lane Ends (W9-5) warning sign (see Figure 9C-1) is intended to alert road users that a bicycle lane is ending and that bicycles will share or occupy the travel lane after merging.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.07 Option 2 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
text:
Section 9C.07 Option 2 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

The Bicycle Lane Ends warning sign may be used in advance of the end of a bicycle lane to warn that a bicycle lane will be ending.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.07 Option 3 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
text:
Section 9C.07 Option 3 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1067

The Bicycles Merging (W9-5a) sign (see Figure 9C-1) may be used where a bicycle merging maneuver might occur. The Bicycles Merging sign may be used in addition to the Bicycle Lane Ends (W9-5) warning sign.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.07 Guidance 4 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
text:
Section 9C.07 Guidance 4 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

To avoid excessive use of signs, the Bicycle Lane Ends warning sign should not be used where a bicycle lane is dropped on the approach to an intersection and resumes immediately after the intersection. December 2025

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.07 Option 5 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
text:
Section 9C.07 Option 5 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

A Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane (R9-20) sign (see Section 9B.14) and/or shared-lane markings (see Section 9E.09) may be installed downstream of the merge area.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.07 Option 6 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
text:
Section 9C.07 Option 6 - Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

A W16-2aP supplemental warning plaque may be used to inform road users of the distance to the end of the bicycle lane and/or to the bicycle merge.

metadata.section_title: Bicycle Lane Ends Warning Sign (W9-5) and Bicycles Merging Sign (W9-5a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.08 Option 1 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
text:
Section 9C.08 Option 1 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

Other bicycle warning signs (see Figure 9C-1) such as PATH NARROWS (W5-4a) and Hill (W7-5) may be installed on shared-use paths to warn bicyclists of conditions not readily apparent.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.08 Option 2 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
text:
Section 9C.08 Option 2 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

In situations where there is a need to warn road users to watch for bicycles traveling along the highway, the Bicycle Warning (W11-1) sign may be used with the IN ROAD (W16-1P) plaque or the IN STREET (W16-1aP) plaque (see Figure 9C-1).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.08 Guidance 3 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
text:
Section 9C.08 Guidance 3 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

If used, other advance bicycle warning signs should be installed at least 50 feet in advance of the beginning of the condition.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.08 Guidance 4 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
text:
Section 9C.08 Guidance 4 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

Where temporary traffic control zones are present on bikeways, appropriate signs from Part 6 should be used.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.08 Option 5 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
text:
Section 9C.08 Option 5 - Other Bicycle Warning Signs
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

Other warning signs described in Chapters 2C and 8C may be installed on bicycle facilities as appropriate.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.09 Standard 1 - Object Markers
text:
Section 9C.09 Standard 1 - Object Markers
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1068

Obstructions in a shared-use path shall be marked with retroreflective material or appropriate object markers as described in Section 2C.70.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9C.09 Option 2 - Object Markers
text:
Section 9C.09 Option 2 - Object Markers
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers
Page: 1069

Fixed objects adjacent to shared-use paths may be marked with Type 1, Type 2, or Type 3 object markers. If the object marker is not also intended to be seen by motorists, a smaller version of the Type 3 object marker may be used (see Table 9A-1). MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
metadata.chapter: Chapter 9C. Warning Signs And Object Markers

title: Section 9D.02 Support 1 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Support 1 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1072

The Bike Route Guide (D11-1 or D11-1c) sign (see Figure 9D-1) is used where no unique designation of routes is desired. Sections 9D.04 through 9D.07 contain information for Bicycle Route signs where the bicycle route is designated by number, name, or both.

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.02 Option 2 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Option 2 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1072

Bike Route Guide signs may be provided along designated unnumbered, unnamed bicycle routes to inform bicyclists of bicycle route direction changes and to confirm route direction and destination.

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.02 Option 3 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Option 3 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1072

If used, Bike Route Guide signs may be repeated at regular intervals so that bicycles entering from side streets will have an opportunity to know that they are on a bicycle route. Similar guide signing may be used for shared roadways with intermediate signs placed for bicycle guidance.

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.02 Option 4 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Option 4 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1073

The Alternative Bike Route Guide (D11-1c) sign may be used to display a word legend that provides information on route direction, destination, and/or route name in place of the “BIKE ROUTE” word legend on the D11-1 sign (see Figure 9D-1).

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.02 Option 5 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Option 5 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1073

Other plaques such as BEGIN (M4-14P) and END (M4-6P) may be used with Bike Route Guide signs.

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.02 Guidance 6 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Guidance 6 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1073

Travel times should not be used on Bike Route Guide signs.

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.02 Support 7 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Support 7 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1073

Travel times can vary greatly for bicyclists based on a variety of factors including individual speed, bicycle type, and type of facility.

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.02 Support 8 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
text:
Section 9D.02 Support 8 - Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1073

Figure 9D-2 shows examples of guide sign applications for bicycle travel.

metadata.section_title: Bike Route Guide Signs (D11-1 and D11-1c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.03 Option 1 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
text:
Section 9D.03 Option 1 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1074

The BIKE ROUTE (D11-1bP) plaque (see Figure 9D-1) may be installed to supplement: A. The Alternative Bike Route Guide (D11-1c) sign (see Section 9D.02); B. The Bicycle Directional (D11-11) sign (see Section 9D.11) for use on a shared-use path; or C. A Street Name (D3-1) sign (see Section 2D.45). Figure 9D-2. Examples of Bicycle Guide Signing (Sheet 1 of 2) Figure 9D-2. Examples of Bicycle Guide Signing (Sheet 2 of 2) Note: Right-of-way assignment and associated traffic controls for intersections are not shown.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.03 Option 2 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
text:
Section 9D.03 Option 2 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1074

When installed above or below a Street Name sign, the D11-1bP supplemental plaque may include a bicycle symbol to the left of the BIKE ROUTE legend.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.03 Standard 3 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
text:
Section 9D.03 Standard 3 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1074

The bicycle symbol shall not be used on a Street Name sign.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.03 Standard 4 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
text:
Section 9D.03 Standard 4 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1074

Where a BIKE ROUTE plaque is used in conjunction with a Street Name sign to identify a street that is part of an overall bicycle network, one of the following signs shall also be used systematically to establish the designated bicycle route on the street identified by the BIKE ROUTE plaque: A. Bike Route Guide signs (see Section 9D.02), B. Alternative Bike Route Guide (D11-1c) sign (see Section 9D.02), C. State or Local Bicycle Route (M1-8 and M1-8a) signs (see Section 9D.05), D. Non-Numbered Bicycle Route (M1-8b and M1-8c) signs (see Section 9D.06), or E. United States Bicycle Route (M1-9) sign (see Section 9D.07).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.03 Standard 5 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
text:
Section 9D.03 Standard 5 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1074

BIKE ROUTE plaques shall not incorporate replicas of the United States Bicycle Route, State or Local Bicycle Route, or Non-Numbered Bicycle Route sign to replace or supplement the bicycle symbol.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.03 Option 6 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
text:
Section 9D.03 Option 6 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1074

The BIKE ROUTE plaque and the Street Name sign may be different widths.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.03 Support 7 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
text:
Section 9D.03 Support 7 - BIKE ROUTE Plaque (D11-1bP)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1075

Figure 9D-3 shows an example of bicycle guide signing using the BIKE ROUTE plaque. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1 Figure 9D-3. Example of Bicycle Route Guide Signing Note: The D1-2 signs are larger than the other guide signs on this figure because the legends on the D1-2 signs need to be legible to motorists.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Support 1 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Support 1 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1075

The purpose of numbering and signing bikeways and bicycle routes is to identify routes and facilitate travel.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Support 2 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Support 2 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1075

The United States Bicycle Routes are numbered by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) upon recommendations of State highway organizations. County and local bikeways and bicycle routes are numbered by the appropriate authorities. Rev. 1

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Support 3 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Support 3 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1075

Bicycle route sign systems can be used to distinguish junctions, turns, the beginning of routes, and route termination points. Extensive use of reassurance markers is typically not needed.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Support 4 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Support 4 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1076

An agency or jurisdiction can use several methods for bicycle route guidance including maps, information guides, or signing. December 2025

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Guidance 5 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Guidance 5 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1076

Establishing bicycle route systems described in Paragraph 2 of this Section and any other bicycle route system should be followed with effective communication between affected jurisdictions. County and local jurisdictions that are establishing numbered routes should coordinate with the respective State transportation agency. Care should be taken to avoid the use of numbers or other designations that have been assigned to U.S. Bicycle Routes or other routes in the same geographical region or State. Overlapping numbered routes should be kept to a minimum.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Guidance 6 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Guidance 6 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1076

Bicycle routes, which might be a combination of various types of bikeways, should establish a continuous routing.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Standard 7 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Standard 7 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1076

Multiple numbered bicycle route systems shall be given preference in this order: United States, State, and county or local. The preference shall be given by installing the highest-priority legend on the top or the left of the sign assembly with other numbered overlapping bicycle routes.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Standard 8 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Standard 8 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1076

Where applicable, multiple bicycle route systems with concurrency shall be signed in accordance with Figure 9D-4.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Guidance 9 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Guidance 9 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1076

Numbered bicycle routes should be identified by route signs (see Sections 9D.05 through 9D.07) and auxiliary plaques (see Section 9D.08).

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Guidance 10 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Guidance 10 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1076

If used, Bicycle Route signs should be placed at locations to keep bicyclists informed of changes in route direction.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.04 Option 11 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
text:
Section 9D.04 Option 11 - Numbered Bikeway Systems
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

Bicycle Route signs may be installed on shared roadways, shared-use paths, or separated bikeways to provide navigational guidance for bicyclists. Figure 9D-4. Examples of Route Signing for Numbered or Named Bicycle Routes A - United States B - State or local numbered bicycle C - State or local numbered bicycle D - Non-numbered E - Non-numbered Bicycle Route interstate bicycle interstate bicycle (USBR) only (interstate numbered route with no route concurrency route with route route with no route concurrency route with route concurrency concurrency bike route) with USBR with USBR with USBR with USBR MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.05 Option 1 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
text:
Section 9D.05 Option 1 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

To establish a unique identification (route designation) for a State or local bicycle route, the Numbered Bicycle Route (M1-8 or M1-8a) sign (see Figure 9D-1) may be used.

metadata.section_title: Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.05 Standard 2 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
text:
Section 9D.05 Standard 2 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

The Numbered Bicycle Route (M1-8) sign shall display a route designation and shall have a green background with a white legend and border.

metadata.section_title: Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.05 Standard 3 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
text:
Section 9D.05 Standard 3 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

The Numbered Bicycle Route (M1-8a) sign shall display the same information as the M1-8 sign and in addition shall display a pictograph or words on the upper portion of the sign panel that are associated with the route or with the agency that has jurisdiction over the route.

metadata.section_title: Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.05 Standard 4 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
text:
Section 9D.05 Standard 4 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

If a Numbered Bicycle Route (M1-8 or M1-8a) sign is used on a roadway, it shall include a bicycle symbol.

metadata.section_title: Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.05 Guidance 5 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
text:
Section 9D.05 Guidance 5 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

If a pictograph is used on the M1-8a sign the maximum dimension (height or width) of the pictograph should not exceed 2 times the height of the route numeral, and should be contained within a green border. The minimum width of the graphic on the M1-8a sign should be ²⁄3 of the sign width, and the maximum width should be 9⁄10 of the sign width.

metadata.section_title: Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.05 Guidance 6 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
text:
Section 9D.05 Guidance 6 - Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

If a bicycle symbol is used on the M1-8a sign, it should have a minimum height of ¼ of the M1-8a sign panel height.

metadata.section_title: Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8 and M1-8a)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.06 Standard 1 - Non-Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8b and M1-8c)
text:
Section 9D.06 Standard 1 - Non-Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8b and M1-8c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

Except as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section, Non-Numbered Bicycle Route (M1-8b and M1-8c) signs (see Figure 9D-1) used on roadways shall have a green background with a white border, and shall include words identifying the bicycle route or a legend consisting of words identifying the bicycle route and a pictograph or bicycle symbol.

metadata.section_title: Non-Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8b and M1-8c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.06 Option 2 - Non-Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8b and M1-8c)
text:
Section 9D.06 Option 2 - Non-Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8b and M1-8c)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1077

Words identifying the bicycle route may be omitted on Non-Numbered Bicycle Route (M1-8b and M1-8c) signs where a pictograph includes the likeness of a bicycle that clearly identifies the route as a bicycle route.

metadata.section_title: Non-Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8b and M1-8c)
metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

title: Section 9D.06 Support 3 - Non-Numbered Bicycle Route Signs (M1-8b and M1-8c)
text:

title: Section 9D.11 Option 1 - Mode-Specific Directional Guide Signs for Shared-Use Paths (D11-11, D11-12, D11-13, and D11-14)

Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1081

Where separate pathways are provided for different types of users, mode-specific Directional Guide (D11-11, D11-12, D11-13, and D11-14) signs (see Figure 9D-1) may be used to guide different types of users to the pathway that is intended for their respective modes. Advance Turn Arrow (M5 series) or Directional Arrow (M6 series) auxiliary plaques (see Figure 9D-1) with white arrows on green backgrounds may be used with Mode-Specific Directional Guide signs. Rev. 1

An identification marker may be used in an assembly for Destination Guide signs applied to shared-use paths, or may be incorporated into the overall design of Destination Guide sign, as a means of visually identifying the sign as part of an overall system of signs. MUTCD 11th Edition - Revision 1

Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities

Page: 1084

The size of an identification marker shall be smaller than the Destination Guide sign. Identification markers shall not be designed to have an appearance that could be mistaken by road users as being a traffic control device.

The area of the identification marker should not exceed ¹⁄5 of the area of the Destination Guide sign with which it is mounted in the same sign assembly.

Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1084

Except as provided in Paragraph 26 of this Section, Destination Guide signs for shared-use paths shall have a white legend and border on a green or brown background and shall be consistent with the basic design principles for guide signs.

text:
Section 9D.12 Standard 24 - Destination Guide Signs for Shared-Use Paths (D11-10a, D11-10b, D11-10c, D11-10d, D11-10e, and D11-10f)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1084

Color coding or pictographs shall not be used to distinguish between different types of destinations. If used, color coding shall be accomplished by the use of different colored square or rectangular panels on the face of the sign, each positioned to the left of the named geographic area to which the color-coding panel applies. The height of the colored square or rectangular panels shall not exceed 2 times the height of the upper-case letters of the principal legend on the sign.

Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1084

The different colored square or rectangular panels may include either a black or a white (whichever provides the better contrast with the color of the panel) letter, numeral, or other appropriate designation to identify the destination.

Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1084

Except where a shared-use path is within the highway right-of-way or crosses a street or highway, Destination Guide signs for shared-use paths may use background colors other than green or brown in order to provide a color identification for systematic destinations within the overall guide signing system.

text:
Section 9D.12 Standard 27 - Destination Guide Signs for Shared-Use Paths (D11-10a, D11-10b, D11-10c, D11-10d, D11-10e, and D11-10f)
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1084

The standard colors of red, orange, yellow, purple, or the fluorescent versions thereof, fluorescent yellow-green, and fluorescent pink shall not be used as background colors for Destination Guide signs for shared-use paths, in order to minimize possible confusion with critical, higher-priority regulatory and warning sign color meanings readily understood by path users.

Section 9D.12 Option 28 - Destination Guide Signs for Shared-Use Paths (D11-10a, D11-10b, D11-10c, D11-10d, D11-10e, and D11-10f)

Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1084

Destination Guide signs for shared-use paths may display telephone numbers, Internet addresses, and e-mail addresses, including domain names and uniform resource locators (URLs).

Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1084

If used, the use of telephone numbers, Internet addresses, and e-mail addresses shall be limited to direct contact information of the jurisdiction with authority of the shared-use path, or contact information for emergency service response, or both. Contact information for advertising purposes shall not be used.

Two-stage bicycle turn boxes provide a way for a bicyclist to make a turn in a manner such that a merge across the general-purpose lanes is not required.

Section 9D.14 Option 1 - General Service Signing for Bikeways
Part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
Chapter: Chapter 9D. Guide And Service Signs
Page: 1085

General Service signs (see Chapter 2I) may be used on bikeways.

metadata.part: Part 9 Traffic Control For Bicycle Facilities
